a10a_14301XX.speaker: Mission Control
a10a_14301XX.text: Stafford reports the clock has started. The tower is clear.

a10-minus0000010.speaker: Stafford
a10-minus0000010.text: And, roll program right on time.

a10-minus0000010.speaker: Mission Control
a10-minus0000010.text: Tom Stafford acknowledges the roll and pitch program to put Apollo 10 on the proper course.

a10-minus0000010.speaker: Stafford
a10-minus0000010.text: Okay. Pitch is tracking. Looking good.

a10-minus0000010.speaker: Mission Control
a10-minus0000010.text: One bravo is a - an abort mode dealing with altitude, function of altitude.

a10-minus0000010.speaker: Stafford
a10-minus0000010.text: Starting to rattle a little bit in here.

a10-minus0000010.speaker: Mission Control
a10-minus0000010.text: Cabin pressure is relieving. Downrange 1 mile, 3.3 nautical miles high.

a10-minus0000010.speaker: Cernan
a10-minus0000010.text: What a ride, babe, what a ride!

a10-minus0000010.speaker: Duke
a10-minus0000010.text: Roger. You're looking good, 10; you're looking real good.

a10-minus0000010.speaker: Mission Control
a10-minus0000010.text: That's Gene Stafford - Cernan reporting, "what a ride"

a10-minus0000010.speaker: Duke
a10-minus0000010.text: 10, you're through the Max Q. You're looking good.

a10-minus0000010.speaker: Stafford
a10-minus0000010.text: Two and a quarter g's. She's looking beautiful.

a10-minus0000010.speaker: Mission Control
a10-minus0000010.text: 000:01:44: One minute, 44 seconds downrange, 7, 12 miles high.

a10-minus0000010.speaker: Stafford
a10-minus0000010.text: Okay. Two and a half g's.

a10-minus0000010.speaker: Duke
a10-minus0000010.text: Okay. And, Mark. Mode 1 Charlie. You're looking great.

a10-minus0000010.speaker: Stafford
a10-minus0000010.text: Roger. One Charlie and 3 g's; it feels great.

a10-minus0000010.speaker: Stafford
a10-minus0000010.text: They're a little Pogo. Pogo damps.

a10-minus0000010.speaker: Mission Control
a10-minus0000010.text: Charlie Duke asking the crew to turn off their Emergency Detection System.

a10-minus0000010.speaker: Mission Control
a10-minus0000010.text: Good ignition on the second stage.

a10-minus0000010.speaker: Stafford
a10-minus0000010.text: And it looks like we got a good S-II...

a10-minus0000010.speaker: Duke
a10-minus0000010.text: Roger. [Garble] 10, on the S-II. It's looking good. Confirm EDS [Emergency Detection System] Off.

a10-minus0000010.speaker: Duke
a10-minus0000010.text: Roger, on the tower. And we confirm second plane Sep.

a10-minus0000010.speaker: Mission Control
a10-minus0000010.text: Flight Dynamics reports trajectory Go at 3 minutes, 9 seconds. Downrange, 81 miles. 46 miles high. Second plane separation, that is the skirt around the engines on the second stage. And the Launch Escape Tower has jettisoned.

a10-minus0000010.speaker: Stafford
a10-minus0000010.text: Man, that staging was quite a sequence!

a10-minus0000010.speaker: Duke
a10-minus0000010.text: The S-II is looking beautiful, Tom. Everything is copacetic.

a10-minus0000010.speaker: Stafford
a10-minus0000010.text: Roger. It looks good to be back up here, Charlie.

a10-s-ii-ignition.speaker: Mission Control
a10-s-ii-ignition.text: Good ignition on the second stage.

a10-s-ii-ignition.speaker: Stafford
a10-s-ii-ignition.text: And it looks like we got a good S-II...

a10-s-ii-ignition.speaker: Duke
a10-s-ii-ignition.text: Roger. [Garble] 10, on the S-II. It's looking good. Confirm EDS [Emergency Detection System] Off.

a10-s-ii-ignition.speaker: Duke
a10-s-ii-ignition.text: Roger, on the tower. And we confirm second plane Sep.

a10-s-ii-ignition.speaker: Mission Control
a10-s-ii-ignition.text: Flight Dynamics reports trajectory Go at 3 minutes, 9 seconds. Downrange, 81 miles. 46 miles high. Second plane separation, that is the skirt around the engines on the second stage. And the Launch Escape Tower has jettisoned.

a10-s-ii-ignition.speaker: Stafford
a10-s-ii-ignition.text: Man, that staging was quite a sequence!

a10-s-ii-ignition.speaker: Duke
a10-s-ii-ignition.text: The S-II is looking beautiful, Tom. Everything is copacetic.

a10-s-ii-ignition.speaker: Stafford
a10-s-ii-ignition.text: Roger. It looks good to be back up here, Charlie.

a10-s-ii-ignition.speaker: Mission Control
a10-s-ii-ignition.text: That's Charlie Duke talking to Tom Stafford.

a10-s-ii-ignition.speaker: Young
a10-s-ii-ignition.text: Just like old times! It's beautiful out there!

a10-s-ii-ignition.speaker: Stafford
a10-s-ii-ignition.text: Man, this is the greatest, Charlie.

a10-s-ii-ignition.speaker: Cernan
a10-s-ii-ignition.text: Charlie, babe. It's fantastic, babe, really!

a10-s-ii-ignition.speaker: Duke
a10-s-ii-ignition.text: Roger. Four minutes. You're Go. Your trajectory and guidance look good.

a10-s-ii-ignition.speaker: Stafford
a10-s-ii-ignition.text: Roger. We look on the line on board.

a10-s-ii-ignition.speaker: Mission Control
a10-s-ii-ignition.text: 171 miles downrange, 67 miles high at 4 minutes, 15 seconds. Still Go.

a10-s-ii-ignition.speaker: Mission Control
a10-s-ii-ignition.text: Glynn Lunney taking a status check. Everyone says Go. Four minutes, 50 seconds; 230 miles downrange, 67 miles high.

a10-s-ii-ignition.speaker: Duke
a10-s-ii-ignition.text: 10, Houston. At 5 minutes, you're all Go. All your systems are looking great.

a10-s-ii-ignition.speaker: Stafford
a10-s-ii-ignition.text: Roger. Five minutes, and 10 is Go.

a10-s-ii-ignition.speaker: Duke
a10-s-ii-ignition.text: Roger. You're right on the track.

a10-s-ii-ignition.speaker: Duke
a10-s-ii-ignition.text: 10, Houston. Coming up on 6 minutes. You're looking beautiful.

a10-s-ii-ignition.speaker: Mission Control
a10-s-ii-ignition.text: We have an estimate of inboard engine cut-off on the second stage at 8 minutes, 15 seconds. Outboard engine cut-off; 9 minutes, 11 seconds. Five minutes, 30 seconds; 299 miles downrange, 83 miles high. All controllers reporting Go. 350 miles downrange, 87 miles high now.

a10-s-ii-ignition.speaker: Stafford
a10-s-ii-ignition.text: Six minutes. Gimbal motors coming On. Pitch 1.

a10-s-ii-ignition.speaker: Cernan
a10-s-ii-ignition.text: Charlie, are you sure we didn't lose Snoopy on that staging?

a10-s-ii-ignition.speaker: Mission Control
a10-s-ii-ignition.text: Guidance says it's looking real good. Ira's 6 minutes, 23 seconds.

a10-s-ii-ignition.speaker: Duke
a10-s-ii-ignition.text: No, I think Snoopy is still there with you. You're looking good. We copy your gimbal motors On and your trim looks good.

a10-s-ii-ignition.speaker: Mission Control
a10-s-ii-ignition.text: Apollo 10 now has the capability to get into orbit on the S-IVB should the second stage malfunction.

a10-s-ii-ignition.speaker: Duke
a10-s-ii-ignition.text: 10, Houston. Coming up on 7 minutes. You are all Go. We have nominal level sense arm, 8 plus 15. S-II cut-off, 9 plus 11.

a10-s-ii-ignition.speaker: Stafford
a10-s-ii-ignition.text: You have the level sense arm, and 9 plus 11 is the S-II.

a10-s-ii-ignition.speaker: Mission Control
a10-s-ii-ignition.text: Seven minutes, 14 seconds. Downrange now 538 miles and 94½ nautical miles high. Coming up on inboard engine cut-off.

a10-s-ii-ignition.speaker: Duke
a10-s-ii-ignition.text: Roger on the inboard's, Tom. We confirm it.

a10-s-ii-ignition.speaker: Duke
a10-s-ii-ignition.text: 10, Houston. Eight minutes. You're looking good. How's the ride?

a10-s-ii-ignition.speaker: Mission Control
a10-s-ii-ignition.text: We are right down the ground track at 8 minutes, 30 seconds. 755 miles downrange, 98 miles high, velocity is 21,499 feet per second. Flight Director is taking a status for staging now.

a10-s-ii-ignition.speaker: Duke
a10-s-ii-ignition.text: Roger, Apollo 10. You are Go for staging.

a10-s-ii-ignition.speaker: Duke
a10-s-ii-ignition.text: Mark. Mode IV, Apollo 10. Mode IV.

a10-0000254.speaker: Stafford
a10-0000254.text: And it looks like we got a good S-II...

a10-0000254.speaker: Duke
a10-0000254.text: Roger. [Garble] 10, on the S-II. It's looking good. Confirm EDS [Emergency Detection System] Off.

a10-0000254.speaker: Duke
a10-0000254.text: Roger, on the tower. And we confirm second plane Sep.

a10-0000254.speaker: Mission Control
a10-0000254.text: Flight Dynamics reports trajectory Go at 3 minutes, 9 seconds. Downrange, 81 miles. 46 miles high. Second plane separation, that is the skirt around the engines on the second stage. And the Launch Escape Tower has jettisoned.

a10-0000254.speaker: Stafford
a10-0000254.text: Man, that staging was quite a sequence!

a10-0000254.speaker: Duke
a10-0000254.text: The S-II is looking beautiful, Tom. Everything is copacetic.

a10-0000254.speaker: Stafford
a10-0000254.text: Roger. It looks good to be back up here, Charlie.

a10-0000254.speaker: Mission Control
a10-0000254.text: That's Charlie Duke talking to Tom Stafford.

a10-0000254.speaker: Young
a10-0000254.text: Just like old times! It's beautiful out there!

a10-0000254.speaker: Stafford
a10-0000254.text: Man, this is the greatest, Charlie.

a10-0000254.speaker: Cernan
a10-0000254.text: Charlie, babe. It's fantastic, babe, really!

a10-0000254.speaker: Duke
a10-0000254.text: Roger. Four minutes. You're Go. Your trajectory and guidance look good.

a10-0000254.speaker: Stafford
a10-0000254.text: Roger. We look on the line on board.

a10-0000254.speaker: Mission Control
a10-0000254.text: 171 miles downrange, 67 miles high at 4 minutes, 15 seconds. Still Go.

a10-0000254.speaker: Mission Control
a10-0000254.text: Glynn Lunney taking a status check. Everyone says Go. Four minutes, 50 seconds; 230 miles downrange, 67 miles high.

a10-0000254.speaker: Duke
a10-0000254.text: 10, Houston. At 5 minutes, you're all Go. All your systems are looking great.

a10-0000254.speaker: Stafford
a10-0000254.text: Roger. Five minutes, and 10 is Go.

a10-0000254.speaker: Duke
a10-0000254.text: Roger. You're right on the track.

a10-0000254.speaker: Duke
a10-0000254.text: 10, Houston. Coming up on 6 minutes. You're looking beautiful.

a10-0000254.speaker: Mission Control
a10-0000254.text: We have an estimate of inboard engine cut-off on the second stage at 8 minutes, 15 seconds. Outboard engine cut-off; 9 minutes, 11 seconds. Five minutes, 30 seconds; 299 miles downrange, 83 miles high. All controllers reporting Go. 350 miles downrange, 87 miles high now.

a10-0000254.speaker: Stafford
a10-0000254.text: Six minutes. Gimbal motors coming On. Pitch 1.

a10-0000254.speaker: Cernan
a10-0000254.text: Charlie, are you sure we didn't lose Snoopy on that staging?

a10-0000254.speaker: Mission Control
a10-0000254.text: Guidance says it's looking real good. Ira's 6 minutes, 23 seconds.

a10-0000254.speaker: Duke
a10-0000254.text: No, I think Snoopy is still there with you. You're looking good. We copy your gimbal motors On and your trim looks good.

a10-0000254.speaker: Mission Control
a10-0000254.text: Apollo 10 now has the capability to get into orbit on the S-IVB should the second stage malfunction.

a10-0000254.speaker: Duke
a10-0000254.text: 10, Houston. Coming up on 7 minutes. You are all Go. We have nominal level sense arm, 8 plus 15. S-II cut-off, 9 plus 11.

a10-0000254.speaker: Stafford
a10-0000254.text: You have the level sense arm, and 9 plus 11 is the S-II.

a10-0000254.speaker: Mission Control
a10-0000254.text: Seven minutes, 14 seconds. Downrange now 538 miles and 94½ nautical miles high. Coming up on inboard engine cut-off.

a10-0000254.speaker: Duke
a10-0000254.text: Roger on the inboard's, Tom. We confirm it.

a10-0000254.speaker: Duke
a10-0000254.text: 10, Houston. Eight minutes. You're looking good. How's the ride?

a10-0000254.speaker: Mission Control
a10-0000254.text: We are right down the ground track at 8 minutes, 30 seconds. 755 miles downrange, 98 miles high, velocity is 21,499 feet per second. Flight Director is taking a status for staging now.

a10-0000254.speaker: Duke
a10-0000254.text: Roger, Apollo 10. You are Go for staging.

a10-0000254.speaker: Duke
a10-0000254.text: Mark. Mode IV, Apollo 10. Mode IV.

a10-0023032.speaker: Duke
a10-0023032.text: Roger, 10. You're Go for TLI. S-IVB is looking as planned.

a10-0023032.speaker: Stafford
a10-0023032.text: Good show. We've got the old 8-ball working on number 2, and powered up P47.

a10-0023032.speaker: Stafford
a10-0023032.text: TVC [Thrust Vector Control] Servo Power On [panel 8].

a10-0023032.speaker: Cernan
a10-0023032.text: Max turn rate; you want 10 degrees?

a10-0023032.speaker: Mission Control
a10-0023032.text: Booster engineer says the Saturn is Go.

a10-0023032.speaker: Stafford
a10-0023032.text: [S-II] SEP light Out. Right on time.

a10-0023032.speaker: Stafford
a10-0023032.text: Fuel lead in the starboard. Getting acceleration.

a10-0023032.speaker: Duke
a10-0023032.text: Hello. Apollo 10, Houston. At 1 minute, you're looking great.

a10-0023032.speaker: Stafford
a10-0023032.text: Roger. One minute, everything looks good on board.

a10-0023032.speaker: Stafford
a10-0023032.text: It's starting to pick up the yaw, just as programmed.

a10-0023032.speaker: Stafford
a10-0023032.text: I don't know. I just - Feels like we're pitching [garble]. Steady as a rock.

a10-0023032.speaker: Young
a10-0023032.text: Feel it - I can see it yawing.

a10-0023032.speaker: Cernan
a10-0023032.text: What a way to watch a sunrise!

a10-0023032.speaker: Mission Control
a10-0023032.text: Tom Stafford reporting ¾ of one G.

a10-0023032.speaker: Cernan
a10-0023032.text: [Garble] the sunrise. We must be getting higher, you know it? Okay, ... coming up on 3 minutes. Mark it.

a10-0023032.speaker: Duke
a10-0023032.text: Apollo 10, Houston. Coming up 3 minutes; trajectory looks great.

a10-0023032.speaker: Stafford
a10-0023032.text: Three minutes. Everything looks good, Charlie.

a10-0023032.speaker: Duke
a10-0023032.text: Apollo 10, Houston. We've got a predicted cut-off: 2 plus 39 plus 10.

a10-0023032.speaker: Stafford
a10-0023032.text: Wow! Right into the Sun, here.

a10-0023032.speaker: Cernan
a10-0023032.text: Okay, babe, there's a 03:50 coming up.

a10-0023032.speaker: Duke
a10-0023032.text: And, Apollo 10, Houston. At 4 minutes everybody is saying Go. The S-IVB is looking great.

a10-0023032.speaker: Mission Control
a10-0023032.text: 31,000 feet per second velocity. Present altitude; 123 miles.

a10-0023032.speaker: Duke
a10-0023032.text: Roger, Houston. 10, here. Looks good on board.

a10-0023032.speaker: Stafford
a10-0023032.text: We're getting a little [garble] high-frequency vibrations in the cabin.

a10-0023032.speaker: Stafford
a10-0023032.text: Were getting small high-frequency vibrations. Nothing to worry about...

a10-0023032.speaker: Cernan
a10-0023032.text: Come on, we've got another 40 seconds to burn.

a10-0023032.speaker: Duke
a10-0023032.text: At 5 minutes, we still have you Go, 10.

a10-0023032.speaker: Cernan
a10-0023032.text: Okay, we're coming up on 05:25, predicted 05:43. 05:30.

a10-0023032.speaker: Duke
a10-0023032.text: 10, Houston, in the blind. At cut-off, Up Telemetry, IU to Accept.

a10-0023032.speaker: Cernan
a10-0023032.text: Going on 40; 1, 2, 3. SECO! Son of a bitch!

a10-0023032.speaker: Duke
a10-0023032.text: Roger. SECO. We confirm the cut-off.

a10-0023032.speaker: Cernan
a10-0023032.text: Okay, we've gone 35,514[fps]. H-dot 42211 [4221.1 fps]. Up Telemetry, IU to Accept at 172.5 [altitude, nautical miles] at cut-off.

a10-0023032.speaker: Stafford
a10-0023032.text: And would you believe, my Delta-V C . reads minus 0.6?

a10-0023032.speaker: Duke
a10-0023032.text: Roger. Minus 0.6 on the Delta-V C . That's beautiful.

a10-0023032.speaker: Young
a10-0023032.text: And, Charlie, we've got an O 2 Flow High and a light in the middle of the burn, here, which we can't account for.

a10-0023032.speaker: Duke
a10-0023032.text: Apollo 10, Houston. In the blind. Have LOS at Redstone 2 plus 41. See you over Hawaii, 2 plus 44.

a10-0023032.speaker: Young
a10-0023032.text: Roger. In trouble-shooting that thing, I went to Auto 2 on the suit circuit water accumulator. That's the only thing I could think of. It was right at 10 minutes when it happened.

a10-0023032.speaker: Duke
a10-0023032.text: Roger. We think that cabin pressure regs kicked in for that O 2 flow, John.

a10-0023032.speaker: Stafford
a10-0023032.text: They just went out, and the flow is starting to drop now, Charlie. Looks like we're in good shape.

a10-0023032.speaker: Duke
a10-0023032.text: Okay, fine. You're beginning to fade out. We think we'll be losing you through the Redstone here in about 30 seconds. Hawaii at 2 plus 44.

a10-0023032.speaker: CapCom
a10-0023032.text: And, 10, in the blind. Everything we got looks nominal. You're on your way

a10-0023032.speaker: Mission Control
a10-0023032.text: This is Apollo Control. 2 hours and 41 minutes into the mission. Apollo 10 on the way to the Moon. We have lost signal for about 3 or 4 minutes. We will pick up at Hawaii at 2 hours, 44 minutes. This is Mission Control in Houston.

a10-0023032.speaker: Stafford
a10-0023032.text: I believe it worked slick as a whistle.

a10-0023032.speaker: Stafford
a10-0023032.text: Yes, okay. Do you want to stow your suit now, babe?

a10-0023032.speaker: Cernan
a10-0023032.text: Well, yes. We won't switch leads.

a10-0023032.speaker: Stafford
a10-0023032.text: Okay, You can use your - your thing here, right? You can talk on that.

a10-0023032.speaker: Young
a10-0023032.text: I can see stars in the day - I can see something in the day - they're not stars. Shit. It's a bunch of crap.

a10-0023032.speaker: Stafford
a10-0023032.text: You got the TV in each side up, José?

a10-0023032.speaker: Mission Control
a10-0023032.text: This is Apollo Control; 2 hours, 44 minutes. Charlie Duke's just put in a call to the spacecraft. We're showing present altitude 608 nautical miles. The velocity starting to drop off already; 33,602 feet per second.

a10-0023032.speaker: Duke
a10-0023032.text: Hello. Apollo 10, Houston through Hawaii. How do you read? Over.

a10-0023032.speaker: Stafford
a10-0023032.text: Roger. Houston, Apollo 10. Would you believe the world is starting to fade away?

a10-0023032.speaker: Duke
a10-0023032.text: Roger. We believe it, Tom. You're all Go here. FIDO confirms it was a perfect insertion. We'd like you to confirm that you're on omni Delta, and we're all Go.

a10-0023032.speaker: Stafford
a10-0023032.text: John, why don't you go hook up that [garble]?

a10-0023032.speaker: Young
a10-0023032.text: I've already hooked it up. How do you think this [garble] here cable here [garble]? You want to talk about something fantastic...

a10-0023032.speaker: Cernan
a10-0023032.text: We're on omni Delta, Charlie, and there sure ain't any question about it from here.

a10-0023032.speaker: Cernan
a10-0023032.text: I don't meant the Delta, I mean the world.

a10-0023032.speaker: Duke
a10-0023032.text: 10, Houston. We expect the S-IVB to start to Sep attitude at 2 plus 54 plus 10, right on time. And your Sep attitude is looking good.

a10-0023032.speaker: Stafford
a10-0023032.text: Okay. John's in the left seat now, and I'm in the center seat. We've already changed,

a10-0023032.speaker: Duke
a10-0023032.text: Roger, Tom. Did you get a chance to get that radiation survey meter out?

a10-0023032.speaker: Cernan
a10-0023032.text: Yes, I did, Charlie, and I read zero on every scale.

a10-0023032.speaker: Duke
a10-0023032.text: Okay. And what was the GET of that, Gene? About 245?

a10-0023032.speaker: Duke
a10-0023032.text: 10, Houston. We'll have you AOS now until you get to LOS at the Moon.

a10-0023032.speaker: Stafford
a10-0023032.text: Sounds like Chris has pretty good coverage.

a10-0023032.speaker: Duke
a10-0023032.text: Yes, sir. He's sitting back there smiling.

a10-0023032.speaker: Duke
a10-0023032.text: Chris says there ain't no backing out now.

a10-0023032.speaker: Cernan
a10-0023032.text: You can play our favorite song, Charlie, the one about Fly me Someplace or Somewhere.

a10-tpd.speaker: Duke
a10-tpd.text: Hey, it's beautiful, Gene. We got the black and white now with a little time delay on the color.

a10-tpd.speaker: Cernan
a10-tpd.text: Okay. And the S-IVB ought to be coming in here in a second.

a10-tpd.speaker: Duke
a10-tpd.text: Roger.

a10-tpd.speaker: Duke
a10-tpd.text: Hey, we got the S-IVB coming into the top. The sun's really shining on it.

a10-tpd.speaker: Cernan
a10-tpd.text: Okay. I'll try to adjust it for you

a10-tpd.speaker: Duke
a10-tpd.text: Hey, we got the color now.

a10-tpd.speaker: Cooper
a10-tpd.text: You're on the air, Babe. Oh, that's beautiful.

a10-tpd.speaker: Cernan
a10-tpd.text: Have you got the color?

a10-tpd.speaker: Duke
a10-tpd.text: Yes, sir. It's looking great!

a10-tpd.speaker: Cernan
a10-tpd.text: I'm sorry it's tilted a little bit. That's the best I could do with the brackets.

a10-tpd.speaker: Duke
a10-tpd.text: No sweat; we got it right in the center of the screen, Gene. It looks like the Sun's really bright on it.

a10-tpd.speaker: Cernan
a10-tpd.text: Tremendously so.

a10-tpd.speaker: Duke
a10-tpd.text: The Sun's got the S-IVB - the LM sort of blotted out; it's so bright.

a10-tpd.speaker: Duke
a10-tpd.text: Hey, your zooming in looks really good, Gene.

a10-tpd.speaker: Cernan
a10-tpd.text: Charlie, I've got it closed down all the way. Does that help any?

a10-tpd.speaker: Duke
a10-tpd.text: Roger. The - In the center of the LM now, we still got a real - couple of real bright spots, but it's looking real good in color. We can, see the probe - correction, the drogue.

a10-tpd.speaker: Duke
a10-tpd.text: Gene, it's really looking good. The - It's the silver panels that are reflecting back real brightly.

a10-tpd.speaker: Cernan
a10-tpd.text: They're awful [garble] right now, too.

a10-tpd.speaker: Duke
a10-tpd.text: Roger. The resolution is fantastic. You're drifting off just to the right a little bit.

a10-tpd.speaker: Duke
a10-tpd.text: 10, Houston. You can't believe the picture we're getting. The resolution is really fantastic.

a10-tpd.speaker: Cernan
a10-tpd.text: I'll tell you, this monitor makes it great.

a10-tpd.speaker: Cernan
a10-tpd.text: How's the color, Charlie?

a10-tpd.speaker: Duke
a10-tpd.text: Say again.

a10-tpd.speaker: Cernan
a10-tpd.text: How's the color?

a10-tpd.speaker: Duke
a10-tpd.text: It's really beautiful, Gene. You've got it framed just perfectly. The resolution...

a10-tpd.speaker: Cernan
a10-tpd.text: Hey, I think the color will be beautiful once, we can show you the Earth.

a10-tpd.speaker: Duke
a10-tpd.text: Roger.

a10-tpd.speaker: Cooper
a10-tpd.text: Old Snoopy sure looks good.

a10-tpd.speaker: Cernan
a10-tpd.text: Yes. He sure do.

a10-tpd.speaker: Young
a10-tpd.text: Old Charlie Brown is a mass of cord and wire floating around here, though.

a10-tpd.speaker: Duke
a10-tpd.text: I can imagine.

a10-tpd.speaker: Cernan
a10-tpd.text: Houston, Charlie Brown. I've settled down now on the zoom, and the closing rate you see is the closing rate we've got.

a10-tpd.speaker: Duke
a10-tpd.text: Roger. We copy. Gene, if it looks like to you - We have a bright spot - it may be on your vidicon, coming in on your vidicon tube on the black and white. It's right above the drogue.

a10-tpd.speaker: Cernan
a10-tpd.text: Yes, we've got it in real life. The camera is fully in the shade. That's just a reflection coming right off the - right off of Snoopy.

a10-tpd.speaker: Duke
a10-tpd.text: Rog.

a10-tpd.speaker: Duke
a10-tpd.text: 10, we're afraid you might be burning a hole into your vidicon tube. Move it off to the - a little bit off of Snoop. I think those panels are so bright we might be getting problems with the vidicon tube.

a10-tpd.speaker: Cernan
a10-tpd.text: All right.

a10-tpd.speaker: Cernan
a10-tpd.text: I can just cover it up for a while if you like.

a10-tpd.speaker: Duke
a10-tpd.text: Stand by.

a10-tpd.speaker: Duke
a10-tpd.text: 10, Houston. We'd like the LM - Snoopy back, if you could give it to us.

a10-tpd.speaker: Cernan
a10-tpd.text: I'd be glad to.

a10-tpd.speaker: Duke
a10-tpd.text: Hey, that's looking great now, except for a couple of fingers there or something.

a10-tpd.speaker: Cernan
a10-tpd.text: Good resolution; that's what they were.

a10-tpd.speaker: Cooper
a10-tpd.text: You got your big hands in the way.

a10-tpd.speaker: Duke
a10-tpd.text: Hey, I don't know what you did, but the - It's really beautiful now. Really great.

a10-tpd.speaker: Cernan
a10-tpd.text: We're just a little closer.

a10-tpd.speaker: Duke
a10-tpd.text: Yes.

a10-tpd.speaker: Cooper
a10-tpd.text: Boy, the color is great, Gene.

a10-tpd.speaker: Duke
a10-tpd.text: Oh, boy. That's beautiful.

a10-tpd.speaker: Cernan
a10-tpd.text: Hell, I got to watch it on TV, too. I've got - can't see out the window.

a10-tpd.speaker: Cooper
a10-tpd.text: Hey, what's that guy doing on the front porch?

a10-tpd.speaker: Stafford
a10-tpd.text: That's a green man, Gordo.

a10-tpd.speaker: Stafford
a10-tpd.text: And John estimates 50 feet closing.

a10-tpd.speaker: Duke
a10-tpd.text: Roger.

a10-tpd.speaker: Stafford
a10-tpd.text: How's the resolution?

a10-tpd.speaker: Cernan
a10-tpd.text: Well, all I can say is it's really happening, and what hasn't happened you haven't seen yet.

a10-tpd.speaker: Duke
a10-tpd.text: Roger.

a10-tpd.speaker: CapCom (Cooper)
a10-tpd.text: Really great resolution.

a10-tpd.speaker: Mission Control
a10-tpd.text: That was Gordon Cooper. He and Charlie Duke are both on the CapCom console. And that orange platform is the front porch.

a10-tpd.speaker: Cernan
a10-tpd.text: Charlie, we can't be more than about 5, 10 feet away.

a10-tpd.speaker: Duke
a10-tpd.text: Roger.

a10-tpd.speaker: Duke
a10-tpd.text: 10, it's looking real stable to us. We show you closing slightly.

a10-tpd.speaker: Stafford
a10-tpd.text: Roger.

a10-tpd.speaker: Cernan
a10-tpd.text: Be docked in a second, I hope.

a10-tpd.speaker: Duke
a10-tpd.text: Roger.

a10-tpd.speaker: Duke
a10-tpd.text: 10, Houston. You're looking good. We can see the markings on the rendezvous window. Looks like you just docked.

a10-tpd.speaker: Stafford
a10-tpd.text: Roger. We've got a capture; we haven't fired yet.

a10-tpd.speaker: Duke
a10-tpd.text: Roger.

a10-tpd.speaker: Duke
a10-tpd.text: Gene, we can read the numbers on the LM docking window.

a10-tpd.speaker: Stafford
a10-tpd.text: Snap, snap, and we're there. Got two grays.

a10-tpd.speaker: Duke
a10-tpd.text: Roger.

a10-tpd.speaker: Cernan
a10-tpd.text: You saw the docking, Charlie.

a10-tpd.speaker: Stafford
a10-tpd.text: We didn't get any Master Alarm. Everything looks snug.

a10-tpd.speaker: Duke
a10-tpd.text: Roger. Didn't look like there was any hardly any after dock - post docking oscillations.

a10-tpd.speaker: Stafford
a10-tpd.text: Check.

a10-tpd.speaker: Stafford
a10-tpd.text: Okay. Pyros coming Off.

a10-tpd.speaker: Duke
a10-tpd.text: Roger.

a10-tpd.speaker: Duke
a10-tpd.text: 10, that's a great picture of the quads.

a10-tpd.speaker: Cernan
a10-tpd.text: I'll try and take you on a quick tour. We're - I may have to hold you up for a little bit here.

a10-tpd.speaker: Stafford
a10-tpd.text: Okay. John's going down to the LEB [Lower Equipment Bay] and, I'm going to the left seat now.

a10-tpd.speaker: Duke
a10-tpd.text: Roger, Tom. We're standing by.

a10-tpd.speaker: Duke
a10-tpd.text: Apollo 10, Houston. We'd like you to Safe the Logic.

a10-tpd.speaker: Mission Control
a10-tpd.text: That was one of the Reaction Control System quads you saw there at the last. We are coming back up here now with another picture. Altitude 6,869 nautical miles, velocity 21,280 feet per second.

a10-tpd.speaker: Cernan
a10-tpd.text: Charlie, you're going to have to look at the same picture for a while until we get this integrity check complete.

a10-tpd.speaker: Duke
a10-tpd.text: Roger. We understand you are busy.

a10-tpd.speaker: Cernan
a10-tpd.text: Okay. I'm watching.

a10-tpd.speaker: Cernan
a10-tpd.text: Houston, this is 10. We are in the process of attempting to pressurize the tunnel.

a10-s-ivb-sep-0035600.speaker: Stafford
a10-s-ivb-sep-0035600.text: Okay. I'm going to count down to Sep.

a10-s-ivb-sep-0035600.speaker: Duke
a10-s-ivb-sep-0035600.text: Roger. Standing by.

a10-s-ivb-sep-0035600.speaker: Stafford
a10-s-ivb-sep-0035600.text: Go.

a10-s-ivb-sep-0035600.speaker: Mission Control
a10-s-ivb-sep-0035600.text: We have TV coming up again right now. The Command Module Service Module and the LM have just separated from the S-IVB.

a10-s-ivb-sep-0035600.speaker: Stafford
a10-s-ivb-sep-0035600.text: Snoopy's coming out of the doghouse.

a10-s-ivb-sep-0035600.speaker: Duke
a10-s-ivb-sep-0035600.text: Roger.

a10-s-ivb-sep-0035600.speaker: Duke
a10-s-ivb-sep-0035600.text: And we got the TV.

a10-s-ivb-sep-0035600.speaker: Cernan
a10-s-ivb-sep-0035600.text: Houston, we have Cryo pressure light; O 2 tank 1 and 2 are reading about 800 [psia].

a10-s-ivb-sep-0035600.speaker: Duke
a10-s-ivb-sep-0035600.text: Roger.

a10-s-ivb-sep-0035600.speaker: Duke
a10-s-ivb-sep-0035600.text: 10, we'd like to have you turn the fans on.

a10-s-ivb-sep-0035600.speaker: Cernan
a10-s-ivb-sep-0035600.text: They're on.

a10-s-ivb-sep-0035600.speaker: Cernan
a10-s-ivb-sep-0035600.text: Houston, we're maneuvering around right now, acquired the S-IVB, going into SEP attitude.

a10-s-ivb-sep-0035600.speaker: Duke
a10-s-ivb-sep-0035600.text: Roger.

a10-s-ivb-sep-0035600.speaker: Cernan
a10-s-ivb-sep-0035600.text: Houston, that was fans in Auto or Off on the O 2 ?

a10-s-ivb-sep-0035600.speaker: Duke
a10-s-ivb-sep-0035600.text: On, Gene; On.

a10-s-ivb-sep-0035600.speaker: Cernan
a10-s-ivb-sep-0035600.text: They're On; On.

a10-s-ivb-sep-0035600.speaker: Duke
a10-s-ivb-sep-0035600.text: Roger.

a10-s-ivb-sep-0035600.speaker: Stafford
a10-s-ivb-sep-0035600.text: Okay, Houston. We can see the S-IVB now.

a10-s-ivb-sep-0035600.speaker: Duke
a10-s-ivb-sep-0035600.text: Roger. Out of which window, Tom?

a10-s-ivb-sep-0035600.speaker: Stafford
a10-s-ivb-sep-0035600.text: John's looking at it out the hatch window.

a10-s-ivb-sep-0035600.speaker: Duke
a10-s-ivb-sep-0035600.text: Roger.

a10-s-ivb-sep-0035600.speaker: Cernan
a10-s-ivb-sep-0035600.text: Houston, it's the S-IVB in the TV right now.

a10-s-ivb-sep-0035600.speaker: Duke
a10-s-ivb-sep-0035600.text: Roger. We got it right over the quad - thrusters there, Gene.

a10-s-ivb-sep-0035600.speaker: Cernan
a10-s-ivb-sep-0035600.text: That's it. I'll see if I can bring it into you.

a10-s-ivb-sep-0035600.speaker: Duke
a10-s-ivb-sep-0035600.text: Roger. Thanks.

a10-s-ivb-sep-0035600.speaker: Stafford
a10-s-ivb-sep-0035600.text: It looks like the dome there of the S-IVB is gold.

a10-s-ivb-sep-0035600.speaker: Duke
a10-s-ivb-sep-0035600.text: Roger.

a10-s-ivb-sep-0035600.speaker: Stafford
a10-s-ivb-sep-0035600.text: It looks like we got good separation, distance and no problems.

a10-s-ivb-sep-0035600.speaker: Duke
a10-s-ivb-sep-0035600.text: Roger. It looks like about the size of a quarter to us here, Tom. What do you estimate your range?

a10-s-ivb-sep-0035600.speaker: Stafford
a10-s-ivb-sep-0035600.text: I'd say at least 300 feet, now.

a10-s-ivb-sep-0035600.speaker: Duke
a10-s-ivb-sep-0035600.text: Roger.

a10-s-ivb-sep-0035600.speaker: Cernan
a10-s-ivb-sep-0035600.text: Are you getting anything, Charlie?

a10-s-ivb-sep-0035600.speaker: Duke
a10-s-ivb-sep-0035600.text: Roger, Gene. That zoom was real good. We have the S-IVB; the Sun's real bright on it.

a10-s-ivb-sep-0035600.speaker: Cernan
a10-s-ivb-sep-0035600.text: How's the focus?

a10-s-ivb-sep-0035600.speaker: Duke
a10-s-ivb-sep-0035600.text: Looks real good.

a10-s-ivb-sep-0035600.speaker: Duke
a10-s-ivb-sep-0035600.text: That LM antenna is showing up real bright.

a10-s-ivb-sep-0035600.speaker: Stafford
a10-s-ivb-sep-0035600.text: Hello, Houston. Apollo 10.

a10-s-ivb-sep-0035600.speaker: Duke
a10-s-ivb-sep-0035600.text: Go ahead, 10.

a10-s-ivb-sep-0035600.speaker: Stafford
a10-s-ivb-sep-0035600.text: Roger. I wish you'd tell Dr. Von Braun, Lee James, Kurt Debus, and Rocco Petrone thanks a lot for all the people who worked on the great ride.

a10-s-ivb-sep-0035600.speaker: Duke
a10-s-ivb-sep-0035600.text: Roger. We're going out to the networks now, I think. They probably heard it; we'll pass it on, though.

a10-s-ivb-sep-0035600.speaker: Stafford
a10-s-ivb-sep-0035600.text: A few thousand people worked on that machine, and we sure appreciate it.

a10-s-ivb-sep-0035600.speaker: Duke
a10-s-ivb-sep-0035600.text: Roger. It looked beautiful from here

a10-s-ivb-sep-0035600.speaker: Duke
a10-s-ivb-sep-0035600.text: Did you move the camera, Gene?

a10-s-ivb-sep-0035600.speaker: Cernan
a10-s-ivb-sep-0035600.text: Say again.

a10-s-ivb-sep-0035600.speaker: Duke
a10-s-ivb-sep-0035600.text: Did you move the camera?

a10-s-ivb-sep-0035600.speaker: Cernan
a10-s-ivb-sep-0035600.text: It's out the hatch window; John's got it now.

a10-s-ivb-sep-0035600.speaker: Duke
a10-s-ivb-sep-0035600.text: Okay.

a10-s-ivb-sep-0035600.speaker: Stafford
a10-s-ivb-sep-0035600.text: In fact, you can see the S-IVB's attitude, thrusters firing, now.

a10-s-ivb-sep-0035600.speaker: Duke
a10-s-ivb-sep-0035600.text: We haven't been able to pick that up yet; S-IVB's really good.

a10-s-ivb-sep-0035600.speaker: Stafford
a10-s-ivb-sep-0035600.text: Yes.

a10-s-ivb-sep-0035600.speaker: Stafford
a10-s-ivb-sep-0035600.text: I'd estimate now that we're a good 300 to 400 feet away.

a10-s-ivb-sep-0035600.speaker: Duke
a10-s-ivb-sep-0035600.text: Roger.

a10-s-ivb-sep-0035600.speaker: Stafford
a10-s-ivb-sep-0035600.text: And we're slowly going away. We're starting to see one side of it.

a10-s-ivb-sep-0035600.speaker: Duke
a10-s-ivb-sep-0035600.text: Roger.

a10-s-ivb-sep-0035600.speaker: Duke
a10-s-ivb-sep-0035600.text: And 10, Houston. "Eagle-Eyes" Cooper said he can see your thrusters firing up there on the S-IVB.

a10-s-ivb-sep-0035600.speaker: Stafford
a10-s-ivb-sep-0035600.text: Good show.

a10-s-ivb-sep-0035600.speaker: Cernan
a10-s-ivb-sep-0035600.text: I can't even see them from here. He must be about 2,500 miles away.

a10-s-ivb-sep-0035600.speaker: Duke
a10-s-ivb-sep-0035600.text: [Laughter.] Roger.

a10-s-ivb-sep-0035600.speaker: Cooper
a10-s-ivb-sep-0035600.text: You're looking out the wrong window.

a10-s-ivb-sep-0035600.speaker: Cernan
a10-s-ivb-sep-0035600.text: I'm sure going to like Snoopy, because that's all I'm going to see.

a10-s-ivb-sep-0035600.speaker: Mission Control
a10-s-ivb-sep-0035600.text: Distance from the Earth now 13,531 miles, velocity 16,063 feet per second.

a10-s-ivb-sep-0035600.speaker: Stafford
a10-s-ivb-sep-0035600.text: Okay. I've got the S-IVB out my window now.

a10-s-ivb-sep-0035600.speaker: Stafford
a10-s-ivb-sep-0035600.text: Okay, Houston. This is CDR. I've got the S-IVB out of my window, here.

a10-s-ivb-sep-0035600.speaker: Duke
a10-s-ivb-sep-0035600.text: Roger, Tom. It's looking great. It's a pretty bright network. We'd like you to keep the camera moving around so we don't burn anything.

a10-earth-views-0050634.speaker: Duke
a10-earth-views-0050634.text: We got you on the black and white. Stand by about 12 seconds. It looks great on the black and white.

a10-earth-views-0050634.speaker: Stafford
a10-earth-views-0050634.text: I figure right there you should be able to see the United States, Mexico, Baja California -

a10-earth-views-0050634.speaker: Duke
a10-earth-views-0050634.text: Hey, it's really beautiful, Tom. It's coming in great.

a10-earth-views-0050634.speaker: Stafford
a10-earth-views-0050634.text: You ought to see it up here, Charlie.

a10-earth-views-0050634.speaker: Young
a10-earth-views-0050634.text: We've got the whole globe there.

a10-earth-views-0050634.speaker: Stafford
a10-earth-views-0050634.text: Yes, you're looking right at the United States there.

a10-earth-views-0050634.speaker: Duke
a10-earth-views-0050634.text: Roger.

a10-earth-views-0050634.speaker: Stafford
a10-earth-views-0050634.text: See the Rocky Mountains sticking out? Baja California? Can't tell whether you have any smog in LA or not, but Alaska is pretty much socked in.

a10-earth-views-0050634.speaker: Duke
a10-earth-views-0050634.text: Roger.

a10-earth-views-0050634.speaker: Duke
a10-earth-views-0050634.text: It's really a beautiful picture.

a10-earth-views-0050634.speaker: Stafford
a10-earth-views-0050634.text: We'll just let it go here for a couple of minutes.

a10-earth-views-0050634.speaker: Duke
a10-earth-views-0050634.text: Okay. Thanks. Hey, Gene-o, on your monitor, which way is the North Pole to you? We've got it up at the northeast corner?

a10-earth-views-0050634.speaker: Stafford
a10-earth-views-0050634.text: That's right, Charlie. The northeast corner is the North Pole.

a10-earth-views-0050634.speaker: Duke
a10-earth-views-0050634.text: Okay.

a10-earth-views-0050634.speaker: Stafford
a10-earth-views-0050634.text: You can see cloud - covers the northern part of Alaska, and it comes down and cloudcovers over the northeastern part of Canada, and I can see out into the New England area. We've got a low pressure area out there.

a10-earth-views-0050634.speaker: Duke
a10-earth-views-0050634.text: Roger.

a10-earth-views-0050634.speaker: Duke
a10-earth-views-0050634.text: The color is fantastic. It really is.

a10-earth-views-0050634.speaker: Stafford
a10-earth-views-0050634.text: Okay. And it looks like the Rocky Mountains are orange colored to me. The rest of U.S., Baja California, that really stands out as all brownish, and the oceans are blue; but there are so many clouds out to the northeast of the United States, you can't believe it. Covers the Far East over to Europe as far as you can see.

a10-earth-views-0050634.speaker: Duke
a10-earth-views-0050634.text: Roger. We see all that. We've got a brownish spot that's pretty hard to pick out just exactly what we're looking at, but we do see the brown and the clouds out over the ocean about the center of the globe.

a10-earth-views-0050634.speaker: Stafford
a10-earth-views-0050634.text: Yes. Okay. The brown spot is the Rocky Mountains. It runs down around into New Mexico, up into Colorado.

a10-earth-views-0050634.speaker: Duke
a10-earth-views-0050634.text: Roger.

a10-earth-views-0050634.speaker: Duke
a10-earth-views-0050634.text: This resolution is fantastic. The LM, you can count the rivets on it, and yet the Earth and the colors are really beautiful.

a10-earth-views-0050634.speaker: Stafford
a10-earth-views-0050634.text: Okay. Well, I can zoom in a bit on a certain part of the Earth here; I'll try to zoom in on the Rocky Mountains and California.

a10-earth-views-0050634.speaker: Duke
a10-earth-views-0050634.text: Roger. Standing by, Tom.

a10-earth-views-0050634.speaker: Stafford
a10-earth-views-0050634.text: How's that, Charlie? Better?

a10-earth-views-0050634.speaker: Duke
a10-earth-views-0050634.text: We're looking at it on the black and white. It looks great. Stand by. Here he comes in on the color now.

a10-earth-views-0050634.speaker: Duke
a10-earth-views-0050634.text: Hey, boy! That is really fantastic. We can pick out Baja and the smog over LA and we see Mexico and we go off to the east, in our picture, and come into the Rockies area. The Baja California and the Gulf, they really stand out beautiful.

a10-earth-views-0050634.speaker: Stafford
a10-earth-views-0050634.text: Okay. We'll move it around.

a10-earth-views-0050634.speaker: Duke
a10-earth-views-0050634.text: Looks like we've got some cloud down over New Orleans and down in that way.

a10-earth-views-0050634.speaker: Stafford
a10-earth-views-0050634.text: Yes. Okay. Charlie. That's full zoom.

a10-earth-views-0050634.speaker: Duke
a10-earth-views-0050634.text: Okay, this has got to be the greatest sight ever.

a10-earth-views-0050634.speaker: Stafford
a10-earth-views-0050634.text: You ought to see it up here.

a10-earth-views-0050634.speaker: Duke
a10-earth-views-0050634.text: Hey, Tom. Boy, it is really fantastic. Could you get Baja in a little bit? We're showing this deal to the Pacific now.

a10-earth-views-0050634.speaker: Duke
a10-earth-views-0050634.text: Okay. We've got the Baja now on the right-hand side of our screen, and it's right in the center now, and we can see Mexico and the clouds up over the Rockies. It's really a fantastic sight, almost see the freeways in LA.

a10-earth-views-0050634.speaker: Stafford
a10-earth-views-0050634.text: Right. Okay, I'm going to move down. You can take a look down by the Gulf of Mexico now.

a10-earth-views-0050634.speaker: Duke
a10-earth-views-0050634.text: Roger.

a10-earth-views-0050634.speaker: Cernan
a10-earth-views-0050634.text: Charlie, this is - It's so hard to describe. You can go right up past Alaska, and you can see the polar caps. It's incredible.

a10-earth-views-0050634.speaker: Duke
a10-earth-views-0050634.text: We see it all here, Gene. The colors are really beautiful.

a10-earth-views-0050634.speaker: Cernan
a10-earth-views-0050634.text: That's great. And the blackest black that you ever could conceive is the setting for all this.

a10-earth-views-0050634.speaker: Duke
a10-earth-views-0050634.text: Roger.

a10-earth-views-0050634.speaker: Stafford
a10-earth-views-0050634.text: Looks like the people of New York have a little bit of cloud cover today. It goes all the way down, in fact, down back by the Cape.

a10-earth-views-0050634.speaker: Duke
a10-earth-views-0050634.text: Roger.

a10-earth-views-0050634.speaker: Duke
a10-earth-views-0050634.text: You guys are really giving us a great show. This is fantastic.

a10-earth-views-0050634.speaker: Stafford
a10-earth-views-0050634.text: We just want to thank all the peop1e who helped get us up here, Charlie.

a10-earth-views-0050634.speaker: Duke
a10-earth-views-0050634.text: Roger. I know.

a10-earth-views-0050634.speaker: Stafford
a10-earth-views-0050634.text: That includes the taxpayers, too.

a10-earth-views-0050634.speaker: Duke
a10-earth-views-0050634.text: [Laughter.] Roger.

a10-earth-views-0050634.speaker: Cernan
a10-earth-views-0050634.text: Charlie, you know, you blink your eyes and you look out there and you know it's three dimensional, but it is just sitting out there in the middle of nowhere and it's unbelievable.

a10-earth-views-0050634.speaker: Duke
a10-earth-views-0050634.text: We copy, Gene. We are getting a real idea now, for the first time, of what you are really seeing up there. The colors on the oceans are just as blue as they can be and real white clouds all over, and the land is a real deep brown, Almost a reddish brown.

a10-earth-views-0050634.speaker: Cernan
a10-earth-views-0050634.text: And the North Pole, the Arctic area, is just solidly, whitely, snow-covered.

a10-earth-views-0050634.speaker: Duke
a10-earth-views-0050634.text: Roger.

a10-earth-views-0050634.speaker: Stafford
a10-earth-views-0050634.text: It's a brown around in the Rocky Mountains and orange down into New Mexico and becomes a little more of a purplish orange...

a10-earth-views-0050634.speaker: Duke
a10-earth-views-0050634.text: Roger. We see all - I cut you off there, Tom. We see all that, and it is looking good.

a10-earth-views-0050634.speaker: Cernan
a10-earth-views-0050634.text: You can actually pick out what I think is the San Joaquin Valley down there, just on the west side of the hills.

a10-earth-views-0050634.speaker: Duke
a10-earth-views-0050634.text: Roger.

a10-earth-views-0050634.speaker: Stafford
a10-earth-views-0050634.text: Okay, I am going to open the zoom and bring it back in the other way.

a10-earth-views-0050634.speaker: Duke
a10-earth-views-0050634.text: Roger, 10. Would you check your TV servo power. We show it On.

a10-earth-views-0050634.speaker: Stafford
a10-earth-views-0050634.text: Sorry. I must have knocked it on there when I was wrestling around here.

a10-earth-views-0050634.speaker: Duke
a10-earth-views-0050634.text: Roger.

a10-earth-views-0050634.speaker: Duke
a10-earth-views-0050634.text: Boy, we are looking at a black background now.

a10-earth-views-0050634.speaker: Stafford
a10-earth-views-0050634.text: There, you have the whole Earth.

a10-earth-views-0050634.speaker: Duke
a10-earth-views-0050634.text: Roger. We - It is really beautiful. Tom, we can even pick up the little tip of the northern part of South America down below Baja.

a10-earth-views-0050634.speaker: Cernan
a10-earth-views-0050634.text: Yes, it's coming in now.

a10-earth-views-0050634.speaker: Duke
a10-earth-views-0050634.text: It's really blue, you guys.

a10-earth-views-0050634.speaker: Stafford
a10-earth-views-0050634.text: That's for sure.

a10-earth-views-0050634.speaker: Cernan
a10-earth-views-0050634.text: We are looking right at you. Looks like you may have a few clouds there right now in Houston.

a10-earth-views-0050634.speaker: Duke
a10-earth-views-0050634.text: It's sort of a constant overcast here in the MOCR but we have never been...

a10-earth-views-0050634.speaker: Cernan
a10-earth-views-0050634.text: You are right on the edge of what might be some clouds, but certainly to the northeast of that area, it's clobbered.

a10-earth-views-0050634.speaker: Duke
a10-earth-views-0050634.text: Roger.

a10-earth-views-0050634.speaker: Stafford
a10-earth-views-0050634.text: Okay. John is going ahead through P52 [IMU realignment] here.

a10-earth-views-0050634.speaker: Duke
a10-earth-views-0050634.text: Roger.

a10-earth-views-0050634.speaker: Cernan
a10-earth-views-0050634.text: I think I can see all the way up into the Newfoundland area now, up along the eastern coast that is not covered.

a10-earth-views-0050634.speaker: Duke
a10-earth-views-0050634.text: Right, Gene-o. It looks to us that it is just completely clouded up over that way.

a10-earth-views-0050634.speaker: Stafford
a10-earth-views-0050634.text: You might say we have moved out in the last couple of hours.

a10-earth-views-0050634.speaker: Duke
a10-earth-views-0050634.text: Boy, I'll say. We got you at about 26,000 miles here - or a little bit more.

a10-earth-views-0050634.speaker: Stafford
a10-earth-views-0050634.text: Okay. I am going to put the zoom on 55, which will give you the exact resolution we have.

a10-earth-views-0050634.speaker: Duke
a10-earth-views-0050634.text: Roger.

a10-earth-views-0050634.speaker: Cernan
a10-earth-views-0050634.text: And, just for the record, it looks to me like a pretty nice place to live.

a10-earth-views-0050634.speaker: Duke
a10-earth-views-0050634.text: Roger. And we see you at P52.

a10-earth-views-0050634.speaker: Stafford
a10-earth-views-0050634.text: Okay. 55 on the zoom, and that is about exactly the same thing we are seeing now.

a10-earth-views-0050634.speaker: Duke
a10-earth-views-0050634.text: Well, that is really fantastic.

a10-earth-views-0050634.speaker: Duke
a10-earth-views-0050634.text: 10, can you see the Hawaiian Islands?

a10-earth-views-0050634.speaker: Stafford
a10-earth-views-0050634.text: Negative. Too much cloud coverage.

a10-earth-views-0050634.speaker: Duke
a10-earth-views-0050634.text: Okay.

a10-earth-views-0050634.speaker: Young
a10-earth-views-0050634.text: 10. Houston, this is 10. Those Gyro torquing angles look okay to you?

a10-earth-views-0050634.speaker: Duke
a10-earth-views-0050634.text: Stand by.

a10-earth-views-0050634.speaker: Duke
a10-earth-views-0050634.text: Roger. They look okay to us, John.

a10-earth-views-0050634.speaker: Young
a10-earth-views-0050634.text: Okay. You can't verify these stars with this LM on right now.

a10-earth-views-0050634.speaker: Duke
a10-earth-views-0050634.text: Roger. Are these your P23 stars?

a10-earth-views-0050634.speaker: Young
a10-earth-views-0050634.text: Negative. These are P52 stars.

a10-earth-views-0050634.speaker: Duke
a10-earth-views-0050634.text: Okay.

a10-earth-views-0050634.speaker: Duke
a10-earth-views-0050634.text: 10, Houston. How do the stars look in this attitude?

a10-earth-views-0050634.speaker: Young
a10-earth-views-0050634.text: Houston, in the telescope, I have difficulty telling the stars from the particles, right now.

a10-earth-views-0050634.speaker: Duke
a10-earth-views-0050634.text: Roger.

a10-earth-views-0050634.speaker: Young
a10-earth-views-0050634.text: There are some that look like stars but I have not been able to stop long enough to really see if they are or not.

a10-earth-views-0050634.speaker: Duke
a10-earth-views-0050634.text: Okay. Through the sextant they are okay?

a10-earth-views-0050634.speaker: Young
a10-earth-views-0050634.text: Affirmative.

a10-earth-views-0050634.speaker: Duke
a10-earth-views-0050634.text: Okay.

a10-earth-views-0050634.speaker: Cernan
a10-earth-views-0050634.text: The Earth is just starting now to take on - a little bit of the terminator is coming across and we are losing the roundness on the bottom side.

a10-earth-views-0050634.speaker: Duke
a10-earth-views-0050634.text: Roger.

a10-earth-views-0050634.speaker: Cernan
a10-earth-views-0050634.text: I should say on the eastern side.

a10-earth-views-0050634.speaker: Duke
a10-earth-views-0050634.text: Roger. We are seeing that now - coming in.

a10-earth-views-0050634.speaker: Cernan
a10-earth-views-0050634.text: I hope the colors are as good down there as they are up here.

a10-earth-views-0050634.speaker: Duke
a10-earth-views-0050634.text: Absolutely fantastic. That is the only way I can describe it. It's really beautiful.

a10-earth-views-0050634.speaker: Stafford
a10-earth-views-0050634.text: Houston, I have a question. Does that picture fill up your whole screen now? I want to correlate it with the monitor.

a10-earth-views-0050634.speaker: Duke
a10-earth-views-0050634.text: Negative. We got about - quite a ways to go before we fill up our screen, Tom. It looks about the size of a basketball, sort of. It's pretty hard, you are zooming in now and we are just about to fill up the whole picture.

a10-earth-views-0050634.speaker: Stafford
a10-earth-views-0050634.text: Okay. The monitor has a little different aspect ratio than the standard view.

a10-earth-views-0050634.speaker: Duke
a10-earth-views-0050634.text: Right.

a10-earth-views-0050634.speaker: Duke
a10-earth-views-0050634.text: Okay.

a10-earth-views-0050634.speaker: Duke
a10-earth-views-0050634.text: Apollo 10, Houston. We are ready for the P27 [AGC update] update, if you can give us P00 and Accept.

a10-earth-tv-0071115.speaker: McCandless
a10-earth-tv-0071115.text: You're filling up about 80 per cent of the screen vertically.

a10-earth-tv-0071115.speaker: Stafford
a10-earth-tv-0071115.text: Okay. Again, it's kind of an awkward position to hold it, but again, you can barely see Baja California and Mexico real well.

a10-earth-tv-0071115.speaker: McCandless
a10-earth-tv-0071115.text: Yes, indeed. If you could roll the camera right or left 90 degrees and then zoom a little more, we could fill up nearly the whole screen.

a10-earth-tv-0071115.speaker: Young
a10-earth-tv-0071115.text: How's that, Bruce?

a10-earth-tv-0071115.speaker: McCandless
a10-earth-tv-0071115.text: There you go, 10. That's good.

a10-earth-tv-0071115.speaker: McCandless
a10-earth-tv-0071115.text: Right. And we've got the North Pole on the right of our screen down here, and the Atlantic Ocean was the terminator at the bottom of the screen.

a10-earth-tv-0071115.speaker: Stafford
a10-earth-tv-0071115.text: Roger. That's correct. Looks like a beautiful sight. And either you have clouds over the Sierra Nevada's or they're snowcaps at this time. I can't tell which from here. You can still see the San Joaquin Valley.

a10-earth-tv-0071115.speaker: McCandless
a10-earth-tv-0071115.text: Roger.

a10-earth-tv-0071115.speaker: McCandless
a10-earth-tv-0071115.text: 10, Houston. Over.

a10-earth-tv-0071115.speaker: Cernan
a10-earth-tv-0071115.text: Houston, we're going to zoom in on it a little bit; and, also, we're deactivating the VHF [VHF Simplex] at this time.

a10-earth-tv-0071115.speaker: McCandless
a10-earth-tv-0071115.text: Roger. Copy. Deactivating the VHF and zooming in. Okay. Hold it about there.

a10-earth-tv-0071115.speaker: Young
a10-earth-tv-0071115.text: You can see that subsolar point very well in this picture.

a10-earth-tv-0071115.speaker: McCandless
a10-earth-tv-0071115.text: Yes, indeed. We can see the very bright spot on the surface of the water that is the subsolar point.

a10-earth-tv-0071115.speaker: Young
a10-earth-tv-0071115.text: Does it look gold?

a10-earth-tv-0071115.speaker: McCandless
a10-earth-tv-0071115.text: Negative. It looks silvery, about the same color as the clouds here, only obviously brighter.

a10-earth-tv-0071115.speaker: Stafford
a10-earth-tv-0071115.text: You can see night-time coming over on the eastern part of the United States, too.

a10-earth-tv-0071115.speaker: McCandless
a10-earth-tv-0071115.text: Roger. And while you're doing this, we'd like to uplink you a PTC REFSMMAT. Go to P00 and Accept.

a10-earth-tv-0071115.speaker: Young
a10-earth-tv-0071115.text: Roger. P00 and Accept, Bruce.

a10-earth-tv-0071115.speaker: McCandless
a10-earth-tv-0071115.text: Roger.

a10-earth-tv-0071115.speaker: McCandless
a10-earth-tv-0071115.text: 10, this is Houston. Can you describe for us the area that the northern clouds seem to be obscuring?

a10-earth-tv-0071115.speaker: Stafford
a10-earth-tv-0071115.text: Yes. They start up in the Northwest Territories of Canada and actually ring out to Alaska, and from there they go down just about to the Canadian - United States border and go on east. But the whole northwest Pacific, across northern Canada and over to Greenland is all obscured with just a solid white mass of clouds as you can see in your - near the North Pole.

a10-earth-tv-0071115.speaker: McCandless
a10-earth-tv-0071115.text: Roger. We can see the California coastline and Baja California down in the lower right-hand corner of our screen.

a10-earth-tv-0071115.speaker: Stafford
a10-earth-tv-0071115.text: I've zoomed down a little bit. Now you can really notice those clouds that cover about the northern - looks about the northern third or quarter of the Earth there.

a10-earth-tv-0071115.speaker: McCandless
a10-earth-tv-0071115.text: Roger, 10. Up in the vicinity of Alaska, we see a swirl. Does that look like a storm system or low pressure area to you?

a10-earth-tv-0071115.speaker: Stafford
a10-earth-tv-0071115.text: Yes. You've got a swirl out there right on the - off the coast of Alaska.

a10-earth-tv-0071115.speaker: Stafford
a10-earth-tv-0071115.text: How are the colors coming through down there, Bruce?

a10-earth-tv-0071115.speaker: McCandless
a10-earth-tv-0071115.text: Oh, the colors are coming through beautifully. The oceans are a beautiful blue-green. We can see the land masses in a brown to reddish-brown. The vicinity of the North Pole, the clouds and ice caps seems to be saturating a little; but on the whole, it's all coming through nicely.

a10-earth-tv-0071115.speaker: Stafford
a10-earth-tv-0071115.text: Okay. Good. And you can - The area right east of the Sierra Nevada's, now - I guess around the Rockies - as night-time starts to spread over the United States, is becoming more of a purplish-red. You can see Texas, Oklahoma, and that area; it's becoming more of a purplish-red, and the rest of it is still a bright red - a bright red to brown.

a10-earth-tv-0071115.speaker: McCandless
a10-earth-tv-0071115.text: That's right. We can see the terminator quite clearly moving up from lower right-hand corner of our screen.

a10-earth-tv-0071115.speaker: Stafford
a10-earth-tv-0071115.text: Roger.

a10-earth-tv-0071115.speaker: Stafford
a10-earth-tv-0071115.text: It's really amazing the cloud cover we have here and the swirls that you can see through.

a10-earth-tv-0071115.speaker: McCandless
a10-earth-tv-0071115.text: Apollo 10, this is Houston. We had a computer problem here that delayed our REFSMMAT uplink. We're ready to go now, though.

a10-earth-tv-0071115.speaker: Stafford
a10-earth-tv-0071115.text: Okay. We are in P00.

a10-earth-tv-0071115.speaker: Cernan
a10-earth-tv-0071115.text: P00 and Accept.

a10-earth-tv-0071115.speaker: McCandless
a10-earth-tv-0071115.text: Apollo 10, this is Houston. You all planning any interior shots this pass?

a10-earth-tv-0071115.speaker: Stafford
a10-earth-tv-0071115.text: We can turn on the floodlights for just a minute here.

a10-earth-tv-0071115.speaker: McCandless
a10-earth-tv-0071115.text: Okay.

a10-earth-tv-0071115.speaker: Stafford
a10-earth-tv-0071115.text: Okay. We are going to go around and shoot an interior now.

a10-earth-tv-0071115.speaker: McCandless
a10-earth-tv-0071115.text: Roger.

a10-earth-tv-0071115.speaker: Stafford
a10-earth-tv-0071115.text: As soon as we get all arranged around here, we'll show you a quick inside shot.

a10-earth-tv-0071115.speaker: McCandless
a10-earth-tv-0071115.text: Houston. Roger. Out.

a10-earth-tv-0071115.speaker: McCandless
a10-earth-tv-0071115.text: Apollo 10, Houston. We've completed the uplink. You can go back to Block.

a10-earth-tv-0071115.speaker: Stafford
a10-earth-tv-0071115.text: Roger. We're in Block.

a10-earth-tv-0071115.speaker: McCandless
a10-earth-tv-0071115.text: Roger. Okay, you're coming through on our black and white monitor now very well. We'll see the color in a minute.

a10-earth-tv-0071115.speaker: Stafford
a10-earth-tv-0071115.text: Okay. John is just sitting upside-down here in the LEB [Lower Equipment Bay].

a10-earth-tv-0071115.speaker: McCandless
a10-earth-tv-0071115.text: Yes. We see Smiling John down there.

a10-earth-tv-0071115.speaker: Stafford
a10-earth-tv-0071115.text: He's just turning around down here.

a10-earth-tv-0071115.speaker: Young
a10-earth-tv-0071115.text: In living color.

a10-earth-tv-0071115.speaker: McCandless
a10-earth-tv-0071115.text: Tom, you can't believe - it's really great. The colors are fantastic.

a10-earth-tv-0071115.speaker: Stafford
a10-earth-tv-0071115.text: Okay. We're flipping on John.

a10-earth-tv-0071115.speaker: McCandless
a10-earth-tv-0071115.text: We're looking into the LEB now, and looking at John Young on the right. You need to focus a little when you get in closer.

a10-earth-tv-0071115.speaker: Stafford
a10-earth-tv-0071115.text: How does that look?

a10-earth-tv-0071115.speaker: McCandless
a10-earth-tv-0071115.text: It's beautiful. Coming through nicely.

a10-earth-tv-0071115.speaker: Stafford
a10-earth-tv-0071115.text: Okay.

a10-earth-tv-0071115.speaker: McCandless
a10-earth-tv-0071115.text: Looks just like you, John.

a10-earth-tv-0071115.speaker: Stafford
a10-earth-tv-0071115.text: Wait just a minute.

a10-earth-tv-0071115.speaker: McCandless
a10-earth-tv-0071115.text: Are you in the interior position on the camera?

a10-earth-tv-0071115.speaker: Stafford
a10-earth-tv-0071115.text: Over here is Gene-o.

a10-earth-tv-0071115.speaker: McCandless
a10-earth-tv-0071115.text: Roger. We're looking at Gene right now. Understand you all haven't got your suits off yet.

a10-earth-tv-0071115.speaker: Stafford
a10-earth-tv-0071115.text: John has his suit off and all stowed, and Gene and I don't.

a10-earth-tv-0071115.speaker: McCandless
a10-earth-tv-0071115.text: Okay. We got a good look at the DSKY a few seconds ago as you panned past it.

a10-earth-tv-0071115.speaker: Stafford
a10-earth-tv-0071115.text: Okay.

a10-earth-tv-0071115.speaker: McCandless
a10-earth-tv-0071115.text: Okay. We see your pack on the screen right now. Can zoom in on that a little?

a10-earth-tv-0071115.speaker: McCandless
a10-earth-tv-0071115.text: That's coming through loud and clear, now.

a10-earth-tv-0071115.speaker: Cernan
a10-earth-tv-0071115.text: That's the best I can do. I'll try to focus it closer.

a10-earth-tv-0071115.speaker: McCandless
a10-earth-tv-0071115.text: Roger.

a10-earth-tv-0071115.speaker: McCandless
a10-earth-tv-0071115.text: That's the one on the front cover of your Flight Plan, I believe. We can read the writing on the Flight Plan.

a10-earth-tv-0071115.speaker: Cernan
a10-earth-tv-0071115.text: That's affirmative.

a10-earth-tv-0071115.speaker: McCandless
a10-earth-tv-0071115.text: It's really coming through beautifully down here.

a10-earth-tv-0071115.speaker: McCandless
a10-earth-tv-0071115.text: Okay, Tom. We see your name plate; there's Stafford.

a10-earth-tv-0071115.speaker: Stafford
a10-earth-tv-0071115.text: That's how you can tell who it is, huh?

a10-earth-tv-0071115.speaker: McCandless
a10-earth-tv-0071115.text: That's how we can tell who it is.

a10-earth-tv-0071115.speaker: Stafford
a10-earth-tv-0071115.text: All right.

a10-earth-tv-0071115.speaker: Cernan
a10-earth-tv-0071115.text: You can see the sun coming in over my shoulder, and then on Tom, it's really tremendous.

a10-earth-tv-0071115.speaker: McCandless
a10-earth-tv-0071115.text: Yes, indeed. It certainly is bright there.

a10-earth-tv-0071115.speaker: Cernan
a10-earth-tv-0071115.text: For information, all these are at f:22.

a10-earth-tv-0071115.speaker: McCandless
a10-earth-tv-0071115.text: Roger.

a10-earth-tv-0071115.speaker: Stafford
a10-earth-tv-0071115.text: In fact, that's what we shot the Earth at, was f:22.

a10-earth-tv-0071115.speaker: McCandless
a10-earth-tv-0071115.text: Roger.

a10-earth-tv-0071115.speaker: McCandless
a10-earth-tv-0071115.text: Looks like you got some suntan yesterday, Tom.

a10-earth-tv-0071115.speaker: Stafford
a10-earth-tv-0071115.text: Right. I have to stay healthy there, Charlie.

a10-earth-tv-0071115.speaker: Stafford
a10-earth-tv-0071115.text: I'll take it back over here at left window and show you Earth again.

a10-earth-tv-0071115.speaker: McCandless
a10-earth-tv-0071115.text: Roger, Tom.

a10-earth-tv-0071115.speaker: McCandless
a10-earth-tv-0071115.text: Okay, 10. We're getting the Earth now. We've got the terminator to our left, and it looks like the South Pole on the top of the screen.

a10-earth-tv-0071115.speaker: McCandless
a10-earth-tv-0071115.text: Apollo 10, this is Houston. We're going to have a communications handover at about 7 hours, 30 minutes GET, or about 4 hours from now, And the black and white is really looking good. The color is showing a little bit of saturation on the white. Could you tell us the position of your ALC [Automatic Light Compensation] switch? Over.

a10-earth-tv-0071115.speaker: Stafford
a10-earth-tv-0071115.text: Stand by.

a10-earth-tv-0071115.speaker: Cernan
a10-earth-tv-0071115.text: In Outside.

a10-earth-tv-0071115.speaker: McCandless
a10-earth-tv-0071115.text: Roger.

a10-earth-tv-0071115.speaker: Stafford
a10-earth-tv-0071115.text: It's in the Outside [position].

a10-earth-tv-0071115.speaker: McCandless
a10-earth-tv-0071115.text: 10, this is Houston. We're showing the orientation reversed from what you had it a few minutes ago. Is it convenient for you to turn the world upside-down or right-side-up here?

a10-earth-tv-0071115.speaker: Stafford
a10-earth-tv-0071115.text: Yes. We can do it.

a10-0270048.speaker: McCandless
a10-0270048.text: Okay. We've got the North Pole over to the upper right-hand corner - the right-hand edge of our screen. Do you have a commentary from up there. 10.

a10-0270048.speaker: Stafford
a10-0270048.text: Yes. Okay. It looks like the North Pole and most of Russia is covered with clouds. The United States is pretty much wide open. In fact, the solar subpoint is right over the Gulf of Mexico now.

a10-0270048.speaker: McCandless
a10-0270048.text: Roger, 10. Could you give us narrow beam on the High Gain Antenna?

a10-0270048.speaker: Stafford
a10-0270048.text: Okay, Houston. I've got the full zoom on it, so you can see we're quite a bit further away today than we were yesterday.

a10-0270048.speaker: McCandless
a10-0270048.text: Yes, indeed.

a10-0270048.speaker: Stafford
a10-0270048.text: Roger. What you see there - What you see there is a little bigger than we actually see it, since I have the full zoom on it. If you look to the south, you can see all of South America there, and west of the Andes is clear.

a10-0270048.speaker: McCandless
a10-0270048.text: Roger.

a10-0270048.speaker: Stafford
a10-0270048.text: And in the tropical rain forest over Venezuela and Brazil and Columbia you can see the clouds that hang over there all the time. I noticed how clear it is west of the Andes.

a10-0270048.speaker: McCandless
a10-0270048.text: Roger. We can see that on the left of our screen. The landmasses don't seem to stand out quite as clearly today as they did yesterday.

a10-0270048.speaker: Stafford
a10-0270048.text: That's correct. A lot of it is the cloud cover, and also you can see night-time moving over Europe now.

a10-0270048.speaker: Stafford
a10-0270048.text: You've got a real weird cloud formation coming around down - just a minute. Let me get it focused.

a10-0270048.speaker: Young
a10-0270048.text: It's a real peculiar-looking cloud swirl. It comes off of what looks like Labrador and goes all the way across the ocean into Europe.

a10-0270048.speaker: Stafford
a10-0270048.text: I'm having a little harder time holding it today because of the narrow beam that we have with the zoom lens. We're out at maximum zoom now.

a10-0270048.speaker: McCandless
a10-0270048.text: Roger. It's coming very nicely here. Would you confirm you are in the Exterior on ALC?

a10-0270048.speaker: Stafford
a10-0270048.text: Right. We're Exterior on ALC.

a10-0270048.speaker: McCandless
a10-0270048.text: Thank you.

a10-0270048.speaker: Stafford
a10-0270048.text: I'll open it up to about a 55 millimeter and show you exactly how it appears to us.

a10-0270048.speaker: McCandless
a10-0270048.text: Roger. We're...

a10-0270048.speaker: Stafford
a10-0270048.text: Sure are a lot of clouds down there today.

a10-0270048.speaker: McCandless
a10-0270048.text: We are standing by for your zoom - out to show us the relative size as it appears to you.

a10-0270048.speaker: Stafford
a10-0270048.text: Okay. Right. Right there is about how the Earth appears to us now. We've made a few miles since yesterday.

a10-0270048.speaker: McCandless
a10-0270048.text: Yes, indeed. Roger. We show you about 115,000 nautical miles [213,000 km] out, here in our plots. Looks like about halfway.

a10-0270048.speaker: Stafford
a10-0270048.text: Yes. How are the colors coming into today, Bruce?

a10-0270048.speaker: McCandless
a10-0270048.text: Oh, the colors are coming beautifully. I'm amazed at the fidelity. The sea seems to reproduce the same color from day to day, so it looks like you guys have a pretty stable piece of equipment.

a10-0270048.speaker: Stafford
a10-0270048.text: Okay. Again, you can see Baja California coming in there just real clear, and the Rocky Mountains, particularly starting into Mexico going up through Colorado and Wyoming, are coming in.

a10-0270048.speaker: McCandless
a10-0270048.text: Roger. I'm having a little difficulty picking out the landmasses down here today.

a10-0270048.speaker: Stafford
a10-0270048.text: That's because of cloud cover. It looks like broken clouds over the southeastern part of the United States. Northeast has a little bit more. Looks like Canada is all socked over today, and over that big cap that goes up over the North Pole and over to Russia it's just solid overcast.

a10-0270525.speaker: Stafford
a10-0270525.text: Okay. Again, you can see Baja California coming in there just real clear, and the Rocky Mountains, particularly starting into Mexico going up through Colorado and Wyoming, are coming in.

a10-0270525.speaker: McCandless
a10-0270525.text: Roger. I'm having a little difficulty picking out the landmasses down here today.

a10-0270525.speaker: Stafford
a10-0270525.text: That's because of cloud cover. It looks like broken clouds over the southeastern part of the United States. Northeast has a little bit more. Looks like Canada is all socked over today, and over that big cap that goes up over the North Pole and over to Russia it's just solid overcast.

a10-0270525.speaker: McCandless
a10-0270525.text: Roger. We can pick up part of South America. Must be the Andes, just above or just to the west of the terminator down in the southern portion of the globe.

a10-0270525.speaker: Cernan
a10-0270525.text: Bruce, you should see all of North and South America from where you are. We're going to zoom it in again here. Show you a little bit closer.

a10-0270525.speaker: Cernan
a10-0270525.text: That's maximum zoom right now on the camera.

a10-0270525.speaker: McCandless
a10-0270525.text: Roger.

a10-0270525.speaker: Cernan
a10-0270525.text: You know, it's a beautiful sight. We're sitting here, and it's almost like science-fiction looking back at it, Bruce.

a10-0270525.speaker: McCandless
a10-0270525.text: Right. We can pick out the continents a little more clearly.

a10-0270525.speaker: Young
a10-0270525.text: I'm voting for the world being round, if there's any dissenters.

a10-0270525.speaker: McCandless
a10-0270525.text: Roger. We'll record your vote on that issue.

a10-0270525.speaker: Young
a10-0270525.text: And, you know, yesterday we said the San Joaquin Valley was very evident. It sits on a bowl. Even though we're looking at it obliquely, you can still pick it out in the western United States. It's just like a big bowl carved out of the coastal end the Sierra Nevada Mountains.

a10-0270525.speaker: McCandless
a10-0270525.text: Roger.

a10-0270525.speaker: McCandless
a10-0270525.text: Apollo 10, Houston. The SPS data has been looked at on both the midcourse 2 and the evasive maneuver, and all the data is good. We'd like to get you to cycle the ALC switch once, so we can observe the effect on the picture down here.

a10-0270525.speaker: Stafford
a10-0270525.text: Okay. Let me go back and get our monitor. Okay. Here we are.

a10-0270525.speaker: McCandless
a10-0270525.text: Roger. You just hold it steady, and then cycle it a few seconds to Interior and back to Exterior for us.

a10-0270525.speaker: Cernan
a10-0270525.text: There's Interior now.

a10-0270525.speaker: McCandless
a10-0270525.text: Boy, we can really see it working out down here.

a10-0270525.speaker: Cernan
a10-0270525.text: Coming back to us again.

a10-0270525.speaker: McCandless
a10-0270525.text: Beautiful.

a10-0270525.speaker: Cernan
a10-0270525.text: And, Tom's cutting down the f-stop now a little bit.

a10-0270525.speaker: McCandless
a10-0270525.text: Beautiful. What f-stop are you using? If you can stop it down one or two stops more it seems like the definition is better.

a10-0270525.speaker: Cernan
a10-0270525.text: There's f:22 right there.

a10-0270525.speaker: McCandless
a10-0270525.text: Okay. Hold it there.

a10-0270525.speaker: McCandless
a10-0270525.text: 10, this is Houston. When you stop it down, we get a second or so of excellent definition and no saturation, and then it tends to saturate again up in the North Polar region as though the ALC weren't quite picking up the intensity of the highlights.

a10-0271029.speaker: Cernan
a10-0271029.text: Bruce, we will not be able to see the Moon because - through the TV - because we got the Sun right along side of it out the right-hand window.

a10-0271029.speaker: McCandless
a10-0271029.text: Roger. Understand.

a10-0271029.speaker: Cernan
a10-0271029.text: We'll bring you on inside the spacecraft, if you like.

a10-0271029.speaker: McCandless
a10-0271029.text: Okay. Before you do that would you open the lens up about two stops slowly and then stop it down fairly rapidly for us?

a10-0271029.speaker: Cernan
a10-0271029.text: Okay. They are coming open now. Up and back.

a10-0271029.speaker: McCandless
a10-0271029.text: Roger. Go ahead and bring the camera inside now if you like.

a10-0271029.speaker: Stafford
a10-0271029.text: Yes, I can see what you mean about the saturation. From this kind of a candid view down here looking down at this distance, you could never tell anybody inhabited the place.

a10-0271029.speaker: McCandless
a10-0271029.text: Roger.

a10-0271029.speaker: Stafford
a10-0271029.text: Okay. We're going to take you inside.

a10-0271029.speaker: Cernan
a10-0271029.text: That's probably been said before.

a10-0271029.speaker: McCandless
a10-0271029.text: Okay. We're picking up your transmission from inside now.

a10-0271029.speaker: Cernan
a10-0271029.text: Houston, this is obviously our patch. How is it coming through in color?

a10-0271029.speaker: McCandless
a10-0271029.text: Not so good really. It looks like you got some rather intense lighting from the back and the side - If you could get the lighting more directly on the patch, it would be better.

a10-0271029.speaker: Cernan
a10-0271029.text: Yes, that's the Sun coming in.

a10-0271029.speaker: McCandless
a10-0271029.text: Roger.

a10-0271029.speaker: McCandless
a10-0271029.text: We got John coming through nicely on the tube. What was the three fingers for?

a10-0271029.speaker: Cernan
a10-0271029.text: Do you see our emblem of today?

a10-0271029.speaker: McCandless
a10-0271029.text: Oh, that's beautiful.

a10-0271029.speaker: Cernan
a10-0271029.text: We were going to put some more things in, but we just ran out of time.

a10-0271029.speaker: McCandless
a10-0271029.text: [Laughter.] Roger! Is this also your emblem?

a10-0271029.speaker: Cernan
a10-0271029.text: This is another emblem. Do you see any resemblance between the card and the guy holding the card?

a10-0271029.speaker: McCandless
a10-0271029.text: Now that you mention it.

a10-0271029.speaker: Cernan
a10-0271029.text: Does he carry the briefcase?

a10-0271029.speaker: Young
a10-0271029.text: Roger. Good grief, Charlie Brown!

a10-0271029.speaker: Cernan
a10-0271029.text: Now you're going to bring on that whizzer here,

a10-0271029.speaker: McCandless
a10-0271029.text: Okay. We got Snoopy now.

a10-0271029.speaker: Cernan
a10-0271029.text: Boy, he's been quiet for 2 days; he's going to get a chance to do a little woofing here in the next couple days.

a10-0271029.speaker: McCandless
a10-0271029.text: Roger. We notice the resemblance there, too.

a10-0271029.speaker: Cernan
a10-0271029.text: Thanks a lot. I didn't know Tom had a big nose like that.

a10-0271029.speaker: Stafford
a10-0271029.text: Ugh.

a10-0271534.speaker: Stafford
a10-0271534.text: Take you over to Gene-o's side of the spacecraft.

a10-0271534.speaker: McCandless
a10-0271534.text: Roger. Picking up Gene now. You've got rather strong backlighting from the window.

a10-0271534.speaker: McCandless
a10-0271534.text: That's the spirit. You all drawing the window shades there?

a10-0271534.speaker: Cernan
a10-0271534.text: How's that? Any better?

a10-0271534.speaker: McCandless
a10-0271534.text: Yes, indeed.

a10-0271534.speaker: Young
a10-0271534.text: We didn't get a chance to shave this morning before this show. I hope that doesn't bother anybody.

a10-0271534.speaker: McCandless
a10-0271534.text: No, it doesn't bother us. The definition is real good; we can just about read your wristwatch there, Gene.

a10-0271534.speaker: McCandless
a10-0271534.text: Roger. Looks like it says about 16:00. 16:05?

a10-0271534.speaker: Cernan
a10-0271534.text: 16:05 Cape time. 16:05 Cape time.

a10-0271534.speaker: McCandless
a10-0271534.text: Roger. We copy.

a10-0271534.speaker: Young
a10-0271534.text: Get it.

a10-0271534.speaker: McCandless
a10-0271534.text: Roger we synchronized our watches here.

a10-0271534.speaker: Young
a10-0271534.text: Beautiful. Beautiful.

a10-0271534.speaker: Stafford
a10-0271534.text: Looks like we have a good piece of gear here.

a10-0271534.speaker: McCandless
a10-0271534.text: Yes, it does.

a10-0271534.speaker: Young
a10-0271534.text: I'll give you a whizzer, give you a whizzer of TP over here.

a10-0271534.speaker: Cernan
a10-0271534.text: One of our problems is trying to figure out which way is up and which way is down.

a10-0271534.speaker: Stafford
a10-0271534.text: And it's beautiful one time you have your choice. If you don't like things right-side-up, you can go upside-down.

a10-0271534.speaker: McCandless
a10-0271534.text: Roger, down here. Okay. We've got one of you in each direction.

a10-0271534.speaker: Stafford
a10-0271534.text: It's really a ball up here living in zero g, believe me.

a10-0271534.speaker: Cernan
a10-0271534.text: It's the only way to fly.

a10-0271534.speaker: Stafford
a10-0271534.text: Once you get going, the cost for individual passenger mile becomes rather reasonable.

a10-0271534.speaker: McCandless
a10-0271534.text: Roger. We Copy.

a10-0271534.speaker: Cernan
a10-0271534.text: I notice, boy, it sure picks up the Sun's reflection and density no matter where you go. That little reflection is coming out of my window behind me.

a10-0271534.speaker: McCandless
a10-0271534.text: Roger. What f-stop are you all using now?

a10-0271534.speaker: Cernan
a10-0271534.text: We're on about f:28, I believe, here. Wait a minute. Yes, about 22 to 28.

a10-0271534.speaker: McCandless
a10-0271534.text: Houston. Roger. Out.

a10-0271534.speaker: Cernan
a10-0271534.text: Still good color?

a10-0271534.speaker: McCandless
a10-0271534.text: Yes, indeed.

a10-0271534.speaker: Cernan
a10-0271534.text: You might notice the dynamics here.

a10-0271534.speaker: Young
a10-0271534.text: I just do whatever he says.

a10-0271534.speaker: McCandless
a10-0271534.text: Say, Tom, the flight engineer wants you to be sure you log all your exercises.

a10-0271534.speaker: Stafford
a10-0271534.text: I got you.

a10-0271534.speaker: Cernan
a10-0271534.text: Like I said earlier, this isn't fanning the Peacock, but it's the best we've got.

a10-0271534.speaker: McCandless
a10-0271534.text: Boy, with dynamics like that, you guys ought to be pretty good at this PTC mode.

a10-0271534.speaker: Young
a10-0271534.text: I mean to tell you.

a10-0271534.speaker: Stafford
a10-0271534.text: Right. That's why we got about 10 hours sleep last night.

a10-0271534.speaker: McCandless
a10-0271534.text: Roger.

a10-0271534.speaker: Cernan
a10-0271534.text: That's perfect zero gravity there. boy, I'll tell you there's nothing like it.

a10-0272033.speaker: Cernan
a10-0272033.text: That's perfect zero gravity there. boy, I'll tell you there's nothing like it.

a10-0272033.speaker: McCandless
a10-0272033.text: 10, this is Houston. Is there...

a10-0272033.speaker: Stafford
a10-0272033.text: ...perfect balance.

a10-0272033.speaker: McCandless
a10-0272033.text: Roger. Are there any sort of air currents there affecting anything you can feel?

a10-0272033.speaker: Stafford
a10-0272033.text: Roger. It's blowing a little movement. But it's not out here much really.

a10-0272033.speaker: Cernan
a10-0272033.text: That's an effect we discovered a long time ago. If you watch it long enough, it'll go up.

a10-0272033.speaker: Young
a10-0272033.text: It's really hard to stabilise something so it won't move.

a10-0272033.speaker: McCandless
a10-0272033.text: Roger. I remember that from Gemini 10.

a10-0272033.speaker: Cernan
a10-0272033.text: We discovered a Cernan effect up here, but can't find which way is up.

a10-0272033.speaker: McCandless
a10-0272033.text: Yes, Gene. Could you move the camera around slightly? I've got a very bright spot coming in the window, I just want to make sure that you don't burn the target with the f:2 - f:28 f-stop.

a10-0272033.speaker: Cernan
a10-0272033.text: Yes. I'll try it here, Bruce, to got it away from some of that if I can.

a10-0272033.speaker: McCandless
a10-0272033.text: Roger.

a10-0272033.speaker: McCandless
a10-0272033.text: Oh, it's really looking good now, Beautiful color here.

a10-0272033.speaker: Stafford
a10-0272033.text: Now we got three objects going.

a10-0272033.speaker: McCandless
a10-0272033.text: This is a real testimonial to prove you were there, in case there were any doubters.

a10-0272033.speaker: Cernan
a10-0272033.text: If people want to know what kind of men go to the Moon, there's a good look at one right there. Could you believe it?

a10-0272033.speaker: Stafford
a10-0272033.text: Some people still don't.

a10-0272033.speaker: McCandless
