a10-0272033.text: I'm surprised you all have not set this to music.

a10-0272033.speaker: Cernan
a10-0272033.text: Oh, you want music, Well, we'll give you some music at the conclusion here.

a10-0272033.speaker: Stafford
a10-0272033.text: Okay. We'll take you back outside now.

a10-0272033.speaker: McCandless
a10-0272033.text: Roger.

a10-0272033.speaker: Cernan
a10-0272033.text: While Tom shows you that, we've got another little rendition we'd like to put your way.

a10-0272033.speaker: McCandless
a10-0272033.text: Roger. We're standing by.

a10-0272033.speaker: Cernan
a10-0272033.text: Here it comes. This - This is just so that you guys don't get too excited about the TV and forget what your job is down there.

a10-0272033.speaker: McCandless
a10-0272033.text: We're ready for what we're about to receive.

a10-0272033.speaker: Unidentified Crew member
a10-0272033.text: [Music being played.

a10-0272033.speaker: Cernan
a10-0272033.text: We don't need it all.

a10-0272033.speaker: Stafford
a10-0272033.text: Just wanted to send some thoughts back to you.

a10-0272033.speaker: McCandless
a10-0272033.text: Roger. Thank you for your thoughts, and with this view of the Earth, it looks like the United States - The landmass of the U.S. is showing up better now than it was few minutes ago.

a10-0272033.speaker: Stafford
a10-0272033.text: Right, Bruce. I can really see them. Looks like the New England states are kind of clobbered in there.

a10-0272530.speaker: Stafford
a10-0272530.text: Right, Bruce. I can really see them. Looks like the New England states are kind of clobbered in there.

a10-0272530.speaker: Stafford
a10-0272530.text: But the main part of it's coming in real good. And again you can see the great American desert, the Rocky Mountains, and the Sierra Nevadas there.

a10-0272530.speaker: McCandless
a10-0272530.text: Oh, it's just beautiful on the - the transients before it saturates there.

a10-0272530.speaker: Cernan
a10-0272530.text: Okay. I'll try to give you another one.

a10-0272530.speaker: McCandless
a10-0272530.text: All those little glimpses are good, but you've got to be fast to catch them,

a10-0272530.speaker: Stafford
a10-0272530.text: Is it - I'm trying to hold it as steady as I can. Is it looking okay?

a10-0272530.speaker: McCandless
a10-0272530.text: Yes. You're doing a good job on holding it.

a10-0272530.speaker: Stafford
a10-0272530.text: Houston, Apollo l0. On the monitor, it appears that I have a couple of little bumps and ragged edges. Is that coming through on the Black and white?

a10-0272530.speaker: McCandless
a10-0272530.text: Yes, it is. It's coming through on the black and white; and, of course, in the color that we've got here, it looks like it's in the horizontal sweep.

a10-0272530.speaker: Stafford
a10-0272530.text: Yes. I noticed it when we first turned it on; it didn't have that, then it slowly started to saturate.

a10-0272530.speaker: McCandless
a10-0272530.text: All right. We saw those little bumps yesterday also.

a10-0272530.speaker: Stafford
a10-0272530.text: Well, I think it was at the end of the transmission yesterday.

a10-0272530.speaker: Stafford
a10-0272530.text: Okay. We'll go ahead and terminate the TV pass here. I just wanted to play a little music for you so we have something up here when it gets lonely during the PTC mode.

a10-0272530.speaker: McCandless
a10-0272530.text: Roger, Apollo 10. We enjoyed the TV and the music.

a10-0272530.speaker: Cernan
a10-0272530.text: We'll be talking to you tomorrow.

a10-0470315.speaker: Cernan
a10-0470315.text: Interior-wise, we're giving them a look at the star chart which has got some colors of both the Earth, the Sun, and the Moon, and some of the planets: Saturn, Jupiter, Venus, Mars.

a10-0470315.speaker: Duke
a10-0470315.text: Roger. How about putting that pretty patch up there again?

a10-0470315.speaker: Cernan
a10-0470315.text: Okay. We'll do that.

a10-0470315.speaker: Stafford
a10-0470315.text: Tell them this is our star chart and how we identify the stars and the planets that we're looking at right now.

a10-0470315.speaker: Cernan
a10-0470315.text: This is what we use...

a10-0470315.speaker: Duke
a10-0470315.text: : 10 Houston...

a10-0470315.speaker: Cernan
a10-0470315.text: ...for our star navigation. The Earth is over here - Go ahead.

a10-0470315.speaker: Duke
a10-0470315.text: Roger. Our signal's down about...

a10-0470315.speaker: Cernan
a10-0470315.text: ...Go ahead, Houston. This is 10.

a10-0470315.speaker: Duke
a10-0470315.text: Roger, Gene-o. Our signal strength is down about 10 dB. We'd like you to go High Gain to Medium width and then back to Narrow. Over.

a10-0470315.speaker: Cernan
a10-0470315.text: Okay. It's Medium, and now I'll go back to Narrow

a10-0470315.speaker: Duke
a10-0470315.text: Roger.

a10-0470315.speaker: Cernan
a10-0470315.text: How's that.?

a10-0470315.speaker: Duke
a10-0470315.text: Stand by.

a10-0470315.speaker: Cernan
a10-0470315.text: Okay. The blue ball here, the big one, is the Earth as it progresses through the - through the heavens here while we're on this trip. The Moon is in yellow, and it also progresses through the heavens.

a10-0470315.speaker: Cernan
a10-0470315.text: Might bring out the famous Apollo 10 symbol patch.

a10-0470315.speaker: Duke
a10-0470315.text: Roger. We'd like to - Wish we were seeing this now, but Madrid is going to record it for us and then we'll see it later on. That was a beautiful astronomical description of the star chart there, Gene.

a10-0470315.speaker: Cernan
a10-0470315.text: I thought you could follow it a little bit closer there, Charlie, if I told you about that.

a10-0470315.speaker: Duke
a10-0470315.text: Roger. Takes me a little while to catch on to those things.

a10-0470315.speaker: Cernan
a10-0470315.text: Where better can you give an astronomical description than in the astronomical heavens?

a10-0470315.speaker: Duke
a10-0470315.text: [Laughter.]

a10-0470315.speaker: Cernan
a10-0470315.text: I think that's where we are.

a10-0470315.speaker: Young
a10-0470315.text: This PTC REFSMMAT really helps you with the orientation of the stars, both - even if you can't see them you can - you can have a feel for where they ought to be, which is - I think - is going to help us out.

a10-0470315.speaker: Duke
a10-0470315.text: Roger, 10. We're still having problems locking up, so we'd like to have you go to Wide Beam for 30 seconds and then back to Narrow. Over.

a10-0470315.speaker: Cernan
a10-0470315.text: Okay. We're in Wide Beam.

a10-0470315.speaker: Duke
a10-0470315.text: Roger. We'll probably lose the TV for a little while. We'd like you to keep going the next time around, and maybe we can get a better picture. Madrid is having a little bit of trouble.

a10-0470315.speaker: Cernan
a10-0470315.text: Charlie, you - You wouldn't believe this, but right now outside my window I've got something. I don't know how far. I assume it might be the S-IVB, just spinning around in reflected sunlight out there.

a10-0470315.speaker: Duke
a10-0470315.text: Roger. If we get our expert FIDO's on - on going and compute and see how far away the S-IVB should be right now from you.

a10-0470315.speaker: Cernan
a10-0470315.text: Well, I can see it with the naked eye, and then I put the monocular on it and I can see it spinning around. I wouldn't bet my life on it being the S-IVB, but it sure has - sure has got to be something like it.

a10-0470315.speaker: Duke
a10-0470315.text: Roger. We hope so. We could - We'd like you to go back to Narrow Beam width now, 10.

a10-0470949.speaker: Cernan
a10-0470949.text: Okay. We're all right now, though?

a10-0470949.speaker: Duke
a10-0470949.text: Roger. We're in good shape now. That was just for future reference.

a10-0470949.speaker: Cernan
a10-0470949.text: For all the folks at home, that should be a pretty good picture of the Stars and Stripes.

a10-0470949.speaker: Duke
a10-0470949.text: Roger. Wish we were seeing it.

a10-0470949.speaker: Duke
a10-0470949.text: 10, Houston. We are expecting High Gain loss in about 1 minute. Over.

a10-0470949.speaker: Cernan
a10-0470949.text: Okay. And here comes the Earth. Let me get it for you first.

a10-0470949.speaker: Stafford
a10-0470949.text: Okay. Now we've got it, Charlie.

a10-0470949.speaker: Duke
a10-0470949.text: Roger. We've got about - still about a minute...

a10-0470949.speaker: Stafford
a10-0470949.text: ...taking a good picture of the Earth right now.

a10-0470949.speaker: Cernan
a10-0470949.text: Okay, Charlie. That's maximum zoom. You should be seeing all of Africa - Matter of fact you should be looking right down at Madrid.

a10-0495451.speaker: Stafford
a10-0495451.text: Hello, Houston. Apollo 10. How do you read on VOX?

a10-0495451.speaker: Duke
a10-0495451.text: I read you five-by on VOX, 10.

a10-0495451.speaker: Stafford
a10-0495451.text: Okay. I'll kind of narrate this, Charlie. I'm kind of at an odd angle to hold it out the window. Again, you can see the west coast of Africa, the Sahara Desert, they're all in orange. You can see the Atlantic Ocean with swirls of clouds over to the eastern part of Brazil. You can see the very weird cloud patterns that Gene described out over the northeastern part of the United States. Again, it looks like the North Pole and that whole area around Canada is completely socked in.

a10-0495451.speaker: Stafford
a10-0495451.text: Again, the one thing that is really so amazing, as you look at the Earth, is the amount of cloud cover that we have down there. Over the tropical rain forest of South America, there's just numerous small cumulus clouds.

a10-0495451.speaker: Duke
a10-0495451.text: Roger. Can you describe the color as contrasted to say, the Andes or the American Desert?

a10-0495451.speaker: Stafford
a10-0495451.text: Roger. The color of the tropical rain forest there is more of a greenish brown. It's a greenish brown versus a brown-orange on the tropical - on the American Desert and the Sahara Desert.

a10-0495451.speaker: Duke
a10-0495451.text: Roger. Can you pick out the Amazons?

a10-0495451.speaker: Duke
a10-0495451.text: Roger. Can you pick out the Amazon River?

a10-0495451.speaker: Stafford
a10-0495451.text: Negative. No. I can't pick out the Amazon. I am looking at it with my naked eye where Gene had the 28-power monocular. I do have the zoom on here, so you are seeing it a little bit bigger than we are on the standard vision, so the Earth as you see it there is bigger. And you can see the terminator, or nighttime, has moved over most of Africa at this time, and is starting to move over to Europe. It'll soon be nighttime in Spain, and also, it is getting daylight over in Hawaii, there. The cloud patterns are utterly fantastic as you look out at it.

a10-0495451.speaker: Duke
a10-0495451.text: Roger, 10. We copy. How about up around the clouds that I asked you about earlier up around the Bering Strait? Is it daylight over there yet?

a10-0495451.speaker: Stafford
a10-0495451.text: They are just starting to come into view and when we have our programmed TV pass, - that's through Goldstone, we should be able to take a look at that cloud frontal situation. It was a beautiful swirl yesterday.

a10-0533536.speaker: Duke
a10-0533536.text: Okay.

a10-0533536.speaker: Cernan
a10-0533536.text: Let us know when you get color.

a10-0533536.speaker: Duke
a10-0533536.text: Okay. We are seeing your patch now in black and white. Be just a few more seconds.

a10-0533536.speaker: Mission Control
a10-0533536.text: Color coming now.

a10-0533536.speaker: Duke
a10-0533536.text: Okay. We just got the color, 10, on the vidicon here and it is looking real good, maybe a little bit focus; but the colors are good and it is a nice, simple little patch we see.

a10-0533536.speaker: Cernan
a10-0533536.text: This is the peacock of Apollo 10.

a10-0533536.speaker: Duke
a10-0533536.text: Roger.

a10-0533536.speaker: Cernan
a10-0533536.text: And we'd like to say hello from the five of us, if we may.

a10-0533536.speaker: Duke
a10-0533536.text: Roger. [Long pause.]

a10-0533536.speaker: Duke
a10-0533536.text: Okay. You want me to be a straight man on that question and ask it?

a10-0533536.speaker: Cernan
a10-0533536.text: Stand by one.

a10-0533536.speaker: Duke
a10-0533536.text: Okay.

a10-0533536.speaker: Cernan
a10-0533536.text: Negative. Stand by one. Got a little technical difficulties here. [Long pause.]

a10-0533536.speaker: Duke
a10-0533536.text: We are still getting the color, 10.

a10-0533536.speaker: Cernan
a10-0533536.text: Okay, 10. Here's the hello.

a10-0533536.speaker: Duke
a10-0533536.text: Okay. Go ahead.

a10-0533536.speaker: Cernan
a10-0533536.text: Here's hello from the five of us from on Apollo 10. Here's Tom Stafford.

a10-0533536.speaker: Duke
a10-0533536.text: He's a beautiful Tom Stafford there. He's in living color.

a10-0533536.speaker: Cernan
a10-0533536.text: John Young. [Pause.]

a10-0533536.speaker: Duke
a10-0533536.text: We've got John. He's a little dark down there now, with his lights not on him, but we can tell it's John with his chin strap loose.

a10-0533536.speaker: Cernan
a10-0533536.text: And yours truly, Gene Cernan.

a10-0533536.speaker: Duke
a10-0533536.text: Roger. We got you, Gene. The sun is up pretty bright.

a10-0533536.speaker: Cernan
a10-0533536.text: Are you still with us?

a10-0533536.speaker: Duke
a10-0533536.text: Yes sir. The Sun is pretty bright coming back out - Now you are coming in better. We see you slipping down in the LEB.

a10-0533536.speaker: Cernan
a10-0533536.text: Okay. That's the three of us. Here's the other two on Apollo 10, your friendly Charlie Brown and our ever loving companion, Snoopy.

a10-0533536.speaker: Duke
a10-0533536.text: Roger. We got it coming in now. Okay. Color on Charlie Brown and Snoopy is a little dark. If you could get a little bit more light on them, it would be fine, but we can recognize the characters. They look pretty happy up there.

a10-0533536.speaker: Cernan
a10-0533536.text: How's that?

a10-0533536.speaker: Duke
a10-0533536.text: That's fine. It looks a little dark on the color. Could you stop it open a little bit more? Wait a minute. Okay. That's fine now. There you go. The red and the background on the cards are coming in fine. We are washing out a little bit on the white of Charlie Brown's coat and Snoop's face.

a10-0533536.speaker: Cernan
a10-0533536.text: Okay. Now, you know that there are five of us up here. We'd like to take you outside and show you what the five of us are looking at.

a10-0533536.speaker: Duke
a10-0533536.text: Roger. [Long pause.]

a10-0533536.speaker: Duke
a10-0533536.text: Okay. [Long pause.]

a10-0533536.speaker: Duke
a10-0533536.text: We got the big Earth in color and it looks like about a half-Earth to us. It's a beautiful blue. We see the tremendous cloud coverage that you were talking about throughout the day, 10.

a10-0533536.speaker: Cernan
a10-0533536.text: Okay, Charlie. you are looking at the world rightsideup, as we know it. The Gulf of Mexico - Mexico goes down and to the right of the picture toward the terminator, South America is in the lower right, and corner of the picture on the terminator. You can look up right smack in the center of the whole picture. You can make out Mexico, is Houston, right on the Gulf, and then North America goes up to about the 11 o'clock position on your picture.

a10-0534012.speaker: Cernan
a10-0534012.text: Okay, Charlie. you are looking at the world rightsideup, as we know it. The Gulf of Mexico - Mexico goes down and to the right of the picture toward the terminator, South America is in the lower right, and corner of the picture on the terminator. You can look up right smack in the center of the whole picture. You can make out Mexico, is Houston, right on the Gulf, and then North America goes up to about the 11 o'clock position on your picture.

a10-0534012.speaker: Duke
a10-0534012.text: Roger. We copy. We see primarily just the blues of the ocean and the whites of the clouds. We have a - the cloud patterns are pretty evident. Agree quite - real closely with the weather map I have. It is pretty difficult to pick out the landmasses, though, I must admit. We see one brownish area which appears to be in the American desert, about the center of the globe right now.

a10-0534012.speaker: Stafford
a10-0534012.text: Yes, Charlie. That's Mexico and the southwestern United States, right there; and Baja California is on the left of that, and the right-hand edge happens to be the Gulf of Mexico. If you can follow it all up, you will follow it right to Houston and thence New Orleans.

a10-0534012.speaker: Stafford
a10-0534012.text: It's awfully hard to ascertain the difference - Okay, Charlie. It's hard to ascertain between the water down there in the Gulf and the landmass, because the whole eastern coast of the United States looks a greenish brown versus water.

a10-0534012.speaker: Duke
a10-0534012.text: Roger. That helps us out here to locate ourselves, at least for me, 10; and I think I see where you are talking about now. We have one section of clouds that looks like it is almost a circular area - a clear area and then clouds appear to come out of South and Central America - swing out into the Pacific and in the center of that it looks like the clear area which I am saying is the southern part of the United States, from Mexico along the Gulf Coast. Is that correct?

a10-0534012.speaker: Cernan
a10-0534012.text: That's it, Charlie. The Gulf of Mexico is right smack in the center up and down of the world. If you follow the terminator down and went halfway and then went about halfway from there toward the rounder part of the Earth, you will find the Gulf of Mexico on that brown area you are looking at, between Mexico and the southeastern United States. That's Houston right smack in the center of that clear area.

a10-0534012.speaker: Cernan
a10-0534012.text: That clear area goes from Central America right on up into the states.

a10-0534012.speaker: Duke
a10-0534012.text: Roger. We copy. It appears that the landmasses are washing out just about as much as the clouds. Could you open it up a couple of stops and then stop it down fast so we can get a little bit - a second or two of sharper definition?

a10-0534012.speaker: Cernan
a10-0534012.text: Okay. Let us know when it is a little better.

a10-0534012.speaker: Duke
a10-0534012.text: Okay. It was a little - there you go. If you can hold that, but I think - That's good right there. It is a lot better, 10.

a10-0534012.speaker: Stafford
a10-0534012.text: Charlie, we are full zoom on you and it's even hard for us to make out things with the naked eye unless we know where they are. So, I imagine it is going to be difficult for you.

a10-0534012.speaker: Stafford
a10-0534012.text: Okay, Charlie. The total globe that you see there is bigger than what we actually see, since we have the zoom lens on and it is probably about one and one-quarter times as big as we see it.

a10-0534012.speaker: Duke
a10-0534012.text: Copy, 10. As I said earlier, we are primarily getting the globe on a black background, and we see the white of the clouds and the blues of the sea with an occasional glimpse of what I make out as landmasses in the brownish. But, it is really difficult for an untrained eye to pick out the exact landmasses. We are sitting here with the in-pad book that - We got it to show the various sizes and with this diagram, it is a big help.

a10-0534012.speaker: Young
a10-0534012.text: What you are saying, Charlie, is that we are too far away to give you a good picture.

a10-0534012.speaker: Duke
a10-0534012.text: Boy, you sure are a long way away.

a10-0534540.speaker: Cernan
a10-0534540.text: Okay. If you follow up - but you might think it is the Gulf of Mexico there - and then go straight north you see a little bit of V in the clouds and there's one going off to the right and a little thin sliver going to the right is the one I've been mentioning all day that goes from Indiana on through the northeast part of the country; and then that bigger blob that forms the left-hand side of the V is over the north, central United States and then right smack in center of the V is Lake Superior and Lake Michigan.

a10-0534540.speaker: Duke
a10-0534540.text: Roger. That is a good description, 10. It clears it up for me, anyway. I can see what you are talking about, now.

a10-0534540.speaker: Cernan
a10-0534540.text: And then way up on the upper left-hand, maybe about 10 o'clock on the globe, you will see a funny cloud pattern that sort of looks like a sea serpent of some sort with his beak pointing to the right. That that cloud pattern that Tom was referring to up in the Alaska area.

a10-0534540.speaker: Duke
a10-0534540.text: Roger. That's nearly apparent to us. When you stop it down, we can see that pattern. Some of the time, though, it's washed out due to the tremendous cloud coverage in that area.

a10-0534540.speaker: Cernan
a10-0534540.text: There it is, Charlie. That ought to be good.

a10-0534540.speaker: Duke
a10-0534540.text: Okay. It just came in on the black and white. We'll see it in just a second. Okay, now we see what you're talking about. Looks like an inverted view, almost.

a10-0534540.speaker: Cernan
a10-0534540.text: Now you ought to be - Right, now you ought to be able to see that V-area I was talking about better, too.

a10-0534540.speaker: Duke
a10-0534540.text: Roger. It's coming in a lot better, Gene.

a10-0534540.speaker: Stafford
a10-0534540.text: Okay. If you got a pretty good view of the outside, we'll take you back inside for one last quick minute.

a10-0534540.speaker: Duke
a10-0534540.text: Thanks a lot, 10, for that view. It's real good. We'll be standing by for the water-bag trick.

a10-0534540.speaker: Stafford
a10-0534540.text: Okay. We'll take you back inside here, now.

a10-0534540.speaker: Stafford
a10-0534540.text: I'll take care of it. [Long pause.]

a10-0534540.speaker: Stafford
a10-0534540.text: Question for today: who is that?

a10-0534540.speaker: Duke
a10-0534540.text: It looks like John Young with four sets of eyes, there. Two sets of eyes.

a10-0534540.speaker: Stafford
a10-0534540.text: There you go.

a10-0534540.speaker: Duke
a10-0534540.text: Let's ball it four eyes.

a10-0534540.speaker: Duke
a10-0534540.text: Looks like a World War I aviator.

a10-0534540.speaker: Young
a10-0534540.text: That's what happens when you look through the telescope to see the Sun. [Long pause.]

a10-0534540.speaker: Young
a10-0534540.text: Okay. It may sound like we've been loafing for the past couple of days, but we haven't. We've been real busy, and every spare minute we get we study our Flight Plan. So you see that pretty soon we're going to be going into orbit, and we have a completely different set of operations to go into that shows our pitch profile all around the Moon, for the first revolution. Tomorrow's a big day, and we're very much looking for it. Even though we're about 180,000 miles [333,000 km] away from the Earth here, you never get away from studying.

a10-0534540.speaker: Duke
a10-0534540.text: That's a great picture, 10. We can see the various spacecraft attitudes with the dark side of the Moon and the bright side. And we see the LM and the Command Module linked together and going into a LOI-1 burn attitude. It's real clear. You can almost read the writing on the pages.

a10-0534540.speaker: Young
a10-0534540.text: Roger. Don't adjust your set. It's in black and white.

a10-0534540.speaker: Duke
a10-0534540.text: Roger. [Long pause.]

a10-0534540.speaker: Duke
a10-0534540.text: We can read on the...

a10-0534540.speaker: Cernan
a10-0534540.text: If you want to know where we're going - We'll show you a little bit of a chart of where we're going. Day after tomorrow, we ought to be seeing this in living Moon color. Right now, it's in the best black and white we've got. This is the area around Landing Site 2.

a10-0535026.speaker: Cernan
a10-0535026.text: If you want to know where we're going - We'll show you a little bit of a chart of where we're going. Day after tomorrow, we ought to be seeing this in living Moon color. Right now, it's in the best black and white we've got. This is the area around Landing Site 2.

a10-0535026.speaker: Duke
a10-0535026.text: Roger. Could you open it up a little bit, 10? We think maybe if you get a little bit wider f-stop, it'll help us out. Your pictures are a little bit dark.

a10-0535026.speaker: Duke
a10-0535026.text: That's a lot better, 10.

a10-0535026.speaker: Stafford
a10-0535026.text: I can't see the f-stop, yet.

a10-0535026.speaker: Duke
a10-0535026.text: Okay, 10. When Gene moved back, it helped out a lot. If you'll just pull the chart back - that's good now. We can - It's coming in a lot better. Gene, could you...

a10-0535026.speaker: Cernan
a10-0535026.text: The moral of the story is, John - The moral of the story is, John just said, "You know you can study all your life and you never finish studying," and here we are almost a quarter of a million miles away, and we're still studying. Like Tom said, he's got two girls taking final exams this week, and this is his way of saying, "Get to work."

a10-0535026.speaker: Duke
a10-0535026.text: Roger.

a10-0535026.speaker: Stafford
a10-0535026.text: Yes, and if those girls are listening, they had better be studying tonight.

a10-0535026.speaker: Duke
a10-0535026.text: Okay. I'm sure they're listening. Would - Gene, how about pointing to a Landing Site 2 on the map for the folks?

a10-0535026.speaker: Cernan
a10-0535026.text: Okay. Landing Site 2, I'll show you here in just a second. We'll be coming up from the bottom and I'll stop my finger up on Landing Site 2.

a10-0535026.speaker: Cernan
a10-0535026.text: That's the area we hope to bring back some good pictures of in a couple of days.

a10-0535026.speaker: Duke
a10-0535026.text: Roger.

a10-0535026.speaker: Cernan
a10-0535026.text: We'll eventually - That's the area where we'll eventually be actually landing on the surface of the Moon. This area is probably just about visible from - in the lighted - with the terminator of the Moon lighted, I mean, from the Earth at this time. just about.

a10-0535026.speaker: Duke
a10-0535026.text: Roger. We copy.

a10-0535026.speaker: Young
a10-0535026.text: That's one advantage we have. If you don't like to turn your pages, you can always turn yourself instead.

a10-0535026.speaker: Duke
a10-0535026.text: Commander, you're in rare form today.

a10-0535026.speaker: Cernan
a10-0535026.text: We figure that, you know, there's always a way of making pigs run downhill and maybe even knowledge will make it run that way.

a10-0535026.speaker: Stafford
a10-0535026.text: Well, I guess that's the message to the kiddies in the country. If they can't get their homework right-side-up, go upside-down. They might be able to absorb more that way.

a10-0535026.speaker: Duke
a10-0535026.text: Roger. [Long pause.]

a10-0535026.speaker: Duke
a10-0535026.text: Looks like John's trying to hog the picture there, Gene. Why don't you - there you go, you pushed him out of the - you got - You got center stage now.

a10-0535026.speaker: Duke
a10-0535026.text: What a ham.

a10-0535026.speaker: Cernan
a10-0535026.text: You want to see me push; watch what happens. [Long pause.]

a10-0535026.speaker: Stafford
a10-0535026.text: That's called one-finger power.

a10-0535026.speaker: Duke
a10-0535026.text: Roger. [Pause.]

a10-0535026.speaker: Stafford
a10-0535026.text: Okay, this is Apollo 10 signing off. We'll give you one more picture of the Earth here, and call it a day. Oh, hold it. We want to show you the bag, too.

a10-0535026.speaker: Duke
a10-0535026.text: Roger. We'd appreciate that. [Long pause.]

a10-0535026.speaker: Young
a10-0535026.text: The bag is full of - half, full of bubbly water.

a10-0535026.speaker: Cernan
a10-0535026.text: And for those of you who are unfamiliar, there's the valve where the air -and then the water comes out, and here's the handle. And notice, they're both on the same side. Are you ready?

a10-0535544.speaker: Cernan
a10-0535544.text: I'll show you the bubbles, after I stop.

a10-0535544.speaker: Young
a10-0535544.text: Okay. It was full of the [garble] thousands of minute little bubbles. You wouldn't pick them up. You can barely see them with the naked eye, but they're there.

a10-0535544.speaker: Duke
a10-0535544.text: l0, try spinning a little bit harder, and maybe that'll put the bubbles to the top.

a10-0535544.speaker: Cernan
a10-0535544.text: Man, I spinned it so hard a little while ago, I was going in the other direction (laughter).

a10-0535544.speaker: Duke
a10-0535544.text: Roger. Gene. Hold it up next to the LEB DSKY. We couldn't see any bubble there. If you got one together. [Pause.]

a10-0535544.speaker: Duke
a10-0535544.text: Hey, that's a good spin; you're really spinning it now.

a10-0535544.speaker: Cernan
a10-0535544.text: Okay. How's that for a bubble now?

a10-0535544.speaker: Duke
a10-0535544.text: Okay. We got it. [Pause.]

a10-0535544.speaker: Duke
a10-0535544.text: Okay. We see that bubble. Really a big one.

a10-0535544.speaker: Young
a10-0535544.text: And it's in the bottom.

a10-0535544.speaker: Cernan
a10-0535544.text: Charlie, about the only thing we get by spinning them is making the little bubbles into a big one and then it stays in the bottom.

a10-0535544.speaker: Duke
a10-0535544.text: Roger. Is there any water left in the top of the bag, 10?

a10-0535544.speaker: Cernan
a10-0535544.text: No, there's no water in the top of the bag. All the water's out. We have tried it with semi-filled bags, with full bags, with half-full bags. What we really have been able to do, I think, is to get the bubble concentrated and then suck the water out from around it.

a10-0535544.speaker: Duke
a10-0535544.text: Roger. Have you tried it filling up - filling the bag - both top and the bottom of the bag and then spinning it?

a10-0535544.speaker: Cernan
a10-0535544.text: Yes. We tried that, too.

a10-0535544.speaker: Duke
a10-0535544.text: Well, it doesn't look like it works then, does it? [Long pause.]

a10-0535544.speaker: Stafford
a10-0535544.text: Charlie, you can see the bubble real good, can't you?

a10-0535544.speaker: Duke
a10-0535544.text: Roger. We have it, Tom. It's quite evident here to us. We'll have the experts look at this and maybe they can come up with something for later on this evening for you.

a10-0535544.speaker: Cernan
a10-0535544.text: Hey, Charlie, it is true, though, that water goes to the bottom of the bag.

a10-0535544.speaker: Duke
a10-0535544.text: Roger.

a10-0535544.speaker: Cernan
a10-0535544.text: And that phenomenon we have proved.

a10-0535544.speaker: Stafford
a10-0535544.text: Also, when the air gets down there, we can stop spinning; the big bubble is at the bottom.

a10-0535544.speaker: Duke
a10-0535544.text: Roger. We copy.

a10-0535544.speaker: Stafford
a10-0535544.text: Okay. This is Apollo 10. We'll take you outside for one last look at the Earth and sign off.

a10-0535544.speaker: Duke
a10-0535544.text: Roger. Thank you very much. [Long pause.]

a10-0535544.speaker: Duke
a10-0535544.text: Okay, 10. We just got the exterior view, and we got the Earth in the center of the screen, and it's a little bit different orientation this time. We see the North Pole up in the northeast about the 2 o'clock position on our screen now.

a10-0535544.speaker: Cernan
a10-0535544.text: And he'll rotate the camera over a little bit. He was just tilting it for ease of handling here. He's rotated it back now, Charlie.

a10-0535544.speaker: Duke
a10-0535544.text: Roger. [Long pause.]

a10-0535544.speaker: Cernan
a10-0535544.text: And from the five of us on Apollo 10: Tom Stafford, John Young, Eugene Cernan, Charlie Brown and Snoopy; we hope you've enjoyed it today.

a10-0535544.speaker: Duke
a10-0535544.text: Thank you much, 10. We appreciated the show; it was very nice. We'll see you tomorrow.

a10-0535544.speaker: Stafford
a10-0535544.text: Okay. And tomorrow we should be around the Moon.

a10-0535544.speaker: Duke
a10-0535544.text: Roger.

a10-0535544.speaker: Stafford
a10-0535544.text: Okay.

a10-0723735.speaker: Duke
a10-0723735.text: Okay. Apollo 10, Houston. We're getting it in black and white now. Stand by for the color. [Long pause.]

a10-0723735.speaker: Duke
a10-0723735.text: We've got the color now, Apollo 10. We have the Earth, and the center of the section. It seems to have a bluish tinge to the background. We see a very bright blue - a pale blue I should say, in the center of the Earth right near the terminator. Could you describe that for us? Over.

a10-0723735.speaker: Stafford
a10-0723735.text: Right. You can see the South Atlantic Ocean there and the orange spot to the right is the North African continent. You can see basically the Sahara Desert and, above that, the Mediterranean Sea. The rest of the world is pretty much encased in clouds. The solid cloud cover that's covered the North Pole, and most of Europe, is still with us today. At this time, as we look at the Earth, we are 210,000 miles [389,000 km] away. We've only got about 9,000 miles [16,700 km] to go to the Moon and we're traveling approximately 2,500 miles an hour [4,600 kph] relative to the Earth. Also, in about 15 min

a10-0723735.speaker: Stafford
a10-0723735.text: ...And again, South Africa - Go ahead, Charlie.

a10-0723735.speaker: Duke
a10-0723735.text: Roger. I was just going to add that we can see the northern part of Africa. We had a bluish tint to it at first but now it's coming in to a sort of orangish brown and we can see the South Atlantic and the cloud covers very well. The colors are very good. Over.

a10-0723735.speaker: Stafford
a10-0723735.text: Roger. Again, the Sahara Desert, the Atlas Mountains, Morocco, Libya we can see from here. It is an orange brownish orange. The night time - the terminator has cut across the Suez Canal and most of Egypt and is now covering most of South Africa. I can see Spain. It is a greenish brown and is completely contrasted with respect to North Africa. However, you may have difficulty seeing it on your set due to resolution at this distance. Again, you can see Brazil, but it is covered mostly with clouds at this time.

a10-0723735.speaker: Duke
a10-0723735.text: Roger 10. We haven't - We can see...

a10-0723735.speaker: Stafford
a10-0723735.text: Roger. This - Roger. At this time Apollo 10 is going through the preparation for the Lunar Orbit Insertion burn, and the next - After we lose contact with the Earth, the next time that we come around, we will - To have contact with the Earth, we'll be at approximately a 60- by 170-mile [111- by 315-km] orbit around the Moon. Right now, we cannot see the Moon, even though it is rapidly accelerating us towards itself by its mass. Over.

a10-0723735.speaker: Duke
a10-0723735.text: Roger, Tom. We copied. A very good description. We have difficulty seeing any landmass in our picture except for North Africa, and we can see the terminator cutting across Africa. Europe - The landmasses of Europe, are - just sort of fade into a bluish color. It looks like an ocean to us. Over.

a10-0723735.speaker: Stafford
a10-0723735.text: Right. Really, the only major landmass we can see is exactly what you can see on your set there. And that is the North African continent. Most of Europe is covered either by high clouds or some scattered low clouds and it's very difficult for us to see it, too. We'll give you a quick shot on the interior now, and then we'll terminate this pass. We'll go inside now.

a10-0723735.speaker: Duke
a10-0723735.text: Roger. Very good. Thank you very much for the view. We'll be standing by for the inside.

a10-0724312.speaker: Duke
a10-0724312.text: 10, we have the color now. The resolution on the 85 is, I think, better than most expected here. The Sun is pretty bright in the background, coming in through the - I guess that's the hatch window. No; side window, I guess it is. The patch is visible but it's pretty dark, due to the background being so bright. [Long pause.]

a10-0724312.speaker: Duke
a10-0724312.text: Roger. Thought we had lost voice there for a moment. You're coming in five-by, now. We've got your arm patch now. That's very dim at this setting. We had Gene's smiling face there for a minute, along with your patch. The flag is coming in a little bit better now. However, it's still pretty dark due, to the bright background. That's a lot better, there, 10. Over. [Long pause.]

a10-0724312.speaker: Duke
a10-0724312.text: There. We have a good view now. Now we can see Gene again. [Long pause.]

a10-0724312.speaker: Duke
a10-0724312.text: We see you waving, Gene. Barbara is in the viewing room. She says "Hi."

a10-0724312.speaker: Young
a10-0724312.text: A little difficult to get the proper lighting up here, Charlie. Spots flood it out, and we've got to deflect the light.

a10-0724312.speaker: Duke
a10-0724312.text: Roger. We see you trying hard on the thing. It looks like the ALC [Automatic Light Compensation] is averaging out, and the background looks real good - the spacecraft, back along the hatch. Tom's hand covering his window is real clear; his face is dark, though. Over.

a10-0724312.speaker: Duke
a10-0724312.text: I see. Thank you very much, John. That wasn't quite...

a10-0724312.speaker: Stafford
a10-0724312.text: That's known as a 72-hour shadow, Charlie.

a10-0724312.speaker: Duke
a10-0724312.text: Apollo 10, Houston. We now have the 210 at Goldstone. The granularity and the resolution is a heck of a lot better here. You're coming in real great. Over.

a10-0724312.speaker: Cernan
a10-0724312.text: There's our overhead hatch window there. [Pause.]

a10-0724312.speaker: Duke
a10-0724312.text: 10, Houston. We see some specks on your hatch window. Could you comment on those? [Pause.]

a10-0724312.speaker: Stafford
a10-0724312.text: Yes. They come from the dumps that we're making overboard as we progress along. I don't think any of it is due to the thruster firing, Charlie.

a10-0724312.speaker: Cernan
a10-0724312.text: Houston, the hatch window is phenomenally clear. There is what appear to be a few dump particles on the outside, maybe a couple of smear prints on the inside. The right-hand window has got a little bit of a smear on the outside; not necessarily particles, but just a general smear. The left-side window has got some definite particles lashed across it.

a10-0724753.speaker: Cernan
a10-0724753.text: Houston, the hatch window is phenomenally clear. There is what appear to be a few dump particles on the outside, maybe a couple of smear prints on the inside. The right-hand window has got a little bit of a smear on the outside; not necessarily particles, but just a general smear. The left-side window has got some definite particles lashed across it.

a10-0724753.speaker: Young
a10-0724753.text: We're not very good at this camera work, but we will probably improve with practice.

a10-0724753.speaker: Stafford
a10-0724753.text: We will show you the navigator down in the LEB.

a10-0724753.speaker: Duke
a10-0724753.text: Roger, 10. We have no complaints at all. That's a pretty good show.

a10-0724753.speaker: Stafford
a10-0724753.text: He's the star of the cast because he gets all the good light down there.

a10-0724753.speaker: Duke
a10-0724753.text: Roger. There's old John's friendly face.

a10-0724753.speaker: Duke
a10-0724753.text: (Laughter.) [Pause.]

a10-0724753.speaker: Cernan
a10-0724753.text: John's pointing right now at the sextant and the telescope, which are our navigation means to get home. And, hopefully, to do part of the rendezvous.

a10-0724753.speaker: Cernan
a10-0724753.text: Yes. This is the best-working part of the whole machine. It's really working beautifully, now.

a10-0724753.speaker: Duke
a10-0724753.text: Got a good operator. [Pause.]

a10-0724753.speaker: Duke
a10-0724753.text: 10, Houston. Show us the piece of tape that you have around the eyepiece.

a10-0724753.speaker: Cernan
a10-0724753.text: One on the bottom of the sextant and on the righthand side of the telescope.

a10-0724753.speaker: Duke
a10-0724753.text: Roger. Thank, you much, 10. We see it. [Long pause.]

a10-0724753.speaker: Cernan
a10-0724753.text: You know, once you lose that thing in here and you have to look for it for about 20 minutes, you find a way not to lose it again.

a10-0724753.speaker: Young
a10-0724753.text: Well, it wasn't quite 20 minutes but it sure was a scramble going for it, I'll tell you that.

a10-0724753.speaker: Duke
a10-0724753.text: Roger. We copy. We have you entering the lunar penumbra at this time. Do you notice the Sun setting at all? Over.

a10-0724753.speaker: Young
a10-0724753.text: Can't see the Sun right now, Charlie.

a10-0724753.speaker: Duke
a10-0724753.text: Roger.

a10-0724753.speaker: Young
a10-0724753.text: We're not in the right attitude to see it.

a10-0724753.speaker: Stafford
a10-0724753.text: In this attitude, to look at the Earth and everything, we can't get a picture of the Sun that we can see. If there is any solar corona, we will give it a quick shot.

a10-0724753.speaker: Duke
a10-0724753.text: Roger. Jack is estimating you will have about 30 seconds only. Over.

a10-0724753.speaker: Cernan
a10-0724753.text: Okay, Charlie. It appears that the Sun's reflection on Snoopy, here, is getting a little bit dimmer. So we very well could be where you [think] we are. I hope we are.

a10-0724753.speaker: Duke
a10-0724753.text: Your friendly FIDO's will bet on it.

a10-0724753.speaker: Stafford
a10-0724753.text: [Garble] some navigating here.

a10-0724753.speaker: Young
a10-0724753.text: Yes. I guess we are too, aren't we?

a10-0724753.speaker: Duke
a10-0724753.text: Roger. [Pause.]

a10-0724753.speaker: Cernan
a10-0724753.text: I never doubted them, anyway. I just - Like I said yesterday, I'll wait until I see that 60 nautical miles [111 km].

a10-0724753.speaker: Duke
a10-0724753.text: 10, Houston. Does it look any different upside-down there?

a10-0724753.speaker: Young
a10-0724753.text: The stars are 180 out of the position they were before.

a10-0724753.speaker: Cernan
a10-0724753.text: That's one thing about this environment. If you don't like it, just turn it upside-down.

a10-0724753.speaker: Duke
a10-0724753.text: Roger, 10.

a10-0724753.speaker: Stafford
a10-0724753.text: Okay, Charlie. We will terminate this pass with one quick look outside to see how the 210-foot dish looks at the Earth from outside. Okay?

a10-0724753.speaker: Duke
a10-0724753.text: Roger, 10. We are standing by. Over. [Long pause.]

a10-0725317.speaker: Cernan
a10-0725317.text: Charlie? It's definitely getting a little darker outside.

a10-0725317.speaker: Stafford
a10-0725317.text: Looks like we're right on trajectory, then. Okay. Here's another look at the Earth through the 210-foot dish at Goldstone, and I hope the colors are coming through a little better. Again, the west coast of North Africa is still a bright orange, and the central part of North Africa is starting to turn purple as night-time approaches over the western part of Libya and the eastern part of Tunisia. Again, it's awful hard to see Spain because Spain is a greenish brown this morning. You have the Mediterranean and the Atlantic covered with some clouds, so it's awful hard to see any part of Spain. But

a10-0725317.speaker: Duke
a10-0725317.text: Thank you much for a good show, 10. Appreciate it. The 210-foot dish is giving us a very good resolution and the colors are a lot sharper. Over. [Pause.]

a10-0725317.speaker: Cernan
a10-0725317.text: Okay, Charlie. We are definitely in darkness, right at this moment. It just went pitch dark outside.

a10-0725317.speaker: Cernan
a10-0725317.text: Boy, that - That's really something, after having the Sun out of one window all the time. We are in total darkness. [Long pause.]

a10_08_moonviews.speaker: Duke
a10_08_moonviews.text: Roger. We're committed, 10. It looks that good.

a10_08_moonviews.speaker: Mission Control
a10_08_moonviews.text: That's John Young that's convinced there.

a10_08_moonviews.speaker: Young
a10_08_moonviews.text: We have our student geologists here overlooking the surface, and they'll report in a minute.

a10_08_moonviews.speaker: Stafford
a10_08_moonviews.text: Okay. We're just passing from the highlands over into the Mare area, and you can pass on to Jack we caught a couple of real pretty little volcanoes, there's no doubt about them, and we got a couple of good high-resolution photos, and it still looks kind of brownish-gray to us here. Over.

a10_08_moonviews.speaker: Young
a10_08_moonviews.text: Yes. There were some places back there where... There was one volcano, whatever it was, that - It was all white on the outside but definitely black around the top of it.

a10_08_moonviews.speaker: Cernan
a10_08_moonviews.text: Charlie, it might sound corny, but the view is really out of this world.

a10o_0995600.speaker: Stafford (in Snoopy)
a10o_0995600.text: Beautiful. It throttled up to 20 per cent. Thrust chamber pressure went down to 20 per cent, but the throttle profile looked good.

a10o_0995600.speaker: Cernan (onboard Snoopy)
a10o_0995600.text: I've go got some updates on there, I've got to copy down, Tom.

a10o_0995600.speaker: Cernan (onboard Snoopy)
a10o_0995600.text: The first one is - What does it say on there?

a10o_0995600.speaker: Young
a10o_0995600.text: I show you in a 61.2 by 9.22 [nautical miles, 113.3 x 17.1 km].

a10o_0995600.speaker: Cernan (onboard Snoopy)
a10o_0995600.text: I've got to copy this thing right here. 100 degrees East at 33:31.

a10o_0995600.speaker: Young
a10o_0995600.text: [Garble] are you guys [garble] down in there?

a10o_0995600.speaker: Stafford (onboard Snoopy)
a10o_0995600.text: I can tell, José. We're just going to be hot to get clearance around the other side for a final approach, but we're coming down, baby.

a10o_0995600.speaker: Cernan (onboard Snoopy)
a10o_0995600.text: These are 10-minute hacks? Or 90 minute - They've got to be 10 minute hacks, not 10 second hacks.

a10o_0995600.speaker: Stafford (onboard Snoopy)
a10o_0995600.text: Tell you what let's do. Let's go ahead and load the phasing burn in unless we have an update for it. He hasn't given us an update has he?

a10o_0995600.speaker: Cernan (onboard Snoopy)
a10o_0995600.text: No, call up 30 and let's load it in.

a10o_0995600.speaker: Stafford (onboard Snoopy)
a10o_0995600.text: OK. So what's the time of it? I'll take it, Gene-o.

a10o_0995600.speaker: Cernan (onboard Snoopy)
a10o_0995600.text: You got it right here, babe?

a10o_0995600.speaker: Stafford (onboard Snoopy)
a10o_0995600.text: It's going to put us in a 191.8 by 11.6 [nautical miles, 355.2 x 21.4 km].

a10o_0995600.speaker: Cernan (onboard Snoopy)
a10o_0995600.text: Baby. Oh, God! It'd be worthwhile to take some pictures right here.

a10o_0995600.speaker: Young
a10o_0995600.text: I can see the whole LM.

a10o_0995600.speaker: Cernan (onboard Snoopy)
a10o_0995600.text: You bet your life we're dropping down.

a10o_0995600.speaker: Cernan (onboard Snoopy)
a10o_0995600.text: The landing site is at 10:30, Tom.

a10o_0995600.speaker: Cernan (onboard Snoopy)
a10o_0995600.text: You went P - through P30, huh?

a10o_0995600.speaker: Stafford (onboard Snoopy)
a10o_0995600.text: Phasing at 47; we pitch down 90 degrees.

a10o_0995600.speaker: Cernan (onboard Snoopy)
a10o_0995600.text: OK, at minus 40, yaw left 180? Right?

a10o_0995600.speaker: Stafford (onboard Snoopy)
a10o_0995600.text: Minus 47, we pitch down 90. And at 42, we yaw left 180.

a10o_0995600.speaker: Cernan (onboard Snoopy)
a10o_0995600.text: Take them, babe, while you're coming down here.

a10o_0995600.speaker: Stafford (onboard Snoopy)
a10o_0995600.text: Everything I turn around, the Velcro won't hold the Hasselblad.

a10o_0995600.speaker: Cernan (onboard Snoopy)
a10o_0995600.text: Well, babe, you can't - It's not in there?

a10o_0995600.speaker: Stafford (onboard Snoopy)
a10o_0995600.text: No, I've got a mag. Do you have it over there?

a10o_0995600.speaker: Cernan (onboard Snoopy)
a10o_0995600.text: This Velcro isn't worth a tinker's dam. There's no telling where it is now, babe. We got to find that before we go over that landing site. Look down on the deck.

a10o_0995600.speaker: Stafford (onboard Snoopy)
a10o_0995600.text: No. Oh, here it is. Way back here. Got it. Got it. Got it.

a10o_0995600.speaker: Cernan (onboard Snoopy)
a10o_0995600.text: They can take this damn Velcro and give it back to - whoever thought they invented this kind of Velcro.

a10o_0995600.speaker: Stafford (onboard Snoopy)
a10o_0995600.text: OK. Coming down here we should be on black and white - f:4 at 250.

a10o_0995600.speaker: Stafford (onboard Snoopy)
a10o_0995600.text: You know, this place is starting to look at home.

a10o_0995600.speaker: Cernan (onboard Snoopy)
a10o_0995600.text: Huh? I'm taking these at 6, and then I'm going to - I got to pick up this landing site at 33 min - 34 minutes when you roll back again.

a10o_0995600.speaker: Stafford (onboard Snoopy)
a10o_0995600.text: Some of those little bitty bears have black stuff in them.

a10o_0995600.speaker: Cernan (onboard Snoopy)
a10o_0995600.text: John, are you still reading us?

a10o_0995600.speaker: Cernan (onboard Snoopy)
a10o_0995600.text: OK. I just - you know, when I don't hear from you, I begin to wonder.

a10o_0995600.speaker: Cernan (onboard Snoopy)
a10o_0995600.text: I tell you, babe, we's getting down among dem.

a10o_0995600.speaker: Young
a10o_0995600.text: Yes. I guess you're about straight under me now - 14 miles.

a10o_0995600.speaker: Cernan (onboard Snoopy)
a10o_0995600.text: I know why the AGS didn't work. That was my fault, babe. I didn't set it up for external Delta-V, but we got a good perigee out of it - 8.6.

a10o_0995600.speaker: Stafford (onboard Snoopy)
a10o_0995600.text: There's what I call Jack's crater. Nice little volcano that I shot yesterday. It really stands out.

a10o_1000700.speaker: Stafford (onboard Snoopy)
a10o_1000700.text: Do I get a Verb - OK, we're synced. I want to Proceed out of here and get a Verb 82 - Verb 83.

a10o_1000700.speaker: Cernan (onboard Snoopy)
a10o_1000700.text: Yes. Good idea.

a10o_1000700.speaker: Stafford (onboard Snoopy)
a10o_1000700.text: Mark.

a10o_1000700.speaker: Cernan (onboard Snoopy)
a10o_1000700.text: Do you know where the hell we really are, Tom?

a10o_1000700.speaker: Stafford (onboard Snoopy)
a10o_1000700.text: No, I've got no idea, babe, right now.

a10o_1000700.speaker: Cernan (onboard Snoopy)
a10o_1000700.text: Hey, I don't mean that way. What's this big - coming up on 50 minutes. I don't know what that big mother is there, but you're going to pitch around here anyway at 47, aren't you?

a10o_1000700.speaker: Stafford (onboard Snoopy)
a10o_1000700.text: Yep.

a10o_1000700.speaker: Stafford (onboard Snoopy)
a10o_1000700.text: There's 329. That's pretty close. Where's Hermann's site. Is this Gene-o's?

a10o_1000700.speaker: Stafford (onboard Snoopy)
a10o_1000700.text: Man, that's the prettiest volcanism I've seen..

a10o_1000700.speaker: Cernan (onboard Snoopy)
a10o_1000700.text: Hey, here's crater IX right here, I'll bet.

a10o_1000700.speaker: Cernan (onboard Snoopy)
a10o_1000700.text: Right here.

a10o_1000700.speaker: Stafford (onboard Snoopy)
a10o_1000700.text: Yes.

a10o_1000700.speaker: Stafford (onboard Snoopy)
a10o_1000700.text: Yes, we're coming up to crater IX. José, we're coming up to crater IX, I think. We'll be going straight across it.

a10o_1000700.speaker: Young
a10o_1000700.text: Roger.

a10o_1000700.speaker: Cernan (onboard Snoopy)
a10o_1000700.text: Maybe you could tell us better where we are, babe.

a10o_1000700.speaker: Young
a10o_1000700.text: We're going right across old number IX. Sure are.

a10o_1000700.speaker: Stafford (onboard Snoopy)
a10o_1000700.text: Things are starting to move faster, John.

a10o_1000700.speaker: Cernan (onboard Snoopy)
a10o_1000700.text: OK, Tom, all our - everything's looking good there, so far.

a10o_1000700.speaker: Stafford (onboard Snoopy)
a10o_1000700.text: You know, instead of going there and yawing over 180, let's take some strips here. See, instead of yaw - phasing? Yaw left.

a10o_1000700.speaker: Cernan (onboard Snoopy)
a10o_1000700.text: Yes. and I would...

a10o_1000700.speaker: Stafford (onboard Snoopy)
a10o_1000700.text: Screw it! We're just going to stay here and take some photo stripping instead of - John?

a10o_1000700.speaker: Young
a10o_1000700.text: Yes?

a10o_1000700.speaker: Stafford (onboard Snoopy)
a10o_1000700.text: OK. Instead of yawing left and yawing right, I'm just going to stay here and take some - I think it would be more interesting for the whole thing just to take strip maps here.

a10o_1000700.speaker: Young
a10o_1000700.text: I think you're right.

a10o_1000700.speaker: Cernan (onboard Snoopy)
a10o_1000700.text: I'll buy that.

a10o_1000700.speaker: Stafford (onboard Snoopy)
a10o_1000700.text: How about that, Gene-o?

a10o_1000700.speaker: Cernan (onboard Snoopy)
a10o_1000700.text: The important film we want to get is down below, babe.

a10o_1000700.speaker: Young
a10o_1000700.text: Hallelujah.

a10o_1000700.speaker: Young
a10o_1000700.text: [Garble] be coming upside down.

a10o_1000700.speaker: Stafford (onboard Snoopy)
a10o_1000700.text: Yeah.

a10o_1000700.speaker: Stafford (onboard Snoopy)
a10o_1000700.text: Man, look at those craters!

a10o_1000700.speaker: Cernan (onboard Snoopy)
a10o_1000700.text: Tom, give me that when you get a chance.

a10o_1000700.speaker: Stafford (onboard Snoopy)
a10o_1000700.text: You got it, babe.

a10o_1000700.speaker: Stafford (onboard Snoopy)
a10o_1000700.text: Look at that big one.

a10o_1000700.speaker: Cernan (onboard Snoopy)
a10o_1000700.text: That's what I'm looking at.

a10o_1000700.speaker: Stafford (onboard Snoopy)
a10o_1000700.text: My monocular's.

a10o_1000700.speaker: Cernan (onboard Snoopy)
a10o_1000700.text: Hey, when I can't see the horizon, Tom, I get the feeling like we're in a dive bombing run.

a10o_1000700.speaker: Stafford (onboard Snoopy)
a10o_1000700.text: Yeah.

a10o_1000700.speaker: Cernan (onboard Snoopy)
a10o_1000700.text: OK, at 47 minutes - OK, you're going to stay at this attitude. That's fine.

a10o_1000700.speaker: Cernan (onboard Snoopy)
a10o_1000700.text: Did you ever call up Verb 83?

a10o_1000700.speaker: Stafford (onboard Snoopy)
a10o_1000700.text: Yep. You're all set.

a10o_1000700.speaker: Cernan (onboard Snoopy)
a10o_1000700.text: I wanted to check it against the AGS. Let me look at it again.

a10o_1000700.speaker: Stafford (onboard Snoopy)
a10o_1000700.text: Hey, there are some huge boulders.

a10o_1000700.speaker: Cernan (onboard Snoopy)
a10o_1000700.text: You've got some?

a10o_1000700.speaker: Stafford (onboard Snoopy)
a10o_1000700.text: You're damn right!

a10o_1000700.speaker: Stafford (onboard Snoopy)
a10o_1000700.text: Look at those bastards down in that crater.

a10o_1000700.speaker: Cernan (onboard Snoopy)
a10o_1000700.text: Right here?

a10o_1000700.speaker: Stafford (onboard Snoopy)
a10o_1000700.text: Yes, that big deep one, right down below here.

a10o_1000700.speaker: Cernan (onboard Snoopy)
a10o_1000700.text: Let me look at them. Let me look at that- let me look at this one here. I - I just took a picture of it.

a10o_1000700.speaker: Stafford (onboard Snoopy)
a10o_1000700.text: That hole right down below us there.

a10o_1000700.speaker: Cernan (onboard Snoopy)
a10o_1000700.text: Oh, you bet your ass there's some huge boulders down there.

a10o_1000700.speaker: Stafford (onboard Snoopy)
a10o_1000700.text: Tremendous boulders.

a10o_1000700.speaker: Cernan (onboard Snoopy)
a10o_1000700.text: Man, there are, Tom.

a10o_1000700.speaker: Stafford (onboard Snoopy)
a10o_1000700.text: Hey, John, with that monocular, you can really see some boulders now, babe.

a10o_1000700.speaker: Cernan (onboard Snoopy)
a10o_1000700.text: You know, the surface around it looks fairly good, though.

a10o_1000700.speaker: Stafford (onboard Snoopy)
a10o_1000700.text: Yeah.

a10o_1000700.speaker: Cernan (onboard Snoopy)
a10o_1000700.text: Here you go. You want this back?

a10o_1000700.speaker: Stafford (onboard Snoopy)
a10o_1000700.text: You want the Hasselblad?

a10o_1000700.speaker: Cernan (onboard Snoopy)
a10o_1000700.text: Yes, I'll take pictures of it.

a10o_1000700.speaker: Cernan (onboard Snoopy)
a10o_1000700.text: Wish I could have got right down in that - right down in among those boulders - I tell you, there's some boulders down there, babe. Are we yaw a little?

a10o_1000700.speaker: Cernan (onboard Snoopy)
a10o_1000700.text: Yeah, just a little bit.

a10o_1000700.speaker: Cernan (onboard Snoopy)
a10o_1000700.text: Look at this cliff there, Tom, right in front of us.

a10o_1000700.speaker: Stafford (onboard Snoopy)
a10o_1000700.text: Yes. There's a cliff there that's at least two or three thousand feet (600 meters or 900 meters) tall.

a10o_1000700.speaker: Cernan (onboard Snoopy)
a10o_1000700.text: Oh, hell, yes. At least...

a10o_1000700.speaker: Young
a10o_1000700.text: Hey, you guys are really out there now.

a10o_1000700.speaker: Stafford (onboard Snoopy)
a10o_1000700.text: Oh, you know it, babe.

a10o_1000700.speaker: Cernan (onboard Snoopy)
a10o_1000700.text: Holy smoley, John. This is incredible!

a10o_1000700.speaker: Young
a10o_1000700.text: [Garble].

a10o_1000700.speaker: Cernan (onboard Snoopy)
a10o_1000700.text: Yes. You thought we were close at 60 miles!

a10o_1000700.speaker: Young
a10o_1000700.text: I still think we're [garble]. Does the terrain seem any different color down close to you?

a10o_1000700.speaker: Cernan (onboard Snoopy)
a10o_1000700.text: No, I don't think so.

a10o_1000700.speaker: Stafford (onboard Snoopy)
a10o_1000700.text: With the monocular, you can see some stuff.

a10o_1000700.speaker: Cernan (onboard Snoopy)
a10o_1000700.text: But I'll tell you, there's some good sized boulders on the sides of these craters. Some of them are very obviously impact. But then there are some others that - look...

a10o_1000700.speaker: Young
a10o_1000700.text: [Garble].

a10o_1000700.speaker: Cernan (onboard Snoopy)
a10o_1000700.text: They got to be - they got to be - volcanic.

a10o_1000700.speaker: Cernan (onboard Snoopy)
a10o_1000700.text: Time hack at 100 - 113:21.

a10o_1000700.speaker: Cernan (onboard Snoopy)
a10o_1000700.text: John, do you know where we are? What we're over?

a10o_1000700.speaker: Young
a10o_1000700.text: No, I lost you, I gave it to the Auto optics and it screwed up and I lost you.

a10o_1000700.speaker: Cernan (onboard Snoopy)
a10o_1000700.text: Oh, OK. Because I'm going to tell you when I think we're about over Neper, because we've got to photograph that area coming down.

a10o_1000700.speaker: Young
a10o_1000700.text: OK.

a10o_1000700.speaker: Cernan (onboard Snoopy)
a10o_1000700.text: Tom, you want this over there?

a10o_1000700.speaker: Stafford (onboard Snoopy)
a10o_1000700.text: Yep.

a10o_1000700.speaker: Cernan (onboard Snoopy)
a10o_1000700.text: (Cough) Get me that thing.

a10o_1000700.speaker: Stafford (onboard Snoopy)
a10o_1000700.text: You've got it.

a10o_1000700.speaker: Stafford (onboard Snoopy)
a10o_1000700.text: Oh, look at that bear. Here's an old one. Hey here's - Gene-o - there's...

a10o_1000700.speaker: Cernan (onboard Snoopy)
a10o_1000700.text: What are you looking at?

a10o_1000700.speaker: Stafford (onboard Snoopy)
a10o_1000700.text: Son of a bitch! I don't know.

a10o_1000700.speaker: Cernan (onboard Snoopy)
a10o_1000700.text: Holy smoley! Hey, look at that black thing in the bottom. Let me see what it is.

a10o_1000700.speaker: Stafford (onboard Snoopy)
a10o_1000700.text: Look at all those black things. Hey, John, I got something that's really standing out here-like-oh gee, can you ever see it! The monocular, Gene-o, the monocular.

a10o_1000700.speaker: Young
a10o_1000700.text: What are they?

a10o_1000700.speaker: Cernan (onboard Snoopy)
a10o_1000700.text: Alright. That's a fantastic crater. I don't know where that is...

a10o_1000700.speaker: Stafford (onboard Snoopy)
a10o_1000700.text: Let me look at it. Oops. Let me look at it.

a10o_1000700.speaker: Cernan (onboard Snoopy)
a10o_1000700.text: They're big boulders, John. Gigantic! We're looking straight down.

a10o_1000700.speaker: Stafford (onboard Snoopy)
a10o_1000700.text: Gee, I'm really getting vertigo here.

a10o_1000700.speaker: Cernan (onboard Snoopy)
a10o_1000700.text: Yes, it's like - like that rendezvous from above, Tom, when we were looking straight down at the mother.

a10o_1000700.speaker: Stafford (onboard Snoopy)
a10o_1000700.text: I nearly lost him - lost him in the light. I need to slant up some more.

a10o_1000700.speaker: Cernan (onboard Snoopy)
a10o_1000700.text: OK. We're coming up on 43 minutes.

a10o_1000700.speaker: Cernan (onboard Snoopy)
a10o_1000700.text: Are you in Orb Rate? No, you're in Inertial, aren't you?

a10o_1000700.speaker: Stafford (onboard Snoopy)
a10o_1000700.text: I'm Inertial. Need to be pitched up more.

a10o_1000700.speaker: Cernan (onboard Snoopy)
a10o_1000700.text: Your ball isn't moving. Is it?

a10o_1000700.speaker: Stafford (onboard Snoopy)
a10o_1000700.text: Yeah, it is. Sure it is.

a10o_1000700.speaker: Cernan (onboard Snoopy)
a10o_1000700.text: OK.

a10o_1000700.speaker: Stafford (onboard Snoopy)
a10o_1000700.text: Your's is moving, isn't it?

a10o_1000700.speaker: Cernan (onboard Snoopy)
a10o_1000700.text: Yes. We want to be seeing 180 upside down when we come into Neper here.

a10o_1000700.speaker: Stafford (onboard Snoopy)
a10o_1000700.text: I pitched over too far. What I wanted to see, I didn't get.

a10o_1000700.speaker: Cernan (onboard Snoopy)
a10o_1000700.text: This camera is getting red hot.

a10o_1000700.speaker: Cernan (onboard Snoopy)
a10o_1000700.text: OK, babe, at 34 minutes, we want to be pitched up, because we will be approaching into the Neper area where we want to get - this - see, Neper here's at 34 minutes - we'll be right in here. We want to start looking - be seeing Neper coming over the horizon.

a10o_1000700.speaker: Stafford (onboard Snoopy)
a10o_1000700.text: Yes. (Cough)

a10o_1000700.speaker: Stafford (onboard Snoopy)
a10o_1000700.text: Look at that [garble] volcanic as the dickens. Let me have the Hasselblad.

a10o_1000700.speaker: Cernan (onboard Snoopy)
a10o_1000700.text: Let me see that a minute.

a10o_1000700.speaker: Stafford (onboard Snoopy)
a10o_1000700.text: You've got it.

a10o_1000700.speaker: Cernan (onboard Snoopy)
a10o_1000700.text: Yes. There are a lot of - a lot of things got to be volcanic, babe.

a10o_1000700.speaker: Cernan (onboard Snoopy)
a10o_1000700.text: And there's boulders down in those holes. Look at that new one.

a10o_1000700.speaker: Cernan (onboard Snoopy)
a10o_1000700.text: Now, that's all black in the bottom.

a10o_1000700.speaker: Stafford (onboard Snoopy)
a10o_1000700.text: Yes. That's black.

a10o_1000700.speaker: Cernan (onboard Snoopy)
a10o_1000700.text: That little - that little crater with the fresh - you know, everything being fresh, it appears to me that the top of the soil - the soil is bleached by the Sun.

a10o_1000700.speaker: Stafford (onboard Snoopy)
a10o_1000700.text: Yeah.

a10o_1000700.speaker: Cernan (onboard Snoopy)
a10o_1000700.text: There's one.

a10o_1000700.speaker: Cernan (onboard Snoopy)
a10o_1000700.text: There is a fresh - and look at the boulders on the side of that one.

a10o_1000700.speaker: Stafford (onboard Snoopy)
a10o_1000700.text: You got it - got it..

a10o_1000700.speaker: Cernan (onboard Snoopy)
a10o_1000700.text: Give me that camera, babe.

a10o_1000700.speaker: Stafford (onboard Snoopy)
a10o_1000700.text: OK. I got some - here.

a10o_1000700.speaker: Cernan (onboard Snoopy)
a10o_1000700.text: OK.

a10o_1000700.speaker: Stafford (onboard Snoopy)
a10o_1000700.text: Here. Where is the monocular?

a10o_1000700.speaker: Cernan (onboard Snoopy)
a10o_1000700.text: There it is.

a10o_1000700.speaker: Cernan (onboard Snoopy)
a10o_1000700.text: Oh the 250 (mm lens) right here would have gotten something.

a10o_1000700.speaker: Stafford (onboard Snoopy)
a10o_1000700.text: Oh, look at those boulders!

a10o_1000700.speaker: Cernan (onboard Snoopy)
a10o_1000700.text: Aren't they fantastic?

a10o_1000700.speaker: Cernan (onboard Snoopy)
a10o_1000700.text: 40 minutes, babe. At 34, we ought to start coming into the Neper area.

a10o_1000700.speaker: Cernan (onboard Snoopy)
a10o_1000700.text: Now look at that one. The way those cliffs are so sheer. There's black underneath them, and when these fresh craters come out, there's - it's all white soil.

a10o_1000700.speaker: Stafford (onboard Snoopy)
a10o_1000700.text: Yes. Here's one that's coming right there.

a10o_1000700.speaker: Stafford (onboard Snoopy)
a10o_1000700.text: Oh, beautiful.

a10o_1000700.speaker: Stafford (onboard Snoopy)
a10o_1000700.text: It's black. A landslide and there's a boulder so damn big you can't believe it.

a10o_1000700.speaker: Cernan (onboard Snoopy)
a10o_1000700.text: Let me see. Trade you. Here.

a10o_1000700.speaker: Cernan (onboard Snoopy)
a10o_1000700.text: There's a little crater on the rim of this one, and there's boulders laying halfway down.

a10o_1000700.speaker: Stafford (onboard Snoopy)
a10o_1000700.text: You can see where the volcanism started, and it rolled out there.

a10o_1000700.speaker: Cernan (onboard Snoopy)
a10o_1000700.text: I - I got to say, there's a lot of impact craters around here, though. God dang.

a10o_1000700.speaker: Stafford (onboard Snoopy)
a10o_1000700.text: Yes, there are.

a10o_1000700.speaker: Cernan (onboard Snoopy)
a10o_1000700.text: A lot of impact craters. You know, this planet must have been beaten to death at one time.

a10o_1000700.speaker: Stafford (onboard Snoopy)
a10o_1000700.text: Oh, you know it.

a10o_1000700.speaker: Cernan (onboard Snoopy)
a10o_1000700.text: Must have been beat to death. OK, Tom, we're coming down to 34 minutes, and that's where we're going to start picking up - Neper ought to be coming over the horizon at 29:31. We ought to be coming over the be right over Neper.

a10o_1000700.speaker: Stafford (onboard Snoopy)
a10o_1000700.text: OK. Landing Radar - Landing Radar circuit breaker Closed at 22 minutes.

a10o_1000700.speaker: Cernan (onboard Snoopy)
a10o_1000700.text: OK, we're ahead of time. We don't - we're in good shape right now.

a10o_1000700.speaker: Cernan (onboard Snoopy)
a10o_1000700.text: There's boulders in every one of those little - little craters and on - on the ridges.

a10o_1000700.speaker: Stafford (onboard Snoopy)
a10o_1000700.text: Yes. That's on the new craters - even a few of the old ones have them right down at the bottom.

a10o_1000700.speaker: Cernan (onboard Snoopy)
a10o_1000700.text: And the boulders are black. They're black...

a10o_1000700.speaker: Stafford (onboard Snoopy)
a10o_1000700.text: They look like they're a mare.

a10o_1000700.speaker: Cernan (onboard Snoopy)
a10o_1000700.text: ...and yet - and yet the stuff that comes out of the new craters is white.

a10o_1000700.speaker: Stafford (onboard Snoopy)
a10o_1000700.text: White, but there's black around them.

a10o_1000700.speaker: Cernan (onboard Snoopy)
a10o_1000700.text: Yes. And there are some pretty sharp cliffs. Some of these seem to be windblown down, but there are some awful sharp cliffs. What a place! You know, it almost looks like this is a painting. Someone took a painting of something.

a10o_1000700.speaker: Stafford (onboard Snoopy)
a10o_1000700.text: Yes.

a10o_1000700.speaker: Cernan (onboard Snoopy)
a10o_1000700.text: Hey, John, this is really a great speed at which to go over the ground, I'll tell you.

a10o_1002050.speaker: Young
a10o_1002050.text: Yeah man.

a10o_1002050.speaker: Stafford (onboard Snoopy)
a10o_1002050.text: Oh, here's one that tossed boulders out of it.

a10o_1002050.speaker: Cernan (onboard Snoopy)
a10o_1002050.text: You've got it?

a10o_1002050.speaker: Stafford (onboard Snoopy)
a10o_1002050.text: Yep. It tossed boulders right out of the stuff.

a10o_1002050.speaker: Cernan (onboard Snoopy)
a10o_1002050.text: Look at that mother.

a10o_1002050.speaker: Stafford (onboard Snoopy)
a10o_1002050.text: See it? Right there. You can see it.

a10o_1002050.speaker: Cernan (onboard Snoopy)
a10o_1002050.text: Yes. Yes.

a10o_1002050.speaker: Stafford (onboard Snoopy)
a10o_1002050.text: This little one right here tossed boulders right out of the son of a gun. Still a bunch in there.

a10o_1002050.speaker: Cernan (onboard Snoopy)
a10o_1002050.text: OK. Neper's got to be coming up there pretty soon. We're at 36.

a10o_1002050.speaker: Cernan (onboard Snoopy)
a10o_1002050.text: I just going to keep - but we're going so slow, I'm going to stay at 6 frames a second, Tom.

a10o_1002050.speaker: Stafford (onboard Snoopy)
a10o_1002050.text: Yes. Oh man. Oh, beautiful. Hey, I could even see a boulder for at least 20 miles [37 km] ahead. In that one crater right on your left, Gene-o.

a10o_1002050.speaker: Cernan (onboard Snoopy)
a10o_1002050.text: Yes. Yes. Oh, look at one, way up. Let me take a look.

a10o_1002050.speaker: Stafford (onboard Snoopy)
a10o_1002050.text: Yes. It's got a big black one right down in the bottom of it.

a10o_1002050.speaker: Cernan (onboard Snoopy)
a10o_1002050.text: Yep. I can - you're right!

a10o_1002050.speaker: Stafford (onboard Snoopy)
a10o_1002050.text: Talk about a boulder! That thing is big enough to - to crush a couple of houses.

a10o_1002050.speaker: Cernan (onboard Snoopy)
a10o_1002050.text: They're lying all down the side and there's no - there is no little rim crater on it, either. They're just lying on the side.

a10o_1002050.speaker: Stafford (onboard Snoopy)
a10o_1002050.text: Shoot a picture of that one - that white one coming up right. in front of you.

a10o_1002050.speaker: Cernan (onboard Snoopy)
a10o_1002050.text: OK.

a10o_1002050.speaker: Stafford (onboard Snoopy)
a10o_1002050.text: You can see...

a10o_1002050.speaker: Cernan (onboard Snoopy)
a10o_1002050.text: Here you go.

a10o_1002050.speaker: Stafford (onboard Snoopy)
a10o_1002050.text: ...where the white ran down.

a10o_1002050.speaker: Cernan (onboard Snoopy)
a10o_1002050.text: We got to be coming somewhere near where Neper is going to be up there, pretty soon, and the Smythe Sea.

a10o_1002050.speaker: Cernan (onboard Snoopy)
a10o_1002050.text: Tom, look at the boulder on the edge of that one. Quick, look over here - way over there. Look at that black one, way - See it? See it?

a10o_1002050.speaker: Stafford (onboard Snoopy)
a10o_1002050.text: Oh yes.

a10o_1002050.speaker: Cernan (onboard Snoopy)
a10o_1002050.text: Look at that! Look at that. I don't know why I'm fascinated with boulders, but son of a gun - those black things stand out. Give me the monocular on that one.

a10o_1002050.speaker: Cernan (onboard Snoopy)
a10o_1002050.text: At first I thought it was shadow on it, but it sure isn't, because we're looking - coming down right through the...

a10o_1002050.text: OK. At 33:31, we're going to coming up on 269 and 192 and Jansky.
