a10o-1023655.speaker: Cernan (in Snoopy)
a10o-1023655.text: OK. And that - the DAP is set - I'll call up P47 at 11 minutes.

a10o-1023655.speaker: Cernan (in Snoopy)
a10o-1023655.text: Let me take another look at the DAP, Tom.

a10o-1023655.speaker: Cernan (in Snoopy)
a10o-1023655.text: 12002. That's go. OK. Call up 47 in 1 minute. OK, Tom. I'll thrust aft [-X] 2 feet per second (0.61 m/s). I'll stop. I'll start thrusting forward [+X] and you stage-fire.

a10o-1023655.speaker: Cernan (in Snoopy)
a10o-1023655.text: OK. Then you got to go up to...

a10o-1023655.speaker: Cernan (in Snoopy)
a10o-1023655.text: My attitude looks good. I'm coming up on 270 upside down.

a10o-1023655.speaker: Cernan (in Snoopy)
a10o-1023655.text: And yours is, looking good. OK. I'm calling up Noun 47.

a10o-1023655.speaker: Cernan (in Snoopy)
a10o-1023655.text: OK, that's that way and then that way. Right?

a10o-1023655.speaker: Stafford (onboard Snoopy)
a10o-1023655.text: Yes. I'll just take a little bit that way.

a10o-1023655.speaker: Cernan (in Snoopy)
a10o-1023655.text: Yes, because we're going to be awful light.

a10o-1023655.speaker: Stafford (onboard Snoopy)
a10o-1023655.text: Yes. We're going to - AGS is going to Mode Control.

a10o-1023655.speaker: Cernan (in Snoopy)
a10o-1023655.text: OK. Stay out of there, babe. OK, stay at that last attitude.

a10o-1023655.speaker: Stafford (onboard Snoopy)
a10o-1023655.text: Something's wrong here. Hold it, Gene-o.

a10o-1023655.speaker: Stafford (onboard Snoopy)
a10o-1023655.text: Going to try Deadband, Min here.

a10o-1023655.speaker: Cernan (in Snoopy)
a10o-1023655.text: AGS ready. AGS any time you want to go.

a10o-1023655.speaker: Stafford (onboard Snoopy)
a10o-1023655.text: Something's wrong with the yaw rate gyro. Let's go in PGNS and Attitude Hold. OK. [Garble].

a10o-1023655.speaker: Cernan (in Snoopy)
a10o-1023655.text: By the way, the DAP is set for a light vehicle. OK, we'll do it...

a10o-1023655.speaker: Stafford (onboard Snoopy)
a10o-1023655.text: OK, hold it. We're in - OK, go.

a10o-1023655.speaker: Stafford (onboard Snoopy)
a10o-1023655.text: Thrust aft. Hold it. Thrust aft. OK, ready?

a10o-1023655.speaker: Stafford (onboard Snoopy)
a10o-1023655.text: Let's go to PGNS. God damn.

a10o-1023655.speaker: Cernan (in Snoopy)
a10o-1023655.text: OK, let's - let's make this burn on the AGS babe.

a10o-1023655.speaker: Cernan (in Snoopy)
a10o-1023655.text: Make this - make this burn on the AGS.

a10o-1023655.speaker: Cernan (in Snoopy)
a10o-1023655.text: Got a good staging. Let's make it on the AGS.

a10o-1023655.speaker: Stafford (onboard Snoopy)
a10o-1023655.text: How are the AGS? Are we OK? I think we're OK, Gene-o. Proceed..

a10o-1023655.speaker: Cernan (in Snoopy)
a10o-1023655.text: Did you get into gimbal lock?

a10o-1023655.speaker: Stafford (onboard Snoopy)
a10o-1023655.text: Yes, but we got out of it.

a10o-1023655.speaker: Cernan (in Snoopy)
a10o-1023655.text: She didn't - she didn't go, huh?

a10o-1023655.speaker: Stafford (onboard Snoopy)
a10o-1023655.text: OK, what's our - ? Did you call P00?

a10o-1023655.speaker: Stafford (onboard Snoopy)
a10o-1023655.text: OK, what's our attitude for staging? What's our angles?

a10o-1023655.speaker: Cernan (in Snoopy)
a10o-1023655.text: OK. Our angles? You didn't lock, huh?

a10o-1023655.speaker: Cernan (in Snoopy)
a10o-1023655.text: Something is wrong with that gyro. OK, roll is 180, pitch is 233.

a10o-1023655.speaker: Stafford (onboard Snoopy)
a10o-1023655.text: Roll is 180 and pitch is what?

a10o-1023655.speaker: Cernan (in Snoopy)
a10o-1023655.text: 233. You better put my ball on Inertial just to check them out and verify them, too.

a10o-1023655.speaker: Cernan (in Snoopy)
a10o-1023655.text: I can't reach it. So if you could put mine, you can verify it on the AGS.

a10o-1023655.speaker: Duke
a10o-1023655.text: Snoop, Houston. We show you close to gimbal lock.

a10o-1023655.speaker: Stafford (in Snoopy)
a10o-1023655.text: Yeah, OK. Something went wild during that staging, but we're all set, we didn't lock it. We are going ahead to the Auto maneuver.

a10o-1023655.speaker: Cernan (in Snoopy)
a10o-1023655.text: Babe, I don't know. Let's put my AGS in Inertial - in Inertial, though to verify that we're at the right attitude, babe.

a10o-1023655.speaker: Cernan (in Snoopy)
a10o-1023655.text: Put it - OK. Just so it's in Inertial.

a10o-1023655.speaker: Cernan (in Snoopy)
a10o-1023655.text: OK. Because in case we have to go to it, that's what we want.

a10o-1023655.speaker: Cernan (in Snoopy)
a10o-1023655.text: Try to get this damn thing - Sure the PGNS...

a10o-1023655.speaker: Cernan (in Snoopy)
a10o-1023655.text: ...is good, huh? Wait until that thing blanks. OK, babe.

a10o-1023655.speaker: Duke
a10o-1023655.text: Charlie Brown. Houston. They - staging - they had a wild gyration though, but they got it under control. Over.

a10o-1024751.speaker: Cernan (in Snoopy)
a10o-1024751.text: We've got a lot of time; 7 minutes. I don't know what the hell that was, babe.

a10o-1024751.speaker: Cernan (in Snoopy)
a10o-1024751.text: OK, it'll be going here in...

a10o-1024751.speaker: Duke
a10o-1024751.text: Snoop, Houston. You're looking OK for the insertion burn.

a10o-1024751.speaker: Stafford (in Snoopy)
a10o-1024751.text: Yes. Roger, Charlie. That, was something we've never seen before. It was real good. We went to AGS and...

a10o-1024751.speaker: Stafford (in Snoopy)
a10o-1024751.text: You want to go through P30 again?

a10o-1024751.speaker: Cernan (in Snoopy)
a10o-1024751.text: No. I went through P30. Go into P40.

a10o-1024751.speaker: Stafford (in Snoopy)
a10o-1024751.text: And, let me tell you what happened there real quick as we come around to this insertion burn. I went to attitude deadband, started thrusting aft, and the thing just took off on us.

a10o-1024751.speaker: Stafford (in Snoopy)
a10o-1024751.text: So I could see we're coming up - and we come up to insertion, so I flipped - I got a hold of it and tried to avoid gimbal lock, and guess I did. Looks like we got a good insertion out of it anyway, and - I mean, a good staging out of it and we are all set to go for insertion here.

a10o-1024751.speaker: Stafford (in Snoopy)
a10o-1024751.text: Are we going forwards or backwards? Oh, we're going...

a10o-1024751.speaker: Cernan (in Snoopy)
a10o-1024751.text: That's the way we want to go.

a10o-1024751.speaker: Stafford (in Snoopy)
a10o-1024751.text: Yes, right, right, right. There's the Orb Rate ball; we're in good shape.

a10o-1024751.speaker: Cernan (in Snoopy)
a10o-1024751.text: I'll tell you, there was a moment there, Tom...

a10o-1024751.speaker: Cernan (in Snoopy)
a10o-1024751.text: ...but let's worry about it after we make this burn. I want to make sure the AGS is up for it.

a10o-1024751.speaker: Stafford (in Snoopy)
a10o-1024751.text: OK, we're going to Auto, and I'm going to P00 - Let me call - let me call the DAP again.

a10o-1024751.speaker: Cernan (in Snoopy)
a10o-1024751.text: We never did go into PGNS, so the DAP didn't do it to us.

a10o-1024751.speaker: Duke
a10o-1024751.text: Snoop, Houston. Stand by for a Mark; 5 minutes to the burn.

a10o-1024751.speaker: Duke
a10o-1024751.text: Five minutes to the burn. Over.

a10o-1024751.speaker: Cernan (in Snoopy)
a10o-1024751.text: OK, Charlie. We're with you. I think we have got all our marbles.

a10o-1024751.speaker: Cernan (in Snoopy)
a10o-1024751.text: We is sure coming down to that ground, I'll tell you.

a10o-1024751.speaker: Stafford (in Snoopy)
a10o-1024751.text: I wonder where that [descent] stage went?

a10o-1024751.speaker: Cernan (in Snoopy)
a10o-1024751.text: I don't know, but I hope we never find it again,

a10o-1024751.speaker: Cernan (in Snoopy)
a10o-1024751.text: Man, I'll tell you, that was wild, babe, and it wasn't the DAP, because you were in AGS. That was AGS.

a10o-1024751.speaker: Stafford (in Snoopy)
a10o-1024751.text: I was in AGS - I was in AGS; Mode Control, Attitude Hold. Right?

a10o-1024751.speaker: Cernan (in Snoopy)
a10o-1024751.text: That's where we're going to stage. OK, babe. I've got good AGS, and everything is looking good. I've got the attitude set so if we have to switch, we'll be alright. OK. 04:07. I'll monitor it until the burn. We're 4 minutes. OK. Four minutes. Boy, that is hard to do with helmet and gloves on. Helium Monitor to Ascent Pressure 1 and 2. Let's take...

a10o-1024751.speaker: Cernan (in Snoopy)
a10o-1024751.text: ...take another look at it. That's looking good. Engine Stop, push buttons, all Reset, and Abort/Abort Stage, Reset. OK.

a10o-1024751.speaker: Young
a10o-1024751.text: Houston, I'm not reading them, so if they don't make it, you've got to tell me. OK?

a10o-1024751.speaker: Duke
a10o-1024751.text: Roger. They are counting down. Looking good, Charlie Brown.

a10o-1024751.speaker: Cernan (in Snoopy)
a10o-1024751.text: ...Delta-V to go. OK, Tom, If - if we've got less than 170 feet - if we've got more than 170 feet per second (52 m/s) to go, we're RCS, and we'll RCS maximum, of 55 seconds, but we will RCS.

a10o-1024751.speaker: Cernan (in Snoopy)
a10o-1024751.text: If Delta-V is greater than 170 [fps] (52 m/s), we're RC - RCS back, to our PAD Delta-V.

a10o-1024751.speaker: Cernan (in Snoopy)
a10o-1024751.text: OK? Which is going to be right in P40 there.

a10o-1024751.speaker: Cernan (in Snoopy)
a10o-1024751.text: OK, babe. Coming up about 2 minutes.

a10o-1024751.speaker: Cernan (in Snoopy)
a10o-1024751.text: OK. And our PAD Delta-V is 220.9 [fps, 67.3 m/s]. So if we burn less than 170 feet per second [52 m/s] - If we don't get up to 170 feet per second [52 m/s] to go, we'll want to burn it back to about-about 220 [fps, 67 m/s]. OK?

a10o-1024751.speaker: Cernan (in Snoopy)
a10o-1024751.text: But let's get over 170 [fps] (52 m/s) - let's get into that 170 feet per second (52 m/s) region.

a10o-1024751.speaker: Cernan (in Snoopy)
a10o-1024751.text: OK. Push your Inverter number 1, Closed, circuit breaker.

a10o-1024751.speaker: Cernan (in Snoopy)
a10o-1024751.text: And at 1 minute, your Stab/Control, AELD, Closed.

a10o-1024751.speaker: Cernan (in Snoopy)
a10o-1024751.text: Boy, I'll tell you, we is down among them again going backwards, you know that?

a10o-1024751.speaker: Cernan (in Snoopy)
a10o-1024751.text: Look at that rille. That's got to be - that's got to be probably Diamondback right there.

a10o-1024751.speaker: Cernan (in Snoopy)
a10o-1024751.text: It's awful close to see that.

a10o-1024751.speaker: Stafford (in Snoopy)
a10o-1024751.text: Yes, let's keep watching this; we're at 2 minutes, babe.

a10o-1024751.speaker: Stafford (in Snoopy)
a10o-1024751.text: Got AELD coming Closed. Have you got yours Closed?

a10o-1024751.speaker: Cernan (in Snoopy)
a10o-1024751.text: OK. Two minutes, babe. Give it a final trim.

a10o-1024751.speaker: Cernan (in Snoopy)
a10o-1024751.text: OK. There it is. OK. My AELD is coming Closed, Tom.

a10o-1024751.speaker: Cernan (in Snoopy)
a10o-1024751.text: OK. And verify your Inverter number 1 breakers, Closed.

a10o-1024751.speaker: Cernan (in Snoopy)
a10o-1024751.text: OK. At 35 seconds, we want the Engine Arm to Arm.

a10o-1024751.speaker: Cernan (in Snoopy)
a10o-1024751.text: We're in PGNS; we're in Auto.

a10o-1024751.speaker: Stafford (in Snoopy)
a10o-1024751.text: 4 Jet, Balance Couple is On. And stand by to...

a10o-1024751.speaker: Cernan (in Snoopy)
a10o-1024751.text: Coming right into the attitude, babe.

a10o-1024751.speaker: Cernan (in Snoopy)
a10o-1024751.text: Got Engine Arm yet to go. Coming up on 01:12.

a10o-1024751.speaker: Cernan (in Snoopy)
a10o-1024751.text: I'll hit 99, and I'll count you down.

a10o-1024751.speaker: Cernan (in Snoopy)
a10o-1024751.text: Burn time is 15 seconds, so it's going to go in a hurry.

a10o-1024751.speaker: Cernan (in Snoopy)
a10o-1024751.text: 50 seconds, 48. Baby, let's make this one.

a10o-1024751.speaker: Cernan (in Snoopy)
a10o-1024751.text: Master Arm is On, Engine Arm, Ascent; AGS Control in Auto, Deadband, Min; and we're set for this attitude on the burn and counting down 500.

a10o-1024751.speaker: Cernan (in Snoopy)
a10o-1024751.text: 100 [fps] (30.5 m/s) to go. 78 [fps] (24 m/s) to go. 50 [fps] (15 m/s) to go. 20 [fps] (6.1 m/s) to go. Stand by, Tom.

a10o-1024751.speaker: Duke
a10o-1024751.text: Charlie Brown, Houston. He got the burn off. We're in good shape.

a10o-1024751.speaker: Cernan (in Snoopy)
a10o-1024751.text: OK. Let me get the - minus 0.3, plus 0.1...

a10o-1024751.speaker: Young
a10o-1024751.text: Outstanding. My congratulations to the Snoopy.

a10o-1024751.speaker: Cernan (in Snoopy)
a10o-1024751.text: Baby, that, made me feel better. Call up Verb 82 when you get a chance.

a10o-1024751.speaker: Cernan (in Snoopy)
a10o-1024751.text: OK, and there the AGS says we made a good burn. Go ahead.

a10o-1024751.speaker: Duke
a10o-1024751.text: Snoop, Houston. We copy the residuals. It looks great.

a10o-1024751.speaker: Stafford (in Snoopy)
a10o-1024751.text: Roger, Houston. We got it. Oh, Roger. The burn looked real good.

a10o-1024751.speaker: Cernan (in Snoopy)
a10o-1024751.text: I tell you we're down here where we can touch the top of some of the hills, though.

a10o-1024751.speaker: Young
a10o-1024751.text: Houston, under cases like this, it sounds like to me you can relay through him because every time you talk to me I hear him talking in the background,

a10o-1024751.speaker: Stafford (in Snoopy)
a10o-1024751.text: OK, Char - Hello, Houston. This is Snoopy. It shows us in 46.7 (nautical miles, 86.5 km) by 11.0 (nautical miles, 20.4 km). Over.

a10o-1024751.speaker: Cernan (in Snoopy)
a10o-1024751.text: OK, and mine's Open. Master Arm, off.

a10o-1024751.speaker: Cernan (in Snoopy)
a10o-1024751.text: And Inverter number 2 - number 1 breaker, Open.

a10o-1024751.speaker: Cernan (in Snoopy)
a10o-1024751.text: OK. And the RCS just for the record on 80 and 78

a10o-1024751.speaker: Stafford (in Snoopy)
a10o-1024751.text: Alrighty. Did you notice that the wobble we got on that burn?

a10o-1024751.speaker: Cernan (in Snoopy)
a10o-1024751.text: Boy, I tell you I thought we were wobbling all over the sky...

a10o-1024751.speaker: Cernan (in Snoopy)
a10o-1024751.text: I'm surprised those residuals ended up where they did.

a10o-1024751.speaker: Duke
a10o-1024751.text: Charlie Brown, Houston. Can you hear that hear them talking when I keep keyed down here. Over.

a10o-1024751.speaker: Young
a10o-1024751.text: Yes. A lot clearer, I thought, all of a sudden. That was great.

a10o-1024751.speaker: Duke
a10o-1024751.text: OK. When they start talking, I'll key down here and relay to you. Over. Until you get them again.

a10o-1024751.speaker: Young
a10o-1024751.text: OK. That'll be kind of you.

a10o-1024751.speaker: Stafford (in Snoopy)
a10o-1024751.text: Yes, I'll get the other one in a...

a10o-1024751.speaker: Cernan (in Snoopy)
a10o-1024751.text: And I'm back on Orb Rate, Tom?

a10a-1025539.speaker: Cernan (in Snoopy)
a10a-1025539.text: Baby, that, made me feel better. Call up Verb 82 when you get a chance.

a10a-1025539.speaker: Stafford (in Snoopy)
a10a-1025539.text: I will. OK.

a10a-1025539.speaker: Cernan (in Snoopy)
a10a-1025539.text: OK, and there the AGS says we made a good burn. Go ahead.

a10a-1025539.speaker: Duke
a10a-1025539.text: Snoop, Houston. We copy the residuals. It looks great.

a10a-1025539.speaker: Stafford (in Snoopy)
a10a-1025539.text: Roger, Houston. We got it. Oh, Roger. The burn looked real good.

a10a-1025539.speaker: Cernan (in Snoopy)
a10a-1025539.text: I tell you we're down here where we can touch the top of some of the hills, though.

a10a-1025539.speaker: Young
a10a-1025539.text: Houston, under cases like this, it sounds like to me you can relay through him because every time you talk to me I hear him talking in the background,

a10a-1025539.speaker: Stafford (in Snoopy)
a10a-1025539.text: OK, Char - Hello, Houston. This is Snoopy. It shows us in 46.7 (nautical miles, 86.5 km) by 11.0 (nautical miles, 20.4 km). Over.

a10a-1025539.speaker: Duke
a10a-1025539.text: Roger. We copy. 46.7 by 11.0.

a10a-1025539.speaker: Cernan (in Snoopy)
a10a-1025539.text: OK, Tom. Engine Arm Off.

a10a-1025539.speaker: Stafford (in Snoopy)
a10a-1025539.text: Yes.

a10a-1025539.speaker: Cernan (in Snoopy)
a10a-1025539.text: AELD Breaker, Open.

a10a-1025539.speaker: Stafford (in Snoopy)
a10a-1025539.text: I already got...

a10a-1025539.speaker: Cernan (in Snoopy)
a10a-1025539.text: OK, and mine's Open. Master Arm, off.

a10a-1025539.speaker: Stafford (in Snoopy)
a10a-1025539.text: Yep.

a10a-1025539.speaker: Cernan (in Snoopy)
a10a-1025539.text: And Inverter number 2 - number 1 breaker, Open.

a10a-1025539.speaker: Stafford (in Snoopy)
a10a-1025539.text: Yep.

a10a-1025539.speaker: Cernan (in Snoopy)
a10a-1025539.text: OK. And the RCS just for the record on 80 and 78

a10a-1025539.speaker: Stafford (in Snoopy)
a10a-1025539.text: Alrighty. Did you notice that the wobble we got on that burn?

a10a-1025539.speaker: Cernan (in Snoopy)
a10a-1025539.text: Boy, I tell you I thought we were wobbling all over the sky...

a10a-1025539.speaker: Stafford (in Snoopy)
a10a-1025539.text: (Laughter)

a10a-1025539.speaker: Cernan (in Snoopy)
a10a-1025539.text: I'm surprised those residuals ended up where they did.

a10a-1025539.speaker: Cernan (in Snoopy)
a10a-1025539.text: OK. Yaw 180 and pitch down 90.

a10a-1025539.speaker: Stafford (in Snoopy)
a10a-1025539.text: Alrighty, let's go off VOX.

a10a-1025539.speaker: Cernan (in Snoopy)
a10a-1025539.text: Circuit breaker, Rendezvous Radar, Closed.

a10a-1025539.speaker: Stafford (in Snoopy)
a10a-1025539.text: OK.

a10a-1025539.speaker: Cernan (in Snoopy)
a10a-1025539.text: Now wait 30 seconds.

a10a-1025539.speaker: Stafford (in Snoopy)
a10a-1025539.text: OK, going to...

a10a-1025539.speaker: Duke
a10a-1025539.text: Charlie Brown, Houston. Can you hear that hear them talking when I keep keyed down here. Over.

a10a-1025539.speaker: Young
a10a-1025539.text: Yes. A lot clearer, I thought, all of a sudden. That was great.

a10a-1025539.speaker: Stafford (in Snoopy)
a10a-1025539.text: No, go the other way.

a10a-1025539.speaker: Duke
a10a-1025539.text: OK. When they start talking, I'll key down here and relay to you. Over. Until you get them again.

a10a-1025539.speaker: Young
a10a-1025539.text: OK. That'll be kind of you.

a10a-1025539.speaker: Duke
a10a-1025539.text: Roger.

a10a-1025539.speaker: Cernan (in Snoopy)
a10a-1025539.text: Got your breakers closed?

a10a-1025539.speaker: Stafford (in Snoopy)
a10a-1025539.text: Yes, I'll get the other one in a...

a10a-1025539.speaker: Cernan (in Snoopy)
a10a-1025539.text: And I'm back on Orb Rate, Tom?

a10a-1025539.speaker: Stafford (in Snoopy)
a10a-1025539.text: OK.

a10a-1025539.speaker: Cernan (in Snoopy)
a10a-1025539.text: Put me back on Orb rate, will you?

a10a-1025539.speaker: Stafford (in Snoopy)
a10a-1025539.text: I'll get it.

a10a-1025539.speaker: Cernan (in Snoopy)
a10a-1025539.text: That son of a bitch was wild. We got to watch the AGS on CDH [Constant DELTA Height].

a10a-1025539.speaker: Stafford (in Snoopy)
a10a-1025539.text: Oh, ho, ho!

a10a-1025539.speaker: Duke
a10a-1025539.text: Charlie Brown, Houston. We recommend for your next maneuver that you load the DAP with a half a degree per second. We see 0.2 (degree per second) now. Over.

a10a-1025539.speaker: Young
a10a-1025539.text: OK. Roger. I'm going to do that.

a10a-1025539.speaker: Duke
a10a-1025539.text: OK.

a10a-1025539.speaker: Cernan (in Snoopy)
a10a-1025539.text: Let's go up and get him.

a10a-1025539.speaker: Stafford (in Snoopy)
a10a-1025539.text: Yes, I'd still like to know what caused that.

a10a-1025539.speaker: Cernan (in Snoopy)
a10a-1025539.text: I would too. You got your other breaker Closed, Rendezvous Radar?

a10a-1025539.speaker: Stafford (in Snoopy)
a10a-1025539.text: Yes, I'll get it Closed.

a10a-1025539.speaker: Cernan (in Snoopy)
a10a-1025539.text: I don't know what the hell that was, but a - that's better.

a10a-1025539.speaker: Cernan (in Snoopy)
a10a-1025539.text: OK, Tom. You can pull your circuit breakers.

a10a-1025539.speaker: Cernan (in Snoopy)
a10a-1025539.text: Your Rendezvous breaker?

a10a-1025539.speaker: Stafford (in Snoopy)
a10a-1025539.text: OK. Ready to pull it?

a10a-1025539.speaker: Young
a10a-1025539.text: Houston. Is he in a 283 by 15.3 [nautical miles, 524 x 28.4 km]? Over.

a10a-1025539.speaker: Cernan (in Snoopy)
a10a-1025539.text: Pull it.

a10a-1025539.speaker: Stafford (in Snoopy)
a10a-1025539.text: OK.

a10a-1025539.speaker: Cernan (in Snoopy)
a10a-1025539.text: OK, we'll make a quick alignment, here.

a10a-1025539.speaker: Duke
a10a-1025539.text: Negative. We've got him at 46.7 by 11.0 [nautical miles, 86.5 x 20.3 km]. Over.

a10a-1025539.speaker: Cernan (in Snoopy)
a10a-1025539.text: AOT Lamp Breaker, Closed.

a10a-1025539.speaker: Stafford (in Snoopy)
a10a-1025539.text: Stand by. It's Closed.

a10a-1025539.speaker: Young
a10a-1025539.text: Roger. I must have loaded this number backwards. This P76 number backwards.

a10a-1025539.speaker: Duke
a10a-1025539.text: Roger. We'll send you a TM [telemetry] vector in just a moment. Charlie Brown, we've got your LM vector coming. Stand by.

a10a-1025539.speaker: Cernan (in Snoopy)
a10a-1025539.text: Tom, set the Elapsed Timer down on - down on CSI [Coelliptic Sequence Initiation]. Here's CSI time because, remember, we got to get that backup mark at 30 minutes [before the CSI burn].

a10a-1025539.speaker: Young
a10a-1025539.text: Alrighty.

a10a-1025539.speaker: Stafford (in Snoopy)
a10a-1025539.text: OK.

a10a-1025539.speaker: Cernan (in Snoopy)
a10a-1025539.text: And 103:45, we don't have a lot of time. Only got 15 minutes to make this alignment, so I'm going to make it only three marks.

a10a-1025539.speaker: Stafford (in Snoopy)
a10a-1025539.text: OK.

a10a-1025539.speaker: Cernan (in Snoopy)
a10a-1025539.text: OK, you can leave it Go, cause I'm going to call up the...

a10a-1025539.speaker: Cernan (in Snoopy)
a10a-1025539.text: I don't know what it is here, babe.

a10a-1025539.speaker: Young
a10a-1025539.text: ... what have we got right now?

a10a-1025539.speaker: Cernan (in Snoopy)
a10a-1025539.text: You don't have to maneuver; I got to go get a star [for P52].

a10a-1025539.speaker: Young
a10a-1025539.text: We're in P00 and Accept right now.

a10a-1025539.speaker: Stafford (in Snoopy)
a10a-1025539.text: OK.

a10a-1025539.speaker: Duke
a10a-1025539.text: Roger. Copy, Charlie Brown. Stand by. Be a while.

a10a-1025539.speaker: Young
a10a-1025539.text: OK. Well, I can do realign in the meantime then.

a10a-1025539.speaker: Cernan (in Snoopy)
a10a-1025539.text: OK, Tom? Can I go get it?

a10a-1025539.speaker: Stafford (in Snoopy)
a10a-1025539.text: OK, you're in, what's - what's it? 351? - 35 - yes, it'll pitch you down quite a bit. You can go get it.

a10a-1025539.speaker: Duke
a10a-1025539.text: Charlie Brown, Houston. Stand by 30 seconds. We'll have the load to you. Over.

a10a-1025539.speaker: Young
a10a-1025539.text: Roger. I'll wait.

a10a-1025539.speaker: Stafford (in Snoopy)
a10a-1025539.text: OK, maneuver. Go.

a10a-1025539.speaker: Cernan (in Snoopy)
a10a-1025539.text: OK, and here's the time, if you can set that elapsed timer, because we got to get that, bagged - that 30 minute mark that we always miss.

a10a-1025539.speaker: Cernan (in Snoopy)
a10a-1025539.text: That was the Earth in there?

a10a-1025539.speaker: Stafford (in Snoopy)
a10a-1025539.text: Where's CS - oh. Where's CSI, 103:45?

a10a-1025539.speaker: Cernan (in Snoopy)
a10a-1025539.text: Right, right down here. Right down here on the left.

a10a-1025539.speaker: Stafford (in Snoopy)
a10a-1025539.text: We're there.

a10a-1025539.speaker: Cernan (in Snoopy)
a10a-1025539.text: Excellent.

a10a-1025539.speaker: Young
a10a-1025539.text: Boy, Houston. That's outstanding. Wish we had done that when we were fooling with the GSFC [Goddard Space Flight Center].

a10a-1025539.speaker: Duke
a10a-1025539.text: Roger (chuckling).

a10a-1025539.speaker: Cernan (in Snoopy)
a10a-1025539.text: That's a light vehicle, Tom.

a10a-1025539.speaker: Stafford (in Snoopy)
a10a-1025539.text: Yes, I know it.

a10a-1025539.speaker: Young
a10a-1025539.text: Are you done with?

a10a-1025539.speaker: Stafford (in Snoopy)
a10a-1025539.text: Counting down.

a10a-1025539.speaker: Duke
a10a-1025539.text: Stand by.

a10a-1025539.speaker: Duke
a10a-1025539.text: Roger. Charlie Brown, you can take the computer back. We're done with the load. Over.

a10a-1025539.speaker: Cernan (in Snoopy)
a10a-1025539.text: There ain't any question we don't have an ascent - or descent stage. How's the chamber pressure and everything holding?

a10a-1025539.speaker: Duke
a10a-1025539.text: Charlie Brown, Houston. We're through with the computer. It's yours. Over.

a10a-1025539.speaker: Stafford (in Snoopy)
a10a-1025539.text: Chamber pressure?

a10a-1025539.speaker: Cernan (in Snoopy)
a10a-1025539.text: You know. Yes, cabin chamber pressure.

a10a-1025539.speaker: Young
a10a-1025539.text: Thank you much.

a10a-1025539.speaker: Stafford (in Snoopy)
a10a-1025539.text: Good.

a10a-1025539.speaker: Duke
a10a-1025539.text: You're welcome.

a10a-1025539.speaker: Cernan (in Snoopy)
a10a-1025539.text: That's four sets, let's Proceed.

a10a-1025539.speaker: Young
a10a-1025539.text: That's more like it.

a10a-1025539.speaker: Stafford (in Snoopy)
a10a-1025539.text: We're all set. Counting down.

a10a-1025539.speaker: Cernan (in Snoopy)
a10a-1025539.text: Let me see.

a10a-1025539.speaker: Cernan (in Snoopy)
a10a-1025539.text: Houston, we're going to Omnis. [Garble] P52 the rest of it.

a10a-1025539.speaker: Duke
a10a-1025539.text: Roger. We copy. We want Aft Omnis. Aft Omnis. Over.

a10a-1025539.speaker: Duke
a10a-1025539.text: Snoop, Houston. Aft Omnis, if you read. Over.

a10a-1025539.speaker: Young
a10a-1025539.text: They want you on Aft Omnis, Snoopy.

a10a-1025539.speaker: Cernan (in Snoopy)
a10a-1025539.text: What'd he say?

a10a-1025539.speaker: Young
a10a-1025539.text: Houston wants you on Aft Omnis, Gene.

a10a-1025539.speaker: Cernan (in Snoopy)
a10a-1025539.text: Tell him that's where I am.

a10a-1025539.speaker: Young
a10a-1025539.text: OK. He's on Omnis, Houston. He's on Aft Omnis.

a10a-1025539.speaker: Stafford (in Snoopy)
a10a-1025539.text: Hold it.

a10a-1025539.speaker: Duke
a10a-1025539.text: Roger. We copy, Charlie Brown. Are you reading him now, Charlie Brown?

a10a-1025539.speaker: Stafford (in Snoopy)
a10a-1025539.text: What star did you take?

a10a-1025539.speaker: Cernan (in Snoopy)
a10a-1025539.text: Altair like we called for in the book.

a10a-1025539.speaker: Young
a10a-1025539.text: Yes, I am. Thank you.

a10a-1025539.speaker: Stafford (in Snoopy)
a10a-1025539.text: Good. OK. Yes, it's looking good.

a10a-1025539.speaker: Cernan (in Snoopy)
a10a-1025539.text: That's it right there.

a10a-1025539.speaker: Duke
a10a-1025539.text: Snoop, Houston. Over.

a10a-1025539.speaker: Stafford (in Snoopy)
a10a-1025539.text: Bang, bang.

a10a-1025539.speaker: Cernan (in Snoopy)
a10a-1025539.text: Right on the money.

a10a-1025539.speaker: Cernan (in Snoopy)
a10a-1025539.text: Boy it's a light vehicle.

a10a-1025539.speaker: Cernan (in Snoopy)
a10a-1025539.text: Boy.

a10a-1025539.speaker: Stafford (in Snoopy)
a10a-1025539.text: Beautiful! Why don't you write that down? What were the stars, 40...

a10a-1025539.speaker: Stafford (in Snoopy)
a10a-1025539.text: I'll write those down. ...

a10a-1025539.speaker: Stafford (in Snoopy)
a10a-1025539.text: Got it?

a10a-1025539.speaker: Cernan (in Snoopy)
a10a-1025539.text: Yes, and let's make a star check on...

a10a-1025539.speaker: Stafford (in Snoopy)
a10a-1025539.text: Let's Proceed.

a10a-1025539.speaker: Cernan (in Snoopy)
a10a-1025539.text: Go ahead.

a10a-1025539.speaker: Stafford (in Snoopy)
a10a-1025539.text: We're not going to have much time.

a10a-1025539.speaker: Cernan (in Snoopy)
a10a-1025539.text: No, I just want it right on the same star. On Altair.

a10a-1025539.speaker: Cernan (in Snoopy)
a10a-1025539.text: Beautiful, Tom. Beautiful...

a10a-1025539.speaker: Stafford (in Snoopy)
a10a-1025539.text: OK. Let's get...

a10a-1025539.speaker: Cernan (in Snoopy)
a10a-1025539.text: It's banging around in deadband.

a10a-1025539.speaker: Stafford (in Snoopy)
a10a-1025539.text: Right on.

a10a-1025539.speaker: Cernan (in Snoopy)
a10a-1025539.text: OK, let's go track that mother. OK, at minus 33 minutes, you want to be calling up - OK, get your Rendezvous Radar breaker Closed.

a10a-1025539.speaker: Stafford (in Snoopy)
a10a-1025539.text: AC Rendezvous Radar breaker, Closed. OK, you want to give me - I don't know what the AGS thinks where we are.

a10a-1025539.speaker: Cernan (in Snoopy)
a10a-1025539.text: OK, right. Here's what the AGS thinks we're at, babe.

a10a-1025539.speaker: Stafford (in Snoopy)
a10a-1025539.text: AGS - We're not moving.

a10a-1025539.speaker: Duke
a10a-1025539.text: [Garble] Houston. Over.

a10a-1025539.speaker: Cernan (in Snoopy)
a10a-1025539.text: That's where we think we are.

a10a-1025539.speaker: Stafford (in Snoopy)
a10a-1025539.text: Go ahead, Houston. This is Snoopy.

a10a-1025539.speaker: Duke
a10a-1025539.text: Roger. We think we can help you psyche out your problem there at staging. It looked like the Mode Control switch was in Auto instead of Att Hold. Over.

a10a-1025539.speaker: Stafford (in Snoopy)
a10a-1025539.text: God damn! OK. We'll try to recollect it. I thought we went right through our checklist, as prescribed, but if you've got telemetry. That'll sure help.

a10a-1025539.speaker: Cernan (in Snoopy)
a10a-1025539.text: OK. You got your Rendezvous Radar breakers closed Tom?

a10a-1025539.speaker: Stafford (in Snoopy)
a10a-1025539.text: Yes.

a10a-1025539.speaker: Cernan (in Snoopy)
a10a-1025539.text: Huh?

a10a-1025539.speaker: Stafford (in Snoopy)
a10a-1025539.text: Yep.

a10a-1025539.speaker: Cernan (in Snoopy)
a10a-1025539.text: That's where the AGS think it is.

a10a-1025539.speaker: Stafford (in Snoopy)
a10a-1025539.text: God...

a10a-1025539.speaker: Duke
a10a-1025539.text: Roger.

a10a-1025539.speaker: Cernan (in Snoopy)
a10a-1025539.text: Hello, Houston. The results of the AOT alignment. Do you read? OK. Plus 4 balls 4; gyro torquing angles are 0, - plus 00311, plus 00121, and plus 00081, and the star check, put her right in the center again.

a10a-1025539.speaker: Duke
a10a-1025539.text: Roger. We copy.

a10a-1025539.speaker: Young
a10a-1025539.text: Snoopy, we're going to acquire - acquire you on VHF again.

a10a-1025539.speaker: Cernan (in Snoopy)
a10a-1025539.text: OK. We'll be quiet, John.

a10a-1025539.speaker: Stafford (in Snoopy)
a10a-1025539.text: OK. How didn't we have that in Attitude Hold?

a10a-1025539.speaker: Cernan (in Snoopy)
a10a-1025539.text: I thought we did, babe. Shh. Be quiet while he's talk-acquiring. He can hear us hot mike.

a10a-1025539.speaker: Stafford (in Snoopy)
a10a-1025539.text: Yes.

a10a-1025539.speaker: Duke
a10a-1025539.text: Snoop, Houston. We noticed on your checklist that minus 14 minutes prior to - prior to insertion, we have an omission on the Mode Control switch. It doesn't call out its position there, and we think that's where we ran astray. Over.

a10a-1025539.speaker: Stafford (in Snoopy)
a10a-1025539.text: I'm ready. I got him here, Gene-o. Go to P20

a10a-1025539.speaker: Cernan (in Snoopy)
a10a-1025539.text: You got him in Slew? OK.

a10a-1025539.speaker: Duke
a10a-1025539.text: Snoop, Houston. Over.

a10a-1025539.speaker: Stafford (in Snoopy)
a10a-1025539.text: Go ahead, Houston.

a10a-1025539.speaker: Duke
a10a-1025539.text: Roger, Tom. Would you like some further amplification on the staging problem? We think the error came at minus 14 minutes [before the insertion burn] where we failed to call out the AGS Mode Control switch into ATT Hold. Over.

a10a-1025539.speaker: Stafford (in Snoopy)
a10a-1025539.text: OK.

a10a-1025539.speaker: Cernan (in Snoopy)
a10a-1025539.text: Bitch it. It just won't acquire for us, Tom. Go into - go into - go into Slew and track it again.

a10a-1025539.speaker: Stafford (in Snoopy)
a10a-1025539.text: Roger.

a10a-1025539.speaker: Young
a10a-1025539.text: OK. I'm coming around now, you guys. I'm probably not pointed at you right this second.

a10a-1025539.speaker: Stafford (in Snoopy)
a10a-1025539.text: Roger, I wondered what happened. We were locked on solid, and the radar slowly faded out. Now it's trying to come in, John, as you pitch up.

a10a-1025539.speaker: Young
a10a-1025539.text: OK.

a10a-1025539.speaker: Stafford (in Snoopy)
a10a-1025539.text: Keep going. The strength is building.

a10a-1025539.speaker: Cernan (in Snoopy)
a10a-1025539.text: Minus 30 minutes [to CSI burn], we need a range rate hack.

a10a-1025539.speaker: Stafford (in Snoopy)
a10a-1025539.text: OK. you ready to go now? Auto? LGC? Ready?

a10a-1025539.speaker: Cernan (in Snoopy)
a10a-1025539.text: Yes.

a10a-1025539.speaker: Stafford & Cernan (in Snoopy)
a10a-1025539.text: [Garble]. There it goes.

a10a-1025539.speaker: Young
a10a-1025539.text: That's more like it.

a10a-1025539.speaker: Stafford (in Snoopy)
a10a-1025539.text: OK. Weve got a solid lock on it now, John, in P20.

a10a-1025539.speaker: Young
a10a-1025539.text: Would you believe this thing was giving you a range in half steps?

a10a-1025539.speaker: Stafford (in Snoopy)
a10a-1025539.text: Yeah.

a10o-1025753.speaker: Duke
a10o-1025753.text: Charlie Brown, Houston. We recommend for your next maneuver that you load the DAP with a half a degree per second. We see 0.2 (degree per second) now. Over.

a10o-1025753.speaker: Young
a10o-1025753.text: OK. Roger. I'm going to do that.

a10o-1025753.speaker: Cernan (in Snoopy)
a10o-1025753.text: Let's go up and get him.

a10o-1025753.speaker: Stafford (in Snoopy)
a10o-1025753.text: Yes, I'd still like to know what caused that.

a10o-1025753.speaker: Cernan (in Snoopy)
a10o-1025753.text: I would too. You got your other breaker Closed, Rendezvous Radar?

a10o-1025753.speaker: Cernan (in Snoopy)
a10o-1025753.text: I don't know what the hell that was, but a - that's better.

a10o-1025753.speaker: Cernan (in Snoopy)
a10o-1025753.text: OK, Tom. You can pull your circuit breakers.

a10o-1025753.speaker: Young
a10o-1025753.text: Houston. Is he in a 283 by 15.3 [nautical miles, 524 x 28.4 km]? Over.

a10o-1025753.speaker: Cernan (in Snoopy)
a10o-1025753.text: OK, we'll make a quick alignment, here.

a10o-1025753.speaker: Duke
a10o-1025753.text: Negative. We've got him at 46.7 by 11.0 [nautical miles, 86.5 x 20.3 km]. Over.

a10o-1025753.speaker: Young
a10o-1025753.text: Roger. I must have loaded this number backwards. This P76 number backwards.

a10o-1025753.speaker: Duke
a10o-1025753.text: Roger. We'll send you a TM [telemetry] vector in just a moment. Charlie Brown, we've got your LM vector coming. Stand by.

a10o-1025753.speaker: Cernan (in Snoopy)
a10o-1025753.text: Tom, set the Elapsed Timer down on - down on CSI [Coelliptic Sequence Initiation]. Here's CSI time because, remember, we got to get that backup mark at 30 minutes [before the CSI burn].

a10o-1025753.speaker: Cernan (in Snoopy)
a10o-1025753.text: And 103:45, we don't have a lot of time. Only got 15 minutes to make this alignment, so I'm going to make it only three marks.

a10o-1025753.speaker: Cernan (in Snoopy)
a10o-1025753.text: OK, you can leave it Go, cause I'm going to call up the...

a10o-1025753.speaker: Cernan (in Snoopy)
a10o-1025753.text: I don't know what it is here, babe.

a10o-1025753.speaker: Young
a10o-1025753.text: ... what have we got right now?

a10o-1025753.speaker: Cernan (in Snoopy)
a10o-1025753.text: You don't have to maneuver; I got to go get a star [for P52].

a10o-1025753.speaker: Young
a10o-1025753.text: We're in P00 and Accept right now.

a10o-1025753.speaker: Duke
a10o-1025753.text: Roger. Copy, Charlie Brown. Stand by. Be a while.

a10o-1025753.speaker: Young
a10o-1025753.text: OK. Well, I can do realign in the meantime then.

a10o-1025753.speaker: Cernan (in Snoopy)
a10o-1025753.text: OK, Tom? Can I go get it?

a10o-1025753.speaker: Stafford (in Snoopy)
a10o-1025753.text: OK, you're in, what's - what's it? 351? - 35 - yes, it'll pitch you down quite a bit. You can go get it.

a10o-1025753.speaker: Duke
a10o-1025753.text: Charlie Brown, Houston. Stand by 30 seconds. We'll have the load to you. Over.

a10o-1025753.speaker: Cernan (in Snoopy)
a10o-1025753.text: OK, and here's the time, if you can set that elapsed timer, because we got to get that, bagged - that 30 minute mark that we always miss.

a10o-1025753.speaker: Cernan (in Snoopy)
a10o-1025753.text: That was the Earth in there?

a10o-1025753.speaker: Cernan (in Snoopy)
a10o-1025753.text: Right, right down here. Right down here on the left.

a10o-1025753.speaker: Young
a10o-1025753.text: Boy, Houston. That's outstanding. Wish we had done that when we were fooling with the GSFC [Goddard Space Flight Center].

a10o-1025753.speaker: Duke
a10o-1025753.text: Roger. Charlie Brown, you can take the computer back. We're done with the load. Over.

a10o-1025753.speaker: Cernan (in Snoopy)
a10o-1025753.text: There ain't any question we don't have an ascent - or descent stage. How's the chamber pressure and everything holding?

a10o-1025753.speaker: Duke
a10o-1025753.text: Charlie Brown, Houston. We're through with the computer. It's yours. Over.

a10o-1025753.speaker: Cernan (in Snoopy)
a10o-1025753.text: You know. Yes, cabin chamber pressure.

a10o-1025753.speaker: Cernan (in Snoopy)
a10o-1025753.text: Houston, we're going to Omnis. [Garble] P52 the rest of it.

a10o-1025753.speaker: Duke
a10o-1025753.text: Roger. We copy. We want Aft Omnis. Aft Omnis. Over.

a10o-1025753.speaker: Duke
a10o-1025753.text: Snoop, Houston. Aft Omnis, if you read. Over.

a10o-1025753.speaker: Young
a10o-1025753.text: They want you on Aft Omnis, Snoopy.

a10o-1025753.speaker: Young
a10o-1025753.text: Houston wants you on Aft Omnis, Gene.

a10o-1025753.speaker: Cernan (in Snoopy)
a10o-1025753.text: Tell him that's where I am.

a10o-1025753.speaker: Young
a10o-1025753.text: OK. He's on Omnis, Houston. He's on Aft Omnis.

a10o-1025753.speaker: Duke
a10o-1025753.text: Roger. We copy, Charlie Brown. Are you reading him now, Charlie Brown?

a10o-1025753.speaker: Cernan (in Snoopy)
a10o-1025753.text: Altair like we called for in the book.

a10o-1025753.speaker: Stafford (in Snoopy)
a10o-1025753.text: Good. OK. Yes, it's looking good.

a10o-1025753.speaker: Stafford (in Snoopy)
a10o-1025753.text: Beautiful! Why don't you write that down? What were the stars, 40...

a10o-1030758.speaker: Cernan (in Snoopy)
a10o-1030758.text: OK, let's go track that mother. OK, at minus 33 minutes, you want to be calling up - OK, get your Rendezvous Radar breaker Closed.

a10o-1030758.speaker: Stafford (in Snoopy)
a10o-1030758.text: AC Rendezvous Radar breaker, Closed. OK, you want to give me - I don't know what the AGS thinks where we are.

a10o-1030758.speaker: Cernan (in Snoopy)
a10o-1030758.text: OK, right. Here's what the AGS thinks we're at, babe.

a10o-1030758.speaker: Cernan (in Snoopy)
a10o-1030758.text: That's where we think we are.

a10o-1030758.speaker: Stafford (in Snoopy)
a10o-1030758.text: Go ahead, Houston. This is Snoopy.

a10o-1030758.speaker: Duke
a10o-1030758.text: Roger. We think we can help you psyche out your problem there at staging. It looked like the Mode Control switch was in Auto instead of Att Hold. Over.

a10o-1030758.speaker: Stafford (in Snoopy)
a10o-1030758.text: God damn! OK. We'll try to recollect it. I thought we went right through our checklist, as prescribed, but if you've got telemetry. That'll sure help.

a10o-1030758.speaker: Cernan (in Snoopy)
a10o-1030758.text: OK. You got your Rendezvous Radar breakers closed Tom?

a10o-1030758.speaker: Cernan (in Snoopy)
a10o-1030758.text: That's where the AGS think it is.

a10o-1030758.speaker: Cernan (in Snoopy)
a10o-1030758.text: Hello, Houston. The results of the AOT alignment. Do you read? OK. Plus 4 balls 4; gyro torquing angles are 0, - plus 00311, plus 00121, and plus 00081, and the star check, put her right in the center again.

a10o-1030758.speaker: Young
a10o-1030758.text: Snoopy, we're going to acquire - acquire you on VHF again.

a10o-1030758.speaker: Stafford (in Snoopy)
a10o-1030758.text: OK. How didn't we have that in Attitude Hold?

a10o-1030758.speaker: Cernan (in Snoopy)
a10o-1030758.text: I thought we did, babe. Shh. Be quiet while he's talk-acquiring. He can hear us hot mike.

a10o-1030758.speaker: Duke
a10o-1030758.text: Snoop, Houston. We noticed on your checklist that minus 14 minutes prior to - prior to insertion, we have an omission on the Mode Control switch. It doesn't call out its position there, and we think that's where we ran astray. Over.

a10o-1030758.speaker: Stafford (in Snoopy)
a10o-1030758.text: I'm ready. I got him here, Gene-o. Go to P20

a10o-1030758.speaker: Cernan (in Snoopy)
a10o-1030758.text: You got him in Slew? OK.

a10o-1030758.speaker: Duke
a10o-1030758.text: Roger, Tom. Would you like some further amplification on the staging problem? We think the error came at minus 14 minutes [before the insertion burn] where we failed to call out the AGS Mode Control switch into ATT Hold. Over.

a10o-1030758.speaker: Cernan (in Snoopy)
a10o-1030758.text: Bitch it. It just won't acquire for us, Tom. Go into - go into - go into Slew and track it again.

a10o-1030758.speaker: Young
a10o-1030758.text: OK. I'm coming around now, you guys. I'm probably not pointed at you right this second.

a10o-1030758.speaker: Stafford (in Snoopy)
a10o-1030758.text: Roger, I wondered what happened. We were locked on solid, and the radar slowly faded out. Now it's trying to come in, John, as you pitch up.

a10o-1030758.speaker: Stafford (in Snoopy)
a10o-1030758.text: Keep going. The strength is building.

a10o-1030758.speaker: Cernan (in Snoopy)
a10o-1030758.text: Minus 30 minutes [to CSI burn], we need a range rate hack.

a10o-1030758.speaker: Stafford (in Snoopy)
a10o-1030758.text: OK. you ready to go now? Auto? LGC? Ready?

a10o-1030758.speaker: Stafford (in Snoopy)
a10o-1030758.text: OK. Weve got a solid lock on it now, John, in P20.

a10o-1030758.speaker: Young
a10o-1030758.text: Would you believe this thing was giving you a range in half steps?

a10o-1030758.speaker: Cernan (in Snoopy)
a10o-1030758.text: OK, we can expect that. Let's take it.

a10o-1030758.speaker: Cernan (in Snoopy)
a10o-1030758.text: We need that range rate at 30 minutes.

a10o-1030758.speaker: Stafford (in Snoopy)
a10o-1030758.text: No. Don't do it Verb... And again: on our first Mark, we see these large updates. We'll reject it and pick up on our second one. Range rate, huh? It's gotta be 290.

a10o-1030758.speaker: Duke
a10o-1030758.text: Hello, Snoop. Houston. We have a CSI update for you. Over.

a10o-1030758.speaker: Duke
a10o-1030758.text: ...21 0100, plus 0453, plus 000 106, plus 453, plus 000, plus 005. Standing by for your readback. Over.

a10o-1030758.speaker: Cernan (in Snoopy)
a10o-1030758.text: Give me Noun 81, again. I don't think I got enough numbers.

a10o-1030758.speaker: Duke
a10o-1030758.text: Roger. Noun 81 is plus 0453 plus 000. Over.

a10o-1030758.speaker: Cernan (in Snoopy)
a10o-1030758.text: Stand by, Charlie. I'll give you a readback in a second. This is in CSI and TPI time we'll use. Is that correct?

a10o-1030758.speaker: Cernan (in Snoopy)
a10o-1030758.text: How's the - how's that range look, Tom.

a10o-1030758.speaker: Young
a10o-1030758.text: What time did they give you, Gene?

a10o-1032126.text: Shall we see what ours is? We ought to be looking at it in about 15 minutes.

a10o-1032126.speaker: Cernan (in Snoopy)
a10o-1032126.text: John, give me your CSM Y-dot again.

a10o-1032126.speaker: Duke
a10o-1032126.text: Snoopy, Houston. We'll have LOS at 103:36 and AOS at 104:25. Over.

a10o-1032126.speaker: Cernan (in Snoopy)
a10o-1032126.text: OK. Verb 9 - Verb 90 Enter [garble] 3, Enter. Plus 00045, Enter. 0.054...

a10o-1032126.speaker: Mission Control
a10o-1032126.text: Showing range now, 165 miles (306 km) as Snoopy closes on Charlie Brown .

a10o-1032126.speaker: Cernan (in Snoopy)
a10o-1032126.text: ... 0 .60, Enter. We're looking right up both balls. We're looking up - we're looking up AGS and PGNS, babe. Of course, I aligned the AGS to the PGNS after the alignment, but that damn alignment was right on. It was right on.

a10o-1032126.speaker: Cernan (in Snoopy)
a10o-1032126.text: No, that was the time, just coming back at me.

a10o-1032126.speaker: Duke
a10o-1032126.text: Snoop, Houston. If you get a chance, pass to Charlie Brown, we've lost his TM and voice, and we'll see him AOS at 104:24. Over.

a10o-1032126.speaker: Stafford (in Snoopy)
a10o-1032126.text: This is Snoopy. Roger. Charlie Brown, this is Snoop, You'll have acquisition at 104:24. Over.

a10o-1032126.speaker: Stafford (in Snoopy)
a10o-1032126.text: Roger. You'll be picking up Houston at 104:24. And our out - of - and out-of-plane was 4.1 and we're tracking...

a10o-1032126.speaker: Stafford (in Snoopy)
a10o-1032126.text: In the other direction, and we're tracking right up the center line here. But we'll just ignore the first out of-plane correction. Over.

a10o-1032126.speaker: Cernan (in Snoopy)
a10o-1032126.text: We need another mark at 10 minutes.

a10o-1032126.speaker: Cernan (in Snoopy)
a10o-1032126.text: Houston, we've got you on Omnis. You hear that music, Tom? That crazy whistling?

a10o-1032126.speaker: Duke
a10o-1032126.text: Snoop, Houston. As you go over the hill, you're looking good. Were all Go here.

a10o-1032126.speaker: Stafford (in Snoopy)
a10o-1032126.text: Roger, Charlie. And we'll hit Proceed at 12 minutes. Everything looking good, we're going to ignore the out-of-plane correction at CSI. Over.

a10o-1032126.speaker: Young
a10o-1032126.text: You're not going to do the out-of-plane at CSI?

a10o-1032126.speaker: Duke
a10o-1032126.text: Snoop, Houston. Say again. We didn't copy.

a10o-1032126.speaker: Stafford (in Snoopy)
a10o-1032126.text: Roger. With everything looking good. We're going to ignore the out-of-plane correction at CSI. Over.

a10o-1032126.speaker: Duke
a10o-1032126.text: Roger. Understand you are not doing the CSI -the out-of-plane. Over.

a10o-1032126.speaker: Young
a10o-1032126.text: ...I don't if this is [garble] or not. Wait till I get ground after CSI.

a10o-1033417.speaker: Cernan (in Snoopy)
a10o-1033417.text: OK, that's all right. We know which way we're going to burn it.

a10o-1033417.speaker: Stafford (in Snoopy)
a10o-1033417.text: We reverse his signs for out-of-plane, right.

a10o-1033417.speaker: Young
a10o-1033417.text: I'd like to know what you guys got.

a10o-1033417.speaker: Cernan (in Snoopy)
a10o-1033417.text: It's coming up right now. Plus 45.3 (fps, 13.8 m/s).

a10o-1033417.speaker: Cernan (in Snoopy)
a10o-1033417.text: OK, so we'll burn our 45.3 (fps, 13.8 m/s). That's exactly what Houston gave us.

a10o-1033417.speaker: Duke
a10o-1033417.text: Hey Snoop, CapCom. We understand you're burning 45.3 (fps, 13.8 m/s). Your FIDO's grinning.

a10o-1033417.speaker: Cernan (in Snoopy)
a10o-1033417.text: OK, Tom. The clock set up? In 10 minutes I need a range rate mark.

a10o-1033417.speaker: Cernan (in Snoopy)
a10o-1033417.text: We'll see how the backup's come up.

a10o-1033417.speaker: Stafford (in Snoopy)
a10o-1033417.text: OK. Mark it. It was 103 feet per second (31.4 m/s).

a10o-1033417.speaker: Mission Control
a10o-1033417.text: This is Apollo Control at 103 hours, 36 minutes and we've had Loss Of Signal. As you heard the crew talking there right before LOS, the on-board solution for the concentric sequence initiation burn agrees exactly with the ground solution that we passed up to them, 45.3 feet per second (13.8 m/s). This burn coming at 103 hours, 45 minutes, 54 seconds while Snoopy is behind the Moon. This CSI burn is designed to make the LM's orbit such that the Terminal Phase Initiation will come at the proper time and under the proper conditions after the Constant Delta Height burn. We're actually programming

a10o-1033417.speaker: Cernan (onboard Snoopy)
a10o-1033417.text: OK, babe, you can take the computer and go into Verb 47 - proceed out of there, and go to Verb 47. And I'll go to update here.

a10o-1033417.speaker: Stafford (onboard Snoopy)
a10o-1033417.text: I got to go to zero, zero (P00), don't I. Enter.

a10o-1033417.speaker: Cernan (onboard Snoopy)
a10o-1033417.text: I've already been in PC. I'm - I'll figure this one out.

a10o-1033417.speaker: Stafford (onboard Snoopy)
a10o-1033417.text: Think we need to put on the helmets and gloves for this one?

a10o-1033417.speaker: Cernan (onboard Snoopy)
a10o-1033417.text: I don't think - I don't want to.

a10o-1033417.speaker: Stafford (onboard Snoopy)
a10o-1033417.text: Let's me try it Just to see what it's like. That's not really a big thing with helmets and gloves.

a10o-1033417.speaker: Cernan (onboard Snoopy)
a10o-1033417.text: Am I glad we didn't torque up the platform.

a10o-1033417.speaker: Stafford (onboard Snoopy)
a10o-1033417.text: How in the hell did we miss that? Still don't know.

a10o-1033417.speaker: Cernan (onboard Snoopy)
a10o-1033417.text: We had to have someone on our side that time.

a10o-1033417.speaker: Cernan (onboard Snoopy)
a10o-1033417.text: Yes, I need - You go into 41.

a10o-1033417.speaker: Stafford (onboard Snoopy)
a10o-1033417.text: You ready for an Auto maneuver?

a10o-1033417.speaker: Stafford (onboard Snoopy)
a10o-1033417.text: OK. OK, I'll go ahead and open the Rendezvous Radar circuit breaker.

a10o-1033417.speaker: Stafford (onboard Snoopy)
a10o-1033417.text: Open the Rendezvous Radars. We're going to pitch down.

a10o-1033417.speaker: Cernan (onboard Snoopy)
a10o-1033417.text: Didn't it? We still got thrusters?

a10o-1033417.speaker: Cernan (onboard Snoopy)
a10o-1033417.text: Man, I tell you, it just got quiet.

a10o-1033417.speaker: Stafford (onboard Snoopy)
a10o-1033417.text: John, we're going to pitch down and have our X-axis towards you. You may lose our flashing light.

a10o-1033417.speaker: Cernan (onboard Snoopy)
a10o-1033417.text: John, do you know what we're going to burn now? 43.5 - 45.3, 0, and 0.

a10o-1033417.speaker: Stafford (onboard Snoopy)
a10o-1033417.text: Those numbers again, Gene-o, are what?

a10o-1033417.speaker: Cernan (onboard Snoopy)
a10o-1033417.text: I tell you, John, that music is really weird.

a10o-1033417.speaker: Young
a10o-1033417.text: [Garble] Think we're going to get it on the front side?

a10o-1033417.speaker: Cernan (onboard Snoopy)
a10o-1033417.text: I know it. You don't suppose something, huh?

a10o-1033417.speaker: Cernan (onboard Snoopy)
a10o-1033417.text: No one will believe us. Okay, Tom, we're set until 35 minutes - 35 seconds. And we're at 4 minutes and 35 from the burn.

a10o-1033417.speaker: Stafford (onboard Snoopy)
a10o-1033417.text: We pitch down - know it's right, but why should I have him out there?

a10o-1033417.speaker: Cernan (onboard Snoopy)
a10o-1033417.text: You're not looking at 105 Inertial. Much better.

a10o-1033417.speaker: Stafford (onboard Snoopy)
a10o-1033417.text: But why should I have down...

a10o-1033417.speaker: Cernan (onboard Snoopy)
a10o-1033417.text: You've got him below you? Where is he?

a10o-1033417.speaker: Stafford (onboard Snoopy)
a10o-1033417.text: Maybe it's a reflection. You got him out there?

a10o-1033417.speaker: Stafford (onboard Snoopy)
a10o-1033417.text: If you didn't have an Orb Rate ball, you couldn't tell where you...

a10o-1033417.speaker: Cernan (onboard Snoopy)
a10o-1033417.text: You wouldn't know where the hell you were. I'm looking at 270, and my Orb Rate ball, according to this thing, is pretty good, Tom. And we just updated it: 258.

a10o-1033417.speaker: Young
a10o-1033417.text: OK. I show you 3 minutes to burn.

a10o-1033417.speaker: Cernan (onboard Snoopy)
a10o-1033417.text: OK, I'll give you mark at 3 minutes, John - 7 seconds.

a10o-1033417.speaker: Stafford (onboard Snoopy)
a10o-1033417.text: That's weird. Why should I see him down there?

a10o-1033417.speaker: Cernan (onboard Snoopy)
a10o-1033417.text: OK Tom, we're going to use the Ascent Feed on this one.

a10o-1033417.speaker: Cernan (onboard Snoopy)
a10o-1033417.text: The AGS is loaded and counting. When you start, I am going to open the ascents and close the solenoids, so I'll get them closed in plenty of time. I'm going to start closing them at 10 feet per second.

a10o-1033417.speaker: Cernan (onboard Snoopy)
a10o-1033417.text: Hey, Tom, you want me to trim final?

a10o-1033417.speaker: Cernan (onboard Snoopy)
a10o-1033417.text: Boy, those are hard to reach. Coming up on 1 minute, John.

a10a-1163306.speaker: Cernan
a10a-1163306.text: ...I've got Battery A on the line, and I'm purging the fuel cells at this time. I've gone through O 2 on 3, and I'm down, I'm on 2 now.

a10a-1163306.speaker: Lousma
a10a-1163306.text: Roger. We copy.

a10a-1163306.speaker: Cernan
a10a-1163306.text: How are things in Houston this morning?

a10a-1163306.speaker: Lousma
a10a-1163306.text: Everything's great. Everybody's raving about your performance yesterday and very happy. No doubt you guys are equally well pleased.

a10a-1163306.speaker: Cernan
a10a-1163306.text: ... good day, Jack. Pretty challenging and pretty satisfying really, when we look back at it.

a10a-1163306.speaker: Lousma
a10a-1163306.text: Apollo 10, this is Houston. You got up kind of early this morning. We were going to let you sleep in for quite a while yet. We've got a little information that will be of interest to you. Your consumables are away ahead of schedule as usual. We have you in a 65.9 by 55.6 orbit [122.0 x 103.0 km]. Your spacecraft looks real good. You might be interested to know that the LM ascent stage is 23,000 miles [42,500 km] from the Moon heading straight up at 5,400 feet per second [1,645 m/s], and haven't quite been able to tell yet whether it's going into orbit around the Sun or if it's going to head st

a10a-1163306.speaker: Cernan
a10a-1163306.text: Hot, isn't he? 23,000 miles [42,500 km] away?

a10a-1163306.speaker: Lousma
a10a-1163306.text: Yes. Old Snoop's really moving out.

a10a-1163306.speaker: Cernan
a10a-1163306.text: I hope I didn't leave my watch aboard there.

a10a-1163306.speaker: Cernan
a10a-1163306.text: You can still track him, can you?

a10a-1163306.speaker: Lousma
a10a-1163306.text: We're still tracking him.

a10a-1163306.speaker: Cernan
a10a-1163306.text: You can?

a10a-1163306.speaker: Lousma
a10a-1163306.text: That's affirmative. We're still tracking him and checking the LGC, and so forth.

a10a-1163306.speaker: Lousma
a10a-1163306.text: Matter of fact, we just got an E-Memory dump of him. Oh...

a10a-1163306.speaker: Cernan
a10a-1163306.text: You got an E-Memory dump?

a10a-1163306.speaker: Lousma
a10a-1163306.text: That's affirmative. Old Snoop, he doesn't give up.

a10a-1163306.speaker: Lousma
a10a-1163306.text: I've...

a10a-1163306.speaker: Cernan
a10a-1163306.text: Holy smoley!

a10a-1163306.speaker: Lousma
a10a-1163306.text: And, 10, this is Houston. I've got a congratulatory message here. It says, "Congratulations on doing what I've been trying to do for a long time." Signed, Red Baron.

a10a-1163306.speaker: Cernan
a10a-1163306.text: Beautiful.

a10a-1163306.speaker: Cernan
a10a-1163306.text: Houston, I've got a status report for you.

a10a-1163306.speaker: Lousma
a10a-1163306.text: Roger. Go ahead.

a10a-1163306.speaker: Cernan
a10a-1163306.text: We're all feeling good, and were about ready to [garble]. We got in about 5 to 6 hours pretty fair sleep. The rads: CDR is 26040; the chimps (CMP) is 05309 [garble] and 15041. Cycling the fans at this time [garble] purge.

a10a-1163306.speaker: Lousma
a10a-1163306.text: Apollo 10, Houston. You're coming in very broken. We're going to have to repeat the report. Wait one until we check out the network. Over.

a10a-1163306.speaker: Cernan
a10a-1163306.text: How do you read me now, Jack?

a10a-1163306.speaker: Lousma
a10a-1163306.text: You're cutting out. Let's attempt to fix it up with the network, and then we'll give you a call in a minute.

a10a-1163306.speaker: Cernan
a10a-1163306.text: Roger.

a10a-1163306.speaker: Lousma
a10a-1163306.text: Okay, Apollo 10. This is Houston. We're ready to try it again. Go ahead with your crew status, please.

a10a-1163306.speaker: Cernan
a10a-1163306.text: Okay. We got 5 or 6 pretty good hours sleep last night. Tom's fixing chow, John's taking targets of opportunity, and our rad readings are as follows in order: 26040, 05309, and 15041. The purge is complete, and the fans have been cycled.

a10a-1163306.speaker: Lousma
a10a-1163306.text: Okay, Gene-o. We copy your 5 to 6 hours, 26040, 05309, 15041. And we'd like you to operate in BD roll today. Over.

a10a-1163306.speaker: Cernan
a10a-1163306.text: You'd like us to operate in BD roll today.

a10a-1163306.speaker: Lousma
a10a-1163306.text: That's affirmative.

a10a-1164635.speaker: Lousma
a10a-1164635.text: Standby.

a10a-1164635.speaker: Lousma
a10a-1164635.text: Apollo 10, Houston. When you're ready, I have some updates. And we have the morning newspaper.

a10a-1164635.speaker: Cernan
a10a-1164635.text: Jack, stand by on that for a minute. We'll all get on a head set.

a10a-1164635.speaker: Cernan
a10a-1164635.text: Hey, Jack.

a10a-1164635.speaker: Lousma
a10a-1164635.text: Go ahead.

a10a-1164635.speaker: Cernan
a10a-1164635.text: Okay. In doing a little troubleshooting on our LM 70mm Hasselblad, it turned out that the batteries are good, but the LM, or the lens - you cannot take the lens off. And what I really anticipated probably is that little docking pin on the lens is jammed. We never did have it off, so it wasn't a case of putting it on wrong. But it appears to be jammed, and I can't get the lens off at all. Do you have an idea that might help us troubleshoot this one?

a10a-1164635.speaker: Lousma
a10a-1164635.text: Okay. Understand.

a10a-1164635.speaker: Young
a10a-1164635.text: Want me to break out my tool kit, Jack, and take that thing apart!

a10a-1164635.speaker: Lousma
a10a-1164635.text: 10, Houston. We'll get an answer to you on which camera procedure to use. We're working on that now.

a10a-1164635.speaker: Cernan
a10a-1164635.text: Hey, Jack. I think that's that it is, though, since I can't take the lens off and the batteries are all good. It appears that it may be jammed.

a10a-1164635.speaker: Lousma
a10a-1164635.text: Roger. Thank you.

a10a-1164635.speaker: Cernan
a10a-1164635.text: Okay, Jack. Tell the camera experts to forget it. I got it psyched out. I had to spin that gear wheel around until I got the flat side up, and now it appears to work. But it was apparently some sort of self-jamming capability.

a10a-1164635.speaker: Lousma
a10a-1164635.text: Roger. We copy. Neatly devised.

a10a-1164635.speaker: Cernan
a10a-1164635.text: Hold off. Wait a minute. Let it work for 1 minute, and let me see what happens.

a10a-1164635.speaker: Cernan
a10a-1164635.text: Hey, Jack.

a10a-1164635.speaker: Lousma
a10a-1164635.text: Go ahead.

a10a-1164635.speaker: Cernan
a10a-1164635.text: Okay, here's the story on the camera.

a10a-1164635.speaker: Lousma
a10a-1164635.text: Say again, please.

a10a-1164635.speaker: Cernan
a10a-1164635.text: There's a gear - Okay. I've got a story on the camera. I need some help, I guess, all right?

a10a-1164635.speaker: Lousma
a10a-1164635.text: Roger. Go ahead.

a10a-1164635.speaker: Cernan
a10a-1164635.text: So listen for a second. Okay, that gear on the back, the gear on the back when you take the magazine off, this is on the camera base itself. It's got teeth on except for one area where there's a flat spot. If you turn the gear over, push the gear over so that the flat spot is face up, I can do two things. I can snap the picture and/or take the lens off. But as soon as I snap one picture, the gear does not rotate and I cannot take the lens off. The lens does not lock and the camera will not cycle any more after that. Now this occurs both with and without a back on.

a10a-1164635.speaker: Lousma
a10a-1164635.text: Okay, Gene. We copy that. And we'll get to work on it.

a10a-1164635.speaker: Cernan
a10a-1164635.text: Okay. Thank you, Jack.

a10a-1164635.speaker: Young
a10a-1164635.text: Remember, Jack, the right kind of picture might find out how all this started.

a10a-1165711.speaker: Cernan
a10a-1165711.text: Houston, this is 10. One little bit of further information on that camera base is the fact that, when I got it cocked for that one shot it'll take, that gear does not rotate, so as to turn the film pack over. It doesn't even rotate without a film pack in it.

a10a-1165711.speaker: Lousma
a10a-1165711.text: Okay. we copy that the gear won't rotate with or without a film pack in it after taking a picture. Is that affirmative?

a10a-1165711.speaker: Cernan
a10a-1165711.text: Yes. And I can send it through one cycle myself and it's all recocked. And I have to do that with a pencil to wedge that gear around and it's recocked. And then it works fine for one more shot and that's it.

a10a-1165711.speaker: Lousma
a10a-1165711.text: Roger. We copy that the gear cycles - has to be cycled manually as opposed to turning automatically after taking a picture.

a10a-1165711.speaker: Cernan
a10a-1165711.text: I'll play with it a little while longer and see if there's something screwed up in this lens thing.

a10a-1165711.speaker: Lousma
a10a-1165711.text: Roger. We have people working on it.

a10a-1165711.speaker: Cernan
a10a-1165711.text: Roger. One final little bit more of information. When I did [garble] recocked that gear took the lens off, rather, and recocked the gear, I get a one-shot affair, and it appears that the mechanism that's jamming is not in the lens, and it's obviously not in the pack, but it's somewhere in the body of the camera.

a10a-1165711.speaker: Lousma
a10a-1165711.text: Apollo 10, Houston. Could you give us an inventory of which cameras you have working and what ones you're having problems with at this time. Over.

a10a-1165711.speaker: Cernan
a10a-1165711.text: Okay. We've got one 70-millimeter camera with all three lenses, LM lens, two CSM lenses, and I guess we've got two sequence cameras working.

a10a-1165711.speaker: Lousma
a10a-1165711.text: Roger. One 70-millimeter and two sequence cameras.

a10a-1165711.speaker: Mission Control
a10a-1165711.text: This is Apollo Control during the break in communications here; the crew is apparently getting ready for breakfast. We'll come back and review the activities since they woke up. They woke up almost on the preflight time line, however, it had been planned that they would sleep in another 2 revolutions, or approximately 4 hours later than the normal time. A lengthy discussion took place between Spacecraft Communicator Jack Lousma and LM Pilot Eugene Cernan on how to troubleshoot the jammed still camera aboard the spacecraft, the one that was taken aboard the LM for the low altitude lunar photogr

a10a-1170954.speaker: Lousma
a10a-1170954.text: Apollo 10, Houston. We'll be going LOS in about 10 minutes; and I still have Rev 22 update and oblique photography update for you.

a10a-1170954.speaker: Cernan
a10a-1170954.text: Okay, Jack. I'll copy it.

a10a-1170954.speaker: Cernan
a10a-1170954.text: Go ahead, Jack. I'm ready to copy it.

a10a-1170954.speaker: Lousma
a10a-1170954.text: Okay. The map update pad REV 22: 117:22:53, 119:32:46, 118:09:03. Sunrise, 117:36:00; sunset, 118:48:26. Ready for your readback, and a go ahead on your photography update.

a10a-1170954.speaker: Cernan
a10a-1170954.text: Okay. 22: LOS, 117:22:53. 150 is 119 [garble] Sunset [garble].

a10a-1170954.speaker: Cernan
a10a-1170954.text: Houston, did you get that?

a10a-1170954.speaker: Lousma
a10a-1170954.text: Okay, 10. This is Houston. No, you were cut off part way through the readback. Start at 150, please.

a10a-1170954.speaker: Lousma
a10a-1170954.text: Okay. That's affirmative. You ready to go ahead with LS2 photography PAD:

a10a-1170954.speaker: Cernan
a10a-1170954.text: Yes. I'm ready to copy something, John - or Jack. Go ahead.

a10a-1170954.speaker: Lousma
a10a-1170954.text: Okay. LS2 PAD: f:8 is 118:28:52. T 1 is 118:33:15, with your TCA [Time of Closest Approach] at 2 minutes; f:2.8 is 118:34:15 with your TCA at 1 minute. T 2 is 118:35:15 TCA.

a10a-1170954.speaker: Cernan
a10a-1170954.text: Hey. Jack. I got that all down but I'm not sure what you all said. I'm looking for the PAD that it goes to.

a10a-1170954.speaker: Lousma
a10a-1170954.text: Okay. It's entitled. "Oblique Photography," and f:8 is camera on [time]. T 1 is start a half a degree...

a10a-1170954.speaker: Cernan
a10a-1170954.text: Yes. But what page - hey, is that - Don't we have an update here somewhere? Can you give me the page it's on?

a10a-1170954.speaker: Lousma
a10a-1170954.text: Apollo 10, Houston...

a10a-1170954.speaker: Young
a10a-1170954.text: Jack, we don't have the same...

a10a-1170954.speaker: Lousma
a10a-1170954.text: Roger. On the Flight Plan...

a10a-1170954.speaker: Young
a10a-1170954.text: Jack, can you tell them like it is in the...

a10a-1170954.speaker: Lousma
a10a-1170954.text: Roger. On the Flight Plan page 3-71 we have an, update for oblique photography. However, that format has been changed and a new format as I have given it to you.

a10a-1170954.speaker: Young
a10a-1170954.text: Well, we can't change it. Now you...

a10a-1170954.speaker: Lousma
a10a-1170954.text: 10. Houston. We'll get it back in the old format for you. I'll get...

a10a-1170954.speaker: Cernan
a10a-1170954.text: Okay. I wish you would. We don't understand the new one.

a10a-1170954.speaker: Lousma
a10a-1170954.text: Roger. We'll get it back in the old format and...

a10a-1170954.speaker: Cernan
a10a-1170954.text: I've got all the words. Jack.

a10a-1170954.speaker: Lousma
a10a-1170954.text: Okay. We'll. get it back in the old format and check with the appropriate people, and in the meantime. I have a correction on your map update PAD. You'll be crossing 150 west at 117:33:36.

a10a-1170954.speaker: Cernan
a10a-1170954.text: Yes. I guess that sounds a little bit better. Listen, while you're getting it in that old form, tell me what you told me, because we're going to lose LOS, and maybe we could do something with it here.

a10a-1170954.speaker: Lousma
a10a-1170954.text: Roger. We want the camera on f:8 at 118:28:52, and we want you to start your half-degree-per-second pitch rate at 118:33:15. And, we want you to go f:2.8 at 118:34:15. And then you can stop your pitch at 118:35:15.

a10a-1170954.speaker: Cernan
a10a-1170954.text: Okay. We'll put the camera on at f:8 at 118:28:52. We start half degree-per-second pitch rate at 118:33:15. We go to f:2.8 at 118:34:15. And then we stop our pitch at 118:35:15.

a10a-1170954.speaker: Lousma
a10a-1170954.text: That's affirmative.

a10a-1170954.speaker: Young
a10a-1170954.text: Boy, I knew you guys just couldn't resist waiting until we got airborne and then change all the formats. How about that?

a10a-1170954.speaker: Young
a10a-1170954.text: That's what we get for missing that data priority meeting you had after lift-off.

a10a-1170954.speaker: Lousma
a10a-1170954.text: Okay, Apollo 10. Houston. Before you go out of sight here, some more information on your update for ALS2. Your roll should be 180, your pitch 339, and your yaw 000. and the TCA numbers we were giving you were time-of-closest-approach, so that T 1 would be 2 minutes before closest approach. And you go to f:2.8, 1 minute before closest approach; and then T 2 , or course is time-of-closest-approach. Over.

a10a-1170954.speaker: Mission Control
a10a-1170954.text: This is Apollo Control. Apparently we have had Loss Of Signal from Apollo 10 as it went over the hill on the 21st revolution. Toward the end of that pass the spacecraft communicator Jack Lousma passed up to the crew some pointing angles and times for some stereo strip photography of landing site 2. The strips will be forward looking as they approach the landing site. The camera will be started when their landing site is first on the lunar horizon, and then the spacecraft will be pitched down to keep the landing site within the camera view until the camera is vertical to landing site 2. Most of

a10a-1170954.speaker: Stafford
a10a-1170954.text: [Garble].

a10a-1170954.speaker: Cernan
a10a-1170954.text: You're [garble].

a10a-1170954.speaker: Cernan
a10a-1170954.text: [Garble] we go ahead?

a10a-1170954.speaker: Young
a10a-1170954.text: I don't know. [Garble].

a10a-1170954.speaker: Young
a10a-1170954.text: Okay. [Garble].

a10a-1180800.speaker: Stafford
a10a-1180800.text: [Garble] oblique thing, what are we using - Did they tell us to use a 250 or an 80 [mm lens]?

a10a-1180800.speaker: Young
a10a-1180800.text: Man, it is - Here's the flattest crater over here.

a10a-1180800.speaker: Stafford
a10a-1180800.text: Oblique [garble].

a10a-1180800.speaker: Stafford
a10a-1180800.text: Yes, babe. Use the 80 and the intervalometer. Where's our intervalometer? José, why don't you get the intervalometer? Also, we need that - we need that mount. [Garble] need the mount [garble]. You know it's...

a10a-1180800.speaker: Mission Control
a10a-1180800.text: This is Apollo Control; 118 hours, 08 minutes Ground Elapsed Time. Less than a minute away now from Acquisition Of Signal as Apollo 10 comes around to the front side of the Moon on lunar revolution number 22. During this pass the crew is scheduled to do the stereo strip photography across Landing Site number 2, at which Apollo 11 likely will land. Also as the communications commence in this rev, the crew will be [giving] a consumable update. Standing by for communications to resume. A few minor changes in the Flight Plan will be read up to the crew. However it appears now that they woke up and

a10a-1180800.speaker: Lousma
a10a-1180800.text: Apollo 10, Houston. How do you read. Over.

a10a-1180800.speaker: Stafford
a10a-1180800.text: Hello, Houston. Apollo 10.

a10a-1180800.speaker: Lousma
a10a-1180800.text: Roger, Apollo 10. Read you loud and clear. How me?

a10a-1180800.speaker: Stafford
a10a-1180800.text: Roger, Jack. We're all set up and we're getting ready to take obliques of the Landing Site 2. Over.

a10a-1180800.speaker: Lousma
a10a-1180800.text: Roger, Tom. When you've got time, we've got lots of information for you here.

a10a-1180800.speaker: Stafford
a10a-1180800.text: Roger. Just to reconfirm, for the obliques on Landing Site 2, they want the 80-mm lens using the intervalometer. Over.

a10a-1180800.speaker: Lousma
a10a-1180800.text: Stand by. We'll get an answer.

a10a-1180800.speaker: Stafford
a10a-1180800.text: Okay.

a10a-1180800.speaker: Lousma
a10a-1180800.text: Okay, Apollo 10. Houston. We confirm. We want the 80-mm lens in intervalometer on obliques for Site 2. Over.

a10a-1180800.speaker: Lousma
a10a-1180800.text: Apollo 10, Houston. Did you copy? We want the 80-mm lens with the intervalometer.

a10a-1180800.speaker: Cernan
a10a-1180800.text: Houston, we're down to one sequence camera, because we don't have a power cable for the camera we brought back from the LM.

a10a-1180800.speaker: Lousma
a10a-1180800.text: Roger. We copy, John.

a10a-1180800.speaker: Cernan
a10a-1180800.text: Jack, did you read us?

a10a-1180800.speaker: Lousma
a10a-1180800.text: That's affirmative. We copied.

a10a-1180800.speaker: Lousma
a10a-1180800.text: Gene, one sequence camera and one power cable ought to do the job.

a10a-1180800.speaker: Cernan
a10a-1180800.text: Jack, we just want to confirm, we use a black and white on this oblique photography. Do you want f:8 or f:4 at 1/250, and then down to f:2.8?

a10a-1180800.speaker: Lousma
a10a-1180800.text: Apollo 10, Houston. Use f:4 for the black and white film.

a10a-1181912.speaker: Lousma
a10a-1181912.text: Apollo 10, Houston. On your camera settings we read up, at 1/250 go to f:4, and, you will get better pictures later on if, at 118:34, you go down to f:2.8. Over.

a10a-1181912.speaker: Young
a10a-1181912.text: Houston, Apollo 10. Over.

a10a-1181912.speaker: Lousma
a10a-1181912.text: Go ahead, 10.

a10a-1181912.speaker: Young
a10a-1181912.text: Roger. Is Jack Schmitt around anywhere today?

a10a-1181912.speaker: Lousma
a10a-1181912.text: Yes. He's here today. Did you copy our last about the f-stops and the speeds and so forth?

a10a-1181912.speaker: Young
a10a-1181912.text: Roger. f:4? Right.?

a10a-1181912.speaker: Mission Control
a10a-1181912.text: This is Apollo Control. Apollo 10 crew at this time is apparently quite busy, getting lined up for the stereo strip photography of Landing Site 2. It has been rather quiet here as they approach that position. They are now at about 50 degrees east longitude, coming up on Landing Site 2 in the next several minutes. They should be directly over the site at 118 hours, 35 minutes, which is about 10 minutes from now. We will continue to monitor the air-to-ground circuit as conversation does come from Apollo 10. Getting the camera set up with the proper setting on the exposure, proper film magazine,

a10a-1181912.speaker: Lousma
a10a-1181912.text: Apollo 10, Houston. We have the final change, change 12, on the camera setting. On the 80-millimeter camera...

a10a-1181912.speaker: Stafford
a10a-1181912.text: Roger, Go on change 12.

a10a-1181912.speaker: Lousma
a10a-1181912.text: On the 80-millimeter camera, should be set at 1/250. And at 28:52, it should be set at f:8 when you turn them on. At 34:15...

a10a-1181912.speaker: Lousma
a10a-1181912.text: That's affirmative. Then at 34:15, you will get better pictures if you will stop to f:2.8 and stop on the time read up to you. Then, one other item of information: actually, we would like you to perform this. We would like you to put both H 2 Cryo tank heaters to Auto. Over.

a10a-1181912.speaker: Stafford
a10a-1181912.text: Okay. Both H 2 are on Auto now. Okay. So we will have f:8 at 1/25 at 118:28:52, ½ degree per second at 118:33:15, and then we will go to f:2.8 at 1/25 at 118:34:15.

a10a-1181912.speaker: Lousma
a10a-1181912.text: That's all correct, Tom, except for the time. It would be 1/250; 1 over 250. Over.

a10a-1181912.speaker: Stafford
a10a-1181912.text: Oh, it's 1 over 250. Okay. We go to f:2.8 at 12 1/250?

a10a-1181912.speaker: Lousma
a10a-1181912.text: That's affirmative. All of your times should be 1...

a10a-1181912.speaker: Stafford
a10a-1181912.text: Okay, Jack. Let's go over this again, doggone.

a10a-1181912.speaker: Lousma
a10a-1181912.text: Okay, Tom. At 28:52, you turn your camera on. Your 80-millimeter setting should be 1 over 250 and f:8. Start your pitch rate at 33:15 and stop down to f:2.8 at 34:15. But your time will still be 1 over 250. And then stop your pitch on T 2 , as indicated.

a10a-1181912.speaker: Stafford
a10a-1181912.text: Let's go...

a10a-1181912.speaker: Cernan
a10a-1181912.text: Houston, Apollo 10. Over.

a10a-1181912.speaker: Lousma
a10a-1181912.text: Go ahead, 10.

a10a-1181912.speaker: Cernan
a10a-1181912.text: Where do these changes to these film settings, come from?

a10a-1181912.speaker: Lousma
a10a-1181912.text: Apollo 10, Houston. We believe that this information was made clear. It's coming from the camera people, and it's information that we set up initially. Over.

a10a-1181912.speaker: Stafford
a10a-1181912.text: Okay. We'll talk about it after we get back on the ground.

a10a-1181912.speaker: Lousma
a10a-1181912.text: Roger, 10.

a10a-1181912.speaker: Stafford
a10a-1181912.text: Houston, Apollo 10. I'm looking straight down at Sidewinder Rille.

a10a-1181912.speaker: Lousma
a10a-1181912.text: Roger, 10.

a10a-1181912.speaker: Young
a10a-1181912.text: Houston, this is Apollo 10. The reason I asked that question is I just shot up a bunch of film on the backside at f:4 at 1/250 in black and white.

a10a-1181912.speaker: Lousma
a10a-1181912.text: Roger. Those were the standard settings, but the settings we're giving you now are the best ones for oblique photography. Over.

a10a-1181912.speaker: Young
a10a-1181912.text: Okay. Thank you.

a10a-1181912.speaker: Lousma
a10a-1181912.text: In other words, 10, the settings we're giving you now are better than the standard settings, but f:4 is standard.

a10a-1181912.speaker: Young
a10a-1181912.text: Okay, Jack. Peace.

a10a-1181912.speaker: Lousma
a10a-1181912.text: Roger.

a10a-1181912.speaker: Stafford
a10a-1181912.text: And for Jack's...

a10a-1181912.speaker: Lousma
a10a-1181912.text: Say again, Tom.

a10a-1181912.speaker: Lousma
a10a-1181912.text: Apollo 10, Houston. If you're transmitting, you're coming in broken. Over.

a10a-1181912.speaker: Stafford
a10a-1181912.text: Okay. We're coming right to the landing site now.

a10a-1181912.speaker: Lousma
a10a-1181912.text: Roger.

a10a-1181912.speaker: Young
a10a-1181912.text: Tell Jack Schmitt there's some very interesting looking type impacts here on the backside and also some very interesting looking things that sort of look like volcanoes. There's one on the backside that I - that, if it was in a different setting, you would call Mount Fujiyama.

a10a-1181912.speaker: Lousma
a10a-1181912.text: Ah so, gazaimaus. [probably 'Ohayou gozaimasu', a Japanese form of 'thank you'.]

a10a-1183738.speaker: Stafford
a10a-1183738.text: ...Apollo 10. I'm looking backwards [garble] past [garble] Sabine and Ritter [garble] couple of minutes [garble] looking down now [garble] area [garble] over here [garble] all types of volcanic [garble] domes and [garble] uprisings, out here [garble] looks like you've had tremendous volcanic action, here.

a10a-1183738.speaker: Lousma
a10a-1183738.text: Roger, 10. We copy. You're coming in a little bit broken, though.

a10a-1183738.speaker: Young
a10a-1183738.text: Roger, Houston, Apollo 10. Over.

a10a-1183738.speaker: Lousma
a10a-1183738.text: Okay. You sound better, John.

a10a-1183738.speaker: Young
a10a-1183738.text: Okay. This morning when we were turning around, first time, we had about - I estimate maybe a foot-and-a-half, a foot-and-a-half or more of Mylar with that insulation coater on the back of it. It would appear out in front of our window, and I guess it was from the top hatch which is where that insulation came from in the first place. It just sort of sat there for a while and then quietly floated off. But my question is, will this cause us any thermal problems? And my answer is, I guess probably not.

a10a-1183738.speaker: Lousma
a10a-1183738.text: John, Houston. We didn't copy the first part of your transmission. You were broken. We'd like you to say again your observation. And we'd also like to get some information as to whether or not you are noticing any moisture collecting around that hatch. Over.

a10a-1183738.speaker: Stafford
a10a-1183738.text: John's going up to take a look at it now.

a10a-1183738.speaker: Lousma
a10a-1183738.text: Roger. We have some questions we'd like to ask you regarding that, that you might be able to help us out with while John's up there doing that. And we'd like you to go over again the description of the forward hatch thermal blanket damage. Describe your recollection of the location, the directions, and the general appearance of the edges of the tears. And the reason we want this is because we're CCB-ing it today on 107 and we need the information.

a10a-1183738.speaker: Young
a10a-1183738.text: Okay, What the problem was, when we opened the pressure equalization valve, it just blew the insulation blanket right up. And I don't know how much air was going in there, and we didn't open it any more than cautiously on that first time, I'll tell you that.
