And so it wasn't being opened very fast, and what it did was it blew the blanket right up and from then on it blew all the insulation out from down in the Mylar covering, right in the center of the hatch, right in the pressure equalization valve, right around that area. So it seems to be a problem in attaching [garble] around that location

a10a-1183738.speaker: Stafford
a10a-1183738.text: Houston, Apollo 10. Just inside the Command Module we picked up the bag that you stow your gloves in inside the helmet. We have one of those bags that we jettisoned in Snoopy completely full of this fiberglass Mylar.

a10a-1183738.speaker: Lousma
a10a-1183738.text: Roger, 10. Understand that when you opened the pressure equalization valve, the insulation blanket blew up and then blew out insulation from around the pressure equalization valve and you filled a whole bag of it. Is that affirmative?

a10a-1183738.speaker: Stafford
a10a-1183738.text: That is affirmative. And we still have - still finding considerable pieces of insulation in the Command Module, and Snoopy looked like a snowstorm hit it inside there. Needless to say, it makes you itch quite a bit in the eyes, ears, nose, all over; but there's no problem to continue.

a10a-1183738.speaker: Young
a10a-1183738.text: Of course we didn't realize we had it until we pulled the hatch off in there, and first we knew was when we got the hatch turned over, boy that was...

a10a-1183738.speaker: Stafford
a10a-1183738.text: Looked like [garble] snowstorm [garble] got all the insulation...

a10a-1183738.speaker: Lousma
a10a-1183738.text: Apollo 10, this is Houston. You're getting unreadable. We're going to have to clear up this comm before we go on. Over.

a10a-1183738.speaker: Stafford
a10a-1183738.text: [Garble].

a10a-1183738.speaker: Lousma
a10a-1183738.text: 10, this is Houston. Let's actuate your High Gain and see if it's any better.

a10a-1183738.speaker: Lousma
a10a-1183738.text: Apollo 10, this is Houston. And could you continue on with your description of the Mylar insulation, please.

a10a-1183738.speaker: Stafford
a10a-1183738.text: Right, Jack. I'm sure you remember from LM-3, and we had the same problem initially on LM-4, when we vented the same forward hatch in the altitude chamber, how all the Mylar blew out and it blew out the skin on the top side. Well, this is exactly what happened except we just had a few layers of Mylar and all this fiberglass insulation or something of that nature down below it, and when the Mylar - There just was no provisions made for really properly venting through the Mylar and when that blew out, that let all the insulation just flake out in the tunnel, and the probe and drogue were just pa

a10a-1183738.speaker: Lousma
a10a-1183738.text: Roger. We copy, Tom. Have you noticed any formation of moisture up around the forward hatch?

a10a-1183738.speaker: Young
a10a-1183738.text: That's affirmative. There are some beads of water up there right now.

a10a-1183738.speaker: Lousma
a10a-1183738.text: Roger, Copy. Beads of water. Thank you, John.

a10a-1183738.speaker: Young
a10a-1183738.text: And it's on the steel outer rim, which is that seat that sits against the seal. It's that outermost aluminum rim, and it's just covered with beads of moisture. For that matter, the whole tunnel walls were kind of moist, but it's nothing. It's nice and cool up there.

a10a-1183738.speaker: Lousma
a10a-1183738.text: Roger. That's another question we wanted to ask you, How was the cabin environment up there during the night? Was the temperature and humidity higher than before? Over.

a10a-1183738.speaker: Young
a10a-1183738.text: It was great.

a10a-1183738.speaker: Stafford
a10a-1183738.text: The inside of the cockpit feels great. The only complaint is just all of the itching and scratching we had, due to the fiberglass. Over.

a10a-1183738.speaker: Lousma
a10a-1183738.text: Roger. Thank you.

a10a-1183738.speaker: Young
a10a-1183738.text: Jack, could we get a consumables update from you, a complete one?

a10a-1183738.speaker: Lousma
a10a-1183738.text: Roger. Consumables update follows: for GET of 117, RCS total 61; A, 51; Bravo, 70; Charlie, 62; Delta, 62; H 2 total 30.4; O 2 total 392; your RCS is 15 percent above the Flight Plan. Also have Flight Plan updates and we are ready for the state vector update when we can have your computer.

a10a-1183738.speaker: Stafford
a10a-1183738.text: Okay. We're in P00 and Accept. We are ready for the state vector.

a10a-1183738.speaker: Lousma
a10a-1183738.text: Roger. It's coming at you. I have a TEI PAD and a Flight Plan update for you.

a10a-1183738.speaker: Cernan
a10a-1183738.text: Go ahead with the update, then I will take the PAD, Jack.

a10a-1183738.speaker: Lousma
a10a-1183738.text: Roger. The Flight Plan update: way up the line, at 135 hours after LOS, we will have our waste water dump and all lunar activities are still about 12 minutes later than the preflight times, and that's the completion of the Flight Plan update.

a10a-1183738.speaker: Young
a10a-1183738.text: Waste water dump at 135 hours. Thank you.

a10a-1183738.speaker: Cernan
a10a-1183738.text: Okay, Jack. Go ahead with the PAD.

a10a-1183738.speaker: Lousma
a10a-1183738.text: Okay. I have a TEI number 23, maneuver PAD. SPS/G&N; 36818; minus 061, plus 076; 121:41:08.32; plus 29928, plus 3 balls 90, plus 01628; NA, pitch is 068; the rest is NA. Over.

a10a-1183738.speaker: Cernan
a10a-1183738.text: Okay. I've got TEI-23, SPS/G&N; 36818; minus 061, plus 076; 121:41:08.32; Noun 81 is plus 29928, plus 3 balls 90, plus 01628; roll is NA and pitch is 068; and the rest in NA.

a10a-1183738.speaker: Lousma
a10a-1183738.text: That's affirmative on that copy, and I have the vertical stereo PAD and a REV-23 update.

a10a-1185241.speaker: Cernan
a10a-1185241.text: Okay. Go ahead, Jack.

a10a-1185241.speaker: Lousma
a10a-1185241.text: Okay. Your map update PAD, REV-23: LOS, 119:21:26; 119:32:46; AOS, 120:07:36; sunrise, 119:34:44; sunset, 120:47:11. Over.

a10a-1185241.speaker: Lousma
a10a-1185241.text: Okay. And I have a vertical stereo PAD for you. T 0 , 119:41:31; T 1 , 120:10:58; T 2 , 120:20:11; T 3 , 120:30:18. And if you want to delay your roll at the sub solar point, you will be at 75 degrees east at 120:16:56. Over.

a10a-1185241.speaker: Lousma
a10a-1185241.text: That is affirmative and also would like to tell you something about your PU valve procedure. It's changed since the last one. The new procedure is this. Start with the PU valve in the Normal position for TEI, and after you bring in the second bank of ball valves, then go to Increase. The old procedures could cause a transient on startup. Over.

a10a-1185241.speaker: Cernan
a10a-1185241.text: Okay, Jack. I got it. Normal for start, we get 4 balls and go to Increase. And I guess we're all on now. If you want to pass us up that news you were going to do earlier, we're listening.

a10a-1185241.speaker: Lousma
a10a-1185241.text: Roger. I want to tell you also that you got the computer back. We're finished with the uplink. You can go to Block.

a10a-1185241.speaker: Cernan
a10a-1185241.text: We're in Block.

a10a-1185241.speaker: Lousma
a10a-1185241.text: Apollo 10, Houston. Before we go on with the news, we'd like to advise you that it's been decided that we will remove the insulation from the hatch of 107, and we tell you that so you just don't worry about not having much up there in yours and we also want to know if you're having problems inhaling or any problems breathing because of this insulation problem. Over.

a10a-1185241.speaker: Stafford
a10a-1185241.text: I figured that last question would come up as soon as we mentioned it. No. We've just been sneezing and coughing for 3 days and we understand what the problem is and how to take care of it. Over. We just wash them down and everything is Okay. It's just kind of irritating and itchy, Over.

a10a-1185241.speaker: Lousma
a10a-1185241.text: Roger. Sounds like living in the Dust Bowl in Oklahoma.

a10a-1185241.speaker: Stafford
a10a-1185241.text: Yes. I had some good training on that (laughter) area.

a10a-1185241.speaker: Young
a10a-1185241.text: That's right; he was right at home.

a10a-1185241.speaker: Stafford
a10a-1185241.text: It's not that way now. It's a beautiful place now, Jack.

a10a-1185241.speaker: Lousma
a10a-1185241.text: Okay, Apollo 10. You've got LOS and AOS. We are well caught up on information going up, so let's go up with the news now. Prague, Czechoslovakia: US astronaut Frank Borman, one of three lunar pioneers on the Apollo 8 Moon flight last year has been awarded the Czech Academy of Sciences Gold Medal for service to science and humanity. About 1,000 Czechs, shouting "Long live, glory, glory" greeted Borman, first American to win the award, as he stepped from the Academy building, Thursday. "By the end of 1970," Borman told the news conference, "we'll be able to take scientists and doctors of many na

a10a-1185241.speaker: Stafford
a10a-1185241.text: Roger. [Laughter.] Thank you very much, Jack.

a10a-1185241.speaker: Lousma
a10a-1185241.text: Oh, by the way, Tom, I've got your astrocast here too. "Your natural tendency for moderate, sparse consumption serves you well. Your system is a little more sensitive to strange foods."

a10a-1185241.speaker: Cernan
a10a-1185241.text: He's been eating like a horse for 4 days. He's the only one that saved us from the Mylar. He ate it up.

a10a-1185241.speaker: Lousma
a10a-1185241.text: Gene, I think we should read your astrocast here, too. Gene, "Conditions are bewildering. There are so many odd and unfamiliar details. Just curb your impatience; question everything, and put things into place, one at a time."

a10a-1185241.speaker: Lousma
a10a-1185241.text: Gene, this is Houston. I think you've got a pretty interesting forecast here, too. It says for you: "Conditions are bewildering. There are so many odd and unfamiliar details. Just curb your impatience; question everything, and put things into place, one at a time."

a10a-1185241.speaker: Cernan
a10a-1185241.text: Yes. That is interesting, isn't it?

a10a-1185241.speaker: Lousma
a10a-1185241.text: I guess so.

a10a-1185241.speaker: Cernan
a10a-1185241.text: Thank you, Jack.

a10a-1185241.speaker: Lousma
a10a-1185241.text: Roger.

a10a-1185241.speaker: Young
a10a-1185241.text: Just looking at that old world in the optics; sure looks nice.

a10a-1185241.speaker: Lousma
a10a-1185241.text: Apollo 10, Houston. We'd like to confirm that the ECS redundant component test is complete.

a10a-1185241.speaker: Cernan
a10a-1185241.text: No, Jack. It is not. We'll get it here immediately after the P52.

a10a-1185241.speaker: Lousma
a10a-1185241.text: Roger. We're standing by.

a10a-1185241.speaker: Cernan
a10a-1185241.text: I'll start on the secondary boilers right now. Okay, I'll start on the secondary boilers right now.

a10a-1185241.speaker: Mission Control
a10a-1185241.text: This is Apollo Control, a little over 12 minutes remaining until Loss Of Signal on this 22nd lunar revolution. Continuing to monitor air-ground for any further conversation.

a10a-1190622.speaker: Lousma
a10a-1190622.text: Apollo 10, Houston. When you have time we'd like to have some discussion regarding three questions about yesterday's activities. Over.

a10a-1190622.speaker: Stafford
a10a-1190622.text: Hello, Houston. Apollo 10.

a10a-1190622.speaker: Lousma
a10a-1190622.text: Roger. Go ahead, 10.

a10a-1190622.speaker: Stafford
a10a-1190622.text: Okay. I talked to Jack Schmitt a time before the flight and on this pass if youd like to correlate it after I roll to 180 degrees there, and you can do that around the sub solar point or before. If you've got Goldstone in configuration, we can shoot you the tube for the vertical pass all the way down and maybe even shoot the solar corona at the end. Over.

a10a-1190622.speaker: Lousma
a10a-1190622.text: Roger. Stand by.

a10a-1190622.speaker: Lousma
a10a-1190622.text: Apollo 10, Houston. In order to have TV without compromising photography and so forth, you'll have High Gain acquisition when you come AOS, but you should do your roll maneuver before 65 degrees east. Over.

a10a-1190622.speaker: Stafford
a10a-1190622.text: Roger. Roll before 65 east. When are you going to correlate that time? Over.

a10a-1190622.speaker: Lousma
a10a-1190622.text: Okay. We've already given you that on the vertical stereo PAD. It's your T 2 time of 120:20:11; that's 65 east.

a10a-1190622.speaker: Stafford
a10a-1190622.text: Okay. And we'll have good High Gain lock after that, Right?

a10a-1190622.speaker: Lousma
a10a-1190622.text: After 65 east, you'll lose it. Over.

a10a-1190622.speaker: Stafford
a10a-1190622.text: Roger. After 65 east we will lose it. Yes. It's hardly worthwhile then to - We'll only be there for a few minutes. We'll hold off.

a10a-1190622.speaker: Lousma
a10a-1190622.text: Roger. Copy holding off.

a10a-1190622.speaker: Lousma
a10a-1190622.text: Apollo 10, Houston. We're unable to copy your P52 torquing angles. We'd like you to read them down. Over.

a10a-1190622.speaker: Young
a10a-1190622.text: Would you believe we didn't copy them down? We figured you were reading them. I seem to recall a 3 and a 6, three-tenths of a degree or something like that.

a10a-1190622.speaker: Lousma
a10a-1190622.text: Roger. Thanks.

a10a-1190622.speaker: Young
a10a-1190622.text: I realize that's not what you're looking for, but it wasn't bad.

a10a-1190622.speaker: Lousma
a10a-1190622.text: Roger. We copy, John.

a10a-1190622.speaker: Young
a10a-1190622.text: Okay, Houston. We're doing the main regulator checks now.

a10a-1190622.speaker: Lousma
a10a-1190622.text: Roger. Copy.

a10a-1190622.speaker: Lousma
a10a-1190622.text: Apollo 10, Houston. We think the unscheduled tube action would best come around Rev-29, and we have a question about the LM acquisition lights after staging. Did John see the LM ACQ lights any time after staging? Over.

a10a-1190622.speaker: Stafford
a10a-1190622.text: Houston. Apollo 10. Talking about the big track light out there above the forward hatch. John saw it all the way, in fact, we had to turn it off for him at the end it was so bright. Over.

a10a-1190622.speaker: Young
a10a-1190622.text: [Garble]. Beautiful. It fills up the whole reticle when it's close - close in, about 10 or 11 miles [18 or 20 km].

a10a-1190622.speaker: Cernan
a10a-1190622.text: Yes, I could see it out to - Shoot, there one time, it was over 200 miles [370 km].

a10a-1190622.speaker: Lousma
a10a-1190622.text: Roger. Copy you saw it all the way.

a10a-1190622.speaker: Stafford
a10a-1190622.text: Could you see us all the way out there? Because that was over 300 [miles, 555 km] [garble].

a10a-1190622.speaker: Lousma
a10a-1190622.text: And, Apollo 10, Houston. Do you have any idea what might have fixed the VHF problem after undocking yesterday?

a10a-1190622.speaker: Young
a10a-1190622.text: Yes. Yes. While I wasn't tracking [garble] No idea whatsoever. We just tried it again and it worked.

a10a-1190622.speaker: Stafford
a10a-1190622.text: Yes. We had the same switch configuration again that was - thought it might be corona but, I mean, there was no way for us to tell, but you did come in just unreadable before and after we undocked and squared away. We tried again and it was unreadable and we tried it one more time...

a10a-1190622.speaker: Lousma
a10a-1190622.text: Roger, 10. See you around the corner.

a10a-1190622.speaker: Young
a10a-1190622.text: [Garble] ain't going to bother him [garble].

a10a-1190622.speaker: Stafford
a10a-1190622.text: [Laughter.]

a10a-1190622.speaker: Young
a10a-1190622.text: What did I say?

a10a-1190622.speaker: Stafford
a10a-1190622.text: No sunlight on us now. That's what we [garble] Got 20 minutes to [garble] again.

a10a-1190622.speaker: Mission Control
a10a-1190622.text: This is Apollo Control. We have had Loss Of Signal as Apollo 10 went around the corner, the back side of the Moon on revolution 22. Next acquisition; 120 hours, 7 minutes Ground Elapsed Time, revolution 23. During that pass, after the crew had completed the oblique strip stereo photography over Landing Site 2, they were read up a consumables update from the ground. Flight Plan update with one minor addition further on in the mission. They were given the revolution 23 TEI PAD. which would be just a contingency batch of numbers to use for ignition of Trans-Earth Injection burn if it became neces

a10a-1190622.speaker: Young
a10a-1190622.text: Okay, Houston, I did a sextant star check just to make sure that was a good alignment. The star's pretty close to being in the middle of the scope.

a10a-1190622.speaker: Young
a10a-1190622.text: Hey, lookie here. Them [garble] finally figured out a way to [garble]. How about that?

a10a-1190622.speaker: Young
a10a-1190622.text: I'm trying to. I can't find it. I don't know where it is - [garble] and say, well, there's [garble] Mars and all that shit. [Garble], babe. It looks to me like it's shit. We going [garble] today?

a10a-1190622.speaker: Stafford
a10a-1190622.text: Yes. Thought we'd [garble].

a10a-12007XX.speaker: Stafford
a10a-12007XX.text: ...that's a volcanic. That's a volcanism, the way it peaks up there, and keeps building up, and...

a10a-12007XX.speaker: Mission Control
a10a-12007XX.text: This is Apollo Control at 120 hours, 7 minutes Ground Elapsed Time. Apollo 10 is within some 21 seconds of being acquired as it comes around to the visible face of the Moon on lunar revolution number 23. Standing by for the first contact and they have the strip photography probably underway at this time. They may be rather busy and will not have a whole lot to say. As soon as we do have acquisition and conversation does begin we'll come up with that. One hour and 11 minutes in this pass until Loss Of Signal.

a10a-12007XX.speaker: Young
a10a-12007XX.text: I just can't believe that.

a10a-12007XX.speaker: Stafford
a10a-12007XX.text: It's got to be a volcano, babe; [garble].

a10a-12007XX.speaker: Young
a10a-12007XX.text: Boy, I tell you. See that real bright one way up yonder, see...

a10a-12007XX.speaker: Stafford
a10a-12007XX.text: Yes.

a10a-12007XX.speaker: Young
a10a-12007XX.text: ...[garble].

a10a-12007XX.speaker: Stafford
a10a-12007XX.text: Monocular. Yes, that monocular is great [garble] you can see all kinds of features.

a10a-12007XX.speaker: Young
a10a-12007XX.text: What they ought to do is give you real usable telescope, so you...

a10a-12007XX.speaker: Stafford
a10a-12007XX.text: Hey, look at - look at the Earth. See that Earth.

a10a-12007XX.speaker: Young
a10a-12007XX.text: Oh, God.

a10a-12007XX.speaker: Stafford
a10a-12007XX.text: Isn't that beautiful?

a10a-12007XX.speaker: Young
a10a-12007XX.text: That's just fantastic.

a10a-12007XX.speaker: Stafford
a10a-12007XX.text: Would you believe Africa?

a10a-12007XX.speaker: Young
a10a-12007XX.text: Oh, that is unbelievable...

a10a-12007XX.speaker: Stafford
a10a-12007XX.text: That's why...

a10a-12007XX.speaker: Young
a10a-12007XX.text: Oh. outstanding. Beautiful.

a10a-12007XX.speaker: Stafford
a10a-12007XX.text: You've never seen that before, have you, John? You just got to see it [garble] Isn't that a beautiful Earth?

a10a-12007XX.speaker: Young
a10a-12007XX.text: Ahhhhhh! Talking about the dawn coming up like thunder. Man. that's [garble] Look at that.

a10a-12007XX.speaker: Stafford
a10a-12007XX.text: That's the whole Earth. That's - [laughter]...

a10a-12007XX.speaker: Young
a10a-12007XX.text: That's unbeliev - that's unreal.

a10a-12007XX.speaker: Stafford
a10a-12007XX.text: That's why I want to get this color - Gene-o, that's why we want to get this color stuff [garble] John does the landmark tracking [garble].

a10a-12007XX.speaker: Young
a10a-12007XX.text: This works damn good for keeping count of where you are.

a10a-12007XX.speaker: Stafford
a10a-12007XX.text: Okay. I'm going to have to roll at 10:58. That's beautiful. What a contrast, tan and - Now we're getting over, Gene-o; [garble]. This thing goes from a little tan to a dark - a dark - it's a brownish tan. It's a black [garble].

a10a-12007XX.speaker: Lousma
a10a-12007XX.text: Apollo 10, Houston is standing by.

a10a-12007XX.speaker: Young
a10a-12007XX.text: Now here it doesn't look as bright in the Smyth's Sea as it did back there.

a10a-12007XX.speaker: Stafford
a10a-12007XX.text: Yes, and also, [garble] black [garble]. No, we're 36 [garble] on John's map. 120:09. I've got to roll. Here we go, babe. I got to roll. Okay.

a10a-12007XX.speaker: Cernan
a10a-12007XX.text: Okay, now what do I do here with this camera?

a10a-12007XX.speaker: Stafford
a10a-12007XX.text: Okay. I'd stop it right there. [Garble] roll and pitch 258.

a10a-12007XX.speaker: Stafford
a10a-12007XX.text: Oh. this is just great. This is just fantastic.

a10a-12007XX.speaker: Young
a10a-12007XX.text: [Garble].

a10a-12007XX.speaker: Stafford
a10a-12007XX.text: Yes. Now that one has white in the middle [garble] that was definitely impact; there's no doubt. the way it describes a rim, sort of.

a10a-12007XX.speaker: Young
a10a-12007XX.text: That raised stuff - it looks like it's painted with a paintbrush...

a10a-12007XX.speaker: Stafford
a10a-12007XX.text: Yes, but you see that little bitty basket up there, John? Now, that's definitely a volcanism, you know; not much ray and kind of rounded.

a10a-12007XX.speaker: Young
a10a-12007XX.text: It is rounded on top. There's one way back there...

a10a-12007XX.speaker: Stafford
a10a-12007XX.text: Yes, but the one way up there...

a10a-12007XX.speaker: Young
a10a-12007XX.text: That peak is...

a10a-12007XX.speaker: Stafford
a10a-12007XX.text: That - that's the volcano right there - that little one over there, but this big white one down here is...

a10a-12007XX.speaker: Young
a10a-12007XX.text: ...that peak is 3-0-whatever-it-is. One of the first craters when it comes off the horizon. You'll see it next time [garble] CP-1.

a10a-12007XX.speaker: Cernan
a10a-12007XX.text: It looks like [garble] to me.

a10a-12007XX.speaker: Mission Control
a10a-12007XX.text: This is Apollo Control. Spacecraft communicator Jack Lousma has called the crew, said he's standing by. We've had no response yet from the crew. We'll continue to leave the air-ground circuit live for any possible conversation during this revolution. Several items of information are scheduled to be passed to the crew during this rev but at the present time they're likely quite busy in conducting the photography task from terminator to terminator.

a10a-12007XX.speaker: Stafford
a10a-12007XX.text: I need to pitch 258.

a10a-12007XX.speaker: Cernan
a10a-12007XX.text: Like that one right underneath it.

a10a-12007XX.speaker: Stafford
a10a-12007XX.text: Yes. Yes.

a10a-12007XX.speaker: Cernan
a10a-12007XX.text: That looks like it's a volcano.

a10a-12007XX.speaker: Stafford
a10a-12007XX.text: That's the volcano - it seems rounded and it doesn't [garble].

a10a-12007XX.speaker: Young
a10a-12007XX.text: Can't prove it by me [garble].

a10a-12007XX.speaker: Cernan
a10a-12007XX.text: Boy, I tell you, I couldn't [garble].

a10a-12007XX.speaker: Stafford
a10a-12007XX.text: Well, you do. You have to look, John.

a10a-12007XX.speaker: Young
a10a-12007XX.text: Well, it does - it has a central dark...

a10a-12007XX.speaker: Cernan
a10a-12007XX.text: [Garble].

a10a-12007XX.speaker: Young
a10a-12007XX.text: I know. but look how it's bowed [garble] like that.

a10a-12007XX.speaker: Stafford
a10a-12007XX.text: Okay. I'm pitching to 258.

a10a-12007XX.speaker: Young
a10a-12007XX.text: Okay, there's [garble].

a10a-12007XX.speaker: Stafford
a10a-12007XX.text: 258 coming up.

a10a-12007XX.speaker: Cernan
a10a-12007XX.text: God. This is bad. Let me know when we get ...

a10a-12007XX.speaker: Stafford
a10a-12007XX.text: Okay. That seems to get it.

a10a-12007XX.speaker: Cernan
a10a-12007XX.text: What's the time now?

a10a-12007XX.speaker: Stafford
a10a-12007XX.text: We're still looking subsolar. No, we're going away from it. No, no. We're looking at - look out there's the subsolar point, right here.

a10a-12007XX.speaker: Cernan
a10a-12007XX.text: What's the time?

a10a-12007XX.speaker: Cernan
a10a-12007XX.text: There's CP-1 [garble] target [garble]; you know, man. anybody who says these things are all flat is touched.

a10a-12007XX.speaker: Mission Control
a10a-12007XX.text: We'll open the circuit and let it run until conversation commences even though there's a great deal of background noise, so that no conversation will be missed.

a10a-12007XX.speaker: Cernan
a10a-12007XX.text: [Garble] subsolar point [garble].

a10a-12007XX.speaker: Stafford
a10a-12007XX.text: The time is 20:14 - 120...

a10a-12007XX.speaker: Cernan
a10a-12007XX.text: Yes. That looks like [garble].

a10a-12007XX.speaker: Young
a10a-12007XX.text: 41:30 [garble], Tom.

a10a-12007XX.speaker: Stafford
a10a-12007XX.text: Yes. Right there.

a10a-12007XX.speaker: Cernan
a10a-12007XX.text: This is the worst map I ever saw in my life.

a10a-12007XX.speaker: Stafford
a10a-12007XX.text: Now we're starting to get a few little rilles down here. And I'm down to zero phase - my reticle is washed out. I can't even see my reticle...

a10a-12007XX.speaker: Young
a10a-12007XX.text: My reticle is washed out [garble].

a10a-12007XX.speaker: Stafford
a10a-12007XX.text: Yes. Mine is washed out.

a10a-12007XX.speaker: Young
a10a-12007XX.text: I didn't - I didn't want to say anything because I didn't want to [garble].

a10a-12007XX.speaker: Stafford
a10a-12007XX.text: [Garble]. Yes. I did. I did.

a10a-12007XX.speaker: Young
a10a-12007XX.text: Man, it's there - ain't no doubt about it. That cotton-picking Moon ain't [garble].

a10a-12007XX.speaker: Mission Control
a10a-12007XX.text: This is Apollo Control. Snoopy , the ascent stage of the Lunar Module, is now some 36,875 nautical miles [68,292 km] outbound from the Moon, going toward solar orbit, traveling at some 5,356 feet per second [1,633 m/s]. Flight Controllers who have been monitoring the Lunar Module are packing up at this time. As a matter of fact, the console is vacant now. They are abandoning the ship as their job is complete. Background noise has dropped somewhat in the air-ground circuit. We'll come back live with that now to pick up conversation during this 23rd lunar revolution.

a10a-12007XX.speaker: Cernan
a10a-12007XX.text: God!

a10a-12007XX.speaker: Stafford
a10a-12007XX.text: [Garble] straight around it, it's a hell of a lot higher. Think maybe Smyth's Sea was one big impact and then the volcano [garble].

a10a-12007XX.speaker: Cernan
a10a-12007XX.text: [Garble].

a10a-12007XX.speaker: Stafford
a10a-12007XX.text: Okay. Minus 71 and 170.

a10a-12007XX.speaker: Young
a10a-12007XX.text: It's beautiful [garble].

a10a-12007XX.speaker: Cernan
a10a-12007XX.text: (Singing)

a10a-12007XX.speaker: Stafford
a10a-12007XX.text: Got minus 70 and [garble].

a10a-12007XX.speaker: Cernan
a10a-12007XX.text: Plus?

a10a-12007XX.speaker: Stafford
a10a-12007XX.text: Minus.

a10a-1201734.speaker: Lousma
a10a-1201734.text: Apollo 10, Houston. Standing by.

a10a-1201734.speaker: Stafford
a10a-1201734.text: Roger, Houston. We're taking our vertical stereo photography now. We just rolled past the subsolar point there.

a10a-1201734.speaker: Lousma
a10a-1201734.text: Roger, 10. we copy. [Long pause.]

a10a-1201734.speaker: Stafford
a10a-1201734.text: Hey, Jack. Now that we've got some time to pick out - really concentrate on this stuff, we're finding all kinds of features in here. And it's mostly been on the tape, but I hope you'll be able to get the tape and play it there.

a10a-1201734.speaker: Lousma
a10a-1201734.text: Roger. While we're talking about the tape, we've been getting on the playback come weak voice and background noise, and we found out on a prior flight that this comes out a lot better if you make sure you have the mike real close to your mouth when you talk into the tape recorder. Over.

a10a-1201734.speaker: . Stafford
a10a-1201734.text: Roger. Is that, for all of us?

a10a-1201734.speaker: Lousma
a10a-1201734.text: That is affirmative. All of you who were talking to the tape recorder.

a10a-1201734.speaker: Stafford
a10a-1201734.text: We're now yawing left, 20 degrees.

a10a-1201734.speaker: Lousma
a10a-1201734.text: Roger, 10.

a10a-1201734.speaker: Mission Control
a10a-1201734.text: This is Apollo Control. While we are waiting for the crew to complete the strip photography session, we have one local note of interest for newsmen here covering Apollo 10. At 1 pm Houston time, Mr. Ray Zedekar of Flight Crew Support Division will cover the lunar exploration time lines for the Apollo 11 mission, scheduled now for July. This will be in the main auditorium at the Manned Spacecraft Center. We return now to monitoring the air-to-ground loop.

a10a-1201734.speaker: Mission Control
a10a-1201734.text: This is Apollo Control. Some 5 minutes remaining in this vertical stereo sequence. The cut-off time at which they reach 34° East lunar longitude will be 120 hours, 30 minutes, 18 seconds; a little less than 5 minutes from now. Likely there will not be too much conversation until after this stereo task is completed. Still monitoring air to ground live.

a10a-1201734.speaker: Stafford
a10a-1201734.text: Houston, Apollo 10. We've just passed over Mount Marilyn and the crater Weatherford. Over.

a10a-1201734.speaker: Lousma
a10a-1201734.text: Roger. We copy.

a10a-1201734.speaker: Stafford
a10a-1201734.text: Yawing right 20 degrees to pick up Landing Site 2, now.

a10a-1201734.speaker: Lousma
a10a-1201734.text: Roger, 10. [Long pause.]

a10a-1201734.speaker: Stafford
a10a-1201734.text: And we're right on top of Maskelyne at this time.

a10a-1201734.speaker: Lousma
a10a-1201734.text: Roger, 10. [Long pause.]

a10a-1201734.speaker: Stafford
a10a-1201734.text: Over Maskelyne B now.

a10a-1201734.speaker: Lousma
a10a-1201734.text: Apollo 10, Houston. Say again, please.

a10a-1201734.speaker: Stafford
a10a-1201734.text: Roger. We're just past Maskelyne B, and I'm right - looking straight down at Sidewinder Rille, coming up to the head of Diamondback Rille.

a10a-1201734.speaker: Lousma
a10a-1201734.text: Roger. We're following you. [Pause.]

a10a-1201734.speaker: Stafford
a10a-1201734.text: Sabine E is on the left. On my left as we go backwards. [Pause.]

a10a-1201734.speaker: Stafford
a10a-1201734.text: There's Faye Ridge.

a10a-1201734.speaker: Lousma
a10a-1201734.text: Roger, 10. We observe you're liable to get sunlight on the windows here pretty soon.

a10a-1201734.speaker: Stafford
a10a-1201734.text: Roger. [Long pause.]

a10a-1203324.speaker: Stafford
a10a-1203324.text: Picking up U.S. 1 on the right.

a10a-1203324.speaker: Lousma
a10a-1203324.text: Roger. [Long pause.]

a10a-1203324.speaker: Cernan
a10a-1203324.text: We've got Moltke out my right window. We're right over Landing Site 2.

a10a-1203324.speaker: Lousma
a10a-1203324.text: Roger. Copy. [Long pause.]

a10a-1203324.speaker: Young
a10a-1203324.text: And there's landmark 130.

a10a-1203324.speaker: Lousma
a10a-1203324.text: Roger. Landmarker. [Long pause.]

a10a-1203324.speaker: Cernan
a10a-1203324.text: And Langrenus is quite a majestic crater with a tremendously beautiful central peak. One that we were just able to look at sunset the other day that's just beautiful today.

a10a-1203324.speaker: Lousma
a10a-1203324.text: Roger, Gene-o. Langrenus. And you'll have to speak up a little louder, please.

a10a-1203324.speaker: Young
a10a-1203324.text: And I see crater 133 with that little crater we talked about on the right of it for tracking.

a10a-1203324.speaker: Lousma
a10a-1203324.text: Roger. [Long pause.]

a10a-1203324.speaker: Stafford
a10a-1203324.text: We have a beautiful panorama looking back from Sabine and Ritter over the landing site back to Maskelyne A and B and then over past Mount Marilyn there.

a10a-1203324.speaker: Lousma
a10a-1203324.text: Roger, Tom. [Long pause.]

a10a-1203324.speaker: Stafford
a10a-1203324.text: I'll tell you, later on today - We'll talk about it when we have a chance for a rev, we may just go to a vertical strip, roll 90 degrees so you can get High Gain, and we'll shoot the tube on it, because I know it will pick it up and you can pick out all these features. Over.

a10a-1203324.speaker: Lousma
a10a-1203324.text: Roger, Tom. We'll start thinking about that. [Long pause.]

a10a-1203324.speaker: Stafford
a10a-1203324.text: Also, you might tell Jack that we couldn't have a better crater named after him, because we are looking at him now back from Sabine and Ritter, and the boulders that have been kicked out of it on the outside slope nearly look like a forest of pine trees, there's so many big black boulders there.

a10a-1203324.speaker: Lousma
a10a-1203324.text: Say again the name of that, Tom.

a10a-1203324.speaker: Stafford
a10a-1203324.text: It's really spotted the countryside with them. That's what we code named it Herr Schmidt.

a10a-1203324.speaker: Lousma
a10a-1203324.text: Roger. He says thanks, but it's - spelled the name wrong.

a10a-1203324.speaker: Stafford
a10a-1203324.text: Well, we were in a hurry anyway. We didn't have too much time to worry about details. It looks just like a scattered - about the same density, you know, as pine trees up on a mountain ridge. That's about what these big black boulders look like.

a10a-1203324.speaker: Lousma
a10a-1203324.text: Roger. [Long pause.]

a10a-1203324.speaker: Stafford
a10a-1203324.text: We're now in an area that is really noticeably marked by volcanic activities. We have all types of lumps - of lumps here and we can really see there's just thousands of volcanoes here, just a tremendous volcanic field at this time. Over.

a10a-1203324.speaker: Lousma
a10a-1203324.text: Roger.

a10a-1203324.speaker: Stafford
a10a-1203324.text: Lots of volcanic mounds.

a10a-1203324.speaker: Lousma
a10a-1203324.text: Roger. That makes the geologists happy. [Long pause.]

a10a-1203324.speaker: Stafford
a10a-1203324.text: I've got one interesting site here. Looks like a - It's probably too dark to take a picture. but you can see where you've had a big impact crater with the ramped edge. It looks like a stream of volcanic material has run over into it.

a10a-1203324.speaker: Lousma
a10a-1203324.text: Roger. Tom. If you went to 1/125 on the Hasselblad. you might get it.

a10a-1203324.speaker: Stafford
a10a-1203324.text: Yes. We've got 1/125 now. It's getting awful dark here. We've got a lot of Sun on the windows. It's pretty bad.

a10a-1203324.speaker: Stafford
a10a-1203324.text: We shot the whole strip. Sure hope we got you some good data. We got it in the sequence camera at one frame per second, color all the way through, and we got the Hasselblad all the way, too. Over.

a10a-1203324.speaker: Lousma
a10a-1203324.text: That's great. [Long pause.]

a10a-1203324.speaker: Lousma
a10a-1203324.text: Apollo 10. Houston. If you're going to fly the next vertical strip photography, namely in Rev-31, in that same attitude, why, then we can give you the TV. Over.

a10a-1203324.speaker: Stafford
a10a-1203324.text: Okay. Did you have High Gain lock on us that time? Say again.

a10a-1203324.speaker: Lousma
a10a-1203324.text: That's affirmative. We had it most of the way, and if we can confirm that you will fly in the same attitude in Rev-31, why, TV will come through all right.

a10a-1203324.speaker: Stafford
a10a-1203324.text: Yes. We will fly the same one as the last. You get a tremendous panoramic view looking back over Landing Site 1, Over. [Garble] as you come over Landing Site 2, looking back over the maria area. It's just fantastic. We'll try to show it to you.

a10a-1203324.speaker: Lousma
a10a-1203324.text: Roger. We'll plan on it for Rev-31, then.

a10a-1203324.speaker: Stafford
a10a-1203324.text: Alrighty.

a10a-1203324.speaker: Stafford
a10a-1203324.text: And the Sun went down and we have the solar corona.

a10a-1203324.speaker: Lousma
a10a-1203324.text: Roger, 10. [Pause.]

a10a-1203324.speaker: Lousma
a10a-1203324.text: And when you get things put away up there, we've got three PADs and a state vector update for you and a couple more discussion type questions.

a10a-1203324.speaker: Stafford
a10a-1203324.text: Okay. If you want to state vector update, we're in P00, and we can toss you the computer.

a10a-1203324.speaker: Lousma
a10a-1203324.text: Okay, 10. We're ready for the update when you're ready.

a10a-1203324.speaker: Young
a10a-1203324.text: Roger, go.

a10a-1203324.speaker: Stafford
a10a-1203324.text: CMC and Accept.

a10a-1203324.speaker: Young
a10a-1203324.text: Go ahead, Houston.

a10a-1203324.speaker: Lousma
a10a-1203324.text: Apollo 10, Houston. We're ready with the state vector update when you're ready to Accept.

a10a-1203324.speaker: Young
a10a-1203324.text: We're P00 and Accept.

a10a-1203324.speaker: Lousma
a10a-1203324.text: Roger. P00 and Accept. [Long pause.]

a10a-1203324.speaker: Lousma
a10a-1203324.text: Apollo 10, Houston. Our signal strength is going down. Could we get Omni Charlie for this, please?

a10a-1203324.speaker: Stafford
a10a-1203324.text: Okay. I'm going to roll 180 degrees in just a minute.

a10a-1203324.speaker: Lousma
a10a-1203324.text: Roger. We'll wait. [Pause.]

a10a-1203324.speaker: Young
a10a-1203324.text: Houston, can we get the map update?

a10a-1204935.speaker: Lousma
a10a-1204935.text: Okay. Apollo 10. I've got a map data - map update for you. Rev-24: LOS, 121:19:59; 121:31:11; 122:06:09; sunrise is 121:33:30; sunset, 122:45:55. Read back, and I've got the landmark tracking update PAD after that.

a10a-1204935.speaker: Lousma
a10a-1204935.text: That's affirmative. You ready for your tracking update?

a10a-1204935.speaker: Young
a10a-1204935.text: Go. Over.

a10a-1204935.speaker: Lousma
a10a-1204935.text: Okay. Charlie Papa 1: 121:39:49, 121:42:49, 3 balls, 050, 3 balls, north 13 miles, 11, 40. Charlie Papa 2: 121:55:10, 121:56:52, 3 balls, 2 balls 8, 3 balls, north 05, 04, 40. Fox 1: 122:07:55, 122:10:06, 3 balls, 326, all balls, north 10, 09, 41. Number 130: 122:29:03, 122:30:37, 3 balls, 265, 3 balls, north at 13, 12, 40. Go ahead. And I've got a maneuver PAD after that.

a10a-1204935.speaker: Young
a10a-1204935.text: Roger. Charlie Papa 1: 121:39:49, 121:42:49, all balls, north 13, 11 and 40. Charlie Papa 2: I missed T1. Over.

a10a-1204935.speaker: Lousma
a10a-1204935.text: Roger. On Charlie Papa 2, we had 121:55 and 10. And we want to confirm the nautical miles on Charlie Papa 1 as being 13 - 13. Over.

a10a-1204935.speaker: Young
a10a-1204935.text: Roger. 13 north. Okay. Charlie Papa 2: 121:55:10, 121:56:52, all balls, 008, all balls, north 05, 04, 40. F-1: 122:07:55, 122:10:06, all balls, 326, all balls, north 10, 09, 41. 130: 122:09:03, 122:30:37, 000, 265, all balls, north 13, 12, and 40.

a10a-1204935.speaker: Lousma
a10a-1204935.text: Roger. You got it, and we're ready with the maneuver PAD.

a10a-1204935.speaker: Cernan
a10a-1204935.text: Go ahead, Jack.

a10a-1204935.speaker: Lousma
a10a-1204935.text: Okay. This is TEI-24: SPS/G&N; 36818; minus 061, plus 076; 123:40:52.33: plus 30443, plus 00131, plus 00682; NA, 066, and the rest is NA. Under ullage, two jets for l4 seconds. Over.

a10a-1204935.speaker: Cernan
a10a-1204935.text: Jack, we had an antenna switch right in the middle of that. You'd better start it over.

a10a-1204935.speaker: Lousma
a10a-1204935.text: Apollo 10, Houston. Before we proceed, lets lock up with the High Gain. Over.

a10a-1204935.speaker: Cernan
a10a-1204935.text: Okay. We're still maneuvering, Stand by one.

a10a-1204935.speaker: Lousma
a10a-1204935.text: Roger. [Long pause.]

a10a-1204935.speaker: Cernan
a10a-1204935.text: Hello, Houston. This is 10. We're in Accept and P00 and ready for your update and ready for your PAD.

a10a-1204935.speaker: Lousma
a10a-1204935.text: Roger, 10. Reading you loud and clear now. The uplink's coming up and here's the PAD. TEI-24: SPS/G&N; 36818; minus 061, plus 076; 123:40:52.33; 0 - correction - plus 30443, plus 00131, plus 00682; roll is NA, pitch is 066. The rest is NA. Your ullage is two jets for 14 seconds. Over.

a10a-1204935.speaker: Cernan
a10a-1204935.text: Okay, Jack. I got TEI-24: SPS/G&N; 36818; minus 061, plus 076; 123:40:52.33; plus 30443, plus 00131, plus 00682; NA, and pitch is 066. The rest is NA; two jets for 14 seconds.

a10a-1204935.speaker: Lousma
a10a-1204935.text: That affirmative.

a10a-1204935.speaker: Lousma
a10a-1204935.text: Apollo 10, Houston. The uplink is complete. Computer is yours; you can go to Block. And we've noted that on the last pass during the strip photography, you were rolled 180 degrees different than that we expected you to be. And we'd like to ask you a couple of questions about the LM S-band yesterday and LM pressurization when you have an opportunity to discuss it. Over.

a10a-1204935.speaker: Cernan
a10a-1204935.text: Go ahead, Jack.

a10a-1204935.speaker: Lousma
a10a-1204935.text: Okay. On the S-band communications around the DOI period - Do you have anything significant to report having lost comm for about 20 minutes on the High Gain there? We were a little concerned as to what the problem might be. Can you discuss that?

a10a-1204935.speaker: Cernan
a10a-1204935.text: No. I noticed we were having, locked - out lockout problems as we went low across the landing site. It appeared that it occurred right at our low time, and the S-band didn't track - didn't follow us when we came across the landing site, and I went to Omnis hoping without having too much time to play with it. And, then, a period of time after that, I played with the S-band again and was able to acquire you and lock on. That's all I can really say, but it did occur somewhere near the low part of our trajectory.

a10a-1204935.speaker: Lousma
a10a-1204935.text: Roger. We understand another question is regarding the LM pressurization. We noted that right after you pickled old Snoopy off Charlie there, that the LM cabin pressurization went down. Do you - did you observe anything or note anything unusual about that. Over.

a10a-1204935.speaker: Cernan
a10a-1204935.text: Jack, he moved away with a blast, and the next thing we had in our eyes was sunlight right through the windows and we couldn't see a thing. I do know that both dump valves were in Auto, however. We had a lot of garbage around after the blast from the pyros, but other than that - Tom may have seen something else.

a10a-1204935.speaker: Stafford
a10a-1204935.text: Well, I was looking out the center hatch window and, as you know, the tunnel - We couldn't get the tunnel depressurized, and when we fired those pyros, some more insulation blew out, and I just saw Snoopy disappear in a big snowstorm going straight up into the Sun and that was all. Over.

a10a-1204935.speaker: Lousma
a10a-1204935.text: Roger. Thank you. And last time we saw Snoopy down here, he was 37,000 miles [68,500 km] going straight up from the Moon at 5,400 feet per second [1,645 m/s], and thank you for your comments. Over.

a10a-1204935.speaker: Stafford
a10a-1204935.text: Okay. And the - look - Okay. I guess I got run ahead. We made some changes in here on that roll.

a10a-1204935.speaker: Lousma
a10a-1204935.text: Roger. We noticed.

a10a-1204935.speaker: Stafford
a10a-1204935.text: And the way that the times have changed. But it didn't - I'm sorry about that - but it didn't seem to - We didn't get any shafting or anything on our windows at all until right at the last when we hit the terminator.

a10a-1204935.speaker: Lousma
a10a-1204935.text: Roger. That was the only thing we were concerned about.

a10a-1204935.speaker: Young
a10a-1204935.text: Yes. I don't think it'll - No, I just don't.

a10a-1204935.speaker: Stafford
a10a-1204935.text: There was no shafting at all on the windows and it looked like - We were giving our comments and I don't think we had any problem at all.

a10a-1204935.speaker: Lousma
a10a-1204935.text: Roger. Thank you for your comments. They're good. And understand we will have this attitude for Rev-31.

a10a-1210626.speaker: Lousma
a10a-1210626.text: Apollo 10, Houston. We'd like you to check the situation with fuel cell 1; ensure that your fuel cell pump's AC circuit breaker on panel 226 is Closed. And that your fuel cell number 1 AC 1 is Closed - correction - is AC1. You copy, 10?

a10a-1210626.speaker: Stafford
a10a-1210626.text: Okay. We just [garble].

a10a-1210626.speaker: Cernan
a10a-1210626.text: Hello, Jack.

a10a-1210626.speaker: Lousma
a10a-1210626.text: Apollo 10. Houston. Do you read?

a10a-1210626.speaker: Cernan
a10a-1210626.text: Yes. We read. I tried to push in breaker A and it's out, and as soon as we did we got an AC bus 1 light, a main bus A and a main bus B undervolt light. The breaker will not reset at this time. and it's fuel cell 1, AC pump breaker on 226.

a10a-1210626.speaker: Lousma
a10a-1210626.text: Roger. That's the one. We're looking at it.

a10a-1210626.speaker: Cernan
a10a-1210626.text: Okay. When I push it in, I get those three lights, AC bus 1, main bus A, and main bus B undervolts.

a10a-1210626.speaker: Lousma
a10a-1210626.text: Roger, 10. We're working on it.

a10a-1210626.speaker: Cernan
a10a-1210626.text: Say, Houston. This is 10.

a10a-1210626.speaker: Lousma
a10a-1210626.text: Roger, 10. We're working on this problem. Stand by, please.

a10a-1210626.speaker: Cernan
a10a-1210626.text: Okay. I just wanted to tell you. Of course, I got - There goes the fuel cell 1 light. I just expected it. I think it's probably because of a condenser exhaust temperature down around 154 degrees [Fahrenheit, 68°C]. Also the skin temperature is going up at this time, and we do have the fuel cell 1 light. The bus lights now are all reset and everything's normal from that. It's just fuel cell 1.

a10a-1210626.speaker: Lousma
a10a-1210626.text: Roger. We copy and confirm.

a10a-1210626.speaker: Young
a10a-1210626.text: [Garble] is 121:19. 6 more minutes.

a10a-1210626.speaker: Stafford
a10a-1210626.text: Mission rules say come home on that, don't they?

a10a-1210626.speaker: Young
a10a-1210626.text: If we lose another fuel cell, we go home? [Long pause.]

a10a-1210626.speaker: Stafford
a10a-1210626.text: Shoot, if we lose one, we go home. Don't we?

a10a-1210626.speaker: Young
a10a-1210626.text: Okay, I want to copy - copy this down, and let me get the Flight Plan.

a10a-1210626.speaker: Stafford
a10a-1210626.text: Here you are, babe.

a10a-1210626.speaker: Young
a10a-1210626.text: Just lose them?

a10a-1210626.speaker: Lousma
a10a-1210626.text: Apollo 10. Houston. Here's what we'd like you to do on fuel cell 1. Open circuit fuel cell 1. Fuel cell 2 go to main bus A only. Fuel cell 3 go to main bus B only. Over.

a10a-1210626.speaker: Cernan
a10a-1210626.text: Roger. You want me to open circuit fuel cell number 1. You want me to go fuel 2 to main bus A and fuel cell 3 to main bus B. I'll do it now.

a10a-1210626.speaker: Young
a10a-1210626.text: Wait a second, here.

a10a-1210626.speaker: Lousma
a10a-1210626.text: That's affirmative. We're standing by.

a10a-1210626.speaker: Young
a10a-1210626.text: Go.

a10a-1210626.speaker: Lousma
a10a-1210626.text: Apollo 10, Houston. In the event that you get an under voltage light, disregard the voltage and come right back up again.

a10a-1210626.speaker: Cernan
a10a-1210626.text: Okay. I'm looking at 26.9 [volts] on both main A and main B at this time.

a10a-1210626.speaker: Young
a10a-1210626.text: Did you open-circuit it? Did you open-circuit?

a10a-1210626.speaker: Cernan
a10a-1210626.text: Yes. I don't like this. Shit, I just don't like this. We have to power down all this.

a10a-1210626.speaker: Lousma
a10a-1210626.text: Roger 10. We copy. And it's looking good.

a10a-1210626.speaker: Cernan
a10a-1210626.text: How good does all that look to you?

a10a-1210626.speaker: Lousma
a10a-1210626.text: Say again, 10.

a10a-1210626.speaker: Stafford
a10a-1210626.text: You want to go over this Orb Rate landmark tracking...

a10a-1210626.speaker: Cernan
a10a-1210626.text: How good does all that really look to you?

a10a-1210626.speaker: Young
a10a-1210626.text: Yes, you hold Orb Rate. Okay? And I'll - and if these times - You still...

a10a-1210626.speaker: Lousma
a10a-1210626.text: We're assessing it right now.

a10a-1210626.speaker: Cernan
a10a-1210626.text: Okay. I guess we're going to lose you in a couple of minutes here.

a10a-1210626.speaker: Cernan
a10a-1210626.text: And, Houston. this is 10. Do you want me to maintain my battery charge on A at this time? [Long pause.]

a10a-1210626.speaker: Stafford
a10a-1210626.text: I would say yes, to make sure those batteries are up.

a10a-1210626.speaker: Lousma
a10a-1210626.text: Apollo 10. Houston. Terminate your battery A charge at this time and if we get a Cryo O 2 heater cycle, well, you may lower the bus voltage momentarily. Over.

a10a-1210626.speaker: Cernan
a10a-1210626.text: Okay. Fine. I understand. I'm terminating the battery A charge at this time. [Long pause.]

a10a-1210626.speaker: Stafford
a10a-1210626.text: Surely we want to start powering down here and still go ahead.

a10a-1210626.speaker: Young
a10a-1210626.text: Hey, that's those fuel cells one of [garble] do early TEI for loss of.

a10a-1210626.speaker: Cernan
a10a-1210626.text: For one fuel cell?

a10a-1210626.speaker: Young
a10a-1210626.text: Yes.

a10a-1210626.speaker: Stafford
a10a-1210626.text: We come back early for that one.

a10a-1210626.speaker: Young
a10a-1210626.text: As far as high [garble] for these items, early TEI will be delayed a reasonable time, pending completion of various lunar-orbit activities.

a10a-1210626.speaker: Stafford
a10a-1210626.text: Houston, do you have a - What's your latest hack on when we'll have AOS, please?

a10a-1210626.speaker: Cernan
a10a-1210626.text: [Garble].

a10a-1210626.speaker: Young
a10a-1210626.text: AOS.

a10a-1210626.speaker: Cernan
a10a-1210626.text: Oh, AOS.

a10a-1210626.speaker: Lousma
a10a-1210626.text: Okay. AOS will be 122:06. And we'l1 be losing you in 2 minutes.

a10a-1210626.speaker: Stafford
a10a-1210626.text: Roger. Roger. 122:06 and we're going to plan to continue on with the landmark tracking, and we'll talk to you about this as soon as we get AOS.

a10a-1210626.speaker: Lousma
a10a-1210626.text: Roger. We'll have some new word for you then.

a10a-1210626.speaker: Stafford
a10a-1210626.text: Okay. Thank you, Jack. [Long pause.]

a10a-1210626.speaker: Stafford
a10a-1210626.text: We got a good state vector. Shit, we could burn the son of a bitch.

a10a-1210626.speaker: Cernan
a10a-1210626.text: Yes, we could.

a10a-1210626.speaker: Stafford
a10a-1210626.text: [Garble]. We're going to come back in the dark though, baby. We're going to land before sunrise [garble] a little bit.

a10a-1210626.speaker: Young
a10a-1210626.text: Oh. God.

a10a-1210626.speaker: Stafford
a10a-1210626.text: [Garble] a long time, baby.

a10a-1210626.speaker: Young
a10a-1210626.text: Then going back slow wouldn't help that. You wouldn't want to go back slow.

a10a-1210626.speaker: Stafford
a10a-1210626.text: Shit, no. When you make that burn, baby, you commit yourself when you splash down, whether you're fast or slow. You can't do anything about it.

a10a-1210626.speaker: Cernan
a10a-1210626.text: In the dark?

a10a-1210626.speaker: Stafford
a10a-1210626.text: That's right, baby. If we burn TEI the next rev around, we're coming back in the nighttime.

a10a-1210626.speaker: Stafford
a10a-1210626.text: Okay, Houston. Apollo 10. I'm going to go ahead and start a roll around so I'll come around to a Orb Rate of 3 - I'll wait until after we get Loss Of Signal and pick up an Orb Rate of 339 for landmark tracking.

a10a-1210626.speaker: Lousma
a10a-1210626.text: Roger. We copy.

a10a-1210626.speaker: Stafford
a10a-1210626.text: Oh, man, I'm glad you didn't leave that fuel cell on while we were out there doing the rendezvous.

a10a-1210626.speaker: Young
a10a-1210626.text: [Garble] getting so nervous I wouldn't know what to do.

a10a-1210626.speaker: Cernan
a10a-1210626.text: [Garble] scared the living [garble] out of me if you had told me [garble].

a10a-1210626.speaker: Cernan
a10a-1210626.text: Now we're sitting right at the point where we're almost going to get a [garble] every time those heaters cycle in this position.

a10a-1210626.speaker: Stafford
a10a-1210626.text: You don't need the heaters anymore, you get that low.

a10a-1210626.speaker: Cernan
a10a-1210626.text: 26.5 to 26 inching to 27. Now I'm going to get the battery chargers off now.

a10a-1210626.speaker: Stafford
a10a-1210626.text: Yes. Going to lose them in 2 minutes; I'm going to roll a hundred and - I'm going to rollover to zero zero, so we can - Stand by with black and white. This may be the only chance to be in color to pick up the earth in the sequence camera.

a10a-1210626.speaker: Cernan
a10a-1210626.text: [Garble] already.

a10a-1210626.speaker: Stafford
a10a-1210626.text: You got the color film in there? No black and white? I got this special color here. That color film - is that - that's still that color film...

a10a-1210626.speaker: Cernan
a10a-1210626.text: [Garble] him out of the LM. That's the only stuff we got left. It came out of the LM.

a10a-1210626.speaker: Stafford
a10a-1210626.text: Okay, let's [garble] fire down the checklist and see if there's a few things we can get off that [garble] maybe to help us a little bit.

a10a-1210626.speaker: Stafford
a10a-1210626.text: Yes. Maybe that foldy junk. I could do without one of those GPI's, right now.

a10a-1210626.speaker: Young
a10a-1210626.text: We don't need the hot-water heater, do we?

a10a-1210626.speaker: Stafford
a10a-1210626.text: No, shit, no. Get that off.

a10a-1220743.speaker: Lousma
a10a-1220743.text: Apollo 10, Houston. Standing by.

a10a-1220743.speaker: Stafford
a10a-1220743.text: Roger. We're right square in the middle of a landmark tracking.

a10a-1220743.speaker: Stafford
a10a-1220743.text: We should hold on the horizon. And at 22...

a10a-1220743.speaker: Lousma
a10a-1220743.text: Roger. And we've cranked up a plan-of-attack on that fuel cell.

a10a-1220743.speaker: Stafford
a10a-1220743.text: Okay. Can you hold off for just a couple minutes? We'll be right with you.

a10a-1220743.speaker: Stafford
a10a-1220743.text: Okay, we're coming across it.

a10a-1220743.speaker: Young
a10a-1220743.text: When is zero time?

a10a-1220743.speaker: Stafford
a10a-1220743.text: Zero time is 122:10:06.

a10a-1220743.speaker: Young
a10a-1220743.text: Okay, about 2 minutes.

a10a-1220743.speaker: Stafford
a10a-1220743.text: 2 minutes.

a10a-1220743.speaker: Young
a10a-1220743.text: [Garble] plan of attack on the fuel cells. We kicked the shit out of it, huh?

a10a-1220743.speaker: Young
a10a-1220743.text: Yes, I bet I know what they'll do.

a10a-1220743.speaker: Stafford
a10a-1220743.text: They'll just bring us home.

a10a-1220743.speaker: Young
a10a-1220743.text: They'll bring it on the line while we're on the back side and shut it off around on the front side. You want to bet?

a10a-1220743.speaker: Stafford
a10a-1220743.text: Okay, you got the landmark?

a10a-1220743.speaker: Young
a10a-1220743.text: Not yet.

a10a-1220743.speaker: Cernan
a10a-1220743.text: I'll [garble] for you guys, but I don't want to interfere with your...

a10a-1220743.speaker: Stafford
a10a-1220743.text: Okay, 22 - it just won't take but a minute. 22:10:06. Just about 20 seconds, John. Let me know when.

a10a-1220743.speaker: Young
a10a-1220743.text: I haven't got it yet.

a10a-1220743.speaker: Stafford
a10a-1220743.text: Okay.

a10a-1220743.speaker: Young
a10a-1220743.text: Oh, hell, there it is. Damn near overshot it.

a10a-1220743.speaker: Stafford
a10a-1220743.text: Do you want me to pitch down for you?

a10a-1220743.speaker: Young
a10a-1220743.text: Yes.

a10a-1220743.speaker: Stafford
a10a-1220743.text: Okay, you got some pitchdown. Okay.

a10a-1220743.speaker: Young
a10a-1220743.text: Oh, shit.

a10a-1220743.speaker: Stafford
a10a-1220743.text: Pitch down some more?

a10a-1220743.speaker: Young
a10a-1220743.text: No.

a10a-1220743.speaker: Stafford
a10a-1220743.text: Let me know when.

a10a-1220743.speaker: Young
a10a-1220743.text: Okay.

a10a-1220743.speaker: Stafford
a10a-1220743.text: Mark it.

a10a-1220743.speaker: Stafford
a10a-1220743.text: 5 seconds, 10 seconds, 15 seconds, 20 seconds, 25 seconds.

a10a-1220743.speaker: Stafford
a10a-1220743.text: Mark.

a10a-1220743.speaker: Stafford
a10a-1220743.text: You've got two of them. 5 seconds, 10 seconds, 15 seconds, 20 seconds, 25 seconds. Got three of them. 5 seconds, 10 seconds, 15 seconds, 20 seconds, 25 seconds. You got four. 5 seconds, 10 seconds, 15 seconds, 20 seconds, 25 seconds. You got five. There you go, babe. Do I have to hold this attitude, or can I pitch down?

a10a-1220743.speaker: Mission Control
a10a-1220743.text: Apollo Control here. The crew is still rather busy in the landmark tracking exercise and a few minutes ago asked Spacecraft Communicator Jack Lousma for a few more minutes to complete this particular run before they picked up with the discussion. We will leave the circuit up, though, and pick up the conversation when it does resume.

a10a-1220743.speaker: Young
a10a-1220743.text: No, you can pitch back up, if you will?

a10a-1220743.speaker: Stafford
a10a-1220743.text: Okay, Houston, Apollo 10. Go ahead. We're between the F-1 and 130 sites.

a10a-1220743.speaker: Lousma
a10a-1220743.text: Okay. Tom. Here is our plan-of-attack on this fuel cell. First, we're going to look at the fuel cell temperature for a little while, and after we've done that, we're going to put it back on line to look at the temperatures it generates versus its loading. And then we're going to work up a fuel cell purge. We've got 25 hours of hydrogen purging available. Looks like we've lost a pump package in that fuel cell 1, but we're going to maintain the temperatures of the fuel cell by purging it, and then we'll use the cell only for burns, et cetera. At the present time, we're not proposing any changes

a10a-1220743.speaker: Stafford
a10a-1220743.text: Okay, real good. Thank you, Jack.

a10a-1220743.speaker: Cernan
a10a-1220743.text: Okay, Jack. We did - when the heater cycled, we were looking at about 20 to 20.2 volts and we've got the main bus voltage undervolts light. I've been cycling the heaters to the Auto position on the Cryos, one at a time, as they appeared to need it. It's just not a good feeling to have those lights - undervolts lights come on in here. I've also temporarily turned the power on the High Gain Antenna, Off, until we can catch a High Gain again.

a10a-1220743.speaker: Lousma
a10a-1220743.text: Roger. We copy.

a10a-1220743.speaker: Stafford
a10a-1220743.text: And we've also turned - We've also turned the potable H 2 O heater, Off. Just some other small things to start saving power.

a10a-1220743.speaker: Lousma
a10a-1220743.text: Roger. High Gain Antenna, and Potable Water Heater, Off.

a10a-1220743.speaker: Cernan
a10a-1220743.text: So, Jack. If you see my Cryo pressure dropping, don't hesitate to tell me to get the heater On. I just don't like to put all four of them on. We split the load when we get the lights on.

a10a-1220743.speaker: Lousma
a10a-1220743.text: Roger. Understand you're cycling your Cryo heaters, and we'll watch the temperatures.

a10a-1220743.speaker: Cernan
a10a-1220743.text: Thank you.

a10a-1220743.speaker: Stafford
a10a-1220743.text: Okay, John. This 130 is 1 nautical mile to the north.

a10a-1220743.speaker: Young
a10a-1220743.text: That look right for the numbers I'm supposed to load in - 1 north?

a10a-1220743.speaker: Stafford
a10a-1220743.text: Yes.

a10a-1220743.speaker: Young
a10a-1220743.text: Okay, roll right 10 - go right 11 degrees.

a10a-1220743.speaker: Stafford
a10a-1220743.text: Okay.

a10a-1220743.speaker: Young
a10a-1220743.text: When do we come up on it?

a10a-1220743.speaker: Stafford
a10a-1220743.text: You acquire at 122:29; you've got 13 minutes to go.

a10a-1220743.speaker: Young
a10a-1220743.text: Okay.

a10a-1220743.speaker: Stafford
a10a-1220743.text: What were the numbers - is this the numbers that you got, babe?

a10a-1220743.speaker: Young
a10a-1220743.text: That's all the numbers I got.

a10a-1220743.speaker: Stafford
a10a-1220743.text: That 89, that's the numbers you got.

a10a-1220743.speaker: Young
a10a-1220743.text: Yes.

a10a-1220743.speaker: Stafford
a10a-1220743.text: Well, you just loaded - What were the numbers you got on F-1?

a10a-1220743.speaker: Stafford
a10a-1220743.text: That was 019...

a10a-1220743.speaker: Young
a10a-1220743.text: Plus 44157.

a10a-1220743.speaker: Young
a10a-1220743.text: Minus 00259. Let me see what I got on F-l the other day.

a10a-1220743.speaker: Stafford
a10a-1220743.text: Minus 00259?

a10a-1220743.speaker: Young
a10a-1220743.text: Yes. I'll put that down.

a10a-1220743.speaker: Stafford
a10a-1220743.text: What was the first one? Plus?

a10a-1220743.speaker: Young
a10a-1220743.text: Plus. Yes, plus 01991. Okay.

a10a-1220743.speaker: Stafford
a10a-1220743.text: Okay, you rolled 11 degrees.

a10a-1220743.speaker: Young
a10a-1220743.text: Let me see the Flight Plan.

a10a-1220743.speaker: Stafford
a10a-1220743.text: There it is. Here you go, babe.

a10a-1220743.speaker: Cernan
a10a-1220743.text: When did we get into lunar orbit?

a10a-1220743.speaker: Stafford
a10a-1220743.text: It was 70 - what? 15 something - 16.

a10a-1220743.speaker: Young
a10a-1220743.text: Okay. I hear that goddam Master Alarm; it's still ringing in my ears.

a10a-1220743.speaker: Young
a10a-1220743.text: Can you track the landing site?

a10a-1220743.speaker: Cernan
a10a-1220743.text: [Garble].

a10a-1220743.speaker: Stafford
a10a-1220743.text: What have you got in there?

a10a-1220743.speaker: Young
a10a-1220743.text: I didn't write it down...

a10a-1220743.speaker: Stafford
a10a-1220743.text: I got a good one out here. Ready to go?

a10a-1220743.speaker: Young
a10a-1220743.text: Yes.

a10a-1220743.speaker: Stafford
a10a-1220743.text: Hold it. I'm talking about the targets of opportunity.

a10a-1220743.speaker: Young
a10a-1220743.text: Well, what time is this other thing here, Tom?

a10a-1220743.speaker: Stafford
a10a-1220743.text: We got a ways to go; we're not even up to landing site 1 yet; we're just coming up to Messier - to Secchi. You got the Flight Plan babe; it's 129 something.

a10a-1220743.speaker: Young
a10a-1220743.text: According to this here, we're coming up on it.

a10a-1220743.speaker: Stafford
a10a-1220743.text: 130? Well, shucks: we couldn't be, baby. I just got a big old Taruntius out there

a10a-1220743.speaker: Young
a10a-1220743.text: Did I load the wrong numbers?

a10a-1220743.speaker: Stafford
a10a-1220743.text: Can't be.

a10a-1220743.speaker: Cernan
a10a-1220743.text: Yes, there's Taruntius H, G, P, and Q right up here.

a10a-1220743.speaker: Stafford
a10a-1220743.text: Let's look at what the Flight Plan says. It's 129 something.

a10a-1220743.speaker: Stafford
a10a-1220743.text: Huh?

a10a-1220743.speaker: Young
a10a-1220743.text: What time does the Flight Plan say?

a10a-1220743.speaker: Stafford
a10a-1220743.text: Well, you got the Flight Plan?

a10a-1220743.speaker: Young
a10a-1220743.text: Yes, here you go. Shit.

a10a-1220743.speaker: Stafford
a10a-1220743.text: It's 129, John. 122:29, so we got 9 minutes. It's by Landing Site 2, you know. That little pimple on the side of 130.

a10a-1220743.speaker: Young
a10a-1220743.text: Yes. Oh - there's the Taruntius twins, there.

a10a-1220743.speaker: Stafford
a10a-1220743.text: Yes, can you see them pretty well?

a10a-1220743.speaker: Young
a10a-1220743.text: Yes.

a10a-1220743.speaker: Stafford
a10a-1220743.text: What we'll do is Messier.

a10a-1220743.speaker: Young
a10a-1220743.text: Tom, could you pitch over about 5 degrees?

a10a-1220743.speaker: Stafford
a10a-1220743.text: Yes.

a10a-1220743.speaker: Young
a10a-1220743.text: And hold that attitude, whatever it is?

a10a-1220743.speaker: Stafford
a10a-1220743.text: Right there?

a10a-1220743.speaker: Young
a10a-1220743.text: Yes.

a10a-1220743.speaker: Stafford
a10a-1220743.text: There's Mount Marilyn.

a10a-1220743.speaker: Mission Control
a10a-1220743.text: This is Apollo Control here; 53 minutes remaining until Loss Of Signal on this 24th lunar revolution; continuing to stand by for resumption of communications between Apollo 10 and the ground.

a10a-1220743.speaker: Stafford
a10a-1220743.text: Here comes big old Maskelyne, way up there.

a10a-1220743.speaker: Cernan
a10a-1220743.text: That bright one; is that Censorinus?

a10a-1220743.speaker: Stafford
a10a-1220743.text: Yes, Censorinus A. I'm holding you right on 11 degrees, John.

a10a-1220743.speaker: Young
a10a-1220743.text: Okay.

a10a-1220743.speaker: Cernan
a10a-1220743.text: I sure hope f:8's going to be alright for looking at this Moon with this color film.

a10a-1220743.speaker: Stafford
a10a-1220743.text: Okay, your IP on this one is Maskelyne B. You got a little blooper right up here on Maskelyne B, and I can lead you into that, babe. How much color film we got left?

a10a-1220743.speaker: Cernan
a10a-1220743.text: I don't know.

a10a-1220743.speaker: Stafford
a10a-1220743.text: We'll shoot some on the way - of the Earth - going back.

a10a-1220743.speaker: Stafford
a10a-1220743.text: Do you have that special color film on while I'm tracking for John, here?

a10a-1220743.speaker: Cernan
a10a-1220743.text: No, I don't have it on, Tom. Got black and white on.

a10a-1220743.speaker: Stafford
a10a-1220743.text: Okay.

a10a-1220743.speaker: Young
a10a-1220743.text: Now's the time to get the world coming up.

a10a-1220743.speaker: Stafford
a10a-1220743.text: No, your world's done gone way behind us, babe.

a10a-1220743.speaker: Young
a10a-1220743.text: Oh, have you already missed it?

a10a-1220743.speaker: Stafford
a10a-1220743.text: Yes, it'll be on the zero horizon at 29:03.

a10a-1220743.speaker: Young
a10a-1220743.text: We already got it, huh?

a10a-1220743.speaker: Stafford
a10a-1220743.text: Oh, yes; I could see the son of a bitch out there. Oh, I got the landing site; I got Moltke, Messier, [garble] the blooper, and shit, we're all set, babe. You want to pop a quick one of Censorinus here?

a10a-1220743.speaker: Cernan
a10a-1220743.text: Yes.

a10a-1220743.speaker: Stafford
a10a-1220743.text: Don't wait too long, because I - too short...

a10a-1220743.speaker: Cernan
a10a-1220743.text: [Garble] to here. Let me get the site through it.

a10a-1220743.speaker: Cernan
a10a-1220743.text: [Garble] Landing Site 1 [garble].

a10a-1220743.speaker: Young
a10a-1220743.text: There's the...

a10a-1220743.speaker: Stafford
a10a-1220743.text: Here you go, Gene-o.

a10a-1220743.speaker: Young
a10a-1220743.text: Apollo Ridge.

a10a-1220743.speaker: Cernan
a10a-1220743.text: Yes.

a10a-1220743.speaker: Stafford
a10a-1220743.text: [Garble] coming up, babe. Okay, we're going to be there at 2:20 - 2:29.

a10a-1220743.speaker: Young
a10a-1220743.text: It's really baldy, isn't it?

a10a-1220743.speaker: Stafford
a10a-1220743.text: Yes.

a10a-1220743.speaker: Young
a10a-1220743.text: That's a bright little bastard.

a10a-1220743.speaker: Stafford
a10a-1220743.text: Yes, I'll bet you can really see boulders on it.

a10a-1220743.speaker: Young
a10a-1220743.text: Yes.

a10a-1220743.speaker: Stafford
a10a-1220743.text: Okay, your IP lead-in is Maskelyne B, and you should just be starting to see it now. I got the landing site.

a10a-1220743.speaker: Young
a10a-1220743.text: Boot Hill.

a10a-1220743.speaker: Cernan
a10a-1220743.text: Let me get that one for a while, will you?

a10a-1220743.speaker: Young
a10a-1220743.text: Duke Island and Boot Hill. There we go.

a10a-1220743.speaker: Stafford
a10a-1220743.text: You got it? Okay, at...

a10a-1220743.speaker: Young
a10a-1220743.text: I don't have it.

a10a-1220743.speaker: Stafford
a10a-1220743.text: ...29:03. It should be up on your horizon...

a10a-1220743.speaker: Young
a10a-1220743.text: You're a ways out. babe.

a10a-1220743.speaker: Young
a10a-1220743.text: There's Dry River. Little Big Snake and Little Snake Rille.

a10a-1220743.speaker: Stafford
a10a-1220743.text: I got it.

a10a-1220743.speaker: Young
a10a-1220743.text: Okay.

a10a-1220743.speaker: Cernan
a10a-1220743.text: There's Moltke, huh?

a10a-1220743.speaker: Stafford
a10a-1220743.text: You better believe it. Okay. John. Let me know when you want to mark.

a10a-1220743.speaker: Young
a10a-1220743.text: Good.

a10a-1220743.speaker: Stafford
a10a-1220743.text: We're shooting at 30:37. You got about 30 seconds to go.

a10a-1220743.speaker: Young
a10a-1220743.text: Yes.

a10a-1220743.speaker: Stafford
a10a-1220743.text: I got one for you there just standing out loud and clear; that pimple oil the edge of the crater. And I've got that crater; it's as big as [garble] I got these three balls [garble].

a10a-1220743.speaker: Young
a10a-1220743.text: Okay. there's [garble].

a10a-1220743.speaker: Stafford
a10a-1220743.text: Yes. Stand by on the mark, babe.

a10a-1220743.speaker: Young
a10a-1220743.text: There we go.

a10a-1220743.speaker: Stafford
a10a-1220743.text: Did you get one?

a10a-1220743.speaker: Young
a10a-1220743.text: No, I ain't got one yet. When do you want one?

a10a-1220743.speaker: Stafford
a10a-1220743.text: Any time now; you're good; you're good; you're Go.

a10a-1220743.speaker: Young
a10a-1220743.text: Go.

a10a-1220743.speaker: Stafford
a10a-1220743.text: Did you get one?

a10a-1220743.speaker: Young
a10a-1220743.text: Go.

a10a-1220743.speaker: Stafford
a10a-1220743.text: Okay. Okay. Okay, 10 seconds gone. 15, 20, 25. That makes two. 5, 10, 15, 20, 25. That makes three. 5, 10, 15, 20, 25. That makes four, John. One to go, babe. 5, 10, 15, 20, 25. That makes five. You got them. Proceed. All we need.

a10a-1220743.speaker: Young
a10a-1220743.text: Yes, that's it, too. That's the right one. God, it's hard to recognize things [garble].

a10a-1220743.speaker: Stafford
a10a-1220743.text: How are your eyes doing? Pretty bad?

a10a-1220743.speaker: Young
a10a-1220743.text: Burning like a son of a bitch.

a10a-1223318.speaker: Cernan
a10a-1223318.text: Yes, got them on Omni. Should have them on Omni. We - For landmark tracking, we have to have - use Omni.

a10a-1223318.speaker: Stafford
a10a-1223318.text: Hello, Houston. Apollo 10.

a10a-1223318.speaker: Young
a10a-1223318.text: Now, listen. We got to let it run - run for 30 seconds.

a10a-1223318.speaker: Lousma
a10a-1223318.text: Apollo 10, Houston. Go ahead.

a10a-1223318.speaker: Stafford
a10a-1223318.text: Roger. We've just finished Landmark 130. We've got them all in.

a10a-1223318.speaker: Lousma
a10a-1223318.text: Very good. We have ginned up a fuel cell 1 plan. Over.

a10a-1223318.speaker: Stafford
a10a-1223318.text: Okay. Stand by. [Long pause.]

a10a-1223318.speaker: Young
a10a-1223318.text: Houston, 10. You got the data off 130?

a10a-1223318.speaker: Lousma
a10a-1223318.text: Houston. Say again, please.

a10a-1223318.speaker: Young
a10a-1223318.text: Roger. Do you have the data off 130 yet?

a10a-1223318.speaker: Lousma
a10a-1223318.text: Stand by. [Pause.]

a10a-1223318.speaker: Lousma
a10a-1223318.text: That's affirmative, 10. We've got the data off 130 now.

a10a-1223318.speaker: Young
a10a-1223318.text: Okay. When we're at real time, I'll just hold on. I understand this is the one that's really important, so I can hang on to this until you give me a Go.

a10a-1223318.speaker: Lousma
a10a-1223318.text: Roger. That's fine. And we got it now. [Long pause.]

a10a-1223318.speaker: Stafford
a10a-1223318.text: Want me to read that stuff to you? Okay, Gene-o. Stand by to copy this stuff.

a10a-1223318.speaker: Cernan
a10a-1223318.text: Alright.

a10a-1223318.speaker: Young
a10a-1223318.text: This is working real good, Tom; boy, it's just beautiful.

a10a-1223318.speaker: Stafford
a10a-1223318.text: For the fuel cell. Are you still shooting pictures?

a10a-1223318.speaker: Cernan
a10a-1223318.text: No, I'm not.

a10a-1223318.speaker: Stafford
a10a-1223318.text: Okay. The camera's still clicking.

a10a-1223318.speaker: Cernan
a10a-1223318.text: Go ahead, Houston. This is 10, with your fuel cell plan.

a10a-1223318.speaker: Lousma
a10a-1223318.text: Okay. Fuel cell plan is relatively simple. We're just going to leave it off line, open circuit, and we want you to turn the fuel cell 1 inline heaters off and then monitor the skin temperature. Monitor the temperature to stay between 390 and 410 [°F, 199° and 210°C], cycling the inline heaters on and off to maintain 390 to 410 [°F, 199° to 210°C]. This will keep our water production to a minimum, reducing our requirement to purge, and we may be able to go as long as 50 hours in this manner without purging. During the day, we will work out procedures to use during your sleep period on skin temp

a10a-1223318.speaker: Cernan
a10a-1223318.text: Okay, Jack. You must have been reading the same malfunction procedures I was. The fuel cell heater has been off now ever since we went through LOS. I've got a question on the heater. It's an Auto heater, which recycles somewhere around 380, 390 degrees [°F, 193°, 199°C]. Do you just want me to turn it to Auto position if it starts dropping, is that correct?

a10a-1223318.speaker: Lousma
a10a-1223318.text: Negative, 10.

a10a-1223318.speaker: Cernan
a10a-1223318.text: Or am I wrong about that heater?

a10a-1223318.speaker: Stafford
a10a-1223318.text: You finished, John?

a10a-1223318.speaker: Lousma
a10a-1223318.text: We want you to manually keep the temperature between 390 and 410 [°F, 199° and 210°C] by cycling the heater switch. Over.

a10a-1223318.speaker: Stafford
a10a-1223318.text: You finished, babe?

a10a-1223318.speaker: Young
a10a-1223318.text: For these four.

a10a-1223318.speaker: Cernan
a10a-1223318.text: What are you reading on the heater - the skin temperature right now?

a10a-1223318.speaker: Lousma
a10a-1223318.text: Stand by.

a10a-1223318.speaker: Stafford
a10a-1223318.text: Okay. I've got to go inertial. Pitch around so we'll pick it up on the other side.

a10a-1223318.speaker: Lousma
a10a-1223318.text: Right now, we're reading skin temperature of 423 [°F, 217°C], 10.

a10a-1223318.speaker: Young
a10a-1223318.text: Yes, but we've got to get a realign, don't we?

a10a-1223318.speaker: Stafford
a10a-1223318.text: Yes. But I'd do this first so you can get a realign, see? Here we're come around and I'll pitch around.

a10a-1223318.speaker: Cernan
a10a-1223318.text: Okay. I'm reading about 430 [°F, 221°C], I guess, and it's been pretty stable. I'll turn the heater On, say down around 390 [°F, 199°C], and keep it between 390 and 410 [°F, 199° and 210°C].

a10a-1223318.speaker: Stafford
a10a-1223318.text: Gimbal and pitch.

a10a-1223318.speaker: Lousma
a10a-1223318.text: Roger, And whenever you've got some time there, we would like to update your state vector and pass you some PADs.

a10a-1223318.speaker: Stafford
a10a-1223318.text: Okay. We're in Accept.

a10a-1223318.speaker: Lousma
a10a-1223318.text: Roger, 10. [Pause.]

a10a-1223318.speaker: Cernan
a10a-1223318.text: Okay. I'm ready to copy your PAD, and I guess I've got another question. You might be thinking up some words and things we can pull off the line here pretty quick in case we do get some under-volting problems going behind the backside, and I'm ready to copy your PAD.

a10a-1223318.speaker: Lousma
a10a-1223318.text: Roger. We're working on that and we will give you the word. I have a map update PAD, Rev-25: 123:18:32, 123:29...

a10a-1223318.speaker: Stafford
a10a-1223318.text: Hold it.

a10a-1223318.speaker: Cernan
a10a-1223318.text: Wait a minute. Wait a minute.

a10a-1223318.speaker: Stafford
a10a-1223318.text: Hold it, hold it.

a10a-1223318.speaker: Cernan
a10a-1223318.text: Hey, Jack. Wait a minute. Wait a minute, Jack. I thought you meant a PAD. Wait. We've got to get the right book out here. Hold it. Start it over again.

a10a-1223318.speaker: Lousma
a10a-1223318.text: Roger, I have a maneuver PAD.

a10a-1223318.speaker: Cernan
a10a-1223318.text: Go ahead with Rev-25, now.

a10a-1223318.speaker: Lousma
a10a-1223318.text: Okay, Rev-25.

a10a-1223318.speaker: Stafford
a10a-1223318.text: Fixing to do a map update. Over.

a10a-1223318.speaker: Lousma
a10a-1223318.text: Roger. Want you to check the AOS to be 124:04:21; sunset, 124:44:39.

a10a-1223318.speaker: Young
a10a-1223318.text: I concur.

a10a-1223318.speaker: Lousma
a10a-1223318.text: Okay. I've got a landmark tracking PAD.

a10a-1223318.speaker: Young
a10a-1223318.text: Go ahead.

a10a-1223318.speaker: Lousma
a10a-1223318.text: Okay. Charlie Papa 1: 123:38:14, 123:41:13, three balls, 051, three balls, north 13 miles, 12, 41. Charlie Papa 2: 123:53:35, 123:55:17, three balls, north 05, 04, 42. Foxtrot 1: 124:06:20, 124:08:30, three balls, 329, three balls, north 10, 10, 40. Landmark 130: 124:27:28, 124:29:00, three balls, 265, three balls, north at 12, 12, 41. Give me a readback and tell me when you are ready for a maneuver PAD. Over.

a10a-1223318.speaker: Young
a10a-1223318.text: Roger.

a10a-1223318.speaker: Lousma
a10a-1223318.text: Readback correct.

a10a-1223318.speaker: Young
a10a-1223318.text: Ready for the PAD.

a10a-1223318.speaker: Lousma
a10a-1223318.text: Okay. This is TEI number 25, SPS/G&N: 36750, minus 0.61, plus 0.75; 125:40:03.81. plus 3100.8, plus 0011.2, plus 0115.4; roll is NA, pitch is 064, and the rest is NA. Your ullage is two jets for 14 seconds. Over.

a10a-1223318.speaker: Cernan
a10a-1223318.text: Roger. TEI 25, SPS/G&N: 36750, minus 0.61, plus 0.75; 125:40:03.81; plus 31008, plus 00112, plus 01154. Roll is NA, pitch is 064, and two jets for 14 seconds.

a10a-1223318.speaker: Lousma
a10a-1223318.text: Roger. That's a good readback, and we're finished with our uplink. The computer is yours; go to Block. Over.

a10a-1223318.speaker: Cernan
a10a-1223318.text: Okay. We're in Block. [Long pause.]

a10a-1223318.speaker: Young
a10a-1223318.text: Houston, this is 10. That F-l was right near the subsolar point, and boy I really had a lot of trouble trying to figure out transfer. You could see it okay in the telescope but when you transfer from the telescope to the sextant it just vanishes.

a10a-1223318.speaker: Lousma
a10a-1223318.text: Roger, 10. What target was that?

a10a-1223318.speaker: Lousma
a10a-1223318.text: Roger. F-1.

a10a-1223318.speaker: Young
a10a-1223318.text: CP-2 is sort of that way, too.

a10a-1223318.speaker: Lousma
a10a-1223318.text: Roger. [Pause.]

a10a-1223318.speaker: Stafford
a10a-1223318.text: Okay, Houston. Apollo 10. I'm going to pitch around and go to 092, inertial.

a10a-1223318.speaker: Lousma
a10a-1223318.text: Roger, 10.

a10a-1223318.speaker: Young
a10a-1223318.text: It doesn't vanish. It's there, but you just can't see it. That sounds kind of funny. It's got the landmark in there, landmark line of sight and the lunar line of sight in there, all in one in the sextant, and you've got two different images and they're so bright it just doesn't - unless it has the dark feature in it, which most of these places don't. You just isn't recognizable.

a10a-1223318.speaker: Lousma
a10a-1223318.text: Roger, 10. Understand it's hard to see because it's bright as opposed to its size. Is that affirmative?

a10a-1223318.speaker: Young
a10a-1223318.text: That's correct.

a10a-1223318.speaker: Young
a10a-1223318.text: I just don't get any definition. It's a bright blob down there, and there's whole bunch of bright blobs down there.

a10a-1223318.speaker: Lousma
a10a-1223318.text: Roger. Copy.

a10a-1224936.speaker: Lousma
