a10a-1224936.text: Apollo 10, Houston. John, wherever you have a target that looks too bright in the sextant, we just recommend finding it in the telescope and using it that way. Over.

a10a-1224936.speaker: Lousma
a10a-1224936.text: Apollo 10, Houston. How do you read?

a10a-1224936.speaker: Lousma
a10a-1224936.text: Apollo 10, Houston. Standing by. Over.

a10a-1224936.speaker: Stafford
a10a-1224936.text: Roger. We're just squared away down to a better IMU align attitude. Over.

a10a-1224936.speaker: Lousma
a10a-1224936.text: Roger. And I'd like to tell John that he can use the telescope where necessary, if field of view in the sextant is too bright.

a10a-1224936.speaker: Young
a10a-1224936.text: Okay. I'm outstanding. 130 is no problem; that's easy to get, so I used the sextant on it. But maybe on F-1 and CP-2, I'll use the telescope.

a10a-1224936.speaker: Lousma
a10a-1224936.text: Roger. Go ahead and use that telescope if it's too bright to get in the sextant. [Long pause.]

a10a-1224936.speaker: Young
a10a-1224936.text: Boy! Whoever thought of using the telescope on landmark tracking.

a10a-1224936.speaker: Lousma
a10a-1224936.text: Say again, 10. [Pause.]

a10a-1224936.speaker: Young
a10a-1224936.text: I was just making a facetious remark.

a10a-1224936.speaker: Lousma
a10a-1224936.text: Roger. That's what I thought. And they'll buy the telescope data. And we'd like to have the High Gain Antenna for a dump. Over.

a10a-1224936.speaker: Cernan
a10a-1224936.text: Okay, Jack. [Long pause.]

a10a-1224936.speaker: Cernan
a10a-1224936.text: Houston, this is 10. Can you give us some...

a10a-1224936.speaker: Lousma
a10a-1224936.text: Apollo 10, Houston. Say again, please. [Long pause.]

a10a-1224936.speaker: Cernan
a10a-1224936.text: Could you give me some High Gain angles, please, for my attitude?

a10a-1224936.speaker: Lousma
a10a-1224936.text: Standby. [Long pause.]

a10a-1224936.speaker: Lousma
a10a-1224936.text: This is Capcom.

a10a-1224936.speaker: Cernan
a10a-1224936.text: Go ahead, Houston. [Pause.]

a10a-1224936.speaker: Lousma
a10a-1224936.text: Apollo 10, Houston. If you haven't found them already, it's pitch minus 70, yaw 192. Over.

a10a-1224936.speaker: Cernan
a10a-1224936.text: Roger, I got them; [garble]. I'll be with you in a minute.

a10a-1230038.speaker: Cernan
a10a-1230038.text: Houston, you got us now?

a10a-1230038.speaker: Lousma
a10a-1230038.text: Hello there, Apollo 10. Houston is reading you loud and clear. We're going to start the dump.

a10a-1230038.speaker: Cernan
a10a-1230038.text: Okay. She's all yours.

a10a-1230038.speaker: Lousma
a10a-1230038.text: Roger. And your LOS will be at 123:18, about 17 minutes. And we owe you a powerdown list.

a10a-1230038.speaker: Stafford
a10a-1230038.text: Roger. Will you have it by then? Over.

a10a-1230038.speaker: Lousma
a10a-1230038.text: If we don't, we'll find out why.

a10a-1230038.speaker: Stafford
a10a-1230038.text: Okay.

a10a-1230038.speaker: Lousma
a10a-1230038.text: Apollo 10, Houston. We have some information on potential powerdown items. Over.

a10a-1230038.speaker: Stafford
a10a-1230038.text: Stand by.

a10a-1230038.speaker: Cernan
a10a-1230038.text: Okay, Jack. Go ahead.

a10a-1230038.speaker: Lousma
a10a-1230038.text: Okay. If you don't want to interfere with tracking and photography operations, there's not much more that you can power down that you've not already powered down. However, if you elect to terminate your tracking and photography operations, refer to checklist page S2-8 which is powerdown, SPS burn. Start at the top and start powering down those items. However, do not power down Batt C. Delete Batt C on Main A and B from the checklist and delete fuel cell pumps, 3, Off. Delete those two items and use that powerdown checklist as your guide. Over.

a10a-1230038.speaker: Cernan
a10a-1230038.text: Okay, Jack. Yes, I was looking at that. I guess what I was looking for was some words on - not on emergency powerdown but, you know, in case this Undervolt comes on and persists to stay on, there might be a few other little things that we've overlooked, like I'm playing these heaters manually. We turned the portable heater off and turn the S-band off when we lose you, and a few of those things. I wasn't looking for the emergency conditions, just maybe a few good words or something that would be very obvious to you and not to us.

a10a-1230038.speaker: Lousma
a10a-1230038.text: Roger. You've already done a pretty good job of figuring that out, Gene.

a10a-1230038.speaker: Cernan
a10a-1230038.text: Okay. We thank you.

a10a-1230038.speaker: Stafford
a10a-1230038.text: Okay, Houston. Apollo 10. Just keep us informed, because this landmark tracking is real important. We'll get this bear wired down and we've already got one set, and we're going to continue on here and we'll monitor this cell. And, naturally, if the thing really starts to go out on us, we know what the mission rule is on it. But right now, we plan to continue on and primarily concentrate on the landmark tracking. We've shot so much photography we're about out of color film. We're saving a little bit for the way back. And we still have some black and white to go, and we'll do some of that, but t

a10a-1230038.speaker: Lousma
a10a-1230038.text: Roger, Tom. We see no reason to change your plan of attack, and we have a change to landmark tracking update PAD Foxtrot 1. Over.

a10a-1230038.speaker: Stafford
a10a-1230038.text: Okay. Stand by and I'll copy it. [Pause.]

a10a-1230038.speaker: Cernan
a10a-1230038.text: Okay. Go ahead.

a10a-1230038.speaker: Lousma
a10a-1230038.text: Okay. On Rev-25, target Foxtrot 1, the T 2 time should be changed. T 2 should be 124:08:03.

a10a-1230038.speaker: Cernan
a10a-1230038.text: Okay. I got: 03 vice 30.

a10a-1230038.speaker: Lousma
a10a-1230038.text: Roger. That's affirmative. And so far, all the tracking data looks real good.

a10a-1230038.speaker: Stafford
a10a-1230038.text: Roger. Thank you. You got a pretty good way to evaluate it in real time, there? Over.

a10a-1230038.speaker: Lousma
a10a-1230038.text: That's affirmative.

a10a-1230038.speaker: Young
a10a-1230038.text: I didn't get all the marks on one of those places, because - because I lost it in the sextant.

a10a-1230038.speaker: Lousma
a10a-1230038.text: Roger. We copy, 10.

a10a-1230038.speaker: Young
a10a-1230038.text: I forget, It's one of the CPs back there. It's not 1.

a10a-1230038.speaker: Stafford
a10a-1230038.text: It's CP-2.

a10a-1230038.speaker: Lousma
a10a-1230038.text: Roger. We detected that on CP-2, but 130 is the real important one, and that's coming through real good.

a10a-1230038.speaker: Stafford
a10a-1230038.text: Roger. Thank you.

a10a-1230038.speaker: Lousma
a10a-1230038.text: Apollo 10, Houston. We have a revision to the way in which we'd like you to maintain temperature in the Cryo tanks. Over.

a10a-1230038.speaker: Cernan
a10a-1230038.text: Okay, Jack. Go ahead.

a10a-1230038.speaker: Lousma
a10a-1230038.text: Roger. Instead of using your heaters to maintain the temperature in the Cryo tanks, use your fans manually. Over.

a10a-1230038.speaker: Cernan
a10a-1230038.text: Okay. Use the fans to maintain the pressure in the Cryo tanks. Right? Is that correct?

a10a-1230038.speaker: Lousma
a10a-1230038.text: Use the fans to maintain the temperature in the Cryo tanks. This will be - correction - pressure. This will require less current and allow finer control. Over.

a10a-1230038.speaker: Cernan
a10a-1230038.text: Very good. Thank you. Those are the kind of good words I really wanted. Thank you very much.

a10a-1230038.speaker: Lousma
a10a-1230038.text: Roger. We'll try to think up some more.

a10a-1230038.speaker: Lousma
a10a-1230038.text: Apollo 10, Houston. You're going around the corner in about a minute and a half. Your AOS is 124:04, and we'd like you to check and make sure the VHF is all Off. Over.

a10a-1230038.speaker: Young
a10a-1230038.text: That's a good point.

a10a-1230038.speaker: Young
a10a-1230038.text: Check the T/R switches. They could be on. As a matter of fact, we can turn off those switches on the audio control panel. There was no need - bad Comm.

a10a-1230038.speaker: Stafford
a10a-1230038.text: 124:04, and we'll check.

a10a-1230038.speaker: Cernan
a10a-1230038.text: Yes, Jack. I checked. All the VHF switches are all Off.

a10a-1230038.speaker: Stafford
a10a-1230038.text: Oh, I've already turned all those off.

a10a-1230038.speaker: Lousma
a10a-1230038.text: Roger. Thank you.

a10a-1230038.speaker: Cernan
a10a-1230038.text: Okay. Ain't many we don't need.

a10a-1230038.speaker: Cernan
a10a-1230038.text: Pshew!

a10a-1230038.speaker: Stafford
a10a-1230038.text: TEI is 3,600 and some feet per second [1,100 m/s].

a10a-1280057.speaker: Stafford
a10a-1280057.text: OK, should be on the horizon [garble] your first acquisition.

a10a-1280057.speaker: Young
a10a-1280057.text: OK, I can't see anything. Optics are in the way. But we'll get that. That's a useless damn thing - that optics. Coming down now.

a10a-1280057.speaker: Duke
a10a-1280057.text: Hello. Apollo 10, Houston. We're standing by.

a10a-1280057.speaker: Stafford
a10a-1280057.text: Roger; we're right in the middle of the track on [garble]. We'll call you later.

a10a-1280057.speaker: Stafford
a10a-1280057.text: OK, at 04: 55, you should be able to start tracking him and - [garble] as far as pushing the button - a little over 30 seconds.

a10a-1280057.speaker: Stafford
a10a-1280057.text: 04:55 should be - 10 seconds, he should be 30 degrees down.

a10a-1280057.speaker: Stafford
a10a-1280057.text: Tell me when you mark, John.

a10a-1280057.speaker: Stafford
a10a-1280057.text: You're clear to mark right now.

a10a-1280057.speaker: Stafford
a10a-1280057.text: One mark. Well, we got 15 seconds [garble].

a10a-1280057.speaker: Young
a10a-1280057.text: Is that 40 seconds from my last...

a10a-1280057.speaker: Stafford
a10a-1280057.text: Yes. I can't - couldn't hear when you marked [garble].

a10a-1280057.speaker: Stafford
a10a-1280057.text: 5 seconds, 10 seconds, 15 seconds, 20 seconds, 25 seconds, 30 seconds. OK? You've got three stars.

a10a-1280057.speaker: Stafford
a10a-1280057.text: Four? Is that all you got?

a10a-1280057.speaker: Stafford
a10a-1280057.text: Sure got [garble] coming up now, John.

a10a-1280057.speaker: Young
a10a-1280057.text: [Garble]. Four marks is just as good as five.

a10a-1280057.speaker: Young
a10a-1280057.text: Four marks is just as good as five. [Garble].

a10a-1280057.speaker: Duke
a10a-1280057.text: 10, Houston. We got the data. You can proceed.

a10a-1280057.speaker: Stafford
a10a-1280057.text: It's 128:24. You've got quite a while.

a10a-1280057.speaker: Stafford
a10a-1280057.text: OK, this is the last one, and we're back to 130. After this, we only have - one landmark to track. [Garble].

a10a-1280057.speaker: Young
a10a-1280057.text: Oh, what a life, being a spaceman. Wish I could have been a professor or something.

a10a-1280057.speaker: Stafford
a10a-1280057.text: For that last - we take oblique landing site [garble] for that last thing.

a10a-1280057.speaker: Stafford
a10a-1280057.text: I can't get too freaking excited about it. After the landmarks, we do a photo strip and then we come around and fire the TEI. I can't get too excited...

a10a-1280057.speaker: Stafford
a10a-1280057.text: That's what I say. I can't get too excited about that last [garble].

a10a-1280057.speaker: Young
a10a-1280057.text: What did they do? All the way around?

a10a-1280057.speaker: Young
a10a-1280057.text: When is this other one due?

a10a-1280057.speaker: Stafford
a10a-1280057.text: OK, let me check them for you, babe.

a10a-1280057.speaker: Stafford
a10a-1280057.text: You got our altitude 166, 161, and 164. You [garble] be right in there.

a10a-1280057.speaker: Young
a10a-1280057.text: I don't know what they means. Tom. It really doesn't mean a great deal. It depends on - See, this thing over - updates as good as [garble] state vector.

a10a-1280057.speaker: Young
a10a-1280057.text: I don't know what that means [garble].

a10a-1280057.speaker: Young
a10a-1280057.text: Oh, lord, there's the gash; there's the gashes.

a10a-1280057.speaker: Stafford
a10a-1280057.text: OK, 24:16 - you got 3 minutes to go, John.

a10a-1280057.speaker: Young
a10a-1280057.text: OK, now, if I ask you to pitch over on that...

a10a-1280057.speaker: Young
a10a-1280057.text: I may have to pitch over...

a10a-1280057.speaker: Young
a10a-1280057.text: Now. I believe this here is - is where we're high around this side of it. T.P.

a10a-1280057.speaker: Young
a10a-1280057.text: Yes. It just - I just get the feeling we're higher over here than I do on the other side.

a10a-1280057.speaker: Stafford
a10a-1280057.text: OK. 128:24. So you got 2 minutes until you first pick him up and we'll be tracking on him in about 26 minutes, John. [Garble].

a10a-1280057.speaker: Young
a10a-1280057.text: OK, [garble] looking down. Well, this may be a bad mistake, but I'll give her a go.

a10a-1280057.speaker: Young
a10a-1280057.text: There's a big dry rille. A little dry rille.

a10a-1280057.speaker: Stafford
a10a-1280057.text: [Garble] track, John. You're all set. OK, 26 minutes you've got 1 minute to go - you can mark.

a10a-1280057.speaker: Young
a10a-1280057.text: [Garble] 1 minute to go and how you marking?

a10a-1280057.speaker: Young
a10a-1280057.text: I think he's too far out right now, Tom.

a10a-1280057.speaker: Stafford
a10a-1280057.text: You got it. You want to take 30 seconds [garble]?

a10a-1280057.speaker: Young
a10a-1280057.text: Oh, God. The boulders stand out.

a10a-1280057.speaker: Stafford
a10a-1280057.text: Why don't you get [garble], Gene-o? I'm going to pitch on down.

a10a-1280057.speaker: Stafford
a10a-1280057.text: OK, Houston. We've finished with landmark 130.

a10a-1280057.speaker: Young
a10a-1280057.text: What do y'all have to do now?

a10a-1280057.speaker: Stafford
a10a-1280057.text: Sleep for 3½ hours. OK, I'm turning off your suit power.

a10a-1280057.speaker: Young
a10a-1280057.text: Mine? Wait a minute. Let me hear what the ground is going to say about this shit. Oh. Excuse me.

a10a-1280057.speaker: Duke
a10a-1280057.text: 10, Houston. We've got quite a few things to talk to you about on the Flight Plan. We'd like you to, for your rest attitude, to change your roll angle from 180 to 090. Rest of it's OK. Your High Gain changes to a pitch of 00 and a yaw of 240. Over.

a10a-1280057.speaker: Young
a10a-1280057.text: OK, Charlie. Why don't you run us by that again. Nobody was on the headset.

a10a-1280057.speaker: Duke
a10a-1280057.text: OK. Roger. We've got the data. You can proceed on out of 22 [program 22], and we got the Flight Plan updates for you starting on page 3-82. Over.

a10a-1282932.speaker: Cernan
a10a-1282932.text: Go ahead, Charlie.

a10a-1282932.speaker: Duke
a10a-1282932.text: OK. On the rest attitude at 128:29, we'd like you to maneuver to a roll of 090 so we can cool down quad A, and the pitch and yaw are the same as listed in the Flight Plan. The High Gain Antenna angles are pitch of 00, yaw 240. OK. Go on down the page to fuel cell O 2 purge - we'd like you to do the fuel cell on O 2 purge on fuel cells 2 and 3. And, same page, we have a map update Rev-29, if you are ready to copy. Over.

a10a-1282932.speaker: Cernan
a10a-1282932.text: Go ahead, and I am going to go ahead and start the fuel - the O 2 purge right now on 2 and 3.

a10a-1282932.speaker: Duke
a10a-1282932.text: Do you want to read that back to me. Over.

a10a-1282932.speaker: Duke
a10a-1282932.text: Roger. And let's go on to page 3-85 in the Flight Plan.

a10a-1282932.speaker: Cernan
a10a-1282932.text: OK. By the way, we changed canister B a little bit late. Let me find it for you. I'll tell you exactly when we changed it.

a10a-1282932.speaker: Duke
a10a-1282932.text: Standing by.

a10a-1282932.speaker: Cernan
a10a-1282932.text: We changed it at 120 - We changed canister B late. We changed it at 127 hours.

a10a-1282932.speaker: Duke
a10a-1282932.text: OK. We copy canister B at 127 hours, and we have an update on page 3-85 if you're ready to copy. Over.

a10a-1282932.speaker: Cernan
a10a-1282932.text: Go ahead, Charlie.

a10a-1282932.speaker: Duke
a10a-1282932.text: OK, Gene. 3-85, the update for the oblique strip - we're giving you the same update as this morning. Roll, pitch and yaw are; roll, 180, 339, 000. Your T 0 f:8 time is 132:17:48, change to f:2.8 at 132:27:16. OK. Your T 1 time is 132:30:16. T 2 is 132:32:16. Now the f:8 and the f:2.8 f-stops are - stop changes are for the sequence camera only. We'd like you to use f:4 at 1/125 for the black and white. Over.

a10a-1282932.speaker: Cernan
a10a-1282932.text: OK. I got oblique strip; roll - roll, 180; pitch, 339; yaw, 000. T 0 is at 132:17:48 - that's at a f:8 and go to f:2 [means f:2.8] at 132:27:16; and that's all under sequence [camera]. T 1 is at 132:30:16. T 2 is at 132:32:16 and use f:4 1/125 on the black and white all the way.

a10a-1282932.speaker: Duke
a10a-1282932.text: OK, Gene-o. Good readback. Those roll, pitch and yaw angles are ORDEAL angles. OK, I've got a T - TEI-29 if you're ready to copy. Over.

a10a-1282932.speaker: Cernan
a10a-1282932.text: Go ahead.

a10a-1282932.speaker: Duke
a10a-1282932.text: OK. Before we start on the PAD, we'd like you P00 and Accept. We have a state vector for you. And coming with a TEI-29, SPS G&N: start with Noun 33, 133:37:36.69; plus 34079, plus 00166, plus 01719; pitch, 056; two jets for 14 seconds on the ullage.

a10a-1282932.speaker: Cernan
a10a-1282932.text: Charlie. Give me Noun 81 Delta-V X again, will you please?

a10a-1282932.speaker: Duke
a10a-1282932.text: Which Delta-V you want, Gene?

a10a-1282932.speaker: Cernan
a10a-1282932.text: Delta-V X .

a10a-1282932.speaker: Duke
a10a-1282932.text: OK. Delta-V X is plus 34079. Over.

a10a-1282932.speaker: Cernan
a10a-1282932.text: OK. TEI-29, SPS and G&N: Noun 33 is 133:37:36.69; Noun 81 is plus 34079, plus 00166 plus 01719; and pitch is 056. It's two jets ullage for 14 seconds.

a10a-1282932.speaker: Duke
a10a-1282932.text: Roger. That's a good readback. Now, I've got some stuff for you on the fuel cells and the cryos wed like for your sleep period. Its quite lengthy. You might have a pencil ready so you can copy down some of it, and Ill try to read it slowly and repeat all that you need. We'd like you to stir the cryos and - before going to sleep - and then turn all the fans off. We'd like optics power switch, Off, SCS Electronics to ECA. O 2 tank 2 heater, Auto, O 2 tank 1 heater to Off. Are you with me? Over.

a10a-1282932.speaker: Cernan
a10a-1282932.text: I'm with you, Charlie.

a10a-1282932.speaker: Duke
a10a-1282932.text: OK, Gene. Continuing on. We'd like H 2 tank 1 heater, Auto, H 2 tank heater to Off. You can leave battery B on Charge, and we'd like to power up the High Gain Antenna for the sleep. On the fuel cell configuration, you can leave as is, and we'll place fuel cell 1 on both Main A and Main B one and a half hours prior to the TEI burn. Over.

a10a-1282932.speaker: Cernan
a10a-1282932.text: OK, Charlie. I understand. I'll cycle the Cryo fans and then I'll [garble] optics power, Off. SCS electronic, ECA. O 2 tank heater number 2 to Auto; number 1 to Off; H 2 tank 1 to Auto, and 2 Off. Continue Batt B Charge, and I'll power up to the High Gain.

a10a-1282932.speaker: Duke
a10a-1282932.text: Roger, Gene. Good readback, Now that - at our present temperature decrease on fuel cell 1, we will not have to put it on the line prior to the above time. The minimum temperature for fuel cell 1 is now 370 degrees - that's 370 skin temp. So we'll place it on the main buses to raise the temp in lieu of using the inline heaters during trans-Earth coast. I'd like to emphasize, please do not use the fuel cell heater on fuel cell 1. And, at the present rate of decay of temperature in fuel cell l, it looks like we'll have to put it on the buses about every 20 hours. Over.

a10a-1282932.speaker: Cernan
a10a-1282932.text: Fine. That suits us fine, Charlie.

a10a-1282932.speaker: Duke
a10a-1282932.text: OK. Good. One little last thing is that we got some word - some word for you on the storage of the LM cameras and the LiOH canister. We'd like - we suggest that you wrap the cameras in an LCG and store them in A-8. Stand by one.

a10a-1282932.speaker: Duke
a10a-1282932.text: 10. Stand by. We got a recent update on the camera stowage. We'll be right with you. Over.

a10a-1282932.speaker: Stafford
a10a-1282932.text: Roger. Houston. Say again, now. We - We're going to go to the - maneuver to the sleep attitude at this time.

a10a-1282932.speaker: Duke
a10a-1282932.text: Roger. That's fine, Tom. Go ahead. Go ahead for the maneuver, and your computer is yours. And I'll be back with you when we get to High Gain on the Hasselblad and canister. Over.

a10a-1282932.speaker: Stafford
a10a-1282932.text: OK.

a10a-1284119.speaker: Young
a10a-1284119.text: Houston, Apollo 10. Over.

a10a-1284119.speaker: Duke
a10a-1284119.text: Go ahead, 10.

a10a-1284119.speaker: Young
a10a-1284119.text: Roger. Let me summarize this landmark tracking thing, the last pass. I think we only got four marks on one of those CPs. And - and let me summarize the whole thing by saying, I think you ought to throw out CP-1's first pass and F-l's first pass because I don't think they were on them - they were on the same site. I don't think CP-1 was the same site that actual CP-1 was on the other three passes. Same way for F-1's first pass. But I feel pretty good about all the rest of the sightings. I think they're all on the same spot of ground, and I'll point it out to you when we get back. And I guarante

a10a-1284119.speaker: Duke
a10a-1284119.text: Roger, John. We cop., It was really a great show on the landmark tracking. Everybody's worked real - very pleased with everything, and we understand you suggest throwing out the first pass of CP-1 and F-1 due to incorrect - possible incorrect landmarks. On the last pass of CP-1, we copy - we're only four marks on that one, but they look real good. And everybody in MPAD is happy as a clam with everything, and we're all set for you guys to go to sleep.

a10a-1284119.speaker: Young
a10a-1284119.text: OK. And if we don't learn nothing else, we ought to know where 130 is.

a10a-1284119.speaker: Duke
a10a-1284119.text: Hey, John. On - On 130 you're within 300 feet [90 meters] on your altitudes on every pass across 130. It's really great. The MPAD's calling you the mechanical man.

a10a-1284119.speaker: Young
a10a-1284119.text: I was just tracking that [garble].

a10a-1284119.speaker: Stafford
a10a-1284119.text: Well, you should have seen him. He was really putting it right on the money there. It was great.

a10a-1284119.speaker: Duke
a10a-1284119.text: Roger. We could tell that from the data, Tom. It 1ooks really great. 10, that's all we got for you. We're going to hold up on...

a10a-1284119.speaker: Stafford
a10a-1284119.text: ...[garble]. Yes, I was going to say, Charlie, if George Mueller is around there, tell him to smile. Over.

a10a-1284119.speaker: Duke
a10a-1284119.text: OK. He was grinning last night. I haven't seen him tonight. That's all we got for you, 10. We're going to hold up on this stowage of the cameras and the canister until we come back in the trans-Earth coast. Over.

a10a-1284119.speaker: Stafford
a10a-1284119.text: Yes. Roger. We're only going to be pulling about one g when the engine fires off here, Charlie. We got everything already pretty much configured for that, so we'll be in good shape to take care of the rest of it. Over.

a10a-1284119.speaker: Duke
a10a-1284119.text: Roger. We concur. Out.

a10a-1284119.speaker: Duke
a10a-1284119.text: Hello, 10. We have you on the High Gain now. Do you read me? Over.

a10a-1284119.speaker: Stafford
a10a-1284119.text: Roger, Charlie. Read you loud and clear.

a10a-1284119.speaker: Duke
a10a-1284119.text: Roger, Tom. One further recommendation. Quads Bravo and Charlie are the fattest, and we recommend for the sleep period you configure the DAP for attitude control using quads Bravo and Charlie. And otherwise you're in good shape. Good night, and we'll see you in 3½ hours or so. Over.

a10a-1284119.speaker: Stafford
a10a-1284119.text: OK. Roger.

a10a-1284119.speaker: Mission Control
a10a-1284119.text: 128:50:XX PAO: This is Apollo Control at 128 hours, 50 minutes. The Apollo 10 crew begins a 3½-hour rest period after a considerable amount of landmark tracking and photography today. We still have 23 minutes acquisition in this pass. We will stay up through the Loss Of Signal, however, we probably will not hear from the crew or contact them again during this pass. First half of the pass during this acquisition on the 27th revolution was very quiet as the crew completed landmark tracking on landmark 130. We then passed up some Flight Plan updates. Gave them procedure for the fuel cells

a10a-1284119.speaker: Stafford
a10a-1284119.text: Houston, Apollo 10. Again on these quads, you want us - we don't want to use quad A. You want us to use quads B and D? Over.

a10a-1284119.speaker: Duke
a10a-1284119.text: That's negative. Quads Bravo and Charlie. Over.

a10a-1284119.speaker: Stafford
a10a-1284119.text: Roger. You want us to fail A and Dog. Over.

a10a-1284119.speaker: Duke
a10a-1284119.text: Affirmative.

a10a-1284119.speaker: Mission Control
a10a-1284119.text: Fuel cell 1 has been off the lines since a pump associated with the fuel cell failed some time ago. The fuel cell itself is all right. There's nothing wrong with the fuel cell and that fuel cell 1 will be placed back on the line an hour and a half prior to the trans-Earth injection burn. John Young again reported on the tracking tasks and received praise from the ground for the job he has been doing in this landmark tracking. We'll continue to stay up through - live through LOS about 20 minutes from now.

a10a-1285422.speaker: Duke
a10a-1285422.text: Hello, Apollo 10, Houston. Sorry to disturb you again, but we notice your DAP quad fails incorrectly. We'd like you to load 00110 so that well have some pitch attitude control. Over.

a10a-1285422.speaker: Stafford
a10a-1285422.text: OK, you want 0 - Say that again, Charlie.

a10a-1285422.speaker: Duke
a10a-1285422.text: Roger, Tom. In register 2, we'd like 00110. Over.

a10a-1285422.speaker: Duke
a10a-1285422.text: Hello, Apollo 10. Houston. We're not going to give up. We got - we noticed your quad Charlie Auto RCS SELECT switch is Off. We'd like for you to configure Bravo and Charlie Auto RCS Select switches, On. Alpha and Dog, Off. Over.

a10a-1285422.speaker: Stafford
a10a-1285422.text: Roger. Alpha and Dog, Off; Bravo and Charlie, On.

a10a-1285422.speaker: Stafford
a10a-1285422.text: Hey, maybe it's late at night, Charlie, but you want Alpha and Charlie, Off; Bravo and Dog, On. How you going to get any pitch control?

a10a-1285422.speaker: Duke
a10a-1285422.text: We want Bravo and Charlie, On, and Alpha and Delta, Off. Over.

a10a-1285422.speaker: Stafford
a10a-1285422.text: Alrighty. Bravo and Charlie, On; Alpha and Delta, Off. Got it. Thank you.

a10a-1285422.speaker: Mission Control
a10a-1285422.text: This is Apollo Control at 129 hours, 13 minutes. We've had Loss Of Signal on revolution 27. Acquisition time for revolution 28 is 130 hours. We do not expect to have the conversation with the crew during that acquisition. We're now in a 3½-hour rest period. We will come up and bring you any conversation we do have on the next revolution. We're now showing Apollo 10 in a 67.9 by 53.8 nautical mile (125.7 x 99.6 km) orbit with an orbital period of 1 hour, 58 minutes, 50 seconds. This is Mission Control, Houston.

a10a-1285422.speaker: Mission Control
a10a-1285422.text: This is Apollo Control at 130 hours, 5 minutes. We have acquired Apollo 10 on the 28 revolution. There has been no conversation, and we do not expect any. The crew still has an hour and 52 minutes in its rest period. The TEI time, trans-Earth injection time has not changed yet, still remaining 137:36:28. This may be refined later, but the present time, that is the latest ignition time. The black team which has been led by Gerry Griffin today will change shifts slightly early this evening, and we have scheduled the change of shift news conference for 10:30 pm Central Daylight Time. If there is

a10a-1285422.speaker: Mission Control
a10a-1285422.text: This is Apollo Control at 130 hours, 15 minutes. Flight surgeon reports that Tom Stafford's heart rate is in the mid-forties, that coupled with his respiration rate indicates that he sleeping. Stafford is the only crew member being monitored at this time. John Young and Gene Cernan are in the sleep stations beneath the couches and do not have biomed monitoring at this time. This is Mission Control, Houston.

a10a_1355425.speaker: Engle
a10a_1355425.text: Apollo 10, This is Houston.

a10a_1355425.speaker: Young
a10a_1355425.text: Go ahead. Over.

a10a_1355425.speaker: Engle
a10a_1355425.text: Roger, 10. I've got a bunch of updates for you. First off, though, I would like to have you turn on your H 2 purge line heater, and we'd like to have P00 and Accept on the computer.

a10a_1355425.speaker: Stafford
a10a_1355425.text: You've got it.

a10a_1355425.speaker: Cernan
a10a_1355425.text: What kind of updates, Joe?

a10a_1355425.speaker: Engle
a10a_1355425.text: OK. I've got a maneuver PAD update and, Gene-o, this is for TEI-31. There are six items that have changed that we have different numbers for. Would you like for me to just call up those changes or do you want me to read the whole PAD?

a10a_1355425.speaker: Cernan
a10a_1355425.text: Why don't you call up the changes and then I'll read back to you the whole PAD?

a10a_1355425.speaker: Engle
a10a_1355425.text: That'll be great. And let me know when you're ready to copy.

a10a_1355425.speaker: Cernan
a10a_1355425.text: [Garble] I'm ready, but give me a lot of time between each change.

a10a_1355425.speaker: Engle
a10a_1355425.text: I sure will. Understand. OK. Then on your maneuver PAD, this is for TEI-31 under Noun 33, the time is - on seconds - is 28.21. Okay, for Noun 81.

a10a_1355425.speaker: Cernan
a10a_1355425.text: Go ahead.

a10a_1355425.speaker: Engle
a10a_1355425.text: Roger. Noun 81: Plus 36252, plus 0...

a10a_1355425.speaker: Cernan
a10a_1355425.text: No.

a10a_1355425.speaker: Engle
a10a_1355425.text: OK. Delta-V Y is plus 00400, and Delta-V Z is plus 01880. OK. Your Delta-V T is 36303, and Delta-V C is 36077. And that concludes all the changes. I'll stand by for your readback, Gene.

a10a_1355425.speaker: Cernan
a10a_1355425.text: OK, Joe. I'm going to read back the whole PAD to you.

a10a_1355425.speaker: Engle
a10a_1355425.text: Roger.

a10a_1355425.speaker: Cernan
a10a_1355425.text: TEI-31, SPS/G&N: 36685; minus 0.62, plus 0.89; 137:36:28.21, Noun 81 is plus 36252, plus 00400, plus 1880 - correction, - that's plus 01880. Roll is 181, pitch is 051, yaw is 002; apogee is NA, perigee is plus 0021.2; 36303, 2:41, 36077; 16, 146.4, 29.4. Noun 61 is minus 15.08, minus 165.00; 1203.8, 36394, 191:50:43. Deneb, 43, and Vega, 36, are the set stars. Roll is 241, pitch is 240, yaw is 013. We're going to be two-jets for 14 seconds using quads Bravo and Delta. The horizon is on the 6-degree window mark at T IG minus 1 minute. The sextant star is not available until 137:06:00. The Sun i

a10a_1355425.speaker: Engle
a10a_1355425.text: Good readback, Gene. That's all correct.

a10a_1355425.speaker: Engle
a10a_1355425.text: OK. Apollo 10, Houston. We'd like for you to put fuel cell 1 back on Main A and B, please.

a10a_1355425.speaker: Cernan
a10a_1355425.text: OK. Fuel cell 1 is coming on; main A and then main B.

a10a_1355425.speaker: Engle
a10a_1355425.text: OK. And I've got a TEI-32 maneuver PAD for you, Gene. Preliminary.

a10a_1355425.speaker: Cernan
a10a_1355425.text: Stand by.

a10a_1355425.speaker: Cernan
a10a_1355425.text: Houston, it should be on the line right now. It's carrying not quite its share of the load. When I put it on, I got the fuel cell bus disconnect, reconnected, and it stayed connected, and the same thing on bus B. It looks like it's warming up slowly.

a10a_1355425.speaker: Engle
a10a_1355425.text: OK, 10. We copy all that, and it looks OK down here.

a10a_1355425.speaker: Cernan
a10a_1355425.text: OK. And you want to give me a TEI what? 32?

a10a_1355425.speaker: Engle
a10a_1355425.text: Affirmative. 32.

a10a_1355425.speaker: Cernan
a10a_1355425.text: Go ahead.

a10a_1355425.speaker: Engle
a10a_1355425.text: OK. And prior to this PAD, 10, you can go to Block on your computer. You can have it back, now. And coming up with TEI-32, SPS/G&N: your first entry is Noun 33, 139:36:25.14; plus 3757.3, plus 0029.2, plus 0034.1. Pitch is minus 050. All else is NA. Ullage will be two jets for 14 seconds. That concludes, and I'll stand by for the readback.

a10a_1355425.speaker: Cernan
a10a_1355425.text: OK. TEI-32 and SPS/G&N: 139:36:25.14; plus 3757.3, plus 0029.2, plus 0034.1. Pitch is minus 050. Two jets for 14 seconds.

a10a_1355425.speaker: Engle
a10a_1355425.text: Readback correct, Gene-o. OK. I've got one more...

a10a_1355425.speaker: Stafford
a10a_1355425.text: OK, Houston. While we're taking this strip photography, we're going...

a10a_1355425.speaker: Cernan
a10a_1355425.text: Go ahead.

a10a_1355425.speaker: Engle
a10a_1355425.text: OK. I've got one more TEI map update, and I'm sorry to cut you out, Tom. Press on with what you were going to say.

a10a_1355425.speaker: Cernan
a10a_1355425.text: [Garble] on the map update a minute ago.

a10a_1355425.speaker: Stafford
a10a_1355425.text: You didn't send us the maneuver load, did you? And don't worry about the map update.

a10a_1355425.speaker: Engle
a10a_1355425.text: OK. Roger that.

a10a_1355425.speaker: Engle
a10a_1355425.text: 10, this is Houston. We sent up a state vector and a target load, external Delta-V.

a10a_1355425.speaker: Cernan
a10a_1355425.text: Yes. We got it.

a10a_1355425.speaker: Engle
a10a_1355425.text: Roger.

a10a_1355425.speaker: Engle
a10a_1355425.text: Apollo 10, Houston. Gene-o, did you notice about the same kind of excursions on your temperature on that fuel cell on this time on the back side?

a10a_1355425.speaker: Cernan
a10a_1355425.text: All the way, Joe, exactly as it was the previous time, only we never did get the Master Alarm, this time. And when we came out in the sunlight, she seemed to slow down. And it's ok now. We also found something; it was this light oscillation in the O 2 needle on both 2 and 3, but it's gone now, too.

a10a_1355425.speaker: Engle
a10a_1355425.text: OK. We copy that. And that's just on the dark side of the Moon. Is that affirmative?

a10a_1355425.speaker: Cernan
a10a_1355425.text: It occurs after we go into darkness about 15 minutes. And then apparently very shortly after we came out of sunrise - in the sunrise, it starts - it starts damping out.

a10a_1355425.speaker: Engle
a10a_1355425.text: OK. Understand.

a10a_1355425.speaker: Engle
a10a_1355425.text: 10, this is Houston. What are you showing for yaw now?

a10a_1355425.speaker: Stafford
a10a_1355425.text: Roger. We're making this in a different attitude than what was called up to us here. We only have just a couple of film shots left here. Over.

a10a_1355425.speaker: Engle
a10a_1355425.text: Mighty fine, Tom. Thank you.

a10a_1355425.speaker: Stafford
a10a_1355425.text: Don't worry about it. We've already got a lot of pictures of this - on this site.

a10a_1355425.speaker: Engle
a10a_1355425.text: Roger. Understand.

a10a_1355425.speaker: Stafford
a10a_1355425.text: Tell Jack to have a cup of coffee and just relax.

a10a_1355425.speaker: Engle
a10a_1355425.text: (Laughter) OK, Tom.

a10a_1355425.speaker: Stafford
a10a_1355425.text: We got more pictures of Censorinus than you can shake a stick at.

a10a_1355425.speaker: Engle
a10a_1355425.text: OK.

a10a_1355425.speaker: Young
a10a_1355425.text: In fact, I'll be surprised if there's anything left to take a picture of up here much.

a10a_1355425.speaker: Engle
a10a_1355425.text: Jack says that that's a highland dike, John.

a10a_1355425.speaker: Cernan
a10a_1355425.text: You got me there, Joe.

a10a_1355425.speaker: Engle
a10a_1355425.text: OK, 10. This is Houston. In your Flight Plan, when you go to your TEI attitude, we're going to recommend Omni Delta. Omni Delta.

a10a_1355425.speaker: Stafford
a10a_1355425.text: Roger. Omni Delta for our attitude there at a pitch of 052.

a10a_1355425.speaker: Engle
a10a_1355425.text: Affirmative.

a10a_1355425.speaker: Stafford
a10a_1355425.text: OK. As soon as we get into that attitude, I'm going to turn all Auto RCS thrusters on. Over.

a10a_1355425.speaker: Engle
a10a_1355425.text: OK. Fine, Tom. And for your info, we'll have LOS this pass at 137:07:53 and AOS with your TEI will be at 137:45:26. And, with no TEI, we'll get you - We won't get you this. But, for your info, it's going to be at 137:54:03.

a10a_1355425.speaker: Stafford
a10a_1355425.text: OK. And where is LOS again?

a10a_1355425.speaker: Cernan
a10a_1355425.text: I like your "atta boy" attitude, Joe. We'll see you at 45:26, huh?

a10a_1355425.speaker: Engle
a10a_1355425.text: Roger that.

a10a_1355425.speaker: Stafford
a10a_1355425.text: And again, just over this maria area here, this area is definitely a brownish tan. And up there in the highlands, it is a light tan and the new craters look like - more like gypsum colors - been around an gypsum mine. Over.

a10a_1355425.speaker: Engle
a10a_1355425.text: OK. We copy that, Tom. Thank you.

a10a_1355425.speaker: Young
a10a_1355425.text: Anyway, that tube ought to give the true pictures, whatever it is. True colors.

a10a_1355425.speaker: Engle
a10a_1355425.text: Yes. The colors we've been seeing on that are just exactly as you've been describing them all the way through - all the way from the whites to the browns down to the blacks. And when you talk about the brownish grays and deep grays and blacks, why, it looks just like that on the tube.

a10a_1355425.speaker: Stafford
a10a_1355425.text: Roger. Good show. One quick thing after TEI and we give you all the report, we're going to turn away so we can just look back at it and take some motion pictures of the Moon. See, then will be kind of relax time, and we'll flip the tube on for you and we'll see what it looks like in total color going away. But I hear we're going to be through Honeysuckle. Is that right? Over.

a10a_1355425.speaker: Engle
a10a_1355425.text: That's affirmative. We're coming through Honeysuckle, Tom, and I guess they're going to be watching you coast to coast for the first program of that type over there, too.

a10a_1355425.speaker: Stafford
a10a_1355425.text: OK. Have they got color over there? I say there, down below.

a10a_1355425.speaker: Engle
a10a_1355425.text: I guess they're black and white over there, Tom.

a10a_1355425.speaker: Stafford
a10a_1355425.text: OK. What I was really getting at, the station can receive it and everything from the color camera?

a10a_1355425.speaker: Engle
a10a_1355425.text: Roger that.

a10a_1355425.speaker: Stafford
a10a_1355425.text: OK. Good show.

a10a_1361453.speaker: Stafford
a10a_1361453.text: OK, Houston; Apollo 10. We're coming up on the highland areas. And again, in our general observation, even when we were down at 50,000 feet [15,000 meters], and yet you do have some rough terrain here, but it doesn't appear as sharp-featured or as rugged in a lot of places like on the back side or over this highland area as the Lunar Orbiter photos showed. Over.

a10a_1361453.speaker: Engle
a10a_1361453.text: OK. We copy that, Tom.

a10a_1361453.speaker: Stafford
a10a_1361453.text: And that's all three independent conclusions there.

a10a_1361453.speaker: Engle
a10a_1361453.text: Roger. Understand.

a10a_1361453.speaker: Stafford
a10a_1361453.text: A real rough area is over past Sabine and Ritter where you have strictly a volcanic area; you have these little cones all tossed up. But out here in the highland area - Yes. You've got a lot of slopes and things, but they're definitely not as rugged as what is shown there in those Orbiter photos. Over.

a10a_1361453.speaker: Engle
a10a_1361453.text: Roger. Understand. Looks like you could find some places to put down in there. Is that affirmative?

a10a_1361453.speaker: Stafford
a10a_1361453.text: Roger. Well, I don't want to try to push it. We'll have to get back on the ground on that one. But out in the mare area, you've got - what we saw yesterday down lower - like to point it out, that's qualitatively 25 to 35 percent smooth. We're in pretty good shape. Over.

a10a_1361453.speaker: Engle
a10a_1361453.text: Roger. Understand.

a10a_1361453.speaker: Stafford
a10a_1361453.text: Hey, as a matter of fact, for Jack, right here I'm locking right down in Censorinus from 60 miles [111 km] up, and you can see the boulders on that outer edge. And the shadows from them. Over.

a10a_1361453.speaker: Engle
a10a_1361453.text: That's pretty amazing, Tom. Those must be pretty good sized rocks down there.

a10a_1361453.speaker: Stafford
a10a_1361453.text: Yes. You could make a building or two out of each one of them.

a10a_1361453.speaker: Engle
a10a_1361453.text: Roger.

a10a_1361453.speaker: Cernan
a10a_1361453.text: We could drop an apple core right in the hole down there.

a10a_1361453.speaker: Engle
a10a_1361453.text: Roger.

a10a_1361453.speaker: Stafford
a10a_1361453.text: OK. We're passing over Site 2 for the last time around. Over.

a10a_1361453.speaker: Engle
a10a_1361453.text: Roger.

a10a_1361453.speaker: Cernan
a10a_1361453.text: Hello, Houston. What's your recommendation on a purge here? I turned the heaters on and I'm looking for it in the Flight Plan and I don't see it.

a10a_1361453.speaker: Engle
a10a_1361453.text: OK. Did you say a purge, Gene-o?

a10a_1361453.speaker: Cernan
a10a_1361453.text: Did you tell me to put the H 2 purge line heater on?

a10a_1361453.speaker: Engle
a10a_1361453.text: Roger. We wanted the purge line heater on. We anticipate purging number 2 here shortly. We don't want to do it just yet, though.

a10a_1361453.speaker: Cernan
a10a_1361453.text: I'll he standing by for some words from you.

a10a_1361453.speaker: Engle
a10a_1361453.text: Roger. We do want the heater on though, Gene.

a10a_1361453.speaker: Cernan
a10a_1361453.text: It's been on 22 minutes now.

a10a_1361453.speaker: Engle
a10a_1361453.text: Very good. Thank you.

a10a_1361453.speaker: Young
a10a_1361453.text: You know, you sure don't have any trouble telling a hole from the hills down here.

a10a_1361453.speaker: Engle
a10a_1361453.text: Roger.

a10a_1361453.speaker: Young
a10a_1361453.text: Like you do in some of those pictures.

a10a_1361453.speaker: Stafford
a10a_1361453.text: Right now we're on top of Sabine and Ritter, looking down in the dark shadows [garble] there, but you can see the ramping on the walls and one or two possible big boulders down in there. You know in the pictures it'll show them as black [garble] shadows down below [garble].

a10a_1361453.speaker: Engle
a10a_1361453.text: Roger.

a10a_1361453.speaker: Stafford
a10a_1361453.text: OK. We checked the P30 and we're about to go through it. We've got the spacecraft configured for TEI [garble] Auto RCS select switches, and everything is strapped down, so we're basically [garble] attitude time around, so as soon as we finish this strip on the landing site here, we're going right to it. [Garble] have any [garble] whether it needs the High Gain. Over.

a10a_1361453.speaker: Engle
a10a_1361453.text: Roger. Understand, Tom,

a10a_1361453.speaker: Stafford
a10a_1361453.text: And we have Landing Site 3 coming up right ahead. It's also marked by the craters [garble].

a10a_1361453.speaker: Engle
a10a_1361453.text: Roger, Tom.

a10a_1361453.speaker: Stafford
a10a_1361453.text: [Garble].

a10a_1361453.speaker: Stafford
a10a_1361453.text: In the area [garble, probably 'between'] Landing Site 2 and Site 3 [garble] the highland area [garble] really marked with a lot of volcanic activity. You can see it all over. You can see the old impact [garble] volcanic activity.

a10a_1361453.speaker: Engle
a10a_1361453.text: Eh, roger.

a10a_1361453.speaker: Engle
a10a_1361453.text: OK, Apollo 10. This is Houston. We'd like for you to go ahead and purge number 2 fuel cell now for 2 minutes. And we'd also like to have the High Gain antennas as soon as you finish this photography. Over.

a10a_1361453.speaker: Stafford
a10a_1361453.text: OK. You got Verb 64 coming at you. And well start - Say you want the fuel cell 2 purged of O 2 at this time?

a10a_1361453.speaker: Engle
a10a_1361453.text: Roger. Fuel cell 2 purged for 2 minutes. That's the hydrogen purge.

a10a_1361453.speaker: Cernan
a10a_1361453.text: That's a hydrogen purge, Right?

a10a_1361453.speaker: Engle
a10a_1361453.text: That's affirmative, Gene.

a10a_1361453.speaker: Stafford
a10a_1361453.text: Purge is started.

a10a_1361453.speaker: Engle
a10a_1361453.text: Roger.

a10a_1361453.speaker: Cernan
a10a_1361453.text: Hello, Houston. Are you reading us?

a10a_1361453.speaker: Engle
a10a_1361453.text: Roger, 10. This is Houston. We're reading you now, Gene.

a10a_1361453.speaker: Cernan
a10a_1361453.text: OK. You got Auto track and narrow beam. About three-quarters signal frame. Coming in clear.

a10a_1361453.speaker: Engle
a10a_1361453.text: Roger. Understand.

a10a_1361453.speaker: Stafford
a10a_1361453.text: OK, Houston. I'm going to go ahead and maneuver to TEI attitude and just fire the pitch. Over.

a10a_1361453.speaker: Engle
a10a_1361453.text: Roger. Understand, Tom.

a10a_1361453.speaker: Engle
a10a_1361453.text: 10, this is Houston. Tom, could you hold off on that attitude change for a while? We'd like to watch this purge until it's complete.

a10a_1361453.speaker: Stafford
a10a_1361453.text: OK. I want to have John get that P52 IMU.

a10a_1361453.speaker: Cernan
a10a_1361453.text: And that's 2 minutes on the purge. How's that look to you?

a10a_1361453.speaker: Engle
a10a_1361453.text: OK. We're not getting the data down - the high bit rate data down, Gene-o.

a10a_1361453.speaker: Engle
a10a_1361453.text: OK. If you've completed the purge...

a10a_1361453.speaker: Cernan
a10a_1361453.text: OK. Tell me what you want to do.

a10a_1361453.speaker: Engle
a10a_1361453.text: OK. You've completed the purge, so go ahead and maneuver to your attitude. That'll be fine.

a10a_1361453.speaker: Stafford
a10a_1361453.text: Roger.

a10a_1361453.speaker: Cernan
a10a_1361453.text: OK. The purge is complete and the H 2 purge line heaters coming off at this time.

a10a_1361453.speaker: Engle
a10a_1361453.text: Roger. Understand. Thank you, Gene.

a10a_1363125.speaker: Cernan
a10a_1363125.text: Houston, how do you read us?

a10a_1363125.speaker: Engle
a10a_1363125.text: Roger, 10. This is Houston. We're reading you ok. Go ahead.

a10a_1363125.speaker: Cernan
a10a_1363125.text: OK. Just wondering, Joe. I'm just playing with the Omni's - just playing with the Omnis to hold onto you until we get to the final burn attitude. Then you recommend Delta.

a10a_1363125.speaker: Engle
a10a_1363125.text: Roger. That's affirmative. And did you go all the way through P30?

a10a_1363125.speaker: Stafford
a10a_1363125.text: We stopped before we got the final countdown. It was over an hour at that time.

a10a_1363125.speaker: Engle
a10a_1363125.text: OK.

a10a_1363125.speaker: Stafford
a10a_1363125.text: We got the Delta-V's. Over.

a10a_1363125.speaker: Young
a10a_1363125.text: Hey, Joe. Did you want us to go all the way through P30?

a10a_1363125.speaker: Engle
a10a_1363125.text: Roger. I guess - It appears down here that you didn't get your external Delta-V flag set, John.

a10a_1363125.speaker: Stafford
a10a_1363125.text: Yes, we planned...

a10a_1363125.speaker: Young
a10a_1363125.text: We didn't go through it. We're going through it as soon as we finish this P52.

a10a_1363125.speaker: Engle
a10a_1363125.text: Oh, ok. Mighty fine, then. I'm sorry.

a10a_1363125.speaker: Stafford
a10a_1363125.text: Yes, but we plan to go through it again. We just wanted to check - Yes, we just wanted to check that you had the values loaded in there and we got a Comp out of it, you know. We understand.

a10a_1363125.speaker: Engle
a10a_1363125.text: OK. Sorry about that. [Garble].

a10a_1363125.speaker: Engle
a10a_1363125.text: Apollo 10, Houston.

a10a_1363125.speaker: Stafford
a10a_1363125.text: Go ahead.

a10a_1363125.speaker: Engle
a10a_1363125.text: Roger. Gene-o, are you on High Gain Antennas, now?

a10a_1363125.speaker: Cernan
a10a_1363125.text: That's a negative. I'm on Omni Bravo.

a10a_1363125.speaker: Engle
a10a_1363125.text: OK. Thank you very much.

a10a_1363125.speaker: Cernan
a10a_1363125.text: Houston, this is 10. I'm going to leave fuel cell 1 on the line until we come around the corner so you can take a look at it, and then we can talk about taking it off.

a10a_1363125.speaker: Engle
a10a_1363125.text: OK. That'll be fine, Gene-o. Thank you.

a10a_1363125.speaker: Mission Control
a10a_1363125.text: 138:38:24 We're now about 30 minutes from Loss Of Signal. You heard Gene Cernan report that the spacecraft is configured right now with the omni antennas, which accounts for the somewhat noisy communications we're getting. Apollo 10 is currently at an altitude of 64.6 nautical miles [119.6 km] approaching apogee, which we now show at 68.8 nautical miles [127.4 km]. The spacecraft orbit perigee is 52.8 [97.8 km] and the orbital weight of the Command and Service Module is 36,685 pounds [16,640 kg]. At the present time, the Apollo 10 crew is involved in a Program 52 platform alignment. The purpos

a10a_1364657.speaker: Cernan
a10a_1364657.text: Hello, Houston. Houston, this is 10. How do you read?

a10a_1364657.speaker: Engle
a10a_1364657.text: Roger, Gene-o. Reading you loud and clear. Go ahead.

a10a_1364657.speaker: Cernan
a10a_1364657.text: OK. How's that DSKY been looking to you?

a10a_1364657.speaker: Engle
a10a_1364657.text: OK. We're watching it. It's looking good, 10.

a10a_1364657.speaker: Stafford
a10a_1364657.text: OK. We went through P30 all the way, and now we're just going to do a crew defined maneuver over to the attitude, and then we're going to call P40. Over.

a10a_1364657.speaker: Engle
a10a_1364657.text: And, 10, this is Houston. I've got some attitudes for your post-TEI TV, if you'd like to copy them down.

a10a_1364657.speaker: Engle
a10a_1364657.text: OK. This will be for time 138:00. Use the hatch window, and your attitudes are roll, 180; pitch, 293; yaw, 000. And we'd like the High Gain Antenna angle pitch, minus 58; and yaw, 005. Over.

a10a_1364657.speaker: Cernan
a10a_1364657.text: OK. For a time of 138:00, out the hatch window; roll, 180; pitch, 293; yaw, 000; pitch, minus 58; and yaw, 005.

a10a_1364657.speaker: Young
a10a_1364657.text: And, Houston, we have all the Auto RCS switches on. Do you confirm them?

a10a_1364657.speaker: Cernan
a10a_1364657.text: Houston, this is 10. I'm going to cycle the cryo fans.

a10a_1364657.speaker: Mission Control
a10a_1364657.text: We're now 16 minutes, 30 seconds from losing contact with Apollo 10. The Flight Director, Milton Windler, has requested that his flight controllers to take a look at all the spacecraft systems and we'll be coming up shortly with the Go/No-Go for Trans-Earth Injection. Flight controllers report all systems Go for TEI.

a10a_1364657.speaker: Mission Control
a10a_1364657.text: 136:57:29 We're coming up now on 10 minutes to LOS. The Guidance Officer here in the Control Center...

a10a_1364657.speaker: Engle
a10a_1364657.text: Apollo 10, this is Houston. We show about 10 minutes until LOS, and at this time everything looks Go for TEI.

a10a_1364657.speaker: Stafford
a10a_1364657.text: Roger. We're going to call up P40 before we have LOS.

a10a_1364657.speaker: Stafford
a10a_1364657.text: OK. The Automaneuver in P40, we're all set there and trimmed up.

a10a_1364657.speaker: Young
a10a_1364657.text: Houston, could you give us a time hack at 35 minutes countdown?

a10a_1364657.speaker: Young
a10a_1364657.text: Roger. We'd like a time hack around 35 minutes countdown.

a10a_1364657.speaker: Engle
a10a_1364657.text: We'll have to give it to you a little before that, John. We show about 6½ minutes until LOS and then you're about 44 minutes. Oh, ok. I'm sorry, we'll get it for you.

a10a_1364657.speaker: Engle
a10a_1364657.text: OK, 10. This is Houston. I can give you a countdown to 34 [minutes]. Will that be ok?

a10a_1364657.speaker: Engle
a10a_1364657.text: And, 10, this is Houston. Did you get that, or would you like another countdown?

a10a_1364657.speaker: Stafford
a10a_1364657.text: We got it. Give us a mark for 33 [minutes] just to correlate.

a10a_1364657.speaker: Engle
a10a_1364657.text: 10, this is Houston. We're showing about 4 minutes until LOS, and that fuel cell 1 is looking good to us right now. Everything looks good for TEI.

a10a_1364657.speaker: Stafford
a10a_1364657.text: Roger. We're Go here, and we'll see you on the way home.

a10a_1364657.speaker: Engle
a10a_1364657.text: You bet your life. We'll see you in about 41 minutes.

a10a_1364657.speaker: Engle
a10a_1364657.text: OK, 10. Houston. We show 2 minutes until LOS. We're still Go; everything looks good.

a10a_1364657.speaker: Stafford
a10a_1364657.text: Roger. We're all set here and we'll check the, boresight star [garble] Over.

a10a_1364657.speaker: Mission Control
a10a_1364657.text: 137:08:04 And we now have LOS, Loss Of Signal, as Apollo 10 has gone around the corner of the Moon. When next we hear from the crew they should be on their way back to Earth after some 61 hours, 40 minutes. Just to recount the information for the Trans-Earth Injection maneuver; ignition is scheduled to occur at 137 hours, 36 minutes, 28 seconds. The burn duration will be 2 minutes, 41 seconds. That should give the spacecraft an added velocity of 3,630 feet per second [1,106 m/s]. The maneuver will occur at 155 degrees, 43 minutes East longitude, which will be on the back side of the Moon. And

a10a_1364657.speaker: Stafford
a10a_1364657.text: 2 minutes and 41 seconds burn. Overburn's [garble] You check it.

a10a_1364657.speaker: Young
a10a_1364657.text: John, this is two-jet ullage for 14 seconds [garble].

a10a_1364657.speaker: Cernan
a10a_1364657.text: [Garble] Want me to do the sextant star, which should be visible now, possibly - possibly on the horizon in the window?

a10a_1364657.speaker: Young
a10a_1364657.text: Tom, I don't mean to be [garble], but [garble].

a10a_1364657.speaker: Young
a10a_1364657.text: Should I load the shaft now?

a10a_1373600.speaker: Stafford
a10a_1373600.text: ...settles down, and then we might play one stanza [garble].

a10a_1373600.speaker: Cernan
a10a_1373600.text: Yes. Yes. That's a prewinder. Oh, [garble] Are you there?

a10a_1373600.speaker: Engle
a10a_1373600.text: Apollo 10, this is Houston. We are standing by.

a10a-13015XX.speaker: Cernan
a10a-13015XX.text: [Garble] pressures are Go, ball valves are Go.

a10a-13015XX.speaker: Cernan
a10a-13015XX.text: Looks like the time is going to be about 02:43.

a10a_1374554.speaker: Stafford
a10a_1374554.text: ...settles down, and then we might play one stanza [garble].

a10a_1374554.speaker: Cernan
a10a_1374554.text: Yes. Yes. That's a prewinder. Oh, [garble] Are you there?

a10a_1374554.speaker: Young
a10a_1374554.text: Just way back, about...

a10a_1374554.speaker: Engle
a10a_1374554.text: Apollo 10, this is Houston. We are standing by.

a10a_1374554.speaker: Cernan
a10a_1374554.text: [Garble].

a10a_1374554.speaker: Stafford
a10a_1374554.text: Can we talk?

a10a_1374554.speaker: Stafford
a10a_1374554.text: Hello, Houston. Apollo 10.

a10a_1374554.speaker: Engle
a10a_1374554.text: Hello, Apollo 10. This is Houston. How did the burn go?

a10a_1374554.speaker: Stafford
a10a_1374554.text: Roger, Houston. We are returning to the Earth. Over.

a10a_1374554.speaker: Engle
a10a_1374554.text: Glad to have you on the way back home, 10.

a10a_1374554.speaker: Stafford
a10a_1374554.text: Roger. The burn was absolutely beautiful and Gene-o has a report, and we have a fantastic view of the Moon now. Over.

a10a_1374554.speaker: Engle
a10a_1374554.text: Mighty fine, Tom. Standing by for that report.

a10a_1374554.speaker: Cernan
a10a_1374554.text: Hey, Joe. You've got an 'atta boy' for that PAD update. Here it comes: burn was on time: it was 2 minutes and 44 seconds. Residuals were plus 0.3 [fps, 0.09 m/s] which were reduced to 0.2 [fps, 0.06 m/s], plus 1.6 [fps, 0.5 m/s] and minus 0.2, Delta-V C is minus 19.9 [fps, 6.07 m/s]. Fuels remaining is 6.7 percent, oxidizer of 9.2 percent. My PUGS is reading Off-scale High on the increase. I put through the procedure but apparently it did no good at all. I'm still reading full scale increase on the PUGS and my oxidizer flow valve is still in Increase at the completion of the burn.

a10a_1374554.speaker: Engle
a10a_1374554.text: Roger, 10. We copied all of that.

a10a_1374554.speaker: Engle
a10a_1374554.text: 10, this is Houston. We'd like to go ahead and take that fuel cell 1 off both buses now.

a10a_1374554.speaker: Cernan
a10a_1374554.text: It's going off right now, Joe.

a10a_1374554.speaker: Cernan
a10a_1374554.text: Houston, the TV is being turned on now, and as Tom is starting to pan we have a couple of quick short words for you.

a10a_1374554.speaker: Engle
a10a_1374554.text: Roger. We're standing by. Go ahead.

a10a_1374554.speaker: Spacecraft
a10a_1374554.text: (Music: "Going Back to Houston" by Dean Martin)

a10a_1374554.speaker: Engle
a10a_1374554.text: Roger, 10. This is Houston. We copied that transmission. Thank you.

a10a_1374554.speaker: Cernan
a10a_1374554.text: Glad you got the message.

a10a_1374554.speaker: Young
a10a_1374554.text: Boy, this view's got to be a fantastic thing.

a10a_1374554.speaker: Stafford
a10a_1374554.text: Houston, 10. I hope the Aussies have their sets tuned in because it's utterly fantastic here.

a10a_1374554.speaker: Engle
a10a_1374554.text: Roger that, Tom. I'm sure they're all watching.

a10a_1374554.speaker: Young
a10a_1374554.text: We are taking a picture right now of Tsiolkovsky down south there. That's impressive.

a10a_1374554.speaker: Engle
a10a_1374554.text: Roger. Copy.

a10a_1374554.speaker: Young
a10a_1374554.text: What a place.

a10a_1374554.speaker: Mission Control
a10a_1374554.text: 137:50:51 And we have a black and white signal at this point.

a10a_1374554.speaker: Young
a10a_1374554.text: Joe, that's Tsiolkovsky back there. It's big and black and very distinguishable. Fantastic! Incredible!

a10a_1374554.speaker: Engle
a10a_1374554.text: Rog. We can see it pretty plain on the set. That's the one right up near the horizon. Is that affirm?

a10a_1374554.speaker: Young
a10a_1374554.text: It's sitting on the horizon; way out there. Right.

a10a_1374554.speaker: Engle
a10a_1374554.text: Hey, there you go. Now we're picking it up. We can see the center of it now.

a10a_1374554.speaker: Young
a10a_1374554.text: We can see the whole of the Smyth's Sea now.

a10a_1374554.speaker: Cernan
a10a_1374554.text: That's it, Joe. That's full zoom. You ought to be able to see that real good.

a10a_1374554.speaker: Engle
a10a_1374554.text: We can. That's just real good, Gene.

a10a_1374554.speaker: Young
a10a_1374554.text: I can see the whole of the Smyth's Sea and I see old F-1 down there.

a10a_1374554.speaker: Cernan
a10a_1374554.text: There's Neper.

a10a_1374554.speaker: Young
a10a_1374554.text: Got this big bright ray crater up on the northern horizon. They are going to try and put that on the tube. Boy, that's a big one. The rays of Schmidt Crater go all the way across the Moon.

a10a_1374554.speaker: Young
a10a_1374554.text: Must be new.

a10a_1374554.speaker: Engle
a10a_1374554.text: What's your f-stop setting on the camera now?

a10a_1374554.speaker: Stafford
a10a_1374554.text: Roger, Joe. I've got it at 22. The Moon's awful bright.

a10a_1374554.speaker: Engle
a10a_1374554.text: Roger that, Tom. Thanks.

a10a_1374554.speaker: Stafford
a10a_1374554.text: I'll occasionally flick it up, down, and then back to help saturate the tube, but that's what you see, there. OK. We're taking all kinds of pictures. I've got the tubes, Gene-o has the sequence camera, and John has the Hasselblad. We're getting all this documented.

a10a_1374554.speaker: Stafford
a10a_1374554.text: Is that better, Joe?

a10a_1374554.speaker: Engle
a10a_1374554.text: Yes. That's a little better there, Tom. What did you do there?

a10a_1374554.speaker: Stafford
a10a_1374554.text: Stand by. I'll change my ALC switch on it.

a10a_1374554.speaker: Engle
a10a_1374554.text: Yes. That's a little better, Tom. That's great, The detail is coming out a lot better.

a10a_1374554.speaker: Stafford
a10a_1374554.text: OK. Again, as we move away, the basic Moon looks tan to us. The new craters are definitely white from the impact and some of the volcanic ones; but from this Sun angle, it's basically tan out there - a white, white tan. And the rays you can see are even whiter. And moving over this way, the one crater you can see over there is a brownish in color with the one central peak in it. I'll try to put the zoom on it for you.

a10a_1374554.speaker: Engle
a10a_1374554.text: Roger, Tom. We're picking it up now. We can see the central peak in the crater.

a10a_1374554.speaker: Stafford
a10a_1374554.text: OK. Do you have any color there, Joe, at all?

a10a_1374554.speaker: Engle
a10a_1374554.text: Say again, Tom, please.

a10a_1374554.speaker: Stafford
a10a_1374554.text: Roger. Do you have color in Houston, or just black and white? Over.

a10a_1374554.speaker: Engle
a10a_1374554.text: We got color here in Houston. There's quite a bit of light for the color, although we can make out the crater and we can see the central peak in it. The black and white is coming out real good.

a10a_1374554.speaker: Stafford
a10a_1374554.text: OK.

a10a_1374554.speaker: Stafford
a10a_1374554.text: OK. What I'm looking at now is a brown, and the peak in it is light tan - around it is a little darker tan. Does that correlate with your colors? Over.

a10a_1374554.speaker: Engle
a10a_1374554.text: Roger. That looks real good on the monitor here, Tom. That's just what we're seeing here.

a10a_1374554.speaker: Young
a10a_1374554.text: This is absolutely incredible!

a10a_1374554.speaker: Stafford
a10a_1374554.text: I thought it was a fantastic view leaving the Earth, but it is going to be even more fantastic one leaving the Moon here and heading back to the good old Earth.

a10a_1374554.speaker: Engle
a10a_1374554.text: Roger that, Tom.

a10a_1374554.speaker: Young
a10a_1374554.text: I got the whole of the Smyth's Sea. [Garble] Crisium.

a10a_1374554.speaker: Engle
a10a_1374554.text: Roger.

a10a_1374554.speaker: Stafford
a10a_1374554.text: OK. The way you're seeing it right now is about f:50, pardon me, 55 [mm] on the zoom. That's about the way we're seeing it now, maybe a little more.

a10a_1374554.speaker: Engle
a10a_1374554.text: Roger. Understand.

a10a_1375642.speaker: Stafford
a10a_1375642.text: OK. I'll hand the camera over to John here and he'll show you the Sea of Crises. Over.

a10a_1375642.speaker: Engle
a10a_1375642.text: Roger. And while you're doing that, Tom, we got confirmation on your burn. It looks like we'll have about 1 foot per second [0.3 m/s] at your first MCC at 15 hours.

a10a_1375642.speaker: Stafford
a10a_1375642.text: Roger. I think we can afford about 1 foot per second [0.3 m/sec]. That isn't bad.

a10a_1375642.speaker: Engle
a10a_1375642.text: Can't hardly beat that.

a10a_1375642.speaker: Stafford
a10a_1375642.text: Yeah. The old guidance system is doing great work for us on this mission.

a10a_1375642.speaker: Engle
a10a_1375642.text: Roger that. That's a real interesting picture that you're showing us now, too.

a10a_1375642.speaker: Stafford
a10a_1375642.text: [Garble]. Tell the people responsible for it that it works just fantastic [garble].

a10a_1375642.speaker: Stafford
a10a_1375642.text: And also for the first time, we're seeing what we call I guess, what Gene just termed a gigantic turtle-backed crater that's fractured. We'll put the zoom on that in just a minute.

a10a_1375642.speaker: Engle
a10a_1375642.text: Roger.

a10a_1375642.speaker: Cernan
a10a_1375642.text: There's a real interesting crater here on my right, Joe. It's an enormous thing and it's fractured almost symmetrically in a number of pie-shaped pieces. Let's see if we can get it for you in a minute.

a10a_1375642.speaker: Engle
a10a_1375642.text: OK. We're standing by.

a10a_1375642.speaker: Stafford
a10a_1375642.text: In fact, looking straight ahead, just now coming into view, even though we're really starting to climb out from it - In fact, I can finally see the whole Moon right in the hatch window. But looking down the road, there's Messier A and B, the Taruntius twins. We have Censorinus there for Jack. And on up ahead I can see Landing Site 1 even from this distance from the landmarks that led in. Over.

a10a_1375642.speaker: Engle
a10a_1375642.text: Roger. Understand. That's real good to know.

a10a_1375642.speaker: Stafford
a10a_1375642.text: Boy, you can't believe this rate of climb. It looks like we're just going out just vertically. Just beautiful. It would scare the heck out of you if you came at this angle, but maybe it was just because we came in the dark and didn't see the thing. Over.

a10a_1375642.speaker: Engle
a10a_1375642.text: Roger. Understand.

a10a_1375642.speaker: Cernan
a10a_1375642.text: Hey, Joe, that's that crater I was talking about. I don't know how that is, but I can see a little bit of it in my monitor.

a10a_1375642.speaker: Engle
a10a_1375642.text: It's coming in real good, Gene. It looks like you're just about to crowd the top part of the window there, but weve got the whole crater, and yeah, we can see those fractures in there.

a10a_1375642.speaker: Stafford
a10a_1375642.text: It looks like the outer rim is slumped down and you have some maria material near the edges and the whole thing is fractured there in the middle from a couple of impacts near the center.

a10a_1375642.speaker: Engle
a10a_1375642.text: Roger. We can make it out.

a10a_1375642.speaker: Mission Control
a10a_1375642.text: 137:59:50 Spacecraft now some 850 nautical miles [1,574 km] from the Moon.

a10a_1375642.speaker: Stafford
a10a_1375642.text: OK. Down in the central part here, it's still a tan color and as we move further away, it's starting to get a little more white in the mare areas, turning to a light brown - a whitish brown. Over.

a10a_1375642.speaker: Engle
a10a_1375642.text: Roger. Understand.

a10a_1375642.speaker: Cernan
a10a_1375642.text: Kind of looks like the real Moon.

a10a_1375642.speaker: Engle
a10a_1375642.text: Roger. The crater that you were show...

a10a_1375642.speaker: Cernan
a10a_1375642.text: It's a little rounder, too, isn't it? Go ahead, Joe.

a10a_1375642.speaker: Engle
a10a_1375642.text: Rog, Gene. I was just going to say that that crater you were showing us, your fractured crater there, it looked like there was a dark patch on the left-hand side. I wonder if that was just something that showed up on the tube or if you observed that up there. In the upper left-hand corner there now.

a10a_1375642.speaker: Stafford
a10a_1375642.text: No, Joe. That looks like maria material. That's right, that's maria material in that crater, Joe. Over.

a10a_1375642.speaker: Engle
a10a_1375642.text: Rog. That's real interesting.

a10a_1375642.speaker: Stafford
a10a_1375642.text: Just wait till about another 30 minutes. Bet you'll be able to see the whole thing, then. Over.

a10a_1375642.speaker: Young
a10a_1375642.text: That engine did it again, boy. What a prince.

a10a_1375642.speaker: Cernan
a10a_1375642.text: Does it look a little rounder?

a10a_1375642.speaker: Engle
a10a_1375642.text: Rog. Looking real round now. If one of you guys get half a chance, see if could give us Accept on the computer, we'll shoot you up a new load.

a10a_1375642.speaker: Stafford
a10a_1375642.text: That sounds good. We're in P00 and Accept. You got it.

a10a_1375642.speaker: Engle
a10a_1375642.text: Roger. Thank you.

a10a_1375642.speaker: Mission Control
a10a_1375642.text: 138:01:26 Altitude 930 [nautical miles, 1,722 km].

a10a_1375642.speaker: Engle
a10a_1375642.text: Man, it looks like you guys are climbing out of there.

a10a_1375642.speaker: Stafford
a10a_1375642.text: Rog. You'd better believe we're climbing out, just like we're in a vertical climb going straight out from the center: it's a fantastic sight. Also for the record, I was just looking here. It's a beautiful beach but where's the ocean? Over.

a10a_1375642.speaker: Engle
a10a_1375642.text: Rog. [Laughter.]

a10a_1375642.speaker: Stafford
a10a_1375642.text: OK. I've got the camera back in the central window again.

a10a_1375642.speaker: Cernan
a10a_1375642.text: Joe, this is incredible. That thing is getting rounder and rounder and rounder and smaller all the time.

a10a_1375642.speaker: Engle
a10a_1375642.text: Rog, Gene-o. Understand.

a10a_1375642.speaker: Cernan
a10a_1375642.text: The real show is on the inside here; it's like three monkeys in a string pod.

a10a_1375642.speaker: Engle
a10a_1375642.text: Yes, I'll bet that's right.

a10a_1375642.speaker: Stafford
a10a_1375642.text: Joe, I'll tell you, what you see out there is real close to what we have; maybe the curvature is a little more. Now one thing real interesting, you see the two dark spots there in the center of your screen, the maria material. Over.

a10a_1375642.speaker: Engle
a10a_1375642.text: I've got them.

a10a_1375642.speaker: Stafford
a10a_1375642.text: OK. Now to us, and all three of us have correlated this, that is a light brown color and surrounding it you have the highland areas there which is a tan color, and you can see that one impact spray crater up there that's a white chalky color. Again, that looks just like the material of gypsum, I'd say. Over.

a10a_1375642.speaker: Engle
a10a_1375642.text: Rog. Were getting the same colors that you are describing, Tom. It's just great, fantastic!

a10a_1375642.speaker: Stafford
a10a_1375642.text: OK. I've got another crater over here I'll zoom in on. It is to the right of that one maria, and you can see it: it's real bright with rays coming out of it, and I'll zoom on it.

a10a_1375642.speaker: Engle
a10a_1375642.text: Roger.

a10a_1375642.speaker: Mission Control
a10a_1375642.text: 138:03:52 Apollo 10 now 1,060 [nautical] miles [1,963 km] from the Moon.

a10a_1375642.speaker: Engle
a10a_1375642.text: OK, 10. This is Houston. You can go back to Block on the computer. It's yours and the fuel cells are looking real good and you might be interested to know you are coming in real great all the way across Australia.

a10a_1375642.speaker: Stafford
a10a_1375642.text: Well, to the people of Australia from the crew of Apollo 10, we'd like to say good morning. We've seen your country many times on the way up to the Moon, and we'll see it many times on the way back. It looks very beautiful from even 210,000 miles [390,000 km] out. Over.

a10a_1375642.speaker: Cernan
a10a_1375642.text: [Attempting an Australian accent] That Tommy is a charmer.

a10a_1375642.speaker: Engle
a10a_1375642.text: I should say.

a10a_1375642.speaker: Cernan
a10a_1375642.text: Hey, Joe, the Moon is almost small enough now where I can see the whole thing from the top, one corner of my forward window to the other corner of my forward window.

a10a_1375642.speaker: Engle
a10a_1375642.text: Roger. Understand.

a10a_1375642.speaker: Cernan
a10a_1375642.text: I can see the whole Moon from top to bottom in my forward window.

a10a_1375642.speaker: Engle
a10a_1375642.text: Roger. Understand, Gene.

a10a_1375642.speaker: Stafford
a10a_1375642.text: Looks like the old camera is doing a pretty good job here, zooming in and out picking up spots.

a10a_1375642.speaker: Engle
a10a_1375642.text: You guys are really hauling the mail out there.

a10a_1375642.speaker: Stafford
a10a_1375642.text: Boy, you better believe it. It's like we're climbing straight out, Joe. It's a fantastic sight: its like we were shot straight out from the center of the Moon.

a10a_1375642.speaker: Cernan
a10a_1375642.text: Is that what you call it, Joe?

a10a_1375642.speaker: Engle
a10a_1375642.text: That's what we call it tonight. You're going about 6,000 feet a second [1,830 m/s].

a10a_1375642.speaker: Stafford
a10a_1375642.text: OK. We're picking up now more of the maria material and, again, even from this distance still, to keep the recording going, it is a brown in the maria area; the surrounding area is a light tan; In fact, I've got one little crater I'm going to try to zoom on. See the maria area on the left side of your screen now? Over.

a10a_1375642.speaker: Engle
a10a_1375642.text: Roger. Got it.

a10a_1375642.speaker: Stafford
a10a_1375642.text: OK. Up in there is a little rather small maria area of round spray crater. Let's see if we can zoom on that spray crater there.

a10a_1375642.speaker: Engle
a10a_1375642.text: Roger. OK.

a10a_1375642.speaker: Cernan
a10a_1375642.text: Joe, that fractured crater that had the dark material off on the left side is also about one-fourth of the bottom right-hand side. You're not looking at it now, the bottom quarter of the right-hand side - It's all full of that very darkish - dark gray material, also.

a10a_1375642.speaker: Engle
a10a_1375642.text: Roger. Copy, Gene.

a10a_1375642.speaker: Stafford
a10a_1375642.text: In fact, right now all the people watching TV are at an advantage because what you're seeing in your screen is a bigger image than what we see. And right there, see that little white crater that I put down there about the center of the screen?

a10a_1375642.speaker: Engle
a10a_1375642.text: Roger. We got it.

a10a_1375642.speaker: Stafford
a10a_1375642.text: The white chalky material is surrounded - you have some tan, and then around the base maria over here on the right, and that is brown. Over.

a10a_1375642.speaker: Engle
a10a_1375642.text: Roger. Thank you, Tom. That maria over on the lower right...

a10a_1375642.speaker: Stafford
a10a_1375642.text: No. Hold on.

a10a_1375642.speaker: Engle
a10a_1375642.text: Is that dark brown, or is that black?

a10a_1375642.speaker: Stafford
a10a_1375642.text: No, no. The maria here that is right in the middle of the screen. Now, Joe, that is a brownish color. We estimate a light brownish color with slight streaks of tan that are over from the right crater. But this one is coming up right here. I'll put the zoom on it. Do you see that rascal?

a10a_1375642.speaker: Engle
a10a_1375642.text: Roger. We got it.

a10a_1375642.speaker: Stafford
a10a_1375642.text: OK. The crater that you have now: the inside of that is chalky color; the rays coming out are light tan; a darker tan surrounds it, and then you move into the maria which is a brown color. Over.

a10a_1375642.speaker: Engle
a10a_1375642.text: OK. We got all that description. Boy, that little crater with the grays sure stands out nice.

a10a_1375642.speaker: Stafford
a10a_1375642.text: Right. And you can see down into it, and the sides are just a chalky white color; at the bottom is a tan like we've seen before, surrounding it is a white tan with the rays lighter. But going over to the maria, you can see the rays in the maria material there, a light tan over a brown. Over.

a10a_1375642.speaker: Engle
a10a_1375642.text: Roger. We understand.

a10a_1375642.speaker: Cernan
a10a_1375642.text: Hey, Joe, down at 9 miles [16.7 km] has to be exciting, but this has got to be unbelievable. The wind - the Moon now is well within the boundaries of my forward rendezvous window.

a10a_1375642.speaker: Stafford
a10a_1375642.text: And now that we're showing you that crater, just one thing I wanted to check - Does our description of the color match with your picture down there? Over.

a10a_1375642.speaker: Engle
a10a_1375642.text: Right. It's coming up pretty good, Tom. The area - maria area that you described as brown looks a very dark brown here, almost black, a real dark brown, and evidently, that's a little lighter to you than it shows up on the screen.

a10a_1375642.speaker: Stafford
a10a_1375642.text: Yeah. OK. What about the tans? Is that somewhat about the same? Over.

a10a_1375642.speaker: Engle
a10a_1375642.text: Roger. That's looking real good. In fact, Tom, I'm at a little disadvantage. I'm looking at the big screen up here on the board, and they say on the monitor in the back of the room there, that the colors are exactly as you're describing them.

a10a_1375642.speaker: Stafford
a10a_1375642.text: OK. Well, I passed my eye test I guess the last time for the T minus 4-day physical so I guess they haven't gone too bad. This is an interesting crater right here; looks like a lot of them formed after you have a big crater, then you have slumping in the walls. Here you can see a series of ridges where the walls are slumped down in, and I'll zoom in a little bit. Over.

a10a_1375642.speaker: Engle
a10a_1375642.text: Rog.

a10a_1375642.speaker: Stafford
a10a_1375642.text: OK. And the whole view now is getting so fantastic I'm going to go out to the wide angle to show you what we're seeing. I can see the whole Moon right out the hatch window.

a10a_1375642.speaker: Engle
a10a_1375642.text: Roger.

a10a_1375642.speaker: Mission Control
a10a_1375642.text: 138:10:09 That view from 1,400 [nautical] miles [2,600 km]...

a10a_1375642.speaker: Engle
a10a_1375642.text: Oh, that's beautiful.

a10a_1375642.speaker: Stafford
a10a_1375642.text: Well, there it is.

a10a_1375642.speaker: Cernan
a10a_1375642.text: See what I mean about size, Joe. It just about fills up, roundwise, right smack in the hatch window. Boy, and is this a full Moon, I'll tell you.

a10a_1381024.speaker: Engle
a10a_1381024.text: You're just about 1,400 [nautical] miles [2,600 km] out now, Gene.

a10a_1381024.speaker: Stafford
a10a_1381024.text: Roger. 1,400 [nautical] miles [2,600 km] out from the Moon, and the view is actually just incredible like Gene has described. We're all just laughing up here. Just looking at it. Again, as we've said before, it's a good thing we came in backwards at nighttime where we couldn't see it because if we came in from this angle you'd really have to shut your eyes. Over.

a10a_1381024.speaker: Engle
a10a_1381024.text: Rog. Understand. Tom, how about going to the other position on ALC [Automatic Level Control] and let's see how it looks.

a10a_1381024.speaker: Stafford
a10a_1381024.text: There's the other position. [Pause.] Joe, we've been shooting this whole thing at f:22.

a10a_1381024.speaker: Engle
a10a_1381024.text: Rog. Understand. Okay. That's good, Tom. Go on back to - let's see, I imagine you're on...

a10a_1381024.speaker: Stafford
a10a_1381024.text: We're going back to...

a10a_1381024.speaker: Cernan
a10a_1381024.text: We're on the outside now, Joe. How's that? That's where we were. We just went inside for a while and then came back.

a10a_1381024.speaker: Engle
a10a_1381024.text: Roger. That's a lot better. Stay on the outside.

a10a_1381024.speaker: Stafford
a10a_1381024.text: And, again, this whole area looks - That maria material is brownish and still the color hasn't changed much. It's brown and tan with lights. Over.

a10a_1381024.speaker: Young
a10a_1381024.text: Hey, Joe, with a midcourse of a foot a second [0.3 m/s] we must be in that corridor.

a10a_1381024.speaker: Engle
a10a_1381024.text: Thats pretty close.

a10a_1381024.speaker: Young
